But now she was a duly-initiated disciple of Srila Prabhupada, and with her usual steadfast determination she resolved to follow him, to try to please him, and to never leave his association.

Before Srila Prabhupada left for New York, a strange and surreal event occurred which involved Yamuna and Janaki’s Aunt Edna Howell. She called one day and blithely told them that their birth father had written to her and wanted to come to San Francisco to meet them. This was, to say the least, astonishing news to both of them because they had been informed in their childhood that he had passed away—something they accepted as literal truth. Now here he was, very much alive. She added that she had told him they were following an Indian swami and he expressed a desire to meet Srila Prabhupada as well. So one day he came to the temple bearing various gifts, including two Benares silk saris, which were still considered rare in the West in those days. Despite their hesitancy to meet him, both Yamuna and Janaki were thrilled with the gifts. He was introduced to Srila Prabhupada, and later the two sisters awkwardly met him and his large new family at their hotel. There they spoke for a few minutes, said their goodbyes, and then never saw or heard from him again. So in one sense, he died a second time by passing away again from their vision. However, for Yamuna, the whole incident caused barely a blip on her memory, and she wrote and spoke little about it over the years. For her, Srila Prabhupada was her father—in fact, her all-in-all—and she felt complete satisfaction in his family of devotees. Later, Yamuna wrote of the gifts Srila Prabhupada gave her and how she hoped to share the gift of his teachings and example with others:

**Yamuna**: *I remember, in illustrating how a devotee gives and receives gifts, first how you had the ability to extend yourself to so many at once. You had the gift of giving fully to those in your company. I recall once, when my father, long lost since my early childhood, showed up to meet you when I was 25. The meeting was brief, but incredibly, he presented you with two Benares silk saris. You gave him prasadam, and in turn, gave the saris to my sister and me. Over the years you gave me so many gifts from your wardrobe: sweaters, chaddars, slippers, jewelry, socks, eyeglasses, and even a tooth. They have long ago been distributed to others. In this connection, I pray to share your gifts of merciful compassion with others throughout my life.*

## Lord Jagannatha Comes to San Francisco

In terms of access to Srila Prabhupada, it was an unprecedented time for the hippies and devotees of San Francisco in early 1967 because on a daily basis they were able to meet with him, hear from him and have informal talks with him. Every morning Srila Prabhupada would take his morning walk, his aristocratic and majestic bearing immediately distinguishing him from other walkers. These walks allowed the devotees access to him that was both intimate and rewarding.

**Yamuna**: *Morning walks with Swamiji were exceedingly pleasurable and informative for anyone who walked with him. They invariably took place in Golden Gate Park, and one of his favorite areas to walk was around Stow Lake. He would also sometimes walk in the park’s famous rhododendron gardens. During these morning walks, he revealed the philosophy of Krishna Consciousness, often using analogies and symbolism drawn from the beautiful nature around him, and then using scripture to substantiate it. In this way he would walk briskly for long periods of time, and these walks became a highlight of my life.*

*One of the humorous pastimes during this period involved our “wreck” of a temple car. It was a 1952 blue Ford coupe that we dubbed the “Krishna Car.” And it was such an ugly car; it only ran by the supreme mercy of the Lord. Swamiji was transported in this car to and from his walks in the park and virtually anywhere else he went. At that time Jayananda das’s occupation was cab driver, so he would often drive this car. Unfortunately, the passenger seat in the car was broken, so rather than sitting up straight, it leaned at a 45-degree angle. And as Swamiji was always majestic in his stature, with his chin held up very high, because of the incline of the seat, his chin was almost pointing straight up because he was practically lying down in the car. And yet, even with this awkward seating arrangement, and even though he was almost completely unable to see outside, still he never complained to us. Such was his kindness.*

If there weren’t kirtans in the temple on Monday, Wednesday and Friday, anyone could visit Srila Prabhupada in his apartment and gather around his feet. He would sit in his rocking chair, gigantic bead bag in his hand as he chanted the Holy Names, and everyone would sit around him asking questions or listening to him speak about the philosophy of Krishna Consciousness. Even the “unacceptables,” the drugged-out hippies high on LSD, were sometimes allowed access to these informal gatherings, which disturbed some of the other devotees. “Why do you waste Swamiji’s time with these crazy people?” they would sometimes ask. But Srila Prabhupada seemed to show by his example the tolerance and patience needed to encourage even one soul to accept a drop in the ocean of Lord Chaitanya’s mercy, and Yamuna observed this quality in him, understood it, and applied it in her dealings with others for the rest of her life.

In those days Malati was the main temple-shopper and deal-finder. From the beginning she had a real gift for getting things done. One day she was in a large import store in San Francisco—Cost Plus—she found a barrel filled with odd-looking three-inch figures with “Made in India” on them. Thinking them unusual and “cool,” she brought one home. Later her husband suggested they take it to Srila Prabhupada to see if he knew what it was, and when Srila Prabhupada saw the figure, his eyes got very big and round, and he offered obeisances to it. Though stunned by his reaction, they were even more stunned when he asked if they could find two more different figures in the barrel. They did, and when they brought them before Srila Prabhupada, he explained the history of Lord Jagannatha and asked if Shyamasundara could carve them in a larger size. He then carved beautiful Deities of Jagannatha, Subhadra and Balarama, and They were installed on the first Gaura Purnima. Hayagriva das described this transforming event:

**Then, in early March, unannounced and unexpected, Lord Jagannatha, the Supreme Lord of the Universe, graces us with His presence, transforming San Francisco into New Jagannatha Puri. “This is Lord Krishna as He is worshiped in the great temple of Jagannatha Puri, Orissa,” Swamiji explains. “There He resides with His sister Subhadra and brother Balarama.” Shyamasundara buys three wooden blocks, each three feet high, and begins carving on the roof of his Haight Street apartment. In a very short time, by mid-March, the Deities are ready and brought to the temple. Above Swamiji’s dais, Shyamasundara constructs a plain redwood altar. At night, we raid Golden Gate Park and return with boxes of flowers for the installation. The Jagannatha Deities are beautiful indeed and amazingly accurate reproductions. Swamiji is pleased. “Krishna has given you the intelligence,” he tells Shyamasundara. “You have done it so nicely.”**

**At the installation, Swamiji performs a new ceremony in which he offers incense, fire, water, cloth and flowers to Lord Jagannatha. “This is called arati,” Swamiji explains, passing the candle around. Following his example, we briefly feel the flame’s heat with our hands, and then touch our hands to our foreheads. “In this ceremony, we take the heat of the flame.” This is the advent of Jagannatha Swami, and now the temple is ready for this worshiping process. Krishna is a person, and we have to make friendship with Him. Just like we have to make connections if we want to see someone very great, we have to introduce ourselves in a friendly way, a loving manner, to Krishna. If we want to transfer ourselves to that supreme planet, Krishna-Ioka, then we have to prepare ourselves to love Krishna. Love of God. We must be intimately in touch with God by love. Swamiji teaches us a new mantra especially for Lord Jagannatha, chanting it to a beautiful melody: Jagannatha swami nayana-patha-gami bhavatu me. Translation: “O Lord of the universe, kindly be visible unto me.”**

**— HARE KRISHNA EXPLOSION**

**Yamuna**: *Masses of devotees were gathered inside and outside the temple to welcome Their Lordships. In the tradition of the times, psychedelic lights had been installed above the Deities which consistently changed color: one was blue, one was red and one was yellow, and they were on a circuit just above the head of the Jagannatha Deities, so they turned in a constant circle, flash flash, flash, flash, flash flash. When the lights would hit the eyes of Lord Jagannatha, His eyes would become three-dimensional, and they would beam in and out, in and out, as the different lights would illuminate Him. So His eyes became the most attractive feature in the room, for they were always pulsating with movement, and it would immediately catch everyone’s attention.*

Yamuna used to say that this must have truly impressed the hippies because not only were the Deities unique-looking Themselves, but They had this perpetual light show on Them. Prior to the installation of the Deities on Their new altar, a large picture of the Pancha Tattva dancing and a beautiful two-foot tall Deity of an electric-blue Krishna, Kartamasayi, His left hand delicately placed on His hip, had been the focal point of temple worship.

Srila Prabhupada used to sometimes sit in his rocking chair looking out the window of his apartment. Once he saw a yellow flatbed truck in front of the Diggers’ Free Store next door. Because he saw everything with eyes consecrated by devotional service, he envisioned a unique use for the truck in Krishna’s service— Rathayatra.

**Yamuna**: *Swamiji had personally drawn the two-ton flatbed truck he had observed from his window, and he gave the drawing to Shyamasundara. And in Swamiji’s drawing it became a grand old truck with a big bed on the back. He had drawn four columns and made a little canopy with some bells and festoon flags hanging off the edge. He said to Shyamasundara, “Make me this cart for Rathayatra.” So this was Swamiji’s vision. He had this combination of being cent-percent Krishna Conscious and being practical at the same time, so he would see an ordinary thing like a truck and envision utilizing it in wonderful ways for Krishna’s service.*

## Srila Prabhupadas Encompassing Mercy — Even to the Animals

**Yamuna**: *Janaki had a black cat, Skutzelbrunzer, who had traveled with us from New York, and this cat would take any opportunity to escape from Mukunda and Janaki’s apartment and creep down the hallway to Swamiji’s. And when he would enter, sometimes he would run underneath the claw-footed bathtub in Swamiji’s bathroom, which was the first door on the right. Every time Swamiji entered the bathroom and saw the cat there, he would patiently ask for it to be taken out; so although he was removed again and again, somehow the cat always found his way back and under the bathtub. So Swamiji knew that Skutzelbrunzer was under the bathtub—we all knew. But we thought, “Well isn’t it cute that he likes to be around Swamiji.” So this bath had no shower, and when Swamiji bathed, he used a lota and would purposely splash water all over the floor, knowing Skutzelbrunzer was under the tub. So Swamiji seemed to play this rasa with the cat again and again, knowing the cat was under the tub and hated to get his paws wet. Sure enough, each time the cat came out he’d tentatively put a paw out, get it wet, and bring it back in; then he’d put it out again and shake the water off and repeat the process, acting like it was the most horrible thing to have his paw wet. Finally, after Swamiji was finished bathing, someone would go retrieve the cat. Somehow, despite his obvious abhorrence of water, Skutzelbrunzer continued to find his way under the bathtub on a regular basis, and this rasa was repeated several times.*

*So Swamiji had quite an unusual relationship with Janaki’s cat. Once during visiting hours, Swamiji was sitting in his rocking chair, all of us gathered around his feet, when out of the corner of our eyes we saw the cat slowly coming down the hallway. As Skutzelbrunzer came closer and closer, he reached Swamiji’s feet and simply sat down, looking intently up at Swamiji and then speaking “Meow.” So we were all wondering what Swamiji would do—what would happen now? And then Swamiji picked up his beautiful lotus foot and began to very gently stroke the back of the cat, saying “Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna.” And he said to Janaki, “You are feeding him Krishna prasadam milk?” So from the onset he was even encouraging the animals to hear the chanting of Hare Krishna and to eat Krishna prasadam. These activities touched our hearts and made us long for further association with such a personality who was even concerned for the spiritual wellbeing of a cat. This one revelation of Swamiji’s character—this one exhibition of his compassion for all living beings—had an enormous impact on me, making my attachment and commitment become more deeply rooted in my heart.*

Yamuna sometimes commented that she did not have a lot of intimate association with Srila Prabhupada during this time. As a newly initiated student, she would engage in temple services and her own devotional practice, yet she was reluctant to push herself forward. Her enthusiastic willingness to perform any needed task, as well as a steady and inflexible service attitude, were what brought her gradually closer to Srila Prabhupada, and one way this manifested was through her calligraphy skills.

## Yamuna Begins Calligraphy Services

Very soon after Srila Prabhupada came to San Francisco, Yamuna wanted to present him with a gift, and so she calligraphed the Siksastakam prayers of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. Where that gift offering traveled over the years can only be imagined, but somehow the now time-worn offering came back into Yamuna’s possession a few years ago. This gift and Srila Prabhupada’s reaction to it would launch what would become one of her primary early services—using her skill at calligraphy to create everything from certificates for initiated students, posters, invitations, signs and letters, virtually anything that Srila Prabhupada wanted beautifully inscribed.

**Yamuna**: *My first exchange with Swamiji in service in San Francisco happened through my calligraphy. I had calligraphed the Siksastakam prayers and presented them to him as a gift. When he looked at them, his eyes opened widely, and he commented that the Goswamis were also very expert in beautiful handwriting, and that I should use this talent in Krishna’s service. So first he asked me to make a sign in lovely calligraphy for the San Francisco temple to hang outside the door. And so meetings were arranged with Swamiji where I would bring him samples of twenty-five or thirty different styles of scripts; and he would look and say, “Oh! You can do all this?” “Yes, I can do.” And so he picked out the script that was used for our first San Francisco temple sign. Swamiji was expert at encouraging each devotee in any way they wanted to serve Krishna. Whether it was taking photos, teaching how to keep accounts or how to cook—whatever ability or interest we had—he would try to encourage us to use it in Krishna’s service. So one of mine happened to be handwriting, and it evolved from that beginning and continued over many years.*

Yamuna’s early calligraphy can also be seen on the first certificates of initiation into the society. In the top corner of a letter written to her in 1968, Srila Prabhupada drew a small illustration of how he wanted the certificate to look. Srila Prabhupada often expressed appreciation for Yamuna’s beautiful calligraphy, both in person and in letters. Sometimes he would hold aloft something she had calligraphed and, almost with a fatherly pride, display it to those in the room. In his first letter to her after her initiation and marriage, he wrote:

**I am very much pleased to see your good handwriting. I shall therefore request you to utilize your talent in the service of Krishna. I think if you write Hare Krishna Hare Krishna in the same style as you have sent me one specimen, on bigger type on canvas, say 30 inches by 20 inches in color or black and white, it would be a very good engagement for you and at the same time we can utilize those sign boards hanging in nice places. So if you have got time you can prepare immediately such signboards Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna, Hare Hare, as you have sent me the specimen, on canvas.**

**— LETTER TO YAMUNA, MAY 5, I967**

## He was Always Thinking of Krishna

The San Francisco devotees knew that Srila Prabhupada would soon be returning to New York. Several of the New York devotees had been writing of important programs they had scheduled for him to attend, and Srila Prabhupada was also concerned that in their attempts to purchase a larger building for a new temple, they had been cheated out of virtually all of the temple savings. As Srila Prabhupada was always extremely frugal andcautious in money dealings, this weighed on him, and he heavily chastised the New York men for their carelessness. Still, he did not want to overly distress or discourage them, so he applied the salve of encouragement along with the sting of chastisement. He wrote on March 28:

**Forget the chapter. Take it for granted that Krishna has taken away this money from you for your deliberate foolishness. In future be very cautious and abide by the orders of Krishna. If you abide by the orders of Krishna, He can give you \[any\]thing that you may need. Be cheerful and chant Hare Krishna without any lamentation. As I have told you several times that my Guru Maharaja used to say that this world is not a fit place for gentleman.**

**— LETTER TO BRAHMANANDA ET AL., MAR. 28, I967**

For the ever-growing cadre of devotees in San Francisco, the very prospect of Srila Prabhupada’s leaving was unthinkable. They had become dependent on him in so many ways—both spiritually and practically. He taught the philosophy of Krishna Consciousness, and he taught the women to cook. He strictly taught and adhered to the regulative principles and practices of Krishna bhakti, yet he patiently tolerated and nurtured the drugged-out hippies of Haight-Ashbury. In his interviews, preaching programs or festivals, he was uncompromising, yet he lovingly teased and bantered with the devotees under his care. He was the quintessential Spiritual Master, perfectly representing the teachings and example of his own guru, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur.

Before his scheduled return to New York, Srila Prabhupada repeatedly assured the San Francisco devotees that he would swiftly return to them. Yet this was little consolation in the wake of his impending absence, which seemed unendurable to them.

**Yamuna**: *During the days leading up to Swamiji’s departure on April 9, we all grew despondent and were already beginning to feel separation from him. Years later, I read in the Caitanya-caritamrta how the highest platform of love of God manifests when Krishna is present before the devotee, but the devotee, lost in separation, cannot see Him standing there. So from my neophyte perspective, this was how I felt then. Swamiji was always thinking of Krishna, and we were always thinking of Swamiji.*

## We are on a Sound Footing in Krishna Consciousness

Srila Prabhupada left as scheduled for New York on April 9,1967. In a letter after his arrival, he wrote to all the affectionate and disconsolate devotees in San Francisco:

**I am so much obliged to you for your devotion and affection for me. I thought of you all throughout my journey from Francisco to New York, and I was praying to Lord Krishna for your more and more advancement in Krishna Consciousness.... The reception in New York was very good organized by our students here and there was distribution of varieties of prasadam to about too men in the temple.... I am now very well although I am feeling your great separation. Please continue kirtan as usual with devotion and you will make more and more advancement in Krishna Consciousness.**

**— LETTER TO JANAKI, ET AL., APR. 9, 1967**

It was clear that Srila Prabhupada was concerned that in his absence his new initiates and interested followers not lose their connection to devotional practices. In a letter to Mukunda das on May 5, he reiterated the importance of attending the temple programs and following the process of Krishna Consciousness:

**The devotees of the temple must keep themselves engaged otherwise they cannot make progress in Krishna Consciousness. Maya is very strong and as soon as there is opportunity maya will come and attack. Therefore everyone should be very careful against the attack of maya. And the only effective defense is to remain in Krishna Consciousness always.**

**— LETTER TO MUKUNDA, MAY 5, 1967**

In reading Srila Prabhupada’s letters to the San Francisco students from this period, it is evident that the separation from him expressed in their letters was also reciprocated by him. Several times over the years he mentioned to Yamuna how much nostalgia he had for those early San Francisco years. In a letter to Ballabhi on May 5,1967, Srila Prabhupada wrote:

**If you try to follow my instruction you will feel that my body is in your presence always. I know that you all devotees of San Francisco are very much anxious to get me back there, and I am also trying to go back there as soon as possible; in the meantime go on with your chanting and hearing and everything will be all right by the grace of Krishna.**

**— LETTER TO BALLABHI, MAY 5, 1967**

Later, in a letter to Janaki and Mukunda on May 21, Srila Prabhupada revealed his plan for returning post haste to San Francisco:

**Your ardent call is responding from heart, and I have decided to return to San Francisco any day after June 5,1967. You can advise therefore the American Air Lines for booking my seat and take my instruction here when I shall start as you did it last time.... you may announce ... that I am coming to San Francisco very soon—sometime in the second week of June 1967.**

**— LETTER TO JANAKI AND MUKUNDA, MAY 21, I967**

## My Spiritual Master Has Not Finished His Work

On Memorial Day, May 30,1967, Srila Prabhupada suffered a stroke in New York. The prognosis was grave. Almost immediately the small Frederick Street temple room became full to overflowing. There was intense grief. So much love and appreciation had developed in the hearts of the residents of San Francisco’s Haight-Ashbury for Srila Prabhupada that people from many faiths joined together with the devotees in chanting and offering prayers for Srila Prabhupada’s life. Some carried rosaries, some came on LSD trips; yet this eclectic and varied group individually and collectively prayed together for the recovery of this great saintly person. Yamuna wrote about their all-night kirtan:

**Yamuna**: *Swamiji had sent us a telegram which said, “If you pray to Lord Jagannatha, and if He hears your prayers, I will stay; otherwise I may go.” And we began the first all-night kirtan that any of us had ever done. There we were in our temple at Lord Jagannatha’s lotus feet, with those strange lights pulsating, and we had an amazingly heartfelt, twelve-hour kirtan for Swamiji. Almost no one left the temple, and it was one of those life-changing events where you go through many, many stages of appreciating the Holy Name. I remember I chanted for about two hours, and then at around 2:00 am something changed in the atmosphere—one of those very powerful yet inexplicable things—and we felt almost intuitively that Swamiji was out of danger. It was an unforgettable experience.*

Srila Prabhupada taught the devotees in New York the prayers to Lord Nrsimhadeva and asked them to request the Lord to allow him to remain alive longer to spread the fledgling mission of Krishna Consciousness. “My Spiritual Master has not finished his work, so dear Lord Krishna, please let him finish.” Jadurani wrote the words down and called the devotees in San Francisco, and they also immediately began to chant the prayer:

*tava kara-kamala-vare nakham adbhuta-sringam*  
*dalita-hiranyakashipu-tanu-bhringam*  
*kesava dhrita-nara-hari-rupa jaya jagadisa hare*

**“O my Lord, Your hands are very beautiful, like the lotus flower, but with Your long nails You have ripped apart the wasp Hiranya-kashipu. Unto You, Lord of the Universe, I offer my humble obeisances.”**

Srila Prabhupada slowly began recovering, and the devotees in San Francisco felt as though a new breath of life had been given to them. They realized from the experience of nearly losing his association how much Srila Prabhupada meant to them, and it gave to many a renewed conviction and strength of purpose. In a prayer reflecting on this incident, Yamuna later wrote:

**Yamuna**:

**I remember how in San Francisco, we were informed by the New York devotees of your life-threatening stroke in 1967. And how, at your request, we stayed in the temple for almost twelve hours straight, praying to our Jagannatha Deities for your protection. I remember how, after some hours praying, the eyes of Lord Jagannatha opened fully wide, and how through the eyes of the Lord, He came to life for me; how we all felt that Lord Jagannatha heard our crying pleas that you stay with us for at least some time more, and indeed you recovered. In this connection, I pray for your continued company and pure devotional service. I wish to live in the shelter of the moment that you invited me to become your disciple, with the words, “Just see. Just see.” I want to see all that you wish to show me in devotional service.**

On June 5, 1967, Srila Prabhupada wrote to the devotees in San Francisco expressing his gratitude for their prayers:

**I am so much obliged to you for your prayers to Krishna to save my life. Due to your sincere and ardent prayers, Krishna has saved my life. I was to die on Tuesday certainly, but because you prayed sincerely, I am saved. Now I am improving gradually and coming to original condition. Now I can hope to meet you again and chant with you Hare Krishna.**

**— LETTER TO KRISHNA DEVI, AUNT EDNA HOWELL, ET AL., JUNE 5, 1967**

It is interesting to note here the mention of Yamuna and Janaki’s aunt Edna Howell in Srila Prabhupada’s letter. From the beginning of her nieces’ commitment to Krishna Consciousness, Aunt Edna had occasionally visited the Frederick Street temple and had a real and genuine affection for Srila Prabhupada. It is clear from his various mentions of her, as well as gifts she received from him, that Srila Prabhupada appreciated her open-hearted acceptance of her nieces’ spiritual path. There was not one time over the years we visited Aunt Edna that she did not speak about Srila Prabhupada with great feeling and fond appreciation. Even on our last visit to her when she was weeks from passing away, she again remembered him with tears in her eyes.In another letter to Mukunda, on June 6,1967, Srila Prabhupada, already directing his attention toward the devotees in San Francisco and the upcoming Rathayatra, wrote:

**Please inform all the devotees, boys and girls, especially Janaki devi, that I am progressing well. As soon as I get a little strength for traveling I shall come to San Francisco. In the meantime I shall be very glad to know what arrangements you are going to do for the Rathayatra festival. Make it a grand procession and unique introduction in the United States.**

**— LETTER TO MUKUNDA, JUNE 6, I967**

Jayananda das, a dedicated and staunch new devotee, couldn’t understand why Srila Prabhupada, who was a pure servant of Krishna, and who had come to America on a selfless mission to deliver the fallen souls of the West, had to suffer such tremendous challenges, health and otherwise. He was so perplexed that he wrote a letter, which Srila Prabhupada partially answered in a postscript to the June 6 letter to Mukunda.

**Also inform Jayananda I have received his letter and the difficulties of life may come as seasonal changes, but we should not be disturbed by all those difficulties. Our process is to chant, and that process will gradually clear everything in due course. There is nothing to be disrupted—you should go on with your work with enthusiasm, and everything will be solved. We are on the sound footing of Krishna Consciousness.**

**— LETTER TO MUKUNDA, JUNE 6, I967**

## Rathayatra — Lord Jagannatha

**Visits Srila Prabhupada in Stinson Beach**

Srila Prabhupada had gone to the coast of New Jersey for a few weeks to recover, but the San Francisco devotees, feeling great separation, longed for him to come back into their loving care. Srila Prabhupada had expressed a desire to be there for the Rathayatra festival on July 9, and much to their delight, he arrived in San Francisco on July 6 to overwhelming expressions of happiness by the devotees. In contrast to his last airport welcome, however, this time he did not speak but simply walked, all the while softly chanting on his beads. Yamuna found this very worrying and hoped that Stinson Beach would provide just the respite he needed for his recovery. After a short visit to the temple, Srila Prabhupada was driven in a flower-covered station wagon by Jayananda to Stinson Beach. Although finding the facility itself comfortable, the drive had made him nauseous, and it dismayed him that he would not be able to visit the temple every day or even attend the Rathayatra procession.

**Yamuna**: *At that time we were all thinking that Swamiji might enjoy the cooling atmosphere of the Pacific Ocean, and that it might hasten his recovery. We rented a house just north of San Francisco in Stinson Beach, and Janaki, Harsharani and I cleaned it and prepared it for his arrival. It was just before our Rathayatra festival, and I remember Kirtanananda accompanied Swamiji as his personal servant. As we were putting paintings onto the walls, Janaki saw a painting that had been sent from New York of Lord Nrsimhadeva, who was appearing in His lila of tearing apart Hiranyakasipu with His nails. So He was literally decorated with blood, and this appeared too ghastly for Janaki. So she covered the painting with a madras cloth and slipped it behind the piano at the residence. For the time being it was hidden from view and forgotten by everyone. But after Swamiji arrived there, he requested Kirtanananda to play the piano, and in moving it out from the wall, there was a distinct banging, which prompted Swamiji to ask, “What was that sound?” Then Kirtanananda found the madras-covered painting behind the piano, and again Swamiji said, “What is this?” “I don’t know, Swamiji.” When the madras was removed and the picture of Lord Nrsimhadeva revealed, Swamiji continued pursuing the issue. “Why is this being kept behind the piano?” And at this point Janaki finally confessed, and Swamiji was so tolerant, so kind, and showed so much patience at her lack of knowledge and respect. He explained who Lord Nrsimhadeva was, and why this pastime was actually very glorious. He said that with a material mentality, someone would feel sorry for Hiranyakasipu, but the devotees, understanding the real history—the real story—are very happy when they see the Lord tearing this great demon with His nails. In this way, he was speaking to us—to persons coming from such a material mentality—and trying to slowly, slowly interject this Krishna Conscious philosophy within our hearts. These lessons were like gems to us—gems of wisdom and gems of his genuine compassion.*

Except for the problems related to its distance from the temple, Srila Prabhupada initially appeared satisfied with the facilities. In a letter to Brahmananda das in New York, he wrote:

**Jayananda in a nice car brought me to the house, which is situated in an exceptionally nice spot, and the house itself is aristocratic. So there is nothing to complain about the house and place. The only difficulty is that I cannot go to the temple on account of the zig-zag course of the road in crossing the mountains.**

**— LETTER TO BRAHMANANDA, JULY II, I967**

**Yamuna**: *On Rathayatra Sunday, July 9, Shyamasundara brought the yellow flatbed truck on which the chariots were mounted, and the Deities were installed and garlanded with hibiscus flowers. Lord Jagannatha was placed on the right side of the cart beneath a foldable canopy engineered by Jayananda. While placing each Deity, the devotees sang “ jagannatha-swami nayana-patha-gami bhavatu me.” “O Lord of the universe, please be visible unto me.” Subhadra looked out from the rear, and Lord Balarama was seated on the left. So no matter what side you were on, you were able to get the face-to-face darshan of Their Lordships. On the cart’s four corners were placed Christian, Muslim, Jewish and ISKCON flags. The ISKCON flag consisted of a Sanskrit AUM and a drawing of a dancing Radha and Krishna.*

*A few wonderful things about this Rathayatra were that the crowd who gathered alongside the cart were either hippies who knew nothing about Lord Jagannatha or hippies who had tasted prasadam in our temple and sampled the nectar of the Holy Name in our kirtans. All were genuinely enthusiastic to celebrate the Rathayatra festival. At one point the truck had to go up one of those near-vertical San Francisco hills. Shyamasundara was driving with his dog Ralph sitting next to him in the front seat. And just as the truck was trying to get up the hill, it stalled and wouldn’t start again. After a great endeavor, with the truck sometimes rolling several yards back down the hill, much to our relief it started, and we were able to again move forward. As soon as Swamiji heard this story, he gave the analogy that in the Caitanya-caritamrta there is a description about Lord Jagannatha’s cart stopping, and despite the efforts of hundreds of men, it would only move again when Lord Chaitanya pushed it with His head. So he was happy that this same pastime was being re-enacted on this first Rathayatra festival in the Western world.*

*The route was from Haight-Ashbury all the way to the sea. And when the cart arrived at the sea, there was a very wonderful kirtan on the beach. We prepared hundreds of chapatis, all smothered in melted ghee; and we cut crates and crates of oranges, and that was our public prasadam distribution for the procession to the beach. Except for a few mishaps, it was a very wonderful procession and festival.*

Yamuna and Janaki sat on one side of the cart, Yamuna playing harmonium and chanting Hare Krishna the whole way. Unfortunately, when they arrived at the beach someone distributed a sugared candy to some of the devotees, including Yamuna and Janaki, and unbeknownst to them it was laced with LSD. After the beach kirtan and prasadam, it was decided that Their Lordships should go to Stinson Beach to Srila Prabhupada's residence. It was a wonderful and thoughtful gesture, and Srila Prabhupada was very pleased. Unfortunately, Yamuna, Janaki and some others were unable to go because of their “illness,” and Srila Prabhupada noted their absence immediately: “Where are Janaki and Yamuna?” he asked. When it was explained to him what had happened, his eyes became very wide, and he said that this should be a lesson to the devotees to eat only prasadam, food offered to the Supreme Lord, Krishna. He explained that food cooked by nondevotees carried karmic consequences, whether laced with LSD or not. But food offered to the Lord becomes sanctified, and just by eating such foods, we make spiritual advancement. It is so sublime.On July 11, Srila Prabhupada wrote about the Rathayatra festival to Brahmananda in New York:

**Anyway, the devotees are coming here, and the Rathayatra Festival was performed with great pomp. More than 500 people followed the procession to the beach, and there were about two dozen cars. They distributed thousands of chapatis, and at last Sri Jagannatha, Subhadra, and Baladeva kindly came here in our house and will stay here for one week and then return. So far my health is concerned, on the whole it is nice, but sometimes I feel not so good. Everything depends on Krishna, and as He desires it will happen.**

**— LETTER TO BRAHMANANDA, JULY II, 1967**

Unfortunately, the Stinson Beach facility had some severe drawbacks. In addition to the winding roads making visits to the temple sporadic, the weather was challenging, and there was little sun.

**Paradisio isn’t quite paradise. The bird stool on the Buddha was no doubt portentous. There is very little sunshine. Behind the beach house, to the east, a mountain range blocks out the morning sun, and by midday, clouds and fog roll in. The temperature is also rather cool for July. To fully recover, Swamiji needs lots of sun. He especially misses the morning sun. He feels that if he can just get enough light and heat, his condition will improve. Because of this, he begins talking of returning to India, and this upsets us. We’ve supplied the nicest place possible near San Francisco, but we can’t supply the sun. Moreover, Swamiji regrets having no close temple contact. He wants to visit the temple at least twice a week, but the winding road into San Francisco is too arduous.**

**He speaks more frequently of India. He wants to consult Ayurvedic doctors, who generally prescribe natural herbs recommended in certain Vedic writings. And then there’s Indian massage, another art unknown to us. Swamiji complains that Western doctors know only how to cut with knives and stick with needles. We don’t know what to suggest. We feel inadequate, helpless.**

**— HARE KRISHNA EXPLOSION**

Even at this early date, Yamuna was either making recordings or writing down Srila Prabhupada’s words in a journal, a practice she carried on diligently throughout his manifest presence with us. Of those journals, only two remain, yet they reveal so much about her sincere determination to record every word of Srila Prabhupada’s teachings. They are physical reminders of an uncanny dedication—page after page of tiny handwriting capturing each word, phrase or sentence of her beloved guru.

**Yamuna**: *I personally was not able to make many recordings because access to him at Stinson Beach was limited for health reasons, and it was not often that we went to see Swamiji. Yet, I do recall one incident that affected us all deeply. Because of his weakened health, he would sometimes say, “I am an old man, and I may die at any moment.” Of course, this was unbearable for us to hear. He had just come into our lives; he had freely and compassionately given the greatest gift of Krishna bhakti to us, so the thought that he might die was simply unthinkable. Still, at one point it was suggested that he might ask one of his Godbrothers to come to the United States to join him in his preaching work. So after two days of contemplation, Swamiji definitively refused to call upon any other person to assist. He said, “My work will go on with the disciples that Krishna has sent me, because if my Godbrother speaks just one word different from what I am speaking, then there will be great confusion among you.” Then tears began streaming down his face, and he haltingly said, “My Spiritual Master was no ordinary man. He saved me.” And I was reminded of that instruction many times as the years passed— the importance of hearing singularly from my Spiritual Master and accepting him as the supreme authority for knowing Krishna.*

By July 20, Srila Prabhupada had already arranged passage by air to India and expressed in a letter to Sumati Morarji that he was “feeling too much to return to Vrindavan at the lotus feet of Vrindavan Bihari.” In the final days before his departure, he was literally pleading with the devotees to stay strong and resist the inevitable attacks of maya. He elaborated on the theme of the Guru being with you whether he is physically present or not, a theme he would remind Yamuna of repeatedly over the years. He spoke about human life being so rare—such a gift—and we should not waste it. With tears in his eyes, he said, “I beg you to take up this process. It is so sublime.” And yet, they were to experience their first devotee defection before Srila Prabhupada even left.

## A Disciple Falls Away

**Yamuna**: *From the onset, Swamiji explained that his Guru Maharaja was preaching to make brahmacharis and sannyasis, while he was principally making grihasthas, or married couples. So he began to marry the boys and girls who were living within our temple—Shyamasundara and Malati, Yamuna and Guru das, Subal and Krishna devi, Gaurasundara and Govinda dasi, Ravindra Svarupa and Halidar—in this way, he was encouraging the grihastha ashram. Our close-knit family under the care of Swamiji suffered intensely when one of his first initiated disciples, Ravindra Svarupa, disavowed the practice of Krishna Consciousness and left Swamiji’s association. An intense young man by nature, he made it known to all of us that he intended to go, so in some way we were prepared for that, but not the dramatic way in which he affected it. In the latter part of the afternoon or evening during the middle of kirtan, Swamiji was on his vyasasana, and Ravindra Svarupa appeared at the temple door, paid his obeisances, and rather than getting up or sitting with the other devotees, he crawled on his hands and knees toward Swamiji. So, of course, this heart-wrenching approach caused an immediate disturbance to the kirtan, and many of us began to cry. Ravindra Svarupa was also sobbing and crying, and as the kirtan slackened, he got to Swamiji’s vyasasana, on which there were two or three small steps. And Swamiji looked down at him lovingly and said, “Come here my boy; come here my son.” He then crawled up the steps and his bushy head of hair fell into Swamiji’s lap. Swamiji then began to gently stroke Ravindra Svarupa’s head, saying, “What is wrong my son?” And Ravindra Svarupa tried to explain that he was a crazy fellow and for some reason or other he couldn’t stay with us and practice Krishna Consciousness. And while he continued stroking the boy’s head, Swamiji explained, “I am an old man; I may die at any moment, but please, please carry on this Sankirtan Movement. Please don’t leave.” And I remember how it struck all of us to the core of our hearts how fortunate we were to have been given the honor of being Swamiji’s disciples, and that if we tried to leave or negate that, we would lose this great and inconceivable gift we had been given—the gift of the most sublime and easy process for going back home, Back to Godhead.*

*And then he explained, just like in Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu’s Siksastakam, that we have to become humble, we have to become very tolerant, and we must have real enthusiasm and patience in order to push on this Krishna Conscious Movement, and he again requested us to please stick together. It was a very profound and moving experience. We were all crying, really overwhelmed, and Swamiji was also crying and actually begging this young boy to stay within the incomparable movement of Lord Chaitanya. This vivid example of Swamiji’s compassion sometimes appeared in my mind’s eye when I later faced challenges. It was so compelling—so real— and I knew that he felt the same way about each and every one of us.*

In a prayer reflecting on this episode, Yamuna wrote eloquently of what she had imbibed from witnessing this first defection—the sense of urgency. I cannot count the number of times I heard her quote Srila Prabhupada’s “We may die at any moment, please do not waste time” instruction over the years. She truly never lost that sense of urgency. Even when she was ill, she could not be kept down. There was always a service, a task, a bhajan or kirtan, a program, a reading, Deity duties, or any number of what she felt were necessary services that had to be performed. It was another defining aspect of her character and dedication to the process of Krishna Consciousness. In telling of her journey in devotional life, it is important for me to reiterate the impact on Yamuna of those early character-building experiences with Srila Prabhupada, for they are what she carried forward in her life, and they are what she gave to others.

**Yamuna**: *I remember in San Francisco the tears you shed the night your first initiated disciple informed you he wanted to leave your association and his devotional service. How, with his head in your lap, and your hand stroking his head, you implored him to stay in our company, practice Krishna Consciousness and experience a wonderful life. How you explained that you might die at any moment, and that all of us had a serious responsibility to take up Krishna Consciousness and try to perfect our lives. We collectively felt a sense of urgency that was compelling and profound. In this connection, I pray that this sense of urgency never leave me.*

Srila Prabhupada visited the temple one more time before leaving and revealed to the devotees that in addition to his protection and guidance, he had asked his own spiritual preceptors to oversee and help guide his disciples. At this early juncture, the concept was too esoteric for Yamuna to understand, but gradually it came to be extremely important and compelling to her.

**I may be going, but my Guru Maharaja and Bhaktivinoda are here ... I have asked them to kindly take care of all of you, my spiritual children. The grandfather always takes care of the children much better than the father. So do not fear. There is no question of separation. The sound vibration fixes us up together, even though the material body may not be there. What do we care for this material body? Just go on chanting Hare Krishna, and we will be packed up together. You will be chanting here, and I will be chanting there, and this vibration will circulate around this planet.**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

As Yamuna matured in her devotional practice, she increasingly sought the shelter of our predecessor Acharyas by chanting their prayers and songs. Not only did she feel a very real and nurturing connection to both Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur and Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur, but she enthusiastically encouraged others to connect with them through their songs, prayers and commentaries. She credited Bhaktivinoda Thakur with teaching her how to improve the quality of her own prayers by revealing such pure and guileless honesty, humility and sincerity in his many songs. Once, in a spontaneous and moving prayer to him, Yamuna thanked the Thakur for his many gifts and prayed for increased sincerity. Over the last decade of her life, she chanted the full songbooks of Bhaktivinoda Thakur many times, both individually and with others, and these experiences were highlights of her life.

Most revered Bhaktivinoda Thakur: Today I fall at your lotus feet because it just occurred to me that of the many gifts you share through your prayers, the gift you taught me is how to pray. If anyone read your heartfelt prayers of longing for Krishna, for Lord Chaitanya, and for your own spiritual preceptors, they would not discover that you were a highly-placed government officer with unsurpassed responsibilities, or that you possessed a large family and dedicated wife, authored a hundred books on devotional practice, edited several magazines and were a stalwart defender of Vaishnava dharma. Instead they would find a humble soul begging for the chance to make progress in spiritual life and begging for the mercy of the Lord and the Vaishnavas. I pray to you for the ability to increase the sincerity of my prayers from one of pretense to one of actual sincerity, and I thank you with all my heart for the unparalleled gifts you have given to us all.

## Love in Separation— Srila Prabhupada Recovers in India

There are a wonderful series of photographs taken by Guru das of Srila Prabhupada at the San Francisco airport which show Janaki “stealing” his passport. Several years ago, Yamuna and I framed the set of them and presented them to her as a gift. In one particular photo, Srila Prabhupada is looking up with such love and affection at his “naughty child.” When I joined ISKCON in 1970, that picture was circulated as a facial shot of Srila Prabhupada, and it became my favorite photo of him. It was only years later that I saw the setting it captured and who it was he was looking at.

After Srila Prabhupada went to India, the initial despondency of the devotees was overtaken by a desire to continue the programs he had instituted—prasadam distribution, temple worship and harinam sankirtan. Some of the couples were inspired to go to other cities to try to open temples there. In San Francisco, Jayananda, considered the staunchest and most practical devotee, was elected temple president, and under his steady direction, the family of devotees endured Srila Prabhupada’s absence. Yamuna remembered a loving family mood prevailed among the devotees, along with a sincere desire to please Srila Prabhupada in separation.

Once ensconced in the native and spiritual setting of his homeland, Srila Prabhupada gradually began to recover. He was able to have Ayurvedic treatment and massage and again the shelter of his rooms in the Radha-Damodara Temple in Vrindavan, a place he often called “the hub of the wheel of the spiritual world.” On August 24, he wrote an encouraging letter to Guru das, and in one paragraph, he affirmed the mercy, power, purity and eternality of the Holy Name, and how the Lord reveals all of these things in the hearts of sincere souls who engage in devotional service.

**Sincere souls who are engaged in the service of Lord Krishna are benedicted by the Lord by revelation. Sri Krishna, His Name, Form, Entourage, Paraphernalia and Pastimes are not material; they are purely spiritual. Therefore, in the beginning they are not appreciated by our materially conditioned senses, but as we go on chanting Hare Krishna with a service mood and attitude, the Name, Qualities, etc., become revealed as Reality. For the unbeliever Krishna and His Name etc. are fictitious, but those who are advanced in Krishna Consciousness realize that Krishna Consciousness is pure and eternal.**

**— LETTER TO GURU DAS, AUG. 24, I967**

In a postscript to the same letter, Srila Prabhupada made a comment about Yamuna:

**Regarding Yamuna, your wife, I’ve got a very great regard, because she is a very sincere girl. I’m sure you should feel fortunate to have such a wife. Please offer my blessings to her, and always cooperate with your wife in the service of the Lord.**

**— LETTER TO GURU DAS, AUG. 24, 1967**

In the meantime, Yamuna’s sister, Janaki, was inconsolable during Srila Prabhupada’s absence, and wrote often to him expressing her feelings of separation and asking him to return. Srila Prabhupada recognized that her affection for him was central to her application of Krishna Consciousness, and he reciprocated lovingly, often as a father would a daughter. In a reply to her on September 16, Srila Prabhupada wrote:

**I am so glad to receive your letter of Sept. 5, ’67. I’m so pleased for your writing such nice sentiment. I’ve especially noted that you could express yourself so beautifully. I know both you and your sister have inherited a good heart from your good mother. Your eagerness to get me back in the States will surely be a success because I’m also eager to return. Tears for Krishna is as good as associating with Him personally. In the spiritual world separation is more valuable than meeting. So your feelings and tears of Krishna Consciousness will make you more enriched in spiritual advancement.**

**— LETTER TO JANAKI DEVI, SEPT. l6, 1967**

Then, in the next paragraph, he lovingly teased her by adding:

**You will be angry if I say that your sister is better than you, but I think I’m right because Mukunda supports me. Rivalry between good hearts is very nice job, but I’m equally pleased with both your sister and yourself.**

**— LETTER TO JANAKI DEVI, SEPT. l6, I967**

It is clear from Srila Prabhupada’s comment here how well he knew the character of his young followers. Janaki was always a plainspoken person and was not shy to display her feelings. She could be extremely loving and a naturally generous and caring person, but if she became disturbed, she would not hesitate to make her feelings known. It appears from this letter that Srila Prabhupada himself was not exempt from that.

Yamuna did not write extensively about the nearly five-month period of Srila Prabhupada’s absence from San Francisco. One of the amusing stories she told was of her unfortunate encounters with the Hells Angels motorcycle gang. The Oakland branch of this group was notorious for their violent actions and despicable conduct, even among the other motorcycle gangs, and they could often be found in the Frederick Street area. Mostly they kept their distance, but when they were intoxicated, the devotees gave them a wide berth.

**Yamuna**: *It became vogue in those days for the girls to pierce their noses. Malati started the trend, and it became more or less de rigueur. If you were a woman in our San Francisco community, you would undergo the pain of having Malati poke a needle through your nose to put a nose ring in it, because in the pictures we saw, the gopis, in order to please Krishna, all had nose rings. So we were taught that as our dress was for the pleasure of the Lord, we women should also pierce our noses. In those days it was such a strange and unique thing. Now, everyone has noses pierced, but then it was unheard of. So I had just had my nose pierced by Malati—a frightening experience, as my pain tolerance was never very high. My nose was still very tender and painful, and there was a kind of gold practice ring in it. So one night I was walking out of the temple at dusk, and on the corner were a group of Hell’s Angels, all dressed in their traditional Levi jackets which, when once put on, were never taken off. They were obviously highly intoxicated and making a loud commotion. So when I saw these frightening characters I tried to circle around them, but instead they circled around me. And I was standing helplessly in the middle. Then almost casually, one of the men took his very black, grimy little finger, put it through my nose ring, and clenched it tightly. In the meantime, the rest of them were all laughing and joking, enjoying the fun of seeing my discomfort while this horrific person held onto my nose ring. All through my life I had been known for having a strong voice, so in the loudest possible voice, with the most feeling I could muster, I screamed at the top of my lungs, “Lord Nrsimhadeva! Lord Nrsimhadeva!” and the vibration of this sound stunned the man so much that he let go, just enough for me to literally dive between his legs and run down the street. So this was a vivid example to me of how the prayers Swamiji taught us to ask the Lord for protection worked in such a potentially disastrous situation.*

This incident with the Hells Angels points to the general deterioration in Haight-Ashbury consciousness after the so-called “Summer of Love.” Admittedly, while the early peace-and-love idealism and utopian aspirations of the hippies included exploring higher consciousness with LSD, marijuana and other mind-altering drugs, it was now becoming spoiled by greed, hard drugs and violence. That magical portal which opened when Srila Prabhupada came and captivated thousands of eager spiritual seekers was now slowly changing. New recruits were still coming, and the daily free prasadam distribution was going on, but as the days passed and the challenges increased, the urgency among the San Francisco devotees for Srila Prabhupada’s return intensified.In New York especially, the serious problems brought on by defections and misunderstandings among the devotees were extremely troubling to Srila Prabhupada. Instead of India being the hoped-for quiet and peaceful environment for his recovery, Srila Prabhupada instead spent much of his time vigorously trying to manage his fledgling society by mail, telegraph and phone. His letters from this time bear witness to his attempts to instruct and cajole his recalcitrant first initiates in the West into remaining strong in their practice. The specific incidences have been comprehensively detailed in the Srila Prabhupada-lilamrta, but some of Srila Prabhupada’s instructions on how seriously he took his position as Spiritual Master are extraordinary and profoundly relevant. In a letter to Umapati from India on November 23, he wrote:

**When you left us I simply prayed to Krishna for your return to Krishna Consciousness because that was my duty. Any good soul who approaches me once for spiritual enlightenment is supposed to be depending on my responsibility to get him back to Krishna, back to Home. The disciple may misunderstand a bona fide Spiritual Master, being obliged to do so under pressure of maya's influence. But a bona fide Spiritual Master never lets go of a devotee once accepted. When a disciple misunderstands a bona fide Spiritual Master, the master regrets for his inability to protect the disciple and sometimes he cries with tears in the eyes. We had an experience while my Guru Maharaja was alive. One of His disciples who accepted sannyasa was one day forcibly dragged by his wife. My Guru Maharaja lamented with tears in His eyes saying that He could not save the soul.**

**— LETTER TO UMAPATI, NOV. 23, 1967**

## Srila Prabhupada Again Surcharges San Francisco

Finally, after what seemed like ages, Srila Prabhupada returned to San Francisco on December 14, 1967. The devotees were once more in the association of their most beloved Spiritual Master and again felt as if new life had been given to them.

**Yamuna**: *When he arrived at the airport in San Francisco, we were once again wildly ecstatic. We immediately noticed that as he stepped off the plane, he appeared stronger. He had a very erect bearing, and for the first time carried a sannyasa danda over his shoulder. A little saffron cloth bag had been tied on the top end of the danda. It was very curious, and we all speculated as to what was in that little cloth bag. This time we arranged for Swamiji to stay in a spacious flat on Willard Street, a block away from the temple. It was a rental my husband and I had occupied, and we vacated it for Swamiji’s stay. Newly renovated, with white walls, hardwood floors and numerous windows, it was large enough for his servant and secretary to reside in as well.*

*A convoy of devotees drove him to the Willard Street apartment and threw flower petals at his feet as he climbed the stairs. Once inside, Swamiji sat on a floor cushion in the bare room, his danda nearby. His presence illuminated the room more than the late afternoon sunshine. All of the disciples came to see him, and the joy of meeting him again was limitless. Soon someone enquired what was in the cloth bag tied to the danda. With a gentle smile, Swamiji tilted the danda and untied the little pouch-bag. Then his beautiful fingers on each hand fanned out, and inside were three strands of crushed silk garlands like those offered to Lord Jagannatha in Puri. They were all crushed and crumpled, because they had been carried in this saffron bundle. But when he displayed them to us, he said, “Now these can be tied around the necks of Lord Jagannatha, Subhadra and Balarama.” And practically speaking, this was the first real decoration Their Lordships had received. Shortly thereafter, Swamiji explained that we could even make clothes for Them. “What kind of clothes would you make? Doesn’t He already have clothes on?” we asked. “Isn’t that what the painting is for that’s on the Deity?” “No,” he replied, “You will find that Deities will sometimes be painted, or sometimes there will be carving on the Deities to show jewelry or clothing, but you can make clothes for Them.” Swamiji continued, “Here’s what to do. He wears a turban; He wears a shawl, and They wear a little skirt.” So then he asked for volunteers who would like to sew for the Deities, and Harsharani and I volunteered. We did not know of these things prior to that time.*

*Then Swamiji opened his suitcase, removed a stack of fine cotton Bengali saris, and handed one to each female disciple. The affection and care in his face at that moment is a mental snapshot I will never forget. My sari was a black cotton one with gold stripes and a gold and red border. I cherished that sari and wore it for many years. Then he removed a medieval-looking wood and iron tool and said it was a coconut scraper. “How do you use that, Swamiji?” we enquired. He then asked us to bake a coconut in the oven, split it open and remove the shell. That done, he put his lotus foot down on the piece of wood—we were watching in rapt ecstasy—and using his hands, he dragged pieces of coconut across a flat, half-moon of sharp iron teeth. Using this method he very quickly produced a whole mound of fluffy coconut pulp. “What do you do with that?” we questioned. “We will go in the kitchen,” he replied, as he picked up the coconut and walked on, with all of us traipsing in behind him. Placing the coconut pulp, ghee, sugar, a hint of camphor and cracked black pepper in a large skillet, he cooked it into a sticky mass. When it was cool enough to handle, he had us roll it into i-inch balls. Swamiji then explained that these were called coconut laddus, and they quickly became a favorite offering on special days. Later Jayananda played with the recipe, and instead of using sugar, he used sweetened condensed milk and baked the mixture into cookie-like golden brown wafers for Ekadasi. They were wonderful. Swamiji gave that coconut grater to me, and I never forgot how gracefully and efficiently he used it. It is difficult to express in words how Swamiji could make the most mundane-looking task appear as the epitome of elegance—almost like a dance—but it was something we witnessed repeatedly.*

In many of the pictures taken of Yamuna over the next few years, she can be seen wearing the sari from India that Srila Prabhupada gave her. The wonderful pictures of her garlanding him as he came out of the Willard Street apartment, followed by the series of walks with Srila Prabhupada around Stow Lake, are two examples. Anything Srila Prabhupada gave her, be it a tooth, a chaddar, or remnants of his prasadam, she worshiped and preserved with great care.

Another change instituted on a society-wide basis after Srila Prabhupada’s return from India was that henceforth he was to be respectfully referred to as “Prabhupada” and not “Swamiji.” This was initially difficult for many of the San Francisco devotees, as they felt that “Swamiji” was more endearing and personal. Yamuna remembered still referring to Srila Prabhupada as “Swamiji” throughout her early London days and was among those who were reluctant to give up the name she had always known him by—Swamiji.

Even though he had recently suffered successive Yamuna wearing the sari gven to her by Srila Prabhupada health crises, Srila Prabhupada plunged into temple activities with the vigor and enthusiasm of a young man. A schedule was instituted where, in addition to morning classes, he would give darshans on Tuesday and Thursday evenings in his room. Yamuna immediately began to record him, not wanting to miss anything he said. There were also some devotees who had come from New York and other places to be with Srila Prabhupada. One was Gargamuni, who also began recording Srila Prabhupada’s lectures and darshans. Another couple who came were Gaurasundara and Govinda dasi, who had served Srila Prabhupada during his initial recovery in New Jersey.

**Yamuna**: *By this time we had all become extremely attached to Srila Prabhupada, and when we learned that Gaurasundara and Govinda dasi had come to act as his personal servants, we were all saddened and confused as to why devotees from “outside” were brought in to perform a service we all wanted so much to do. We felt as a family in San Francisco at this time, and Prabhupada was the cynosure of our eyes, so it was disheartening to us because we felt that our own members could serve him and nicely provide for his needs. I can’t remember which of us brought it up to him, but when Srila Prabhupada heard how we felt, he gave us our first in-depth instruction on the perils of envy in spiritual life. He said that envy exists at the highest levels in the material world, even among the demigods, and that the very reason we are in this material world is that we became envious of Krishna. But in the spiritual world, there is no envy. He said that here, if someone sees another person excelling or making advancement, he becomes envious, and if he sees someone fail, he becomes happy. But in the pure state of Krishna Consciousness, everyone becomes happy at seeing others making more advancement or receiving the special mercy of Krishna or the Spiritual Master. They are enthused and gladdened by it. He then explained that if someone is placed in a position of service to the Spiritual Master, it should be seen as Krishna’s grace, and we should accept the situation and not allow the affliction of envy to manifest in our hearts.*

To Yamuna it seemed like she left nearly every encounter with Srila Prabhupada with new and profound instructions for her spiritual life. She had never seen “envy” defined as an inborn tendency, what to speak of an inborn tendency responsible for our fallen condition in the material world. In going through her effects not long ago, I came upon a note she had written to herself which said simply:

**Envy in the heart is the weed that must be eliminated. It cannot be allowed to grow. Examine, examine, examine within. Where there is envy, I cannot appreciate the process or the goal.**

**Yamuna**: *So, at this time, Srila Prabhupada wanted Gaurasundara and Govinda dasi to help on his manuscripts for the Teachings of Lord Caitanya. Govinda dasi would type the manuscripts and Gaurasundara would work on the Bengali. But at this time she did not know how to type, so she did not think she could help in the project, and she revealed this to Srila Prabhupada. Prabhupada simply said, “So you can learn to type.” She replied that this was not her inclination. And then Srila Prabhupada said, “A devotee can learn to do anything if they repeat this prayer before they begin any service.” And then he spoke this wonderful prayer:*

**om ajnana-timirandhasya jnananjana-salakaya**  
**caksur unmilitam yena tasmai sri-gurave namah**  
**sri-caitanya-mano-bhistam sthapitam yena bhu-tale**  
**svayam rupah kada mahyam dadati sva-padantikam**

*These words are so very, very powerful. They are our invocation for purification, and they were given to us by Srila Prabhupada long before we had a songbook, or before we knew the words to the Vande ham prayers—before we knew the words to almost anything except the mahamantra. So this invocation is for internal purification. Ever since then, I’ve said this prayer before any service, no matter where I am—whether I am in a simple kitchen or in the middle of a field collecting cow dung and trying to cook over an open fire, in a marble kitchen or in a temple—I always say these prayers. And, very quickly, Govinda dasi did learn to type for Srila Prabhupada.*

Many years later Yamuna repeated this story of Govinda dasi’s learning to type to a group of eager young students she was teaching cooking to. She used the story to reveal not only the necessity of our own internal purification, but also the underlying importance of approaching any endeavor in devotional service with prayer, just as Srila Prabhupada taught through the instructive experience of Govinda dasi.

As the devotees and supporters in San Francisco were drinking in the life-giving ambrosia of Srila Prabhupada’s association again, he was also continuing his vigorous campaign of managing the society by mail and telephone. The residual problems left by the dissident students in New York while he was in India were still affecting innocent devotees, and they wrote him often for advice and encouragement. In a letter to Jadurani on December 16,1967, he wrote:

**When I left your country on the 22 of July, I had very little hope to come back again. But Krishna informed me that I’m not going to die immediately; therefore, I have come back again to get inspiration of Krishna Consciousness from all you good souls. Although officially I am your Spiritual Master, I consider you all students as my Spiritual Master because your love for Krishna and service for Krishna teach me how to become a sincere Krishna Conscious person.**

**— LETTER TO JADURAN1, DEC. l6. 1967**

In light of what had been transpiring in his absence, such a letter is simply extraordinary in its humility and open-hearted acceptance of the inherent goodness of his students. How this must have encouraged them in remaining steady on the devotional path can only be imagined.

Yamuna recalled that her first recordings of Srila Prabhupada were on the First Canto, second chapter of Srimad-Bhagavatam, “Divinity and Divine Service.” He said that the entire philosophy of Krishna Consciousness is encapsulated in that one chapter. It always remained one of Yamuna’s favorite chapters of Srimad-Bhagavatam, and she would often quote from it to clarify or illuminate a philosophical question.

**Yamuna**: *He chanted the verses so beautifully in Sanskrit, and then during the next visiting hours he would give beautiful purports to the verses. He stressed the importance of this chapter and expressed his fondness for it. We brought Lord Jagannatha, Balarama and Subhadra into his room, and They sat right in front of him during this time.*

Srila Prabhupada again began his practice of taking morning walks each day in Golden Gate Park, and Yamuna recalled these walks as being exceptionally enlivening and informative.

**Yamuna**: *When Swamiji was in India, Acyuta-nanda das once sent pictures of him on sankirtan in Calcutta. When we saw Swamiji chanting in the streets of India, all of us were just praying for the day that we would be able to join him there. So, of course, Srila Prabhupada knew of my long-held desire to go to India, and one day on a morning walk around Stow Lake he said to me, “So you want to go to India?” And I said, “Yes, very much.” Then he questioned, “What do you want to do there?” And I said, “Any service that you will allow me to do, in any capacity.” So he said, “Now, I am receiving letters from Acyutananda that there is no facility for gri-hastas at this time, but even though you cannot go to India now, someday I will personally take you there on foot.” From my perspective in San Francisco at the time, I had no idea what that meant, but later we learned that going to a place for pilgrimage is one thing; but until you walk the paths and streets on foot, chanting the Holy Names as those before us walked and chanted the Holy Names, you can’t truly experience pilgrimage in India. I thought that was the most hopeful thing I had ever heard in my life.*

*On another morning walk around Stow Lake, Srila Prabhupada revealed to us that we would establish magnificent temples in Mayapur and Vrindavan to glorify our Vaishnava Acharya Bhaktivinoda Thakur. He said that actually there are already so many places of worship in these holy dhamas, but because Bhaktivinoda Thakur wanted to bring Krishna Consciousness to the West, we would do something wonderful for his pleasure and for the pleasure of Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur.*

## Srila Prabhupada Visits Los Angeles

**Yamuna**: *Srila Prabhupada never complained about his health during the next few weeks, yet it was clear to us that he had not regained his previous strength, even though he maintained a rigorous schedule of programs. Previously he had promised to visit any temple opened by his disciples, and Dayananda and his wife Nandarani had found a facility on Pico Blvd in Los Angeles. Although it was small and not in a desirable location, it was thought that the warmer climate of Los Angeles would assist in Srila Prabhupada’s recovery. Even though we could not imagine his leaving after arriving from India just weeks before, our main concern was for his health, and we were willing to make any sacrifice if it would allow him to live longer to give us his loving association and spread the Hare Krishna Sankirtan Movement. Mukunda and Janaki went down to help prepare for his arrival and rent an apartment for Srila Prabhupada.*

Three weeks after his arrival in San Francisco, Srila Prabhupada went to Los Angeles. Yamuna felt some relief because she knew of the loving care Janaki and Mukunda would give to Srila Prabhupada there. Despite his continuing health problems, Srila Prabhupada freely and selflessly gave his association to all of the devotees in Los Angeles and continued his sometimes teasing relationship with Janaki. On January 16,1968, he called Janaki in to dictate a letter. This was not a service Janaki usually rendered so she entered with a steno pad, and Srila Prabhupada had her write “Yamuna, you are a little better than Janaki but don’t get puffed up and be good to those a little less fortunate.” He also praised the working relationship Yamuna had with her husband Guru das. So to Yamuna, this light and teasing steno pad letter gave her hope that Srila Prabhupada’s health was improving. But again in February his health seemed to take a turn for the worse.

**Yamuna**: *In February, Janaki asked me to come to Los Angeles to help her cook for Srila Prabhupada. She said his health was weakening again. I was very concerned and immediately left for Los Angeles. On arriving, I went to see him right away and asked about his health. He replied simply that he was not feeling well. “I am having buzzing in my head—pressure. It is diabetes.” He took Ayurvedic medicine, but would not take insulin. We would hold meetings among ourselves to discuss his health, and then we would make recommendations. He would patiently listen to us, but then he wouldn’t follow. For example, we tried removing sweets from his diet-say halava or gulab jamuns. “What is this?” he would ask when he saw the sweets missing from his plate. Always in the end, his was the last word, and so it continued in this vein.*

Yamuna encountered this particular challenge often in her cooking for Srila Prabhupada over the years, as did his other cooks. Sometimes he would ask that a particular food not be included on his plate, but when the plate was set before him, he would then ask them to bring it.

**Yamuna**: *Another problem in Los Angeles was the accommodations. As more devotees came to have Srila Prabhupada’s association, we became spread out all over the place, often in the worst neighborhoods. Finally, Srila Prabhupada pointedly asked the devotees how long they expected him to stay there in these conditions, and this ultimately motivated them to find their first suitable temple.*

## Srila Prabhupada Plans for a “World Sankirtan Party”

Srila Prabhupada was always thinking of ways to spread Lord Chaitanya’s Sankirtan Movement throughout the world. An appearance on a radio program in Los Angeles inspired him to form a “World Sankirtan Party.” This was not to be an eclectic collection of volunteers, but rather a party carefully conceived by Srila Prabhupada to have the maximum impact on the audiences. In a letter to Hansadutta on February 4,1968, he expressed his vision for the party:

**My idea is that at least one dozen persons should form a kirtan party. Two persons play mridangas, eight persons play kartals, one person playing tamboura, and one person playing melodious harmonium. The person who will play on tamboura will be lead singer. You have just calculated what I want, when you suggest that the leader should sing as I do, and the others will respond. That will be very nice. But all the members of the party will be pure devotees. None of them should be outsiders ... If all the members keep their faith in Krishna and try to please Him, certainly everyone will be pleased by hearing our kirtan. It is sure and certain. When such kirtan will be demonstrated, only the harmonium player may sit, and all the others may stand up and join the kirtan and dancing properly dressed.**

**— LETTER TO HANSADUTTA, FEB. 4, 1968**

Srila Prabhupada was openly enthusiastic about the program, and sent many letters to Hansadutta to encourage and motivate him. On February 17, he wrote:

**I am very happy to hear you are making nice arrangements for the kirtan party; I am anxious to see the idea take shape. Yes, the more you develop the attitude for service sincerely, the more opportunities Krishna will give you to serve Him, in so many varieties of ways. And I am so happy to hear that you are finding strength to be determined to spread Krishna Consciousness all over the world; my Guru Maharaja wanted like that, especially the Western world, and my only request is that all you sincere boys and girls ... spread this Krishna Consciousness to every home, to every village and town, and take this mission very seriously. Organization of the Kirtan Party for world tour should be given our first consideration.**

**— LETTER TO HANSADUTTA, FEB. 17, 1968**

**Prabhupada’s original idea was to import experienced musicians from India, but now he decides to combine the American and Indian kirtaniyas together for his World Sankirtan Party. He follows up with another letter explaining that Hansadutta will be successful if the kirtan party is successful. He stresses an important point: never develop a professional mood, just make the kirtan perfect from the point of view of Krishna Consciousness. He thanks Hansadutta for organizing the sankirtan party and booking engagements. As encouragement, Prabhupada explains that when he comes to New York, he will take the sankirtan party with him to the different cities he will visit in America. Then they will go to England, Holland, Germany, and finally Bombay. The World Sankirtan Party is constantly on Prabhupada’s mind.**

**— HARE KRISHNA EXPLOSION**

## Standing Erect on the Spiritual Platform—San Francisco

Srila Prabhupada returned to San Francisco on March 8. Yamuna had preceded him, and she and Guru das were still under the impression that they would be going to India soon. In a letter on January 17, 1968, Srila Prabhupada wrote:

**The plan of your husband and yourself, Yamuna, of going to India is approved by me. I am simply waiting for the place where you shall stay ... We shall require at least one dozen students to go to India and stay there at least for 6 months, and be completely trained up on our line of activities. The place which I am arranging by negotiation with authorities will be sufficient of accommodating at least 50 students and if Krishna gives us that place it will be a great success.**

**— LETTER TO YAMUNA, JAN. 17, 1968**

In another letter written on February 13 to Guru das, Srila Prabhupada quotes from Acyutananda in India:

**Yamuna and Guru das are welcomed and they may come soon so I must have your decision. So you can prepare yourself for going there and keeping correspondence with Acyutananda, so that as soon as the house is settled there you can go with a car.**
