**— LETTER TO GURU DAS, FEB. 13, 1968**

In the meantime, much had changed in the San Francisco devotee community in Srila Prabhupada’s absence. In January, tensions had become so extreme between the new manager, Gargamuni, and some of the devotees that Yamuna and Harsharani co-wrote a long letter to Srila Prabhupada outlining the problems they were causing. Specifically they were concerned that the loving family atmosphere so carefully developed and nurtured from the beginning would be obliterated through insensitivity in devotee dealings. Srila Prabhupada wrote back encouraging them to not become disturbed:

**Physically and mentally we may be disturbed sometimes, but we have to stand erect on the spiritual platform. I may inform you in connection that I am at the present moment physically unfit; I am having always a buzzing sound in my brain. I cannot sleep soundly at night, but still I am working because I try to be in my position of spiritual platform. I hope you shall try to understand me right, and do the needful.**

**— LETTER TO YAMUNA AND HARSHARANI, JAN. 15, 1968**

The devotees observed Gaura Purnima with Srila Prabhupada on March 14, and he spoke about the special mercy Lord Chaitanya gave by introducing the Hare Krishna mahamantra in this difficult and quarrelsome age of Kali Yuga. He also explained the significance of observing Ekadasi until moonrise on this day.

In the meantime, many speaking engagements, interviews and other programs had been arranged for Srila Prabhupada, and Yamuna used her calligraphy skills to create posters and invitations for them. Young spiritual seekers from communes such as the Morningstar Ranch were continuing to find their way to the Frederick Street temple and were becoming serious students. Morning and evening kirtans at the temple were always packed to overflowing. When Srila Prabhupada observed the level of commitment of the students and the exuberance of the kirtans, he was very pleased, and on March 17, he wrote to Hayagriva:

**So, here the temple has spiritually improved. Whenever there is kirtan, either morning or evening, immediately there is a different atmosphere by the Grace of Lord Krishna. And all people, both devotees and outsiders, begin to dance in ecstasy. I am very much encouraged by seeing the atmosphere from San Francisco temple, and when you come here you shall see personally how they are nicely executing Krishna Consciousness. I have some lectures in the colleges, both in Los Angeles and San Francisco, and the other day I delivered a lecture in San Francisco State College, and the students enjoyed the atmosphere very much.**

**— LETTER TO HAYAGRIVA, MAR. 17, 1968**

On March 24, two of the spiritual seekers from the Morningstar Ranch, Tamai Krishna and Vishnujana, both of whom would have a prominent role in the Sankirtan Movement, became initiated disciples of Srila Prabhupada. In a profound and moving initiation lecture, Srila Prabhupada cautioned all of the devotees, whether new initiates or already committed disciples:

**So these initiation formalities are there. You are instructed, you are guided, but you have to act. Unless you act, then the same thing as in India—the so-called brahmanas and ksatriyas are degraded. There will be no meaning. You have to stick to the brahminical qualities, and at the same time, work, brahma-karma ... So you have to engage yourself; brahmakarma means Krishna Consciousness, and exhibit your quality—that you are truthful, you are controlling over the senses, control over the mind, and you are simple and you are tolerant. Because as soon as you take up spiritual life, the whole class conducted by maya, they will be against you. That is maya’s influence.**

**— LECTURE, MAR. 24, I968**

Yamuna had her recorder with her whenever she entered Srila Prabhupada’s presence, and she determined to record virtually anything he said. She always remembered and sometimes quoted from the above lecture, especially about maya’s influence. She also noted that the tenor of Srila Prabhupada’s preaching was changing. Before, while he preached the philosophy, he encased it in layers of humor, tolerance and sweetness—allowing the devotees to take the sometimes difficult-to-swallow medicine of the philosophy with a smattering of honey. Now she noticed he was more direct, more grave and more pointed in his preaching, revealing more and more of the fundamental philosophy, practice and etiquette of Krishna bhakti to them—in this case, the true position and purpose of initiation.

**Yamuna realizes that everything Prabhupada says is extremely important, so she vigilantly records every talk he gives... She and Gargamuni arrange to record him singing Vande ham and the prayers from Brahma Samhita.**

**— RADHA DAMODAR VILASA**

Yamuna noted that as he gently played the kartals during the recording of the verses from the Fifth Chapter of the Brahma Samhita, he displayed a mood of ecstasy as he chanted, and this can be heard clearly on the recording. This particular recording of Vande ham always remained very dear to Yamuna, as Srila Prabhupada can be heard, voice breaking, as he becomes ever more deeply absorbed in the prayers.

Srila Prabhupada continued his program of morning walks, and Yamuna took every opportunity to join them. She would often greet him outside his Willard Street apartment and garland him with a lovely garland, usually made from the abundant rhododendrons surrounding the park. And then their small group would walk briskly beside Srila Prabhupada. In this intimate setting, interspersed with chanting japa, he would expand on his plans for a World Sankirtan Party as well as his plan to take them to India. Yamuna cherished these walks, and later, whenever Srila Prabhupada brought up his fondness for these early years in San Francisco, he mentioned the walks in Golden Gate Park.

**Yamuna**: *In the early San Francisco period, Srila Prabhupada allowed us to spend time with him all day and into the night, but morning walks were one of the most relishable, glorious times with him. I generally wanted to be on the morning walk. One of the other devotees and I used to get up at two in the morning, pick flowers in Golden Gate Park, make garlands for Srila Prabhupada, present them to him, and go on the morning walk. Those moments in the park were always very special for us, walking next to our Spiritual Master and trying to chant Hare Krishna just as he chanted Hare Krishna. He walked like a young man of twenty-five. The first day I went, I was wearing wooden yogi shoes, and my feet bled because Srila Prabhupada was walking so fast.*

Srila Prabhupada left San Francisco for New York on April 17,1968. He then planned to go on to Montreal. Previously he had entrusted Hansadutta with establishing the World Sankirtan Party, but he was eventually unsuccessful, so Srila Prabhupada gave the task to Mukunda. He and Janaki were still in Los Angeles at this time, but they began preparing to move back to San Francisco to take up this service.

**Yamuna**: *On a personal level, there have been serious challenges for my sister, Janaki. After moving to Los Angeles with Mukunda, she suffered a miscarriage in early July. Calling me in San Francisco, she simply said, “I’ve lost the child” and hung up. I decided a major change was needed, and called Aunt Edna to reserve her cabin. Then Janaki, Harsharani and I went to Klamath Falls for a week. When we arrived, Harsharani said, “Okay, so what do you want to do here, Janaki?” Janaki explained that she already had two plans in mind to deal with her grief. One was to have morning and evening kirtans with us, something she said she had missed terribly since leaving San Francisco; and the other was to read together from a book she and Mukunda started reading in Los Angeles. It was called the Ramayana, and Srila Prabhupada read from it on Lord Ramachandra’s Appearance Day the previous year. I remembered it well. It’s a thick book that you can read from anywhere and immediately become riveted by it. Epic characters jump off the pages. Compelling twists and plot turns—about love, hate, war, justice, good, evil—it’s got it all. And especially it defines spiritual ethics through a magical narrative about the life of Lord Ramachandra. Janaki told us that she and Mukunda had been reading it during her pregnancy. Then she became emotional. But the Ramayana had the desired effect on all of us. The next six days passed by quickly, each day better than the one before. We read the Ramayana for six hours every day—sometimes more. Janaki was right; it’s a spectacular story, the kind of page-turner you want to read again and again*

Yamuna reminded Janaki about a letter Srila Prabhupada had sent to her and Mukunda on February 28, 1968, after an earlier miscarriage. In it he explained philosophically why a soul sometimes leaves a womb before birth, and how chanting and readings such as the Ramayana eternally benefit the child.

**So far the spirit soul is concerned, if conditions are for some reason not favorable in some place, he is forced to leave that womb and take shelter in another. And if there is chanting of Hare Krishna, even the soul is there for a short time, oh, he will hear and become advanced. This sound vibration is not material; it is spiritual, and powerful beyond our conception. So it cannot be hindered in any way by something material; it surpasses all these material barriers. So you can know that when you are chanting.**

**— LETTER TO MUKUNDA AND JANAKI, FEB. 28, 1968**

## San Francisco's Second Rathayatra —1968

The devotees in San Francisco were determined to make the second Rathayatra an extravaganza such that San Francisco had never before seen. Jayananda and Shyamasundara had been working diligently on new designs for the Rathayatra cart and had submitted them to Srila Prabhupada for his approval. Everyone was joyfully engaged in the many services required to create the glorious festival they all envisioned. Yamuna calligraphed invitations which were freely distributed everywhere, and posters wer placed on poles and in storefronts. Srila Prabhupada wrote to Yamuna from Montreal on June 8:

**Please decorate Jagannatha with very attractive nice clothing and ornaments, helmets, as brightly and magnificently as possible. The sample of decorating Jagannatha is already instructed to Harsharani, and in that way you can make arrangements. There shall be sufficient flower garlands for them daily also. The decoration should be so attractive that people when seeing Jagannatha will forget attractiveness of maya. Then it will be successful, and actually, this is the process of decorating Jagannatha. Our eyes are attracted by the beauty of maya, but if our eyes are attracted by the beauty of Krishna, Jagannatha, then there is no more chance of our being attracted by maya. In other words, when seeing Jagannatha nicely decorated, we become freed from the clutches of maya.**

**— LETTER TO YAMUNA, JUNE 8, 1967**

**Yamuna**: *The cart was built right behind the temple. It was unlike any Rathayatra cart that’s ever been built since. It was very, very large, square in nature, and it had beautiful circular cupolas that hung off the edge of it, which were upholstered in a wonderful yellow-golden satin, with red satin tassels on them. It was a very opulent cart, not high and tall like the classic Rathayatra cart, but Prabhupada had asked us to not only dress the Deities opulently, but also to make a very elaborate and beautiful cart so that people would be attracted to coming and seeing the Lord. So Jagannatha, Subhadra and Balarama were in red satin, looking very beautiful, and we even managed to get some wonderful garlands of fragrant flowers for Their red turbans.*

*So thousands of people followed the carts to the ocean, and it was a very memorable experience. We all felt the blessings of the Lord on this day. For me, one very exciting thing about this Rathayatra festival was the prayer, ‘'Gauranga bolite habe, pulaka-sarira.” This bhajan was for me the theme of that Rathayatra. When there wasn’t a kirtan going on, Srila Prabhupada singing this bhajan was played over a little megaphone system on the cart. Although I didn’t stay at the beach long, at the end of the procession, when the cart was at the beach, the devotees said that this bhajan of Srila Prabhupada’s played for hours on end. I remember that just during the short time I was at the beach, when the wind would move back and forth, it would catch the sound of this magnificent prayer. And in my mind it s always been the theme of our 1968 Rathayatra festival, the prayer of Lord Chaitanya’s longing for Krishna, and Srila Prabhupada singing it in that wonderful deep and rich melody.*

When Yamuna had a heart attack a month before she passed away, she asked me to come with her into the temple room, and holding a picture of Srila Prabhupada near her heart, she began to slowly and melodiously chant this prayer in a semi-conscious state. She chanted the whole prayer, line by line, very feelingly. I was surprised because this was not a prayer we often chanted in our ashram. But somehow she was drawn to another place, another time—a time where she was able to call on this prayer of longing for Lord Chaitanya’s mercy. I did not know the story of the 1968 Rathayatra before researching this book project, and when I heard about Srila Prabhupada’s chanting this bhajan on the cart, it all became clear. Yamuna very much appreciated being at the ocean, and somehow, in that critical moment, everything came together for her in that one prayer of deep longing. This was, simply put, the essence of Yamuna’s dedication to Krishna bhakti. The translation of this glorious prayer of longing by Narottama das Thakur is:

- 1\. When will that opportune moment come to me when there will be shivering of the body as soon as I chant Lord Gauranga’s name? And after the shivering, while chanting Hare Krishna, when will there be tears pouring down from my eyes?
- 2\. When will that day come when Lord Nityananda’s causeless mercy is bestowed upon me so that my desire for material enjoyment becomes very insignificant?
- 3\. When my mind is completely purified, being freed from material anxieties and desires, then I shall be able to understand Vrindavan and the conjugal love of Radha and Krishna, and then my spiritual life will be successful.
- 4\. When shall I be very much eager to study the books left by the Six Goswamis? One has to learn of the conjugal loving affairs of Radha-Krishna through the teachings of these Six Goswamis.
- 5\. Narottama das always wishes to understand this conjugal love under the direction of the Six Goswamis.

**Yamuna**: *I remember that when we were at an ocean kirtan one night, months before, at the very end of the prayers, Srila Prabhupada said, “All glories to the Pacific Ocean,” and we said, “Hare Krishna.” He then said again, “All glories to the Pacific Ocean,” and we replied, “Hare Krishna.” “All glories to the Pacific Ocean.” And he had his hands raised and was facing the ocean. I think it was the only time that I can remember Srila Prabhupada adding something other than our classic prayers at the end of a kirtan, but it moved us all. We were thinking how liberal he was that he was appreciating the majesty of the place we were.*

Many devotees wrote to Srila Prabhupada about the wonderful Rathayatra festival and how many souls were touched by the elaborate arrangements, kirtans and wonderful prasadam. In a reply to Upendra on July 4, Srila Prabhupada wrote of his appreciation for their service:

**And your vivid description of the prearrangement of Rathayatra ceremony was so nice and elaborate that it has moved my heart. I thank you very much for grasping the momentum of Krishna Consciousness by your advanced service attitude. I can only wish that Krishna may give you more and more strength in understanding His transcendental nature. The only process for perceiving Krishna and His name, qualities and form is our sincere service attitude with our senses. Beginning from the tongue, all our senses are practically led by the tongue sense, whose business is to vibrate and to taste. If we can change the materialistic nature of the tongue, by changing of taste and vibration, then automatically the other senses become purified. And we can render service to Krishna with purified senses. As such we should try to chant and eat Krishna prasadam as much as possible.**

**In the meantime, Gargamuni has come here and I have heard from him the details of your procession and it is so much englad-dening to my heart. I thank you all very much for making the Rathayatra festival so successful. Please convey my gratitude to all the boys and girls who participated in this great transcendental service. This is the second year, and you have made a great stride from the first year, and in the third year, I hope it will be still more successful.**

**— LETTER TO UPENDRA, JULY 4, 1968**

Srila Prabhupada wrote a letter on July 16 thanking Yamuna for her appreciation of the Rathayatra festival:

**I thank you very much for your letter dated July 9,1968, giving a vivid description of the Rathayatra festival ... Your appreciation of the Rathayatra festival and realizing the beauty of Kirtan and Jagannatha, as well as the magnanimity of Lord Chaitanya in His sublime teachings, are some of the wonderful things that I mark in your progressive advancement in Krishna Consciousness. Please try to continue this attitude and you will be more and more happy in your life, and at the end get entrance into the association of Krishna.**

**— LETTER TO YAMUNA, JULY l6, 1968**

## Harinam Sankirtan Becomes a San Francisco Fixture

Srila Prabhupada was so encouraged by the enthusiasm of the devotees for chanting that he requested them to go out every day on harinam sankirtan. Tamai Krishna was a good organizer and Vishnujana was a charismatic leader with a strong, melodious voice and phenomenal endurance. Together they organized the harinams, and they were an immediate success. Srila Prabhupada had already appreciated Yamuna’s beautiful and powerful voice for kirtans, and even in those early days would often ask her to lead. So she was a natural choice for the early harinam programs.

**Mukunda leaves Los Angeles to take charge of developing the World Sankirtan Party from San Francisco. Every day he goes out chanting with the brahmacharis. Because he is the senior devotee, they always ask him to lead. Vishnujana wants to pick up some authentic beats that Mukunda has learned from Srila Prabhupada, so he is especially keen to hear him chant and play mridanga. But the energy of the kirtan is always a balance, so Vishnujana and Yamuna also regularly lead kirtan. Everybody feels very connected and excited about being part of Prabhupada’s personal sankirtan party.**

**— RADHA DAMODAR VILASA**

**Yamuna**: *Perhaps one of the reasons Srila Prabhupada engaged me in leading kirtans was because when we were traveling, we didn’t have loud sound systems. And even early in San Francisco, for some reason, he started having me lead kirtans. It was not a natural position for me, but I was honored when Srila Prabhupada asked any service of me.*

**The devotees in San Francisco have been chanting from time to time in Haight-Ashbury and Golden Gate Park, but not as a regular activity. They accept Prabhupada’s new instruction with full faith. This is the impetus that inspires them to go out on sankirtan in an organized fashion for the first time. Mukunda played the mridanga, Vishnujana strummed a large tamboura, and Muralidhara, Yamuna and I all played kartals. We began by chanting the prayers to Srila Prabhupada, then the Pancha Tattva mantra to Lord Chaitanya and His associates, and finally Hare Krishna, all the while swaying to and fro, just as we did in the temple.**

**— SERVANT OF THE SERVANT**

**Yamuna**: *One of our regular chanting venues became the Fisherman’s Wharf area. We all took turns leading the kirtans. There’s a picture of Vishnujana, Tamai Krishna and me during our first kirtan together at Fisherman’s Wharf. Vishnujana and I often used to lead kirtans, but in those days we didn’t have kirtan luminaries. It was a sharing experience; whoever wanted to lead took the microphone. All of us ultimately led, but I remember Vishnujana’s kirtans were amazing for his stamina. We chanted together for several months, and in reflecting back, I am drawn to remembering his stamina. He had an almost pied-piper-like charisma, and that combined with the voice, drumming and stamina created a perfect storm of attraction for others to the chanting experience.*

## The World Sankirtan Party Shifts to London

By now Srila Prabhupada had progressed through several incarnations of the World Sankirtan Party idea. In letter after letter and in multiple exchanges with different devotees, he sketched out his vision for a party of devotees he would personally take around the world, spreading the chanting of the Holy Names. Even though challenges prevented its manifestation thus far, his basic concept and his enthusiasm for it had not abated. He discussed with Mukunda the same strategies for creating the party he had previously developed with Hansadutta.

Now, another change was to take place. Shyamasundara had been encouraging Srila Prabhupada about the potential for preaching in London. As London had at one time been described by his Spiritual Master, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur, as “the most important city in the world,” and as he had started the preaching mission of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu in the West by sending disciples there in 1933, it naturally held a special appeal for Srila Prabhupada. He would start the World Sankirtan Party, but first he would send a core group of sankirtan party devotees to London to see if they could establish a preaching center there. If that was successful, they could then travel around the world. In a letter written on June it to Mukunda, Srila Prabhupada encouraged him in this plan:

**Your presence in the London center with other assistants will be greatly helpful, considering the fact that I wish to form a nice kirtan party consisting of 12 heads—2 mridanga players, I harmonium player in melody, I tamboura player, and at least 6 cymbal players. In this way 12 heads shall perform kirtan very rhythmically and melodiously. The harmonium should be practiced just to follow the song, not simply for tuning. I think you can very well organize this sankirtan party, and if we have a successful sankirtan party, with me, backed by our books and literature, we can make a nice propaganda of this sublime movement in all the European cities. And if we are successful in Europe, then we may go to other countries also in Asia. In India also if we go with this sankirtan party we shall be very much welcome, and there is great possibility of cooperation of the richer section of India. So I am thinking of organizing this nice sankirtan party very seriously, and you may also think in that way.**

**— LETTER TO MUKUNDA, JUNE II, I968**

Srila Prabhupada’s enthusiasm is so palpable in this letter that Yamuna and the other devotees who would initially travel to London were ecstatic. It is clear from all of Srila Prabhupada’s letters on the subject that what he envisioned was not a hodgepodge of chanters, but rather a sophisticated, well-trained cadre of musically sound devotees who would attract others to Krishna bhakti by presenting harinam sankirtan in its most attractive and pleasing manner. All of the six devotees who would go to open the center were thrilled at the challenge, at the prospect of pleasing Srila Prabhupada, and the prospect of igniting England with the fire of the Holy Names, even heavily-pregnant Malati, who would be taking a newborn infant with her to England. Srila Prabhupada wrote to Yamuna during this time assuring her that their endeavors would be a grand success.

At the beginning of August, the three couples—Mukunda and Janaki, Yamuna and Guru das, and Shyamasundara and Malati (with baby Saraswati)—went to Montreal to meet Srila Prabhupada before their London sojourn. In Montreal, Srila Prabhupada would train them in every intricacy of chanting Krishna kirtan and presenting it to others. The World Sankirtan Party was now going out into the world.

Specific memories of devotees who served with Yamuna devi during her San Francisco years will be ' included on the companion website to this book: www. unalloyed.org, but perhaps her contribution to others can be summarized most eloquently in the memories of one young devotee in San Francisco in 1968:

**Tosan Krishna das:** *When one is on the bhakti marg everything is personal. Yamuna devi’s abundantly nutritious persona was the direct catalyst making the crucial difference between myself merely looking at the honey inside the jar and my deliberate decision to dive in it.*

*By way of my attendance of a Srimad-Bhagavatam class she gave one morning in the summer of 1968 at the Fredrick Street temple in San Francisco (my first visitor’s experience of a temple morning program), 1, a 17-year-old agnostic, was delightfully treated to the warm realization that Krishna Consciousness was not only a very good concept but was, in fact, a wealth of wholesome food-for-the-soul that you could practically experience, relish and be fortified with. She was the unpretentious personification of this with both heart and mind.*

*As an existential sojourner, I was weary of 6o’s faux counter-cultural promises. Yamuna was a breath of rich nourishing reality. She was the un-hippy, the real deal, hard-core with a soft inner-core. She delivered. I wanted what she was dishing out—shabda brahma, transcendental sound spoken with piercing intelligence, deep love and a beguiling, sparkling, playful smile—transferred from one soul to the next. Simply put, Yamuna was the key impetus for my deciding to move into the temple and then take initiation from Srila Prabhupada. She placed the kanti mala around my neck. Profoundly understood—she saved my life.*

Years later, Yamuna reflected on her transition from tentative to committed devotee. For her, the living example of Srila Prabhupada was core to that change. Her hearing from the scriptures about the qualities and character of a pure devotee, and seeing in Srila Prabhupada the living example of those qualities, gradually cemented her dedication and commitment to the process of Krishna bhakti.

**Yamuna**: *When I reflect back on the months we spent with Swamiji in San Francisco, I see it as a process of discovery. There would be times where I couldn’t understand or grasp what he was saying perhaps in a lecture, but then I would hear something that made so much sense, and was so relevant and important in my life, that I would grasp that little realization and embrace it, and think about it, and try to discuss it with others. And they came like that—little drops— because as soon as a lecture was over, then Swamiji became the emblem or the reservoir of all good qualities; he became the human representative of the personalities we were studying about in the books. So of course, things like kindness and forgiveness and magnanimity—all those things that we associate with a saintly soul—they came out. One was his humor; he was so humorous and very jolly—prasanatma. So he would give a very lofty discourse, and then afterwards become so human and such an example of what he spoke of that naturally we were pulled along. No matter how dull you were, or how covered you were by some kind of conditioning, he would pull you on to another stage of Krishna Conscious understanding. So it was a day-by-day process of revelation, which over time made me realize that I did want to become a devotee. Some devotees just decided, “Oh, I’m going to do it” right away. They would say, “When I met him I knew that here is my guru and I want to do this.” But for me it took some time, and it was revealed through the personality and behavior of Srila Prabhupada*

## Chapter 4

**Immersion in the Ocean of Mercy (Montreal 1968)**

## A Flood of Transcendental Ecstasy

THE SAN FRANCISCO contingent of the World Sankirtan Party, consisting of Yamuna and Guru das, Shyamasundara and Malati (with their three-week-old daughter, Saraswati) and Mukunda and Janaki, arrived in Montreal on August io, 1968, for further training with Srila Prabhupada before traveling on to London. Although Srila Prabhupada often expressed over the years the magnitude of what establishing a temple in London meant to him—how his Spiritual Master, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati, had desired a permanent temple there, and how Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur had foreseen it—the opportunity to now fulfill that desire of Saraswati Thakur with his sincere yet neophyte disciples must have given him great happiness.

**Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur desired that Sri Chaitanya Maha-prabhu’s message be accepted by East and West equally and that the Indians, Europeans and Americans should dance together in the ecstasy of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu’s mercy. Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur simply expressed the desire, “When shall I see this happening, that the Eastern and Western people are united on the basis of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu’s cult and dancing together in ecstasy?” That was the ambition of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and the ambition of Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur. And Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur took up this affair.**

**— LECTURE, DEC. 13, 1973**

During his tumultuous journey from India on the \]aladuta, Srila Prabhupada expressed in a heartfelt prayer his certainty that the mission of spreading Krishna Consciousness in the Western countries would succeed because it was the desire of his Guru Maharaja, a great saintly personality who was “unparalleled” in his service to Krishna.

**Sri Srimad Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati, who is very dear to Lord Gauranga, the son of Mother Saci, is unparalleled in his service to the Supreme Lord Sri Krishna. He is that great saintly Spiritual Master who bestows intense devotion to Krishna at different places throughout the world. By his strong desire, the Holy Name of Lord Gauranga will spread throughout all the countries of the Western world. In all the cities, towns and villages on the earth, from all the oceans, seas, rivers and streams, everyone will chant the Holy Name of Krishna. As the vast mercy of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu conquers all directions, a flood of transcendental ecstasy will certainly cover the land....**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA ON THE JALADUTA**

So again, as had previously occurred in New York and San Francisco, what Yamuna referred to as the “Krishna Magic” portal opened in London. By the mercy of Srila Prabhupada and Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, the sankirtan party would arrive at the most opportune time for flooding the country with the nectar of the Holy Names. Shyamasundara had enthused Srila Prabhupada by telling him of the Beatles and their extraordinary popularity, as well as their interest in Eastern culture and mysticism. They would go to London, somehow make a connection with the Beatles, and in this way, the Holy Names would be spread with lightning speed. Looking back in retrospect, it seemed an impossible dream, but as Srila Prabhupada wrote on the \]aladuta, by the mercy of Guru and Gauranga, success would be assured.

Now that the manifest desires of his Guru Maharaja and Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur were gradually becoming realized, Srila Prabhupada wanted to be certain that those devotees carrying the message of Guru and Gauranga to London and Europe were properly equipped to promulgate Krishna Consciousness through sankirtan and preaching. In Montreal, he began a program of daily kirtan practice, and would also periodically ask each of them to speak on the philosophy of Krishna Consciousness. He would then correct them when necessary, whether in their Sanskrit or Bengali pronunciation or their philosophical understanding.

**Prabhupada asked the three couples to remain with him in Montreal for a week or two, so that he could train them to perform kirtan expertly. Chanting Hare Krishna was not a theatrical performance but an act of devotion, properly conducted only by pure devotees—not by professional musicians. Yet if Prabhupada’s disciples became proficient in their singing, Londoners would better appreciate Krishna Consciousness. The thought of these devotees preaching in England made Prabhupada ecstatic.**

**In the daily kirtan rehearsals, Prabhupada taught the devotees to chant Hare Krishna and other devotional songs, beginning with a slow tempo and building gradually. He would regularly interrupt and have them begin again. Listening carefully as Yamuna led the chanting, Prabhupada would stop her at times to correct her Sanskrit pronunciation.**

**— SRILA PRАВHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

**Yamuna**: *The nine days our London party spent with Prabhupada in Montreal were a turning point in our spiritual lives. We spent our first Janmastami and Vyasa Puja in his presence. We received Gayatri mantra. He trained us in kirtan and gave us unlimited blessings. In the morning Srila Prabhupada had us come into the temple room around 9:00 am, and we would sing the Gurvastakam and Mangalacaranam (Vande ham) prayers. He often asked me to lead, and would stop me to correct my pronunciation: “No, it is this way.” He hadn’t done that before. He also taught us what he called the afternoon melody for Gurvastakam. So we now had the morning and the afternoon melodies, and he was rather keen on us following either of those melodies at the proper time.*

Anyone who chanted with Yamuna from that time on would have known that the propriety of the morning or evening melody of the Gurvastakam prayers remained an important distinction to her; and on some occasions she would sweetly sing the afternoon melody to a chanter if they did not know it.

Srila Prabhupada also began training the devotees in chanting the Brahma Samhita (Govindam) prayers each day, having them repeat each line after him and correcting any mispronunciations. One day, he elaborated on the prayer, encouraging the devotees to express their feelings through the chanting:

**For offering prayers to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, you do not require any high qualification. It doesn’t matter. You can offer your prayer from any standard of life. Not that you have to become a very learned man, very scholarly man, and you have to present your prayers in very nicely selected words so that poetry, rhetoric, prosody, everything is there, metaphor. Nothing is required. Simply you have to express your feelings.**

**— LECTURE, AUG. l8, 1968**

Prabhupada predicted that when the devotees chanted Hare Krishna, the people of London would hear the mantra, become devotees, and then enlighten others. Krishna Consciousness would grow. The only requirement was that the chanting be done purely, without any material motivation. Prabhupada’s enthusiasm was contagious, and as he spoke he filled his disciples with the same contagious enthusiasm.

**When Mukunda asked Prabhupada if he had any specific instructions, Prabhupada replied with a story. In his youth, he had once seen a movie of Charlie Chaplin. The setting was a formal ball held outdoors, and off from the main dance arena were lanes with benches where couples sat. Some mischievous boys had plastered glue on one of the benches, and a young man and his girlfriend came and sat down. “When the young man got up” (Prabhupada laughed as he told the story) “his tails tore up the middle.” Prabhupada told how the couple had returned to the dance, unaware of what had happened. But now they drew stares from the other dancers. Wondering why he was suddenly attracting so much attention, the young man went into the dressing room and saw in the mirror his ripped coattails. Deliberately, he then tore his coat all the way up to the collar, returned to his partner and began dancing exuberantly. Then another man joined, ripping his own coattails and dancing with his partner, as if to compete with the first couple. One by one, the other dancers followed, ripping their coattails and dancing with abandon. By the conclusion of the story, the devotees in Prabhupada’s room were all laughing uproariously. But finally their laughter subsided and the meeting ended. Not until the devotees were already at the airport did Mukunda, talking with Shyamasundara, begin to appreciate and marvel at how expertly Prabhupada had answered his question. By their bold, enthusiastic, confident preaching, they would attract people. Not everyone would immediately “join in the dancing,” as had the people in the Charlie Chaplin film; the devotees might even be considered crazy at first. But they would be offering Krishna Consciousness, the highest and rarest gift, and intelligent people would gradually appreciate this, even if at first they scoffed. By Srila Prabhupada’s order, his London-bound disciples, holding kirtan in public, would present a profile quite different from the reserved profile of his sannyasi Godbrothers. His Godbrothers had imitated the British ways; but Prabhupada wanted the British to imitate the Vaishnavas. To appear in the streets of London with shaven heads and dhotis would require boldness. But it would be exciting to chant, carrying out the order of Lord Chaitanya. And the people would follow—gradually, but definitely. It was the will of Lord Chaitanya.**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

In fact, this point was beautifully elucidated in a letter written by Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati to the devotees he sent to London in 1934:

**If you establish centers in villages in England, with deities of Jagannatha and Sriman Mahaprabhu, and offer Indian-style preparations and distribute maha prasadam, then the English will gradually develop a sympathy for and faith in Indians and then be inclined to further the Lord’s service. Oh, for the day when the people of that country will sing the names of Gaura and, with a spiritual attitude, honor transcendental prasadam from the temple. Then they will understand true spiritual life and cultivate Krishna Consciousness.**

**— May 29, 1934**

For all of the devotees, the Montreal interlude was a life-changing experience. Not only were they consistently encouraged and trained in kirtan and preaching by Srila Prabhupada, but they accepted brahmana initiation as well. When Yamuna, Malati and Janaki were given the Gayatri mantra by Srila Prabhupada, they could not have imagined what an extraordinary and controversial act of love and mercy this was. They did not know that this was the first time Gayatri had been awarded to women in the line of his Guru Maharaja. It showed an undisguised respect and honor for the dedication of the women of his growing movement, and would remain a sticking point among many of his Godbrothers to the very end. In a lecture given at the initiation, Srila Prabhupada beautifully spoke about the blessings given to those who preach Krishna Consciousness:

**Just try to spread this message of Krishna Consciousness. It is very easy and very fast. Everyone can accept. So on this occasion, when you have come here from San Francisco prepared to go to London, so my hearty welcome to you, and please do this missionary work very nicely and Krishna will be pleased upon you. It is said in the Bhagavad-gita that anyone who is trying to spread this Krishna Consciousness Movement is the most dear friend of Krishna. If you want to please Krishna, Krishna says that “Anyone who is trying to spread this Krishna Consciousness Movement, he is My most dear friend”... So you are all pledged to satisfy Krishna. So if you take up this work seriously, Krishna will be very much pleased upon you. Thank you very much.**

**So the idea is that whatever I have brought \[through this\] Krishna Consciousness message to your country, that is due to the grace of His Divine Grace, my Spiritual Master, who is sitting here. And I am very glad that you have come here from San Francisco for going to London mission. And in auspicious moment you have come there was going to be... initiation ceremony. So all auspicious symptoms, and let us be situated firmly in Krishna Consciousness and act this missionary work, spreading Krishna Consciousness all over the world. That will make our life successful, and those who will take up this line of activities, they will also be very happy.**

**And when the Gayatri mantra is offered \[to\] men, they are also offered sacred thread, and girls, they are not offered sacred thread. If their husband is a brahmana, she automatically becomes brahmana because wife is considered to be the better half. She is the better portion. So she automatically becomes a better brahmana. So better brahmana does not require any thread. There is a Bengali proverb. The proverb is that in India if one has got a sacred thread, \[it\] is immediately understood that he must be belonging to the higher caste, brahmana, ksatriya or vaisya. But if somebody knows that he is brahmana or ksatriya, he doesn’t require to show the sacred thread. Similarly, the wife of a brahmana is already known \[as a\] brahmana, so she does not require to show the sacred thread. So don’t be sorry because you will not be offered the sacred thread. That’s all right.**

**— LECTURE, AUG. 11, 1968**

## The Real Meaning of Sankirtan

**Yamuna**: *Also at this time, Srila Prabhupada would speak about the glories of preaching to the people at large. And I remember one time there was a question and answer period, and one devotee asked Srila Prabhupada what sankirtan was. And Srila Prabhupada replied that sankirtan is the process of going to a place, sitting down, chanting the Holy Names, and attracting others to come and chant the Holy Names. Then when the others were practiced in chanting the Holy Names enough to go out on their own, you move on to another place and chant the Holy Names. He said that this was the definition of Lord Chaitanya’s sankirtan movement. Going, chanting Hare Krishna, attracting others, training them up and then moving on to another place. Srila Prabhupada said, “I am just like a cow. I will take grass in any pasture.” Srila Prabhupada graced the six of us grihasthas and the small baby Saraswati with so much of his personal association in the afternoon hours at his small cottage—all for the purpose of encouraging us in our service. He would hold baby Saraswati on his lap and just pour so much affection onto this small child. I remember him looking up, smiling and saying, “A sannyasi should not do this.” Yet he was seeing how enlivening it was for the other devotees to see him treat her with so much affection and love. He embodied in his every interaction what personalism means in devotional relationships.*

One day Yamuna went on a preaching engagement with Srila Prabhupada. Their audience was comprised of young schoolchildren. After his lecture, she asked if she could say something before the chanting began, and Srila Prabhupada, pleased that his disciple was stepping forward to encourage others in the chanting, agreed:

**Yamuna**: *I want everybody to listen very carefully. This is a new song that it would be very nice if you could learn how to sing, and learn how to sing very well. And the only way you can do this is by listening very carefully, everybody, so please give your attention to these words: Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna, Hare Hare, Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare. Now, if everybody will do this—stand up, close your eyes very tightly, put your hands up in the air and sing this song so you really learn the words—and then you can go home and teach it to your brothers and sisters and your mother and your father, and tell them what you learned today. You have to say you learned something. So if you teach them this song, that would be very nice. But you must learn it by listening. So listen to the words. Then get up, close your eyes and just sing. And you’ll find it’s a very nice song. But unless you try it, you won’t learn it. just like all the other songs you learn in your class. So try it. So I’m going to say the words, and then you say the words after me. We’re going to practice it once. Okay, (with children repeating) Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna, Hare Hare, Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare. Okay. Now we’re going to clap our hands too*

This was quintessentially Yamuna. She was always enthusiastic to encourage young people to chant, and was very physically engaging with them. This was a tool she often used in her preaching programs. She would speak and then ask the audience to repeat after her. I have seen so many indomitable or indifferent young souls charmed within minutes—becoming almost mystically compelled to chant or dance or simply shout out “Hare Krishna!” with loud enthusiasm—simply by the dynamic power of her presence.

## Janmastami and Vyasa Puja with Srila Prabhupada

A highlight for all of the London-bound devotees in Montreal was the opportunity to spend Janmastami and Vyasa Puja with Srila Prabhupada. For Yamuna especially, watching him in the tiny temple kitchen as he cooked special dishes that were his Spiritual Master’s favorites were treasured moments. She carefully wrote each recipe down in her ever-present notebook, waiting for the opportunity to make it herself for his pleasure. On Janmastami, all of the women cooked special preparations, and many more were brought by the guests.

**Yamuna**: *The occasions of Janmastami and Vyasa Puja were very joyous. Janmastami fell on August 16,1968, and Vyasa Puja combined the celebration of Srila Prabhupada’s Appearance Day with Nandotsava. His Divine Grace supervised several cooking preparations for these festivities. He made a preparation for the pleasure of his own Spiritual Master on Vyasa Puja consisting of a variety of urad badas. Using urad dal, a little hing, black pepper and salt, the preparation is made by soaking the dal and grinding it into a light batter, then deep-frying balls of it in clarified butter. The devotees had bought cultured sour cream instead of yogurt, so rather than floating the badas in the traditional lightly-churned yogurt, they were floated in this churned sour cream. I remember it as being a spectacular hit at the feast. Srila Prabhupada also instructed us how to make pantoa, which is a Bengali sweet made traditionally with fresh panir cheese and fresh khoa, a solid, condensed dried milk. Srila Prabhupada, however, made the preparation out of powdered milk and fresh cheese. Then they were deep-fried in clarified butter and soaked in thick sugar syrup. They appeared very similar to the preparation of gulab jamuns. These were also a spectacular success at the feast.*

Again, it is interesting to note Yamuna’s total recall of preparations made by Srila Prabhupada in 1968. Each Appearance or Disappearance Day of Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur, regardless of where we were in the world, she would make this urad dal bada dish. Even though urad dal is an acquired taste for the Western palate, when the badas are prepared in this way, as Srila Prabhupada prepared them in Montreal, they are sublime.

**Yamuna**: *A substantial showing of the Indian community appeared for the Janmastami program, which lasted many hours, and one by one, beginning with the senior male members, then the senior female members, and then the newer brahmacharis and brahmacharinis, each disciple spoke something about their appreciation for Krishna and their Spiritual Master. At the end of all the discourses, one young French-speaking brahmachari, just newly initiated, got up to speak something, and with a choked-up voice he made apologies that he wasn’t very experienced in this Krishna Conscious philosophy, but somehow or other he had been engaged in rolling chapatis in the kitchen. And day in and day out as he rolled the chapatis, he had been listening to lecture tapes of Srila Prabhupada. And with tears in his eyes, he said: “Please, just allow me the opportunity to eternally roll chapatis for my Spiritual Master and listen to these tapes.” And at this point Srila Prabhupada, with tears in his eyes, very feelingly said, “Thank you. Thank you very much.” Srila Prabhupada appreciated each and every devotee’s service, and each of us felt honored to be able to perform even the smallest of services for him.*

Yamuna realized that Srila Prabhupada’s spontaneous request to have each of the devotees speak on the philosophy of Krishna Consciousness was his way of preparing them to preach all over the world. It was unexpected, so each of them had to draw on their innate understanding. Yamuna spoke the following:

**Yamuna**: *I am offering my repeated, humble obeisances unto my spiritual preceptor, A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami. Please try to understand that everything we are learning here in Krishna Consciousness is received through the ears. And if one does not listen submissively, one cannot hear the transcendental message. This is the opening of the Srimad-Bhagavatam. It states that at the reading of the Srimad-Bhagavatam in the forest of Naimisaranya, many sages were present, and it was so quiet that the dropping of a pin could be heard on the sand. So the science of Krishna Consciousness must be received submissively. Our spiritual preceptor has brought Krishna Consciousness to the Western world in the hopes that the people here will sincerely take to this process of practicing bhakti-yoga, or the yoga of devotional service and love unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Sri Krishna. This is not a sect. This is for people of the world who understand one premise, that “I am not this body; I am pure spirit soul”; that this body is simply a dress, just like you wear clothes. But what is it that keeps you alive that is eternal? That is spirit soul. This is so simple that even a child at the age of five years can understand this. If it’s from a bona fide source, he can understand this. We are requesting that you please come to the practices of Bhagavata. Come to kirtan. By chanting Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna, Hare Hare, Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare, you at once are elevated onto the spiritual platform, and our contaminated material senses may become purified simply because of this association with the names of God. These names are absolute. They are not material. If you chant “water, water, water, water,” your thirst will not be quenched. But if you cry “Krishna, Krishna, Krishna,” you may find your position in this world—where you came from, why you are here, what you are doing, and where you are going. These questions man must answer, or he’s not making use of the ability of man. He’s simply living an animal life—eating, sleeping, mating, defending. It does not matter if you are a man, a woman or a child, or whether you are Indian or American. You simply must ask these questions. And when one comes upon a bona fide source, one must take advantage of that source and not pass it up. Krishna Consciousness, or the practice of the Srimad-Bhagavatam and the Srimad Bhagavad-gita, is open to all, and we invite you to please come. Chant Hare Krishna. Feel the sublime ecstasy. Thank you very much.*

This extemporaneous offering of Yamuna devi references some of the analogies that Srila Prabhupada often used in preaching Krishna Consciousness during those early years, yet she still manages to express her own intuitive realization of the philosophy in a personal and poignant way. Her attraction for chanting the Holy Names and for the Srimad-Bhagavatam is also very much evidenced in her offering. In a prayer remembering this day years later, she reflected:

**Yamuna**: *I remember the first time I was present when you requested your disciples to speak something of the philosophy of Krishna Consciousness on the occasion of Janmastami in Montreal in 1968. I was 26 years old, and had only been your initiated disciple for 16 months. Yet, even in that short period of time, I’d glimpsed something of your greatness and what a phenomenal gift you were giving us. I remember feeling numb and completely inadequate in attempting to speak. How could I express myself properly in front of you? You played so many roles in my life: Guru, guide, hero, wellwisher, best friend, sometime father, sometime son, and deepest object of love. When out of your presence, I spoke frequently and with some ease, but in front of you, in your presence, all I felt was tongue-tied.*

## Taking the Ultimate Blessing to London— Prabhupadas Lotus Feet

**Yamuna**: *For me the pinnacle of our Montreal time with Srila Prabhupada occurred during what was perhaps our last darshan with him before leaving for London. He was sending us out to fulfill his Spiritual Master’s dream of establishing the sankirtan movement in the great international metropolis of London. He was so openly enthusiastic about establishing a temple there that all of us became filled to overflowing by Srila Prabhupada’s enthusiasm. So one evening the six of us and baby Saraswati went to his room. He was in a jolly mood. He asked for baby Saraswati and played with her, saying, “If my Godbrothers saw this, they might criticize me.” Then he explained how much our going to London to start a temple there meant to him. He spoke about the grand send-off that his own Guru had given his disciples on their departure. He was filling us with inspiration and determination and hope so that we could start this temple. We really didn’t have a clue what it would entail.*

*Then Malati asked if we could touch his lotus feet. She said, “Srila Prabhupada, I don’t think we can go to London unless we have the shelter of your lotus feet.” How each one of us did this was different. Some touched with their head, some with their hands, but I kissed the bottom of his feet. I didn’t know any better. They were soft and pink, like pictures of the Vrindavan sky. I felt I had never experienced a touch so profound. It was such a joyous occasion. Within twenty-four hours we were at the New York temple preparing to fly to Amsterdam*

## The Vibration Conception Defined

An initiation was held one day in Montreal for a young girl, Rukmini. During the ceremony Srila Prabhupada asked Yamuna to chant Hare Krishna, and then he proceeded to chant the prayers to the Six Goswamis by himself. As he continued gently playing kartals, he began to speak:

**Today, a devotee is being initiated, so we are praying to the lotus feet of the Six Goswamis, who inaugurated this movement under the instruction of Lord Sri Chaitanya. Who are they? sri rupa-sanatanau raghu-yugau sri-jiva-gopalakau. Just try to chant these six names.**

**— LECTURE, AUG. 15, 1968**

Srila Prabhupada then began chanting and asked the devotees to repeat:

**Vande rupa-sanatanau raghu-yugau sri-jiva-gopalakau. There were two Raghunathas. One was Raghunatha Bhattacharya and one Raghunatha das. Two Raghunathas, and Rupa, Sanatana. Vande rupa-sanatanau raghu-yugau sri-jiva-gopalakau. So what was their business? Krsna kirtana-gana-nartana-parau: always engaged in chanting Hare Krishna. Krishna kirtan. Hare Krishna means Krishna kirtan. Krsna kirtana-gana-nartana-parau. Nartana means dancing. So chanting and dancing. That was their business. And Krishna kirtan, whenever one is merged in Krishna kirtan, that means he is merged into the ocean of love of Krishna. That should be the test. As soon as “Krishna,” this sound, is vibrated, one immediately becomes merged into the ocean of love. That is the sign of pure devotion. Immediately. So these Goswamis ... They merged immediately into the ocean of love of God.**

**— LECTURE, AUG. 15, 1968**

Then Srila Prabhupada again began to sing:

**Krsna kirtana-gana-nartana-parau premamratambho-nidhi ... And these Goswamis were dear both to the devotees and nondevotees. Not that they were simply liked by the devotees, but nondevotees also liked them. That was their position. A devotee’s position is that he has no enemy. Ajatashatru. Nirmatsara means because they are not envious. A devotee is always open to everyone. There is no question of discrimination, that “This person should be allowed to chant Hare Krishna and this person should not be allowed.” No ... And such a person can deliver the suffering humanity from this material contamination. Therefore we offer our respectful obeisances unto the Six Goswamis, Rupa, Sanatana, the two Raghunathas, Gopala Bhatta and Sri Jiva Goswami. Vande rupa-sanatanau raghu-yugau sri-jiva-gopalakau.**

**— LECTURE, AUG. 15, 1968**

The devotees then repeated this prayer several times with Srila Prabhupada.

Several days later, during a question and answer period, Srila Prabhupada elaborated on the power of kirtan, calling it the “vibration conception.” Rukmini said that when Srila Prabhupada was not there, she felt far away from him. Srila Prabhupada profoundly and movingly explained that if we give emphasis to the sound vibration of chanting, we will always feel the presence of Krishna and the Spiritual Master:

**There are two conceptions: the physical conception and the vibration conception. So the physical conception is temporary. The vibration conception is eternal. Just like we are enjoying or we are relishing the vibration of Krishna’s teachings. So by vibration He is present. As soon as we chant Hare Krishna or chant Bhagavad-gita or Bhagavata, so He is present immediately by His vibration. He is absolute. Therefore try to remember His words of instruction; you’ll not feel separation. You’ll feel that He is with you. So we should associate by the vibration, and not by the physical presence. That is real association—by sound. Just like we are touching Krishna immediately by sound, sound vibration. So we should give more stress on the sound vibration, either of Krishna or of the Spiritual Master. Then we’ll feel happy and no separation.**

**— LECTURE, AUG. l8, 1968**

In summing up the Montreal interlude, Yamuna wrote a short prayer to Srila Prabhupada. They were on their way to experiencing the great unknown in London, totally depending on the mercy of Guru and Krishna, yet there was no fear, no trepidation—only a desire to please, to serve, to make something wonderful happen: the Krishna Magic.

*I remember in Montreal, en route to London with five others, the wonder of our second initiation ceremony there, and our first Janmastami and Vyasa Puja in your presence. How you taught by example, by personally doing, not just saying. How you personally taught us how to make an urad bada dish much favored by your own Guru Maharaja; how you had us speak as you did in front of your own Guru Maharaja; how you taught us melodies for chanting prayers, and corrected our pronunciation of Sanskrit. In this connection, I pray to follow your example by always living in your preaching mood, doing everything in the spirit of trying to please you.*

## Chapter 5

**All you Need is Love of Godhead (London 1968-1970)**

BECAUSE THE EARLY London period of ISKCON resulted in an explosive growth in Srila Prabhupada’s Sankirtan Movement, many devotees have comprehensively written and spoken about these pivotal events, among them the well-researched history of Ranchor Prime, When the Sun Shines, which Yamuna contributed to significantly. In expanding on Yamuna devi’s memories of the London years, which she later termed “a magical experience which taught me lifelong lessons in my devotional life, it is important to again reiterate that this is a recounting of Yamuna devi’s own devotional odyssey rather than a retelling of or addendum to the history of the Hare Krishna Movement in England.

It was inherent in Yamuna’s nature that she inevitably saw each situation, event, exchange or service to Srila Prabhupada in a uniquely personal way which either enhanced or reinforced a needed lesson in her devotional life.

In reviewing some of the remembrances of those years by other devotees, I was not surprised to see that events or exchanges which were extremely meaningful to them were often rarely mentioned by Yamuna or were assimilated differently by her. Therefore, although we have endeavored to remain historically accurate throughout the book, in some instances Yamuna’s remembrances diverge from those of others, and we have remained true to her very personal and unique perspective. By weaving the tapestry of Yamuna devi’s internal devotional journey with the threads of her dedication, determination and sincerity, we hope to share through her realizations and personal example the tremendous and enduring impact she had on others and on the Hare Krishna Movement itself.

## An Unforgettable Send-off for Yamuna and Janaki

The London-bound sankirtan party left Montreal on August 19, 1968, for New York. As the six friends prepared for their London mission, Yamuna always wore her sari, tilak and nose ring wherever she went. They had freely walked the streets of San Francisco in this way and foresaw no problems doing so in a cosmopolitan city like New York:

**Yamuna**: *One day Janaki and I were casually walking down the street. I was by now so used to wearing a sari in San Francisco that it didn’t occur to me that we would appear strange in a city already as full of oddities and eccentrics as New York. Obviously, I was wrong. At one point, Janaki tugged at me and almost casually mentioned that a crazy-looking man was following us with what looked like a machete in his hand. I told her to pay no attention to him—just another crazy New Yorker. After another half-block, she became more urgent, telling me he was now closer and was definitely following us. By now I was also becoming more concerned. We decided to quicken our pace and make for the temple, still hoping he was just following the same road we were on, but no—he was following us, and what’s more, was now jogging toward us. We took off running as fast as our legs could carry us to the temple, with this crazy man with a machete behind us all the way. When we got there, literally bursting through the door and slamming it shut, there was only one young brahmachari, who must have thought we were two crazy ladies ourselves. Not having any available “weapon,” we each took a conchshell in hand and blew them with all the air in our lungs and ferocity in our hearts. Somehow it worked, and the sound scared him away. Although we were shaken by the experience, afterward we felt that perhaps this was Krishna’s way of telling us it was time to leave.*

They flew to Amsterdam sometime in the last week of August, and Yamuna and Guru das arrived by ferry from Holland to Harwich in England on August 31,1968. Malati and Shyamasundara had previously crossed by ferry, sending money back to Guru das and Yamuna in Holland so they could show enough money to the customs and immigration officials to convince them they did not intend to work in England. They in turn sent the money to Mukunda and Janaki, who then came in the same way. Now all together in England, everything was in place for the enthusiastic sankirtan party members to inundate England, Europe and the world with the Holy Names and establish a temple in London—something dear to the hearts of Srila Prabhupada and his Guru, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur.

**Yamuna**: *In Amsterdam we all stayed together. We had less than two thousand dollars among us, so we went by ferry one couple at a time, dressed in long skirts and smart pants. Shyamasundara and Malati were first across on the hovercraft. The first thing they did with a small amount of money was to buy a red pick-up truck. Then they telegrammed the money back to Guru das and me, and we went across; then we sent the remaining money, and Janaki and Mukunda came. By that time Shyamasundara had already secured a job as a carpenter in Herne Hill, where we stayed in an attic while he fixed the flat beneath. We advertised kirtan programs two nights a week in our flat. We also went to a macrobiotic restaurant to have kirtan, and we held kirtan outside of subway stations. We approached the Hindu Centre and other Hindu gathering places, and some Hindus started coming, and young Westerners as well.*

*Our real preparation for the London Yatra was to follow the simple Krishna Conscious tenets—chant, feast, dance, study our philosophy and share it with others. Srila Prabhupada called this our Peace Formulaactivities that would do good to you and do good to others as well.*

*When Srila Prabhupada sent a letter to any one of us, it was shared among us all. He always added his greetings for the others. We felt very close to Srila Prabhupada—that he was making us dance, pulling the strings. Sometimes we didn’t dance in unison, but we had affection and love for one another. We felt protected by Srila Prabhupada from the front, from the back and on the sides. For a year we were tested and we struggled. But collectively, we had firm faith that if we simply tried to repeat what we had heard from him, we could convince others to take to Krishna Consciousness. That was our great hope, and Srila Prabhupada constantly encouraged us and affirmed that hope in his letters. The letters kept us going. They motivated us when we were discouraged, and they assured us of his love and faith in us.*

**I was in due receipt of your letter dated Sept. 3, 1968, and now I have received a letter from Mukunda, and I am pleased to learn that you are now together, all six. So please try to start the temple as soon as possible and call me for your service. Offer my blessings to Yamuna as well as to Malati and her husband and the little child. I have sent one newspaper cutting to Shyamasundara that is a very nice article. If you get it photostatted, you can use it for propaganda work. Hope this finds you in good health.**

**— LETTER TO GURU DAS, SEPT. 14, I968**

## The Genesis of the Hare Krishna Movement in the West

In his desire to spread the teachings of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, the great Vaishnava saint Srimad Bhaktivinoda Thakur wrote in his magazine Sajjana-toshani in 1895 that Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu did not descend with His associates to deliver only the human beings in India, but rather His purpose was to deliver and uplift all living beings in all countries of the world. He prophesied, “Soon there will be a time when chanting of Krishna’s name will be heard in England, France, Russia, Germany and America.” The following year, 1896, he wrote a booklet entitled Sri Gauranga-lila-smarana-mangala-stotram, or Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu: His Life and Precepts. Appended to the booklet was an essay on the Srimad-Bhagavatam entitled, “The Bhagavat, Its Philosophy, Ethics and Theology,” a beautiful exposition he had previously written in 1869.

The booklet was sent to the library of McGill College in Canada, the library of the Royal Asiatic Society of London, and a few other highly respectable institutions. The following remarks appeared in the Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society of London:

**Under the title of the well-known Vaishnava Sri Kedaranatha Bhaktivinoda, M.R.A.S. has published a poem in Sanskrit on the life and teachings of Chaitanya. It is accompanied with a commentary, also in Sanskrit, in which the subject further elucidated is preceded by an introduction of sixty-three pages in English in which the doctrines taught by Chaitanya are set out in somewhat full detail. This position, and more especially as against Sankaracharya and the Advaita Vedantists, is explained at length. The little volume will aid our knowledge of this remarkable reformer, and we express our thanks to Bhaktivinoda for giving it to us in English and Sanskrit rather than in Bengali, in which language it must necessarily have remained a closed book to European students of the religious life in India.**

One reviewer summarized the contents for any reader unschooled in Vaishnava thought.

**The spirit that is to animate this new church is to be found on the principle that spiritual cultivation is the main object of life. Do everything that keeps it and abstain from doing anything which thwarts the cultivation of the spirit. A devoted love of Krishna is to be the guiding light, as preached by Chaitanya. Have a strong faith that Krishna alone protects and none else. Admit him as your only guardian. Do everything which you know Krishna wishes you to do, and never think that you do a thing independent of the holy wish of Krishna. Do all you do with humility. Always remember that you are a sojourner in the world, and you must be prepared for your own home.**

**— A. C. FRASER, MADRAS CIVIL SERVICE**

Bhaktivinoda Thakur also predicted that “A personality will soon appear to preach the teachings of Lord Chaitanya and move unrestrictedly over the whole world with His message.” Srila Prabhupada sometimes mentioned the auspiciousness of his having been born in 1896, the same year Bhaktivinoda Thakur first sent the teachings of Sri Chaitanya to the West. He perceived the sweet will of the Lord guiding all things, and therefore foresaw the correlation between his birth and Sri Chaitanya’s message reaching the West.

**\[In\] 1896, Bhaktivinoda Thakur wanted to introduce this Krishna Consciousness Movement by sending this book. Fortunately, that year was my birth year, and by Krishna’s arrangement, we came in contact. I was born in a different family; my Guru Maharaja was born in a different family. Who knew that I would come to his protection? Who knew that I would come in America? Who knew that you American boys will come to me? These are all Krishna’s arrangements. We cannot understand how things are taking place.**

**— LECTURE ON THE DISAPPEARANCE DAY OF BHAKTISIDDHANTA SARASWATI, DEC. 9, 1968**

In a conversation with the Canadian Ambassador to Iran on March 13, 1975, Srila Prabhupada further hinted that he might be the fulfillment of Bhaktivinoda Thakur’s prediction:

**In 1896, Bhaktivinoda Thakur was the first origin of this Movement. But he simply thought of it. And he was expecting some others willing to take up the work. Well, somebody says that I am the same man. And I was born in 1896.**

**— CONVERSATION, MAR. 13, 1975**

Thirty-seven years later, Bhaktivinoda Thakur’s son, the great Vaishnava Acharya Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur, sent three of his disciples to London to establish a temple there and preach the message of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. This project, begun by Bhaktivinoda Thakur, was so dear to the heart of Srila Saraswati Thakur that his mission funded it for its entire duration of three years. During that time he wrote consistently to them, encouraging and reinforcing the importance of developing a preaching platform in the West. In an eloquent and moving speech preceding their departure, he said:

**The happy day has come when we are destined to spread the message of our Great Master \[Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu\] to distant corners of the earth. The spiritual service to which we are dedicated has now passed the bud stage and blown fully into a flower whose aroma we have to carry across the seas with that willingness which characterized Sri Hanuman when he leapt over the wide ocean with the message of Sri Rama. This extension of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu’s spiritual gift to foreign countries is our humble offering at His Feet.... The Words of instruction of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu are verily His beautiful body; the preachers of His Word through the ages are His secondary limbs; the teaching of Sri Gaurasundara is His potent weapon; and the Grace of Sri Hari Himself, established in the Word of Sri Chaitanya, is His eternal associate.**

Then, drawing on a musical analogy, he said:

**We must always bear in mind that we are not the operators of instruments, but merely instruments.... We must constantly offer our music at the lotus feet of Sri Guru. We should practice the function of being the peripatetic preacher by carrying aloft the victory banner of Sri Gaurasundara’s divine commands, by perpetual submission to Sri Guru and the Vaishnavas, fixing our eye on the polestar of the heard transcendental voice.... If in that duty under the guidance of Sri Guru we are always inspired to discourse about the truth, then no hankering for travel, or any veiled form of desire other than the chanting of harinam, will ever strike terror into our hearts.**

**— SARASWATI THAKUR, ADDRESS TO LONDON-BOUND DISCIPLES, 1933**

## Srila Prabhupada's Wish Becomes Yamuna’s Wish

This realization—that she was merely an instrument of Srila Prabhupada’s heartfelt desire to establish a temple in London—was already clearly understood by Yamuna at this stage of her Krishna Consciousness. She exemplified this principle not only in the context of the London mission, but in the full spectrum of her devotional life.

**Yamuna**: *Until very shortly before our Montreal and then London travels, Guru das and I were still hoping to go to India with Srila Prabhupada. So we were the last of the three couples to join the London party. All this time, I had allowed no other possibility to enter my heart but my determination to somehow go to India. Yet a surprising thing happened to me when our plans changed. I found myself fully surrendered to anything Srila Prabhupada wanted me to do! Not just abstractly, but on a deep, heart level. Srila Prabhupada had promised us that if we just chanted Hare Krishna, everything would become known to us, and somehow this became known to me—that attempting to fulfill the wishes of the Spiritual Preceptor is the “highest place.” The irony was that now the willingness was there, the desire to please Srila Prabhupada was there, but a heavy feeling of inadequacy took center stage in my consciousness.*

Of course, this “inadequacy” was her natural humility—a quality inherent in all sincere devotees. In a talk to the young students of the Govardhan Academy at Saranagati in 2010, Yamuna elaborated on this theme. It is especially heartwarming and revealing because she had been asked how this movement started, and her answer so beautifully shows how she was able to “connect” with people of all ages, making them feel the excitement of the time and place and the wonder of Srila Prabhupada’s accomplishments:

**Yamuna**: *For us in England, the time was ripe. All of us know that Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur sent Bon Maharaja and others to England in 1933. Although they had the opportunity to meet ministers, royalty and other high members of society at the time, the climate was just not right for making a huge impact. When we look at Srila Prabhupada, he didn’t meet Lords and Ladies. He met these hippies— young people in their early twenties. But somehow or other, by Krishna’s incredible arrangement, Srila Prabhupada was able to make an impact very, very quickly. He was only here with us for eleven years. And in that time there were over one hundred temples, and tens of thousands of people began chanting Hare Krishna. And it is quite fascinating how these young people became so empowered. We were young. We had no qualifications. We didn’t know bookkeeping or anything it takes to run a temple. But we took to heart the principles of Krishna Consciousness and learned how to chant, how to worship the Deity, and everything that it takes to run a temple.*

*In England, there were just six of us in the beginning. What happened in two years was incredible. It was just impossible. We didn’t know what we were doing. But we were just enthusiastic to try. That’s really something. So that is what I want you to try to catch—that ray, that moonbeam of Krishna Magic, that allows you to do things that you never thought you could do. They are way far away from your comfort zone, but just because you love your Guru Maharaja, he said to do it, and with his blessings a lame man can walk over mountains, a dumb man can speak and a blind man can see. That is the mercy factor, back to the big, huge mercy factor. Sometimes I felt like I was in a play where they use marionettes, and the little guy is dancing, and you flop down and jump back up. And I felt like we were on these strings, and Prabhupada was pulling the strings and making us dance. While on the Jaladuta, Prabhupada prayed to Krishna, “I am just like a puppet in Your hands, so if You have brought me here to dance, make me dance, make me dance, make me dance as You like.” And that is actually what I have felt in my whole Krishna Conscious life—that Prabhupada was allowing us to dance the dance of Krishna Consciousness. And that is the parampara system. That is the power of the parampara—so juicy, so nectarean.*

Srila Prabhupada, although highly advanced in devotional service, also felt such humility and inadequacy, which he beautifully expressed in his prayer while coming to America on the Jaladuta:

**Sri Srimad Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur, who is very dear to Lord Gauranga, the son of Mother Saci, is unparalleled in his service to the Supreme Lord Sri Krishna. He is that great saintly spiritual master who bestows intense devotion to Krishna at different places throughout the world. By his strong desire, the holy name of Lord Gauranga will spread throughout all the countries of the Western world. In all the cities, towns and villages on the earth, from all the oceans, seas, rivers and streams, everyone will chant the holy name of Krishna. As the vast mercy of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu conquers all directions, a flood of transcendental ecstasy will certainly cover the land. When all the sinful, miserable living entities become happy, the Vaishnavas’ desire is then fulfilled. Although my Guru Maharaja ordered me to do it, I am not worthy or fit to do it. I am very fallen and insignificant. Therefore, О Lord, now I am begging You for Your mercy so that I may become worthy, for You are the wisest and most experienced of all. If You bestow Your power, by serving the Guru Maharaja one attains the Absolute Truth—one’s life becomes successful. If that service is obtained, then one becomes happy and gets Your association due to good fortune.**

**— BHAGAVAN KRSNER PADA PADME PRARTHANA, SEPT. 13, 1965**

## Offering Our Music at the Lotus Feet of Sri Guru

Yamuna felt that perhaps Srila Prabhupada had chosen the six of them for the London Yatra because they had known each other for a long time and worked well together. Once she was asked to give brief, succinct descriptions of each of the six of them in those days. She described Mukunda as the mimic of the group—a person who could change to fit any occasion or need instantly. He was also a good organizer. Janaki was plainspoken and loving—not afraid to express herself. She was often sardonically humorous and naturally generous. Shyamasundara was the idealist of the group, always presenting grand plans with an ever-present chuckle; a visionary. And Malati was wry, daring and possessed of a piercing wit. Yamuna’s husband, Guru das, was affable, outgoing and up for anything. She described herself with her usual humility as “a stranger in a strange land.” And yet, somehow they all coalesced in their desire to please Srila Prabhupada and were determined and united in their efforts.

By October the six devotees were chanting at various venues, including the Hindu Centre and a hub of the alternative London scene known as the Arts Lab. They used these venues for practicing their kirtans, including the Cintamani (Govindam) prayers from the Brahma Samhita. Each Wednesday and Friday night they chanted at the Arts Lab, with Yamuna, in her usual exuberant manner, exhorting the audience to chant by raising her arms and shouting “Haribol! Haribol!”
