But those early names are all dead and gone.” Then he resumed walking and chanting japa, leaving me perplexed. But I never pursued it further.*

*This was also near the time when pictures were taken on a morning walk of me taking pebbles out of Srila Prabhupada’s Wellington boots. We had walked some distance past John Lennon’s main house, down the big front steps, and down one large, wide gravel path about two hundred yards long. Srila Prabhupada’s boots came well up to his mid-calf, and we had walked only a small distance—fifty or sixty yards. Then Srila Prabhupada stopped, turned around and said, “There is some pebble in my boot; take it out.” So he leaned on my shoulder, and I bent down and took off his boot and extracted two or three very small pebbles, which I put in my pocket. And then we walked on. Perhaps we’d walked another fifty yards when Srila Prabhupada again said, “There are more pebbles in my boot; please take them out.” He leaned on his cane and put his other hand on my shoulder, and I took them out. I looked at him in amazement. How could these pebbles get in his boot? And he looked down at me and said, “Why do they jump in there?” as though the pebbles were personalities. And I said, “Of course, Srila Prabhupada, they can’t resist the opportunity of being close to your lotus feet.” He chuckled and said, “No. It is not so. I do not know how they are getting in there.” These were such sweet memories with Srila Prabhupada. Again, he reiterated after this incident that his Godbrothers would misunderstand. It was only later, when I knew something of the history between him and the Gaudiya Math, that I became even more astounded and grateful for the sacrifices he had made to preach to us in the West. For me it illustrated the concept of yukta vairagya in its fullest and most accurate way—that he changed some of the strict rules so he could reach out to the masses of the West, both men and women, but he never compromised or changed the philosophy of Krishna Consciousness to facilitate it. So often over the years he would say that if he had any quality, it was that he did not change what his Guru Maharaja, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur, had taught him, and that he had passed that philosophy on to his own disciples. I later lamented that I could not fully understand that principle then, because it later served to greatly enhance and strengthen my appreciation of his contribution to the Movement of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.*

*Because of the no-cutting rule, the grasses were from eight inches to a foot tall. One particular morning, the long grasses were particularly wet from the dew, and it was very foggy. So we were going down a hillock, and Prabhupada was walking a little ahead of me. As I was watching Srila Prabhupada’s feet, I thought, I will step where he walks, as a disciple is thinking to try to walk in the footsteps of the Spiritual Master. All of a sudden it hit me, “There’s no footprints!” It was uncanny because I was the only person there at the time. But it struck me so profoundly, and I turned around and looked, and there were really large, deep impressions where I had walked. So I stopped and said, “Prabhupada, I am confused; you are walking in front of me, but there are no footprints where you are walking, and where I walk there are footprints. How is that?” So actually he was quite sober and he said, “That will be revealed to you in time.” But he never gave me an answer. And it still hasn’t been revealed to me, other than that he was from another place—he was a Vaikuntha man.*

*Srila Prabhupada could see things we couldn’t. On another walk, as we passed the stables, he said, “Do you see them? There are more ghosts here than anywhere.” “I don’t see any, Srila Prabhupada.” He continued on, “There are so many ghosts here; they are all around us. They were persons who were very attached to the nice quarters here and didn’t want to leave. It is very common for them to linger on in a place that they were much attached to.” We had already been made aware of problems with ghosts at Tittenhurst Manor, especially in their moving furniture and knocking things about at the Tudor Lodge. There were two guests of John and Yoko who had very violent experiences with ghosts, which were creating a great disturbance. So Srila Prabhupada sent all the devotees there for chanting Hare Krishna. And the kirtan went on for many hours, and after that kirtan the ghosts evidently left. Srila Prabhupada said that ghosts are not able to stay where there is the chanting of the names of Vishnu or Krishna.*

## Conway Halt and Outside Engagements

During the entire period of their stay at Tittenhurst, the Apple team had arranged various programs to promote the “Hare Krishna Mantra” single, not just in England, but also in Europe. The devotees were also arranging speaking engagements for Srila Prabhupada, and one of those was a weekly engagement in London at Conway Hall in Holborn.

**Yamuna**: *One night a week, we all went into London, where Prabhupada had a program at Conway Hall. Conway Hall was a 500-seat auditorium in Red Lion Square. The programs always followed a similar format, and at the time they were virtually Srila Prabhupada’s only public preaching from Tittenhurst. So there would be a kirtan led by Srila Prabhupada, then a lecture, followed by another kirtan, which I usually led. We sat on an old wooden stage with Prabhupada in our midst on a raised dais covered with cloth. An oversized satin “World Sankirtan Party” banner hung behind us. I brought the six-inch Deities in a little wooden box, and They were placed on a table altar with vases and a bowl of burning incense. Our party had grown to about fifteen members now. The first gathering was small, perhaps 50 attendees. Later, more people began to come. Sometimes there were more Indian guests than Europeans, and then vice versa.*

*One night an extraordinary thing happened. Prabhupada led the first kirtan and then gave a lecture. I sat on the floor just to his right with the harmonium, and after the lecture, I began leading the second Hare Krishna kirtan. All of a sudden, Srila Prabhupada’s voice cut through the auditorium with the potency of Lord Nrsimha right in the middle of my chanting. I had never heard Prabhupada do that, nor had I heard the words he chanted.*

*“Narada muni bhajay vina radhika-ramana-name,” he sang. And then again he repeated it.*

*I looked up, and he looked down at me, signaling me to carry on. So I continued chanting Hare Krishna, and he continued singing his prayer to Narada Muni into his microphone. I closed my eyes and carried on, not knowing what was happening. Then he started leading with me. We could all understand that something inexplicable but amazing was happening. Everyone was literally jumping off the ground, leaping in the air; even little baby Saraswati was two feet off the ground, and the audience was leaping into the air. We jumped off the stage and all of us began running around the perimeter of the auditorium with the audience. It was one those Krishna Magic moments. Just amazing! The next morning I asked Prabhupada what had happened the previous night. “Didn’t you see?” Srila Prabhupada said. “Narada Muni came to our kirtan.” “No, I didn’t see him,” I answered. “Yes, Narada Muni came.”*

The next day, Yamuna wrote a short note about the event, and how she had perceived it:

*Last night, when Prabhupada sang this song—Narada muni bhajay vina—my eyes never left him. I felt as if I was witnessing something most transcendental. His own eyes closed, he simply played his kartals, his head moving back and forth in rhythm. Now I begin to understand. He saw Narada Muni in Conway Hall and was relishing his company. Unbelievable!*

**Mukunda Goswami**: *One time, Prabhupada made a sketch of how the devotees should sit on the stage in Conway Hall when he would give a series of lectures. Conway Hall was in the center of London.... It \[the drawing\] consisted of two rectangular tables (the kinds we have at the Sunday Feast).... He made the two tables side by side. And in the middle he had a small rectangle, and that was to be the harmonium. And he said, “This is where Yamuna will sit. Yamuna will sit here. I will sit here. And the Deities will sit here.” The Deities were his small Radha Krishna Deities \[and\] were on one table. He would sit on the other table, and Yamuna would sit in the middle playing the harmonium.*

*So he drew this picture of these three rectangles, the two tables with the small harmonium in the middle. So then the devotees would stand at the sides of the tables, perpendicular to the horizontal position of the tables. There were these two lines. So I said to Prabhupada, “Maybe we should stand in a bit of a curved way so that people could see us and we could see them. So it wouldn’t be just a straight line looking out at the audience.” So he said that would be okay.*

*So Yamuna led the kirtans, even though Prabhupada was there and was fully capable of leading kirtans. But she led the kirtans sitting at the harmonium. He would give a class. We found a lectern, more like a music stand, reaching all the way to the floor, maybe two meters high. He would place his Bhagavatams there, and it would reach up to the height of the table, where he would speak. So after each class he would ask for questions. Generally they were interesting comments. One evening a man asked in a challenging tone: “Why did you come to this country? Why didn’t you stay in India and preach to the politicians of your country?” And Prabhupada, without missing a beat, said, “You are a very great politician, therefore I am approaching you.” And the man was completely defeated, and he sat back down. He stood up to ask the question, and on hearing Prabhupada’s answer, he sat back down. And the whole hall was very silent except for Yamuna, who let out this very deep laugh, and it echoed throughout the hall. And that was the end of that.*

## On Top of the World with Srila Prabhupada

At the end of September, the devotees were invited to appear on the Dutch version of the wildly popular Top of the Pops program. It was to be a five-minute slot, and Srila Prabhupada wanted to attend. He would speak for two minutes, and the devotees would chant for three minutes.

**Just before Prabhupada and the devotees went onstage, they had to wait in the wings while a local Dutch group danced around, pretending to play their saxophones, trumpets and drums. Then the producer brought in a table with a cushion on it for Prabhupada and seated the devotees around Prabhupada on the floor.**

**The cameras began, the record played, and the devotees started to mime. Suddenly clouds, produced by dry ice, rolled in on the set—a “mystical” effect. As the devotees disappeared under clouds of carbon dioxide, only Prabhupada remained clearly visible. Seeing the special effect unsuccessful, the producer motioned the devotees to stand and dance beside the Swami.**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-L1LAMRTA**

**Yamuna**: *This was the beginning of rock videos, and the music was all mimed. Srila Prabhupada should never have gone, but somehow he wanted to come with us. I was to lie down inside this big crescent moon, and then out came dry ice and the stars. It was surreal. So we mimed for our three minutes, and then the camera focused on Srila Prabhupada, and he said:*

*“We have been chanting this Hare Krishna mantra. This is a transcendental sound vibration, nondifferent from the Lord. The Lord’s name and His form are the same. Please chant this sublime sound, and your life will become perfect. You’ll become happy, and you’ll realize your true nature—that you are an eternal servant of God, Krishna. This process is called bhakti-yoga, and we request everyone to take to this chanting. Thank you very much.”*

*In Paris, they put us out in the snow in the fields without any coats on, spread out in a big field, chanting without a microphone, under a rock, with Mondakini behind me. It was again completely surreal, but all part of the tour. There is a series of photos of Srila Prabhupada and me sitting on the same bench together at the airport. Janaki had been sitting there. Srila Prabhupada was leaning on his cane observing everything. We were all feeling a little unhappy that we had put him through such difficulty for so little result, but he was equipoised and encouraging as usual.*

Yamuna was always alert to try to get any morsel of mercy from Srila Prabhupada. Dhananjaya remembered their waiting in the airport for their KLM flight, and a piece of Srila Prabhupada’s cane came loose. Srila Prabhupada broke it off and had his servant put it in the dustbin. Yamuna, watching this, immediately went over to the dustbin, removed the piece of Prabhupada’s walking stick, and stuck it in her diary. This was a beautiful remembrance which was so indicative of Yamuna’s nature. Anything that came from Srila Prabhupada—his words, instructions, chastisements, remnants of his clothing, his writing, even his tooth—she kept and cherished as living reminders of him to be worshiped always. Fortunately, the wonderful photos of this episode capture Yamuna’s one-pointed attention to what Srila Prabhupada was doing with the cane—just waiting for the opportunity to get this little piece of “Prabhupada mercy.”

In England, the devotees had also begun appearing on television and at various venues to promote the record. Srila Prabhupada was immensely pleased that the Holy Names were being heard on such a large scale. In one letter he wrote:

**The Hare Krishna record is selling very nicely. Yesterday, it sold 5,000 copies, and this week it is on the chronological list as 20. They say next week it will come to be 3, and after that it may come to 1. So they are very much hopeful of this record.**

**— LETTER TO TAMAL KRISHNA, SEPT. 19 , 1969**

## Oxford Town Hall Program

A program was also arranged by the devotees for Srila Prabhupada to lecture at the Oxford Town Hall, which pleased him very much because it was something his own Spiritual Master had wanted. Srila Prabhupada was also thrilled at the reception they received.

**Yamuna**: *We brought the little six-inch Deities and set Them on a table. As the kirtan started, Mukunda played the organ, and the sound was tumultuous—celestial. So all of a sudden, as Mukunda played, Srila Prabhupada got up and danced. At first I was playing harmonium, but when Srila Prabhupada got up, I got up, as though lifted by a higher force. When Srila Prabhupada danced, it was simply indescribable how he moved. Arms raised, hands open as though inviting mercy from on high, he swayed in graceful back-and-forth movements. With his regal presence, robes down to the ground, and graceful movements, he danced like you would imagine a celestial being dances. The sound of the organ, the sound of our voices, watching Srila Prabhupada dance—it was all an historic moment in an historic place. Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati had wanted this to happen. How he must have been pleased by Srila Prabhupada*

**Yesterday we had a very successful meeting at Oxford at the Town Hall. About 350 boys, girls, old men, ladies and gentlemen participated, and we made them all dance and chant with us, every one. After the meeting, many boys and gentlemen came to congratulate me.... So it is a fact that our Movement will appeal to the heart of everyone, and they will join us. If one is not very much sophisticated and overburdened by material contamination, then he must respond to our call. The only thing is that we as preachers must be very, very pure, sincere and serious.**

**— LETTER TO SATSVARUPA, OCT. 31, 1969**

## Special Mercy and Special Instructions

Srila Prabhupada gave many classes during his Tittenhurst months, and Yamuna either recorded or wrote down most of them. As they were touring to promote their single, they sometimes had to associate and even live with people who either didn’t follow or respect any of the principles of Krishna Consciousness. Yamuna was concerned about this, and brought it up to Srila Prabhupada by asking that if we are forced into a situation where we have to interact with them, should we just talk about any topic or try to avoid it altogether. Srila Prabhupada answered:

**No. If we can find out a suitable place; but it is difficult nowadays. That we have to tolerate. What can be done? Let others do whatever they like. We can preach that “Do not do it,” but you cannot force, because the whole world has \[taken to\] these four principles of life, this meat-eating, drinking, gambling. And so our regulation is very strict. You see? If we say that “You do whatever you like,” then many people may come and join, \[laughter\] But we are not going to say that. We ... Our principle is that better not to have any cow than to have a cow and disturb him. You see? If one person can understand this Krishna Consciousness science, in future there is hope that he can \[bring\] many other persons to this knowledge of Krishna Consciousness. Although it is very difficult.... But if you can deliver even one man in your life, then you’ll be doing a great service for Krishna. It is not required that you have to deliver hundreds and hundreds of men, so-called. No. If you can train only one man, that’s a great service to Krishna. You saved one man from the clutches of maya. It is such a nice thing. So do it peacefully, and as far as possible, people may accept or not accept, but we shall do our duty. That’s all.**

**— LECTURE, SEPT. 17, 1969**

Srila Prabhupada gave so many valuable instructions to Yamuna over the course of her association with him. She often told of how, feeling herself deeply inadequate, she asked Srila Prabhupada how he accepted her service:

**Yamuna**: *Once I brought Srila Prabhupada’s lunch plate to him and set it down. He was saying his Gayatri mantra, and when he finished, he asked what each preparation was. I explained the dishes one by one and then, feeling very inadequate, I asked Srila Prabhupada, “How can you accept my service? I have so little qualification, so little ability.” And Srila Prabhupada revealed in a matter-of-fact tone that he had no choice but to accept the service of anyone who Krishna sent to him. He had left Vrindavan because his Guru Maharaja asked him to preach in the West, so whoever Krishna sent he had to accept that service to satisfy his Guru Maharaja. I was not expecting this answer. Perhaps I was feeling a little proud of my cooking abilities or some other fault had appeared in my service. But this affected me because I saw his phenomenal sense of duty and proportion. He was engaging whoever Krishna sent. It was as simple as that. Later this realization helped me through many difficulties of mismanagement and misadventure in my devotional life.*

In another talk given by Yamuna in 2002, she spoke about taking shelter of the Holy Names, using the example of Srila Prabhupada’s instructions to a young British devotee named Visakha (not the Visakha who is Yadubara’s wife), who had been married at Tittenhurst Manor by Srila Prabhupada. She and her new husband, Kulashekar, were asked to go to Germany to help in that temple project, and Yamuna could tell that she was clearly uneasy and fearful. Srila Prabhupada always encouraged the devotees that they could do virtually anything by taking shelter of the Holy Names, so even though she was fearful, she wanted to please Srila Prabhupada:

**Yamuna**: *And Srila Prabhupada said, “So are you ready to go?” and she said, “Yes.” But in her heart, I could tell there was some fear, so Srila Prabhupada said to them, “This is a glorious thing, this spreading Krishna Consciousness. I give you all blessings; just do your best.” I will never forget how he said the next sentences. First, he said, “Sometimes we may find ourselves alone.” We may be in the middle of devotee association, and sometimes we may feel lonely. So he said, “Even if you are alone, chant Hare Krishna and you will never feel lonely.” So that didn’t satisfy her. I could tell she still was worried about going, but then Srila Prabhupada said, “Even if you are in the wilderness of illusion, chant Hare Krishna, and you will never feel alone.” (He said the word “wilderness” like “the wilds of Africa”) That was so powerful—just a few lines. So he was empowering her, giving her the necessary strength of purpose by saying, “You can do this.” And then he began talking about this power of the Holy Name, regardless of what our situation is, regardless of where our place is. So you know, in your Krishna Conscious journey back to Godhead, be prepared that you’re going to have ups and downs and ins and outs—all kinds of challenges. But maybe you will remember back to today, when some day you are depressed, or not enthused, or feel alone. You’ll be out battling in the battlefield of illusion, where there’s not a big phalanx behind you or a big group. And just remember that you can always take shelter of the Holy Name, take shelter of the memories of the devotees, read the shastras, protect, then head for the shelter of the Vaishnavas.*

## Srila Prabhupada Leaves Tittenhurst

It was clear by early November that Srila Prabhupada wanted to leave Tittenhurst. Although John Lennon was accommodating to them, Srila Prabhupada wanted to be settled in their own temple, where he could preach and spread the Sankirtan Movement with full freedom and vigor. The devotees had only one vehicle, so getting around had been difficult even for work purposes. Srila Prabhupada had given Shyamasundara full reign to design the temple room according to his vision, and it was taking much longer than expected. Also, Mukunda had taken the responsibility for dealing with the extensive legal issues, and all of this was putting a strain on the men. Recognizing this, Srila Prabhupada wrote to Tamai Krishna in Los Angeles, requesting him to immediately come to London. Tamai Krishna had already proven himself to be a good organizer, and so Srila Prabhupada saw that he could expedite the Bury Place temple opening and assist the sankirtan mission:

**So far as I am concerned, as I already told you, after this European tour I am going to retire from active work and retire for writing books. So any place suitable I shall stay and give you directions. I am now confident that at least one dozen of you have understood the philosophy and the matters by which it can be handled. So from the background if I give you some inspiration, the whole society shall run on nicely. We shall talk of these things when you come. So try to go to New York as soon as you are able, and the ticket will be duly sent there. P.S.: Address future correspondence to 7 Bury Place, London.**

**— LETTER TO TAMAL KRISHNA, NOV. 4, 1969**

It is interesting to note in this letter that Srila Prabhupada, even at this early stage, planned to retire from active work so he could write, something he ultimately was never able to do. It is simply astounding to consider that even amidst his continual travels, his having to deal with constant managerial issues, writing thousands of letters to devotees, delivering hundreds of lectures and personally interfacing with thousands of devotees and guests, that he was still able to write over one hundred books. This would not be possible for anyone without the spiritual strength so obvious in every aspect of Srila Prabhupada’s character.

## The Storm

Shortly before Srila Prabhupada and the devotees left Tittenhurst, John and Yoko invited him for a meeting. Various versions of the meeting have been presented in the Srila Prabhupada-lilamrta and elsewhere. Yamuna gave a brief version of the events leading up to the event in a talk in 1980.

**Yamuna**: *So the main house downstairs was all carved wood; it was beautiful. And Yoko Ono was having the devotees scrape all this wood down, so that she could paint it black and white. She had a black and white floor, and on the walls were more or less pornographic drawings of different poses of her and her husband in black and white. And this was the room that they invited Srila Prabhupada to. So, of course, the meeting was uncomfortable and horrendous, and when Prabhupada came back, he was just livid for about an hour and a half speaking about it. “We are leaving this place tomorrow,” he said. So that was the end of it. And only two days after we left, there was a storm at John Lennon’s house, and an immense tree crashed through the roof right into the room Srila Prabhupada had been staying in. Actually, trees were felled all over the land. It was a graphic statement of finality. \>•*

*So in this dramatic manner, the Tittenhurst Manor interlude with Srila Prabhupada and the devotees ended. As the Bury Place temple was not yet ready for Prabhupada to reside there, a temporary apartment on Baker Street was found, and Yamuna was dispatched to Bury Place to prepare Srila Prabhupada’s quarters. To a large degree, everyone was filled with the enthusiasm of new challenges, new opportunities for spreading the Holy Names, and the excitement of being part of the dynamic preaching outreach that was the Krishna Consciousness Movement in London.*

## Baker Street

On November 3, 1969, Srila Prabhupada moved into his interim apartment on Baker Street. Now he would be more easily accessible to guests, devotees, reporters and others who sought his association, including many from the Indian community who had assisted the devotees in various services during their London stay. Although the Baker Street apartment was comfortable and centrally located near the Planetarium and the Baker Street underground station, Srila Prabhupada was tired of living in temporary housing and wanted the Bury Place temple and his quarters there to be completed. He therefore unrelentingly instructed, encouraged, cajoled and pushed his disciples to finish what had become a protracted and expensive undertaking.

On November 11, as requested, Tamai Krishna das arrived to assist in the organizational aspects of the sankirtan party, and his impact was immediately and profoundly felt. The management in London had always been a loosely-defined collaboration among the three original men, Mukunda, Shyamasundara and Guru das. Yet Shyamasundara was fully engaged with the temple construction and Mukunda with legal and other issues, so Srila Prabhupada felt that more organization and structure were required. Tamai Krishna had what Yamuna called a “linear mentality.” He saw a problem; he saw the desired result; and he was sometimes willing to take what Prabhupada called “cutting” measures to achieve that result. Of course, this caused some dissatisfaction among the more easy-going members of the London devotee community, and cracks appeared in the effortless intimacy which had developed not only among themselves, but with their new members as well. Still, it was clear that Srila Prabhupada, impressed with how Tamai Krishna had organized the sankirtan party in the United States, had given his blessings and empowerment to create the same sankirtan dynamic in London. Tamai Krishna coordinated the sankirtan party, established a schedule with quotas, and sent parties out on daily harinam sankirtan, chanting the Holy Names and distributing Back to Godheads. The results were immediate and palpable.

**Yamuna**: *During the first week of November, Srila Prabhupada moved from John Lennon’s estate, and of course, he wanted to move into the Bury Place temple immediately, but it was not yet ready. Srila Prabhupada had a sense of urgency. Not only did he try to encourage each of us individually to really take to heart what he was saying, but also to develop a sense of focus—of engaging the hearing and other senses with urgency. Hearing in Krishna Consciousness as Srila Prabhupada taught us goes right to the heart. It starts cleansing the heart of all kinds of dirty things, and when you act upon it with your will, enthusiasm and intelligence, you make advancement in spiritual life. Srimad-Bhagavatam describes it as drinking liquid nectar through the ears. So he gave us the ultimatum that we were to finish the Bury Place temple in two weeks, otherwise he would see to it himself. As his quarters were not yet ready, he lived for an interim period in an apartment on Baker Street across from the Planetarium. Every day he would go from his quarters to the temple to see how it was progressing and give directions by pointing with his cane: “This must be done. That must be done.” So the pace and the scope of the activities that were to be completed within this short period of time were phenomenal. Srila Prabhupada was the conductor, and we were the orchestra. His cane was his conductor’s baton, and he was directing everything—how the kitchen was being arranged or how there would be facility for prasadam distribution. He was a master conductor with a master vision for Krishna and his Guru Maharaja.*

*So when Srila Prabhupada spoke to his disciples, it was our responsibility to really hear him and then act upon it. He had extended so many leniencies to us on securing and establishing the Bury Place temple, and he was tired of waiting for it to open. We had been in London from the fall of 1968—over a year—and only now did our temple near completion. So in retrospect we may think that a year was not so long, but Srila Prabhupada was never slow in his dealings. The devotees were always amazed at the focus and speed with which he carried out his projects; and even though he was extremely lenient in those days, he expected that we would all eventually acquire the same focus and speed*

## Srila Prabhupada Appreciates Yamuna’s Cooking Service

**Yamuna**: *During this time Purushottama was acting as his servant. Srila Prabhupada had a living room, bedroom, small kitchen, a bathroom, and a place for Purushottama to stay. Malati or Janaki cooked Srila Prabhupada’s lunch, Purushottama cooked his evening prasadam, and I prepared his breakfast. Perhaps I cooked a lunch or dinner meal only two or three times during those weeks, whenever someone else was unavailable. Otherwise, I was fully absorbed in preparing his quarters at Bury Place and working toward our temple opening. On one of my cooking days, I brought his plate in just after his massage, bath and Gayatri mantra. With his tilak and golden, radiant skin, he looked as brilliant as the sunrise. When he saw his plate, he immediately said, “What have you prepared today?” So I explained each preparation. And he said, “Where have you learned to cook all these things?” I replied, “Everything I know is from you, Srila Prabhupada.” Furrowing his brow, he answered, “No, I have not taught you this. Who has taught you these things? I am asking you where you have learned to cook these things.” And I said, “Srila Prabhupada, I have been doing as you instructed and trying to learn from the Gujarati ladies.” He then became grave and emotional, his eyes glistening, and said, “You have prepared this so nicely. When I left India, I was prepared to eat bread and potatoes. I never dreamed that I would be eating this kind of prasadam.” Then he added, “But it is all by Krishna’s arrangement. Krishna is giving you the intelligence to do these things. And just see; when one takes a risk for Krishna, he is never the loser; he is always the winner. Thank you. Thank you very much.”*

*In the evening, Srila Prabhupada would often take a late meal. Usually either janaki or Malati would cook these meals, as they were both expert cooks. When Janaki cooked, she typically made Western-style sweets—for example, apple pies or a glazed cake. She would place the plate in front of him, and he would smile, take a little nibble of something and then stop. Finally he revealed to us, “These are very nice, but no one has made me any sandesh.” None of us knew how to make sandesh, so he described how to make it, and try as we might, we could never make it taste as it should. So one day he wandered down into the kitchen and showed us how to make good cheese and good sandesh. And from then on, we offered sandesh every morning at mangal arati so it could be eaten throughout the day, and especially in the evening. And from then on, the cakes and pies stopped.*

*Sometimes I would walk with Srila Prabhupada in the mornings—always a cherished time for me—and then he would come to see the progress of our work on the Bury Place temple. Now that he was in London, he was meeting many more people. There were people who had been rendering service, and also members of the Gujarati and other Indian communities who had established relationships with the devotees. They had all patiently waited for a long time to meet Srila Prabhupada, and now their wishes were being fulfilled*

## Yamuna Assists in Installing Radha and Krishna in Hamburg

As the preparations for opening the temple progressed at an accelerated pace, the agents at Apple Records continued to organize events to promote the “Hare Krishna Mantra.” Taking advantage of engagements between November 20 and 24 in Germany, Srila Prabhupada sent Tamai Krishna with the party and asked him and Yamuna to install small Radha-Krishna Deities in the Hamburg temple. They would be ISKCON’s first Radha and Krishna Deities in Europe.

**Yamuna**: *These small Radha-Krishna Deities were the same ones an Indian gentleman had donated to Srila Prabhupada, and which he had taught me to paint in his rooms at Tittenhurst Manor by essentially painting Them himself. So now Tamai Krishna and I were dispatched to Hamburg to install Them. Tamai Krishna performed the fire yajna, and I performed the abhishekam \[bathing\] and dressing. These Deities were special to me not only because of the installation, but because Srila Prabhupada had manifested Their look by painting Them with his own elegant hands.*

## Yamuna and Tilak

Anyone who spent time with Yamuna undoubtedly noticed how beautiful her Шак always looked. From the earliest days in San Francisco, she observed the care Srila Prabhupada took with his Шак and wanted to emulate that. She commented that even during his most austere living conditions in New York, Srila Prabhupada still washed his clothing each day and always wore clean clothes. She also wanted to emulate that. During the Tittenhurst, Baker Street and early Bury Place months, for example, although she only had two saris, she would carefully wash one each day and then wear the other one.

**Yamuna**: *As was my habit, since I only had two saris, I would wash one every day, and in the early morning hours, I would iron it and wear it. And they were just ordinary cotton saris, but I would try to keep them very neat and clean. So one day as I came into arati, it so happened that as I got up from offering obeisances, that particular morning Prabhupada noticed that Purushottama had come to arati unshaven and wearing the same sweater he had slept in. So Srila Prabhupada looked at each of us and then said to me, “You have so many beautiful saris.” So I stared at him—a bit stunned— and said, “No, Srila Prabhupada, I only have two.” He then said, “Every day you are wearing a brand new sari. It is so nice. You are always looking so neat and clean, and your tilak is very nice.” He then chided, “Purushottama, who do you think has the best tilakl” So Purushottama was very embarrassed, and he didn’t say anything. Srila Prabhupada then said, “Beautiful tilak means beautiful person.” I understood Srila Prabhupada’s subtle chiding. Of course, he knew my sorry sari situation, but he was acknowledging my attempts at cleanliness and at trying to be representative of how a Vaishnava should look. He said that we show by our appearance our respect for the Spiritual Master. On several occasions over the years, Srila Prabhupada would for some reason point out my tilak to others, fully embarrassing me each time.*

## The Moon Episode

The episode of the moon landing exchanges between Srila Prabhupada and the devotees began while they were still living at Tittenhurst Manor and continued during his short stay at the Baker Street apartment. This episode has been so thoroughly covered in other places that I revisit it only to iterate how Yamuna understood Srila Prabhupada’s position. For much of the Baker Street period, she spent most of her days preparing his quarters at the Bury Place temple. Except for an occasional morning walk or cooking service for him, she was not present as much as she had been at Tittenhurst. However, for Yamuna, any service that was delegated to her was discharged to the best of her abilities. It could be said about her that she lived to serve and served to live—such was her dedication to Srila Prabhupada’s instructions. She had already imbibed one of the most abstract devotional principles in the Guru and disciple relationship—one that Srila Prabhupada and our previous Acharyas wrote and spoke about often—that if the Guru says a rope is a snake, the disciple accepts it as a snake; if he says a snake is a rope, the disciple accepts it as a rope. Yamuna had often noted that prior to meeting Srila Prabhupada, she had never known a genuine saintly personality, but in him she experienced all of the qualities of saintliness. Because he personified for her the highest level of saintliness, it was not difficult for her to accept his spiritual realization—one that was also backed by Guru, scripture and other perfected devotees—as the highest. Therefore, any controversy involving the moon landing episode did not trouble her. She simply remained engaged in her many services and as far as possible avoided the issue.

One afternoon in his rooms, Srila Prabhupada spontaneously addressed the importance of the principle of becoming the servant of the servant in one’s spiritual life:

**The more we become the servant of the servant of the servant, the more we become elevated in spiritual life. In material life we become masters of the masters. The difference is there is no struggle in becoming servant of the servant, but there is a great struggle to become master.**

**— Yamuna’s journal**

## Adore Ye All

Yamuna always had a deep affection for the Adore Ye All poem Srila Prabhupada wrote to his Guru Maharaja, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati, for his Vyasa Puja homage in 1936. Many of us who heard Yamuna regularly sing this prayer felt the singular and heartfelt love she expressed for Srila Prabhupada when singing it. Srila Prabhupada originally presented the poem to a gathering at the Bombay Gaudiya Math, along with a short elaboration. At the end of his presentation, he humbly stated before the assembled Vaishnavas:

**Personally I have no hope to have any direct service for the coming crores of births of the sojourn of my life, but I am confident that someday or other I shall be delivered from this mire of delusion in which I am at present so deeply sunk. Therefore, let me with all my earnestness pray at the lotus-feet of my Divine Master to let me suffer the lot which I am destined to do for all my past misdoings, but to let me have this power of recollection that I am nothing but a tiny servant of the Almighty Absolute Godhead, realized through the unflinching mercy of my Divine Master. Let me therefore bow down at his lotus feet with all the humility at my command.**

**—Vyasa puja, 1936**

**Yamuna**: *Sometime in late 1969, Guru das discovered some of the early manuscripts of Bhaktivinoda Thakur in the British Museum Library. But astonishingly, he also found a 1936 poetic offering of Srila Prabhupada’s within the pages of a Harmonist magazine in glorification of his own Guru, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur. Our society was then only three years old, and we were very young devotees; we knew very little about Krishna Consciousness. But those deeply profound and prayerful words composed in English struck us to the very core of our hearts. Making it even more poignant was the fact that Srila Prabhupada had thought the poem lost, so when it was shown to him, he was deeply moved. Just imagine being only three years old in Krishna Consciousness and getting such an intimate glimpse into the inner life and prayerful mood of Srila Prabhupada when he wrote those words in 1936. So every year since we found this poem of Srila Prabhupada’s, it has been my habit to gather together a group on the Vyasa Puja of Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati, whether two or two hundred, wherever I happen to be in the world, and try to enter into the meditation of these words of our beloved Srila Prabhupada*

**Adore ye all, the happy day, blessed than heaven, sweeter than May; when he appeared at Puri, the holy place, my Lord and Master, His Divine Grace.**

**Oh! my Master the evangelic angel, give us thy light, light up thy candle; Struggle for existence, a human race, the only hope, His Divine Grace.**

**Misled we are, all going astray, save us, О Lord, our fervent pray; Wonder thy ways, to turn our face, adore Thy feet, Your Divine Grace.**

**Forgotten Krishna, we fallen soul, pay most heavy, the illusion’s toll; Darkness around, all untrace, the only hope, His Divine Grace.**

**Message of service thou hast brought, a healthful life, as Chaitanya wrought; Unknown to all, it’s full of grace, that’s your gift, Your Divine Grace.**

**Absolute is sentient, thou hast proved, impersonal calamity, thou hast moved; This gives us a life, anew and fresh, worship thy feet, Your Divine Grace.**

**Had you not come, who had told, the message of Krishna, forceful and bold; That’s your right, you have the mace, save me, a fallen, Your Divine Grace.**

**The line of service, as drawn by you, is pleasing and healthy, like morning dew; The oldest of all, but in new dress, miracle done, Your Divine Grace.**

**In 1936... during this Vyasa Puja day, whenever I studied about our relationship with my Guru Maharaja, I expressed it in poetry, and since that day my Godbrothers used to call me “poet.” My Guru Maharaja very much appreciated this poetry. Now somehow or other you have found it. I thought the poetry was lost, but I do not know how it was found out by some of our disciples. I think it was found out in a London museum or somewhere else by Guru das. They had a stock of Harmonists, and from the Harmonist, my Guru Maharaja’s paper, this poetry was found. Otherwise, I thought it was lost.**

**— LECTURE, DEC. 10, 1976**

It was obvious that Srila Prabhupada held a special place in his heart for opening a temple in London, but the depth of its meaning to him, given the heartfelt wishes of his Guru Maharaja, would not have been understood by the young devotees in London at the time because they knew little of the earlier history of the Gaudiya Math. Years later Yamuna understood something of the extent of what London must have meant to Srila Prabhupada when she learned of the determined attempts of Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati to establish a foothold in the West. Several times Srila Prabhupada mentioned to Yamuna and others that the Adore Ye All poem again prompted his Guru Maharaja to request Srila Prabhupada to preach in the English-speaking countries. After hearing the poem, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta told his editors to “publish anything he \[Srila Prabhupada\] writes.” He also commented that “Here is someone who will be able to defeat the impersonalists.”

## A Temple Grows on Bury Place

**Yamuna**: *We used to literally run from service to service. Srila Prabhupada somehow inculcated within us the simple understanding that time was of the essence, and we had no time to waste in anything other than Krishna’s service, or the pursuit of Krishna Consciousness. So, fueled by Srila Prabhupada’s desire, by chanting the Holy Names and by the power of each other’s association, we completed most of the renovations at Bury Place by the beginning of December. Yet some of the finishing work still needed to be completed. Srila Prabhupada had done some calculations, and established December 14,1969, Odana Shasti, as the formal temple opening and Deity installation day. He clearly informed us that whether the temple was complete or not, the installation would take place on that day. This added more fuel to our already fast and furious pace.*

*After I finished preparing Srila Prabhupada’s rooms at Bury Place, I was free to begin arranging for the Deity installation. At that time, we were going to install the large Lord Jagannatha, Subhadra and Balarama Deities that Shyamasundara had carved, but we still did not have Radha and Krishna Deities. In a letter to Aniruddha on November 24,1969, Srila Prabhupada asked in a footnote for him to send the Deities that were carved in wood by Gaurasundara in 1968. Sri Krishna was about fifteen inches high and painted a bright cobalt blue, and Radharani was thirteen inches high and painted a very bright, cadmium yellow color. I had my heart set all this time on large marble Deities, and this was not what I had envisioned for our worshipable Radha and Krishna at all. Yet, it seemed there was no other alternative, and now I lamented that my deep-seated hopes of having marble Deities in the London temple were gone forever.*

One of the new brahmacharis who joined the temple at this time was Dhananjaya das, who vividly recalled his first cooking episode with Yamuna:

**Dhananjaya das**: *When I arrived at the temple, one of the first people I met was Yamuna—she was downstairs in the kitchen and came out to greet me. I said, “Maybe you can use this for lunch.” She took it and smiled and said “Thank you very much; how kind of you,” and then looked inside the bag—totally horrified to see a load of eggs! She said, “Actually, we don’t eat eggs,” and then explained the four principles to me. Then she said, “Do you like cooking?” and I said, “Well, I know how to make porridge and muesli and boil eggs.” She said, “Well, I’m making this preparation called Eggplant Balarama; if you’d like you can help—just wash your hands and come and 1’1I show you what to do.” She pretty much taught me on the spot, as it was close to lunchtime. She then asked if I knew how to make chapatis, and I said, “I have no idea what that is,” so she again taught me what to do, and we made them together. I really felt a connection with her because she was just so nice, so straightforward. She said, “I hope you’re staying for lunch,” and of course I agreed. She was cooking with her sister.... They had prepared an amazing lunch, and it was the first time I’d ever tasted eggplant in my life; I thought it was out of this world. I didn’t know that she was the best cook ever and always remained so.*

## Sri Sri Radha-Londonisvara and the Krishna Magic

**Yamuna**: *And then, a mysterious and magical thing happened. Srila Prabhupada wrote a letter to Hit Sharanji on December 5,1969, cancelling an order he had previously made for marble Deities for London:*

**You need not send the murtis by air cargo to London because some devotee here has contributed a Radha-Krishna murti pair imported from Jaipur. It is 42” high and very nice. So Krishna has saved us in this point because we are going to have our opening ceremony on the 14 December through the 2I of December.**

**— LETTER TO HIT SHARANJI, DEC. 5, I969**

*So the “trick” of the arrival of Sri Sri Radha-Londonisvara occurred sometime between November 25 and December 4, a mere ten days before the installation ceremonies were to begin.*

*There’s a wonderful story about how Sri Sri Radha-Londonisvara manifested and were installed in the Bury Place temple. For me it began about a year prior to Their installation, when we first visited the London Hindu Centre in 1968. This was the first time any of us had seen three-foot-tall, white marble Radha and Krishna Deities. The whole Hindu Centre room was an altar of sorts—virtually the entire pantheon of demigods surrounded the room on three sides. Yet the moment I set eyes on their Radha and Krishna Deities, I determined that we should have something similar for our London temple.*

*I convinced the others that we should try to get white marble Radha-Krishna Deities for our temple, and we decided to start a fundraising campaign. We put little tin cans with calligraphed labels saying “Donation for Radha-Krishna Temple” on each floor of the India House. Each fortnight one of us would empty them, and after a few months we had collected £42. I was ecstatic, and guarded that money like it was the most precious gem. But then one day Shyamasundara ruefully approached me and said, “We have to talk. We need to use that Deity fund. The red truck broke down, and it is our lifeline, so we need to use the money to fix the truck.” I was crestfallen, just devastated, and I wrote and informed Srila Prabhupada. He assured me that I should not mind—that somehow Krishna would come, and so I continued to have my heart set on somehow getting marble Deities. The previous year I had also endured a protracted episode with Shyama Mataji, where she had “given” us Radha-Krishna Deities; and that also ended unfortunately.*

*In early December, a call came from Mr. Goyal, quickly followed by a visit and more calls. There are different versions of those exchanges, and I was not a party to them. My understanding was that Mr. Goyal had procured three-foot white marble Radha-Krishna Deities from India, and They had become slightly damaged in transit. He wanted Srila Prabhupada to bless Them. Would he come to see Them? Prabhupada said, “Yes, I’ll come.”*

*Then a magical and mysterious pastime took place. Prabhupada and three men, Shyamasundara, Mukunda and Tamai Krishna, went in the van to Mr. Goyal’s house. After they arrived, they had some cordial talks, and at some point, it was understood that after a short while, the Deities would be offered to our temple. But Srila Prabhupada was taking no chances. A few more moments passed and then, looking intently at the Deities, Srila Prabhupada said, “Yes, we’ll take Them.” Mr. Goyal was clearly shocked and said, “No, we will bring Them to you later.” Srila Prabhupada said, “No, we will take Them now.” He then asked Shyamasundara if he could lift Krishna. Then he asked Mukunda if he could lift Radharani. When they replied in the affirmative, Srila Prabhupada said, “Then you each take one, and we’ll go. Thank you so much.” And they left with the Deities, leaving behind a stunned Mr. Goyal.*

*Once in the van, Srila Prabhupada said, “Now drive.” Then off they went with Srila Prabhupada smiling at Mr. Goyal and his family, who stood together on the curb. Shyamasundara drove on a few blocks, and then Srila Prabhupada ordered him to stop. He turned in his seat and began offering prayers to the Deities: Govindam adi-purusam tam aham bhajami ... He looked long at Krishna, who was white with a slight bluish cast, and an almost impish smile on His gorgeous face. Then he looked at the exquisite white Radharani. Srila Prabhupada then gravely said to the devotees, “Krishna is so kind that He has come to us like this.”*

*I knew that Srila Prabhupada had gone in the van to the Hindu Centre, but I had been disappointed in my aspirations for large marble Deities so often before that I hardly dared hope They would ever come. I really had no idea it would happen in such an unprecedented way. It was truly the Krishna Magic at work. I was in Prabhupada’s room looking down, and the van pulled up. Srila Prabhupada was still living in his Baker Street apartment, as his rooms in Bury Place were not quite ready. As I watched, the back doors of the van opened, and Mukunda and Shyamasundara come out, their arms full. Srila Prabhupada directed them to carefully bring the Deities up the stairs to his room and then gently set Them down.*

*I will never forget my own shock, surprise and joy. My mouth was literally open in awe, and I felt faint. Then Srila Prabhupada looked at me with a joyous, mysterious smile, and said: “Your marble Radha and Krishna have come. Put Them in the back corner and cover Them with cloth.” With tears of joy pouring down my face, I looked at these magnificent Deities—all that I could ever have wished for—and was overwhelmed at Their beauty; then I covered Them. Prabhupada continued, “Krishna has played a great trick on Mr. Goyal.” As he spoke, his eyes were smiling, his mouth was smiling—his entire body was jubilant. “This Krishna wanted to come here all along.”*

*Of course, part of the “trick” involved the fact that in transport from India, Srimati Radharani’s hand had broken, and so there was some question as to whether She would be suitable for installing. For Srila Prabhupada, this was a non-issue, as he felt that once repaired, She would be installed and fully present, so there was no disparity. But to some Hindus, the fact of the breaking made Her imperfect and therefore “uninstallable.” Srila Prabhupada’s vision was quite the opposite, and he saw these Deities as the quintessence of beauty. All in all it was a wonderful trick. Srila Prabhupada gave the analogy of the Lord in His form of Damodara tricking Mother Yasoda by defeating her every effort to tie Him up by making the rope always too short. So here he felt that Krishna had wanted all along to come to our temple, and therefore created this “trick” to come.*

*Srila Prabhupada said to me, “One can never understand how Krishna acts, but all the time He was planning to come and stay in this temple. Krishna has come in this form because of your prayers, but He waited until now to increase your desire for Him.” He then reminded me that he had written to me that Krishna would come in His own time. He said that sincerity always attracts the attention of Krishna, and if you pray with sincerity for something service-related, Krishna will answer your prayers.*

*Srila Prabhupada then instructed me to make Their dresses, jewelry and crowns for the installation. He instructed Shyamasundara to complete an altar for Them, and he came every single day to see the progress on the construction and the Deity service. Although he gave me the service of decorating the Deities, I had never done this before, so he helped me at every step. He said, “Krishna’s favorite color is a golden saffron color.” So he had me bring back several colors of silk—from yellow to orange to saffron. And he personally selected two colors of contrasting silks with both gold and silver borders. Giving me the most rudimentary instructions on designing for Krishna, he simply said, “You just copy what is there in the pictures—the Brijbasi prints.” He explained that Krishna should wear a dhoti, shirt and shawl. Radha should wear a pleated Brijbasi-style skirt, choli (short blouse) and chuni (veil). We bought stones and buckram and made crowns the exact sizes of the ones already carved on Them. We also made necklaces, bracelets and ankle bells on the same principle. I asked him how many peacock feathers Krishna should wear, and he replied that they could be any odd number—1, 3, 5, or 7.*

*Although we were already running from service to service, the pace intensified after Radha and Krishna arrived. Devotees worked on each of the five floors—from the basement kitchen to the top floor office—with great determination.*

*Shyamasundara had been given the service of repairing Radharani’s hand, and again he asked for George’s help. George arranged for the famous sculptor David Wynne to do it.*

*Two weeks before the installation, Shyamasundara had yet to start building the altar. I only had a vague idea of his plan, but no measurements to do my own work. He had asked George Harrison to donate marble for the altar—a thick slab of yellow-gold sienna marble for Radha and Krishna to stand on, and two thin slabs of reddish-black marble to serve as steps in front of the larger piece. I could do little work on the Deity room itself, so I directed my energies toward sewing clothes for Jagannatha, Subhadra and Balarama. Virtually all I remember of those days was sewing for Their Lordships forty-eight hours a day.*

*When Srila Prabhupada finally moved into his rooms at Bury Place, the Deities were still being kept in a special cordoned-off area, and he stayed there with Their Lordships until the installation. The morning before the installation, a new dark blue carpet was laid in the temple room. Deity room curtains were hung, and the marble altar slabs put in place. A four-inch-thick redwood plank for Lord Jagannatha was already in place. Four of the best spotlights we could find had been wired. Shyamasundara promised that the overnight crew would install the Deity umbrella and columns. Unfortunately, there was not enough time to secure the columns to the marble base, and this would almost prove disastrous during the ceremonies.*

*Srila Prabhupada instructed that the night before the installation we should have a special kirtan to invite the Lord to come; so as flowers and candles rested on the marble, the temple lights were subdued, and we began chanting. Each devotee knew he or she was on the cusp of a truly historic moment. We were chanting softly when Prabhupada came into the temple room that night. He sat down on his new vyasasana for the first time. Mukunda placed a white chrysanthemum garland around his neck, and devotees placed chrysanthemum petals at his feet. He indicated that each of us should place a flower on the marble where Radha and Krishna would stand the next morning. Then Srila Prabhupada sat down with his shoulder towards where the Deities would stand and began chanting the Vande ham prayers. This was the first time he had chanted in the new temple. We all just listened and softly played instruments. It was just us—the family. This was what he had wanted all these years, ever since Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur’s express desire. He was so absorbed in the chanting that his eyes didn’t open at all. It was the most soothing, lilting, flowing, lyrical, transcendental kirtan I had ever heard. The kirtan flowed like liquid silk Ganges water. It was a deeply emotional moment for each of us. Then he looked over to where Their Lordships would stand, and we all began to chant. I did not think that anything could ever top that feeling of belonging to something so wonderful—something so magical as this. I remember thinking, “What have I done to be so fortunate to come into contact with Srila Prabhupada, with Krishna Consciousness and with the family of Vaishnavas? I am just an ordinary person from Butte, Montana, and here I am now feeling the greatest fortune.” It simply increased my resolve to try to become a real devotee. Towards the end of the kirtan, Srila Prabhupada looked at each of us, and later some devotees said they felt him looking right through them, seeing everything about them, simply by his glance. After the kirtan and prayers, Srila Prabhupada walked to the altar, placed his flowers on top of ours, paid his obeisances and left.*

*As soon as he went upstairs to his room, we began our last frenzied night shift. Apple Records had donated five elaborate floral wall arrangements, which were hung on the redwood temple walls. George Harrison arranged for two spectacular flower arrangements to be placed on either side of the altar. The columns and umbrella were then put in place on the altar. We then cleaned through the early morning brahma muhurta hours right up until mangal arati. Although I knew that the columns had not been secured to the marble base, I hoped for the best. We had simply run out of time.*

## The Installation Ceremony

Yamuna often spoke of the installation ceremony of Sri Sri Radha-Londonisvara. For her it was a life-changing experience, not only because of Srila Prabhupada’s continued personal training in how to worship the Deities, but because she witnessed his very real, loving and intimate exchanges with the Deity forms of the Lord. Through the unexpected and extraordinary events surrounding the installation, Yamuna understood that Srila Prabhupada truly saw Krishna and Radharani standing before him, not statues or idols, and this dramatically affected her approach to worshiping her own Deities throughout her life. Her seva of her personal Deities, Sri Sri Radha-Banabehari, always reflected the same loving and intimate mood she imbibed from Srila Prabhupada’s training. He explained that whatever you offer to the Deities, try to do it with love—with feeling. When she asked, “What if I don’t have that love or feeling?” he told her that she should pray to the Deities to develop it. He once answered a similar inquiry about how to become sincere if you feel you are not sincere. Srila Prabhupada again illuminated the importance of prayer by saying that if you feel you are not sincere, you should pray for sincerity. Over the years, whenever Yamuna was asked questions about Deity worship, she would preface her reply by explaining that because Srila Prabhupada had trained her in a simple, particular way, she always maintained that standard, although it was somewhat different than that later formalized within ISKCON.

**Shyamasundara had completed most of the altar, except for Lord Jagannatha’s altar and the canopy over Radha and Krishna’s throne. Both the canopy and Lord Jagannatha’s altar would be supported by four heavy wooden columns more than six feet high.**

**Two rear columns would hold a marble slab for the Jagannatha Deities to stand on, and two front columns were now supporting Radha and Krishna’s large velvet canopy. The columns were big and heavy; Shyamasundara called them “elephant-leg columns.” The columns now stood in place on the altar, although Shyamasundara hadn’t had a chance to secure them. The day before the installation, Shyamasundara collapsed upstairs in exhaustion.**

**— SRILA PRАВHUPADA - LILAMRTA**

**Yamuna**: *The day of the temple opening, December 14, 1969, had finally arrived, and the temple was filled to overflowing. The BBC brought bright lights for fi Iming the ceremony. Srila Prabhupada bathed Radha and Krishna, and I assisted him. Then Purushottama and Tamai Krishna brought the Deities to the altar. Prabhupada and I followed, and I closed the curtain. All four of us were in the Deity room. Then an elbow hit one of the columns and immediately a chain reaction occurred. Right in front of us, the column began collapsing. For me everything happened in slow motion. My vision changed. I saw several things simultaneously. Firstly, I had never seen Srila Prabhupada move so fast. With one sweeping motion of his hand, he cleared the items on the bottom step. Then with his right hand, he steadied the column, and with his left hand, he gently but firmly held Srimati Radharani’s hand. It appeared to me almost like a choreographed dance, and yet his movements were so heroic, strong and graceful. It all happened in a split second. As he turned and looked at me, I saw on his brow tiny droplets of perspiration— his mouth frozen into a grim expression. He appeared to me at that moment as the embodiment of chivalry—strong, commanding—saving his beloved Radharani. Srila Prabhupada allowed us to see in that small, extremely intimate gesture that this Radharani was real, not a marble statue, but a person—the Supreme Goddess. In addition, the alacrity of his movements and his manifestation of superhuman strength within a moment’s notice amplified the experience for me. The love, strength, grace, clarity, protective instinct and immediate service mood he exhibited, these qualities were coming from a higher place—that highest place I wanted to go to.*

*At that moment, the umbrella started to crack loose and fall. Tamai Krishna grabbed it in free fall before the unthinkable happened. Srila Prabhupada looked at the men, his voice soft and controlled, and simply said, .    "You—out.” Then to me, he said, “Dress Them quickly.” Then he turned and walked out of the Deity room.*

*The columns were carried out in full view -of the BBC cameras, followed by the umbrella. I could not imagine what the devotees were thinking, but the BBC and most of the guests thought it was just part of the program—a procession carried out before the unveiling. I dressed the Deities as quickly as I could, and then during a foot-stomping kirtan, I blew the conch and opened the curtains. The roar was tumultuous. A disaster had been averted, and I had seen something extraordinary in Srila Prabhupada—what a real relationship with the Deity form of Radha and Krishna entailed. I would never forget it. I would never be the same.*

**Mondakini devi**: *We came, three French girls—the other two were Ilavati and Jyotirmayi. The first time we came to Bury Place was actually the installation day of Sri Sri Radha-Londonisvara.... The first memory I have of Yamuna was seeing her doing the puja for the Deities. At this time, Srila Prabhupada had told us that we should get up one and a half hours before sunrise, so Yamuna was actually the only one to get up for mangal arati, and she was alone with the Deities in the beginning because all the other devotees and the newcomers like us were doing harinam in the streets three times a day. So Yamuna did all the Deity worship alone, and she took such personal care of the Deities.*

*In my own case, it was just magical because I had been studying impersonal philosophy, and it was very deep within me, and only by Yamuna’s grace and association did God become a person. Devotional service with Yamuna was an adventure; it was never boring, not “we have to do it,” but that it is an adventure, and Krishna was reciprocating. I remember the way she was engaging guests and how merciful she was. We were just very new, Jyotirmayi and myself, and the first Sunday Yamuna was dressing the Jagannatha Deities, she told us, “You can come.” But we were very impersonal, young girls—only nineteen years old—and a little mischievous too. We weren’t used to the form of Lord Jagannatha. So Yamuna had to climb up a ladder to serve Them, and we started to laugh as we didn’t know it was offensive. In French we call it fourire—you laugh, and you cannot stop. The Lord was undressed, and we just could not stop laughing—it was awful! Yamuna was looking at us as she was on the ladder, not knowing what to do about us. So very gently she just said, “You had better leave.”*

## A Description of the Bury Place Temple

**Yamuna**: *There were four stories and a basement in the Bury Place temple. The basement contained the kitchen, as well as a small prasadam distribution room. That kitchen was used to prepare all of the Deity offerings, as well as Srila Prabhupada’s special prasadam.*

*Pictures give a good illustration of the temple room of the Bury Place temple. Sometimes devotees likened it to inside the belly of a whale because of the redwood columns which came out of the sides and arched at the top. Shyamasundara had arranged to have the redwood shipped from California, and he and one brahmachari, Digvijaya, were responsible for virtually everything that was done in that temple room. It was a very unique space and, as the pictures clearly illustrate, it was actually very small. The altar was placed at the far end of the room behind a curtain with Jagannatha, Subhadra and Balarama on top and beautiful Sri Sri Radha-Londonisvara underneath. Srila Prabhupada’s small wooden vyasasana was on the right side as one faced the Deities. A curtain separated the Deities from the darshan area where all the guests sat. It was a very small, cozy temple.*

*Srila Prabhupada’s room on the second floor was large, with high ceilings and good light from several windows. An American girl, Aditi, and three young girls from France volunteered to help me; we stitched, upholstered, painted and cleaned. The tall windows had sheers and dark blue damask drapes with swags and valances. We upholstered an asana in dark blue velvet—seat, back, cushion and bolster pillows. The walls were eggshell white with white gloss wood trim. A low table served as his desk, with under-the- window shelves for his books. His bed was to the left of the doorway, and at the far right end of the room was a fireplace. There was also a bedroom and adjoining bathroom.*

*The third and fourth floors were for housing the students. The entire building was adequate for comfortably housing from fifteen to twenty-five students, with the brahmacharis living mostly in one room. However, we soon outgrew the building, not only with the resident devotees, but with the constant flow of travelers passing through, going to or from other temples.Also, the Sunday preaching and feast programs attracted many members of the Indian community, and the building would sometimes be filled with up to 150 people sitting up and d own the stairways to take prasadam.*

## Srila Prabhupada Leaves and Yamuna Thrives

**Yamuna**: *The Deities were given the names Sri Sri Radha-Londonisvara, the Grand Supreme Lords of London. Srila Prabhupada stayed a mere six days after the installation, and left for Boston on December 21,1969. It was such a poignant moment for me, after everything we had been through— the challenges, the highs, the lows, the ultimate thrill of now having this temple and those glorious Deities. All of the devotees went to the airport to see Srila Prabhupada off except me; I stayed back at the temple to attend to my services. Just before he left, Srila Prabhupada came into the temple room and offered his obeisances to the Deities—full, flat dandavats on the blue carpet. He remained on the ground in that position for a long time, and when he got up, I noticed that he had tears in his eyes. And he looked over at me, very gravely yet matter-of-factly, and said, “If you just do as I have instructed—what I have taught you so far—you will go back to Godhead. Do it. Just do it!” And at that point I, with tears welling up, folded my hands and simply watched Srila Prabhupada as he turned and walked out the front door. All I could say was “Thank you, Srila Prabhupada. Thank you.”*

*From that moment on I was engaged in the Deities’ service around the clock. My feet never touched the ground. I had no life other than Radha-Londonisvara. I would get up at 2 am, bathe, and go down to the Deity room. I was so immersed in Deity worship that out of fear of being late for waking Them up, I would offer obeisances and then fall asleep in that position outside the curtain until it was time to wake Them. At the time I was the only person doing it. Then in the evening, the devotees would sweetly sing as I put Their Lordships to rest. I often felt that even though I was constantly on the move and engaged in so many variegated services, this must be what the spiritual world was like—positive attachment to the Positive Form.*

**Mondakini devi:** Srila Prabhupada was telling everyone that Radha-Londonisvara have tricked you: They didn’t come as Deities; They came as Themselves, as Radha and Krishna. That was really the mood. He was teaching Yamuna a Vrindavan way of worship—very simple, although he was teaching differently in Los Angeles. What I remember was the loving care. Yamuna was full of life, and she had a strong personality.... full of joy and laughter ... She was teaching us the basics and always engaging us. We hear in the scriptures that Srimati Radharani is even happier when She sees that the gopis are engaged in the service of Krishna, and Yamuna was like that. She would always engage us in doing lots of little things for Srila Prabhupada. She would arrange for us to go on the walk with him in the morning or to go upstairs to see him in his rooms. When Srila Prabhupada was away, we used to send packages of sweets or other little things. She was always encouraging us to write to Srila Prabhupada about our progress.

**Yogesvara das**: When \[Yamuna\] took care of the Deities, it had this very mystical allure to it. I’m talking about the evening arati now—putting the Deities to rest. I was always there in the temple room playing harmonium, because I was an organ player in college. Sometimes she would sing; sometimes I would sing. Others would show up, but sometimes it was just the two of us. She would put out the evening glasses of water and the other utensils and get the Deities ready for bed. She always sang the same melody at night. She had that way of bending notes, especially on the end of phrasing—it was a very mystical experience. We’d be chanting, and then very, very slowly, she would close the curtain, until on the final note the curtains would be closed. That was my training with Yamuna ... She was memorable in that you wanted to be like her in the depth and mood of her devotion—the theatrical acting as a path of salvation. Theater—this was divine theater, what she did. That appealed a lot to me.

**Yamuna**: *Before he left, Srila Prabhupada taught me how to bathe the Deities by means of sacred mantras. Speaking very deliberately and soberly, he said that while chanting Hare Krishna, you meditate that you are placing a golden or silver vessel on your shoulder, going to the Yamuna River and collecting her sacred waters in the vessel. Then after bringing the vessel back, you meditate that you are massaging Them with rare scented oils, and then that you are pouring the holy Yamuna water over Their Lordships. After the bathing, you dry Them with soft cloths. So in this way, he taught me how to bathe the large marble Deities.*

*Srila Prabhupada was extremely fond of the unique and exquisite faces of Sri Sri Radha-Londonisvara, and he instructed me to never disturb Their beautiful faces. He said in a firm and unequivocal way: “Don’t try to repaint or rub oils on Them so the paint will come off. They are so perfectly painted. Take care of Them as I’ve instructed you, and your life will be successful.”*

**Mondakini devi:** Yamuna taught me how to close my eyes and think, “O my Lord, now I am going to the Yamuna,” and I was picturing the pots on my head—they could be gold or silver, as we wished—then collect the water of the Yamuna and bathe the Lord. It was so exciting. In a very concise way, I would say Yamuna was teaching us to serve God as a person, a loving person, Radha and Krishna—the persons we cherish the most—and to meditate every minute of the day, whether in the streets or in the temple, how we can serve Them. At that time she was doing all the sewing of Their outfits by herself, because I was so bad at sewing, and Digvijaya was doing most of the cooking with his wife.

**Yamuna**: *As I was initially the only Gayatri-initiated pujari, I performed all the offerings and aratis. All of the new brahmacharinis and I stayed in a tiny room, and we slept very little. They were such wonderful company. In fact, the whole family of devotees was exceptional. We all had so much affection and appreciation for each other, as well as a genuine desire to serve. It was a happy time. We felt empowered by Srila Prabhupada that we could do anything. That was the mood.*

**Yogesvara das**: Her time was just devotional service, and she was ready to do whatever was needed, whether going to ask for half-rotten fruits and vegetables from the market, or preparing the Sunday Feast, which was always incredible, or caring for the Deities—that was really her thing. I never think of Yamuna in a vacuum. It’s always Yamuna and the Deities—that image is inseparable for me. But interacting with the public was never her thing unless Srila Prabhupada asked her to do it... This was humility on a whole other level, because whatever she did was so alluring, so hypnotic, that everyone couldn’t help but watch her, but she never wanted to draw attention to herself.

**Mondakini devi**: On Deity worship she would always say that cleanliness and punctuality were the most important. She used to tell us that Srila Prabhupada would say that you should clean your own house as if your Spiritual Master and Krishna were going to come at any moment! Every little task was full of excitement. I think it is very important to pass this on to the young people—when they do, maybe they can taste that same joy of Krishna Consciousness that we tasted so long ago, and maybe we can taste it again too!

Yamuna wrote to Srila Prabhupada in early January about the temple activities, progress and mood, and he replied:

**I am so happy to know that the activities in London center are progressing with such great success. It is our desire that we shall always be engaged fully 24 hours in the service of Lord Krishna; in this way our lives will become perfectly joyful simply by singing and dancing and taking prasadam. So if you carry on your service to Radha and Krishna according to the prescribed rules, your love of Krishna will increase more and more; this you are seeing practically by the Grace of Krishna.**

**— LETTER TO YAMUNA, JAN. l6, 1970**

**Yamuna**: *Shyamasundara and Malati were living with George, and Janaki and Mukunda were living outside. So all I remember is being really, really busy. There was not a moment of “personal space” time. We used to pick flowers in Russell Square, and the temple devotees, both brahmacharis and brahmacharinis, would enthusiastically assist in each service. We felt so filled with blissfulness that someone collecting flowers or overripe fruits from the market felt as though their service was the most essential and wonderful thing.*

**Yogesvara das**: We would go shopping, and Yamuna had befriended all of the fruit and vegetable vendors in the market. We would take the Tube \[Underground\] and she would just be chanting Hare Krishna pretty much the whole time to herself, sometimes rather loudly. I would walk behind her, and she’d come up to the vendors in their stalls. She had this beatific smile that just melted your heart. The vendors all knew that she was going to be coming and had put aside for her all the bruised and slightly out of date produce that wouldn’t sell. I picked it up, and we’d get back to the temple with enough bhoga for the week—and it was all for free. That was how we made all the prasadam, with what she collected at the market

**Yamuna:** *Srila Prabhupada had instructed that the Deities were to be bathed and dressed in new clothes every day. But until the spring of 1970, Sri Sri Radha-Londonisvara remained in the clothes they were installed in while we worked on sewing a second set—dark blue with silver and gold trim, to be offered on Adwaita Acharya’s Appearance Day. At some point I phoned George Harrison to invite him, and immediately he asked if I would be making baked flat rice. “You know,” he said, “that kind of flat rice that you bake in the oven with milk and sugar and spices. It’s baked until the top is crusty and golden brown. Are you going to offer some of that?” I replied, “That’s a great idea, George. I’m sure Their Lordships would enjoy that.”*

*So for a second time, George arranged for a florist to deliver five gigantic flower arrangements for the walls, and four smaller ones for the altar. We had so many guests that day that for prasadam we filled the basement and the temple room. It was a grand festival—we had a long-awaited darshan of Their Lordships in a new dress, two enthusiastic kirtans and an amazing feast. The unrivaled favorite dish was the baked flat rice and strawberry rhubarb compote with clotted cream. George ate so many bowls that he eventually begged me not to serve him anymore.*

## Recording the “Govindam” Prayers

In January, George Harrison arranged studio time to record the long-anticipated Govindam prayers. The recording was to take place at Trident Studios. During the same period, promotional events were still being conducted for the “Hare Krishna Mantra” single, and Yamuna was fully engaged in her Deity service and seeing to the spiritual and material needs of the resident devotees.
