Giriraja brahmachari also spoke. Yamuna mentioned in her journal that Srila Prabhupada told her he was very fond of hearing Giriraja das speak because he would quote directly from the shastras. Yamuna sensed that Srila Prabhupada felt proud of his students—that despite being relatively new to the practice of bhakti, they would so fearlessly and boldly speak in front of all of these established yogis and then hold wonderful kirtan.

**Giriraja Swami**: After the first couple of days Srila Prabhupada himself didn’t go, but he was sending us, and now it seemed that he wasn’t anxious for us to have to go and listen to the Mayavadis speak either. Of course, in one sense it was encouraging the way Srila Prabhupada sent us in place of himself, because first of all it showed how much faith Srila Prabhupada had in us that we could carry on the program without him; and second of all, it made us feel that we were assisting Srila Prabhupada, not only by preaching, but by relieving him of having to come, so that he could do other work at that time.

## Prabhupada Begins His Discourses on the Life of Ajamila

A very special feature of the Indore experience for Yamuna devi was the beginning of Srila Prabhupada’s lectures from the first chapter of the Sixth Canto of Srimad-Bhagavatam on the life of Ajamila. These lectures, which carried on through Surat, Allahabad and Bombay, were immensely enlivening and encouraging—not only because they chronicled an amazing history, but because they gave a certain and secure hope that nothing is ever lost in devotional service. They would have an enormous and lasting effect on Yamuna’s devotional life.

**Who is a sadhu? One who is performing devotional service without deviation and with an undivided mind. He is a devotee.... Even if his behavior is not on the perfectional platform, he is a sadhu if he is unconditionally engaged in the service of Krishna. One who has taken shelter of Krishna as the Supreme Personality of Godhead will very soon become completely reformed. Sukadeva Goswami said that anyone who has taken shelter of Krishna and who is attracted by His transcendental qualities, be assured they will never be touched by Yamaraja or his assistants, not even in dreams.**

**— Yamuna’s journal, dec. 9, 1970**

**Devotional service is so nice that even if done a little, it will purify. Simply a little attraction for Krishna can purify one from all sinful reactions. Those who are attracted do not even dream about Yamaraja and his constables coming for them.**

**— Yamuna’s journal, dec. 10, 1970**

During most afternoons in Indore, Srila Prabhupada would hold darshans in his rooms. These were particularly memorable for the devotees because they were informal and intimate. Sometimes they included attendees from various impersonalist affiliations, and Srila Prabhupada would become especially animated in preaching to them. Yamuna recorded some of the exchanges and Srila Prabhupada’s commentary in her journal.

**Yamuna’s Journal**:

**December 9, 1970**

*It was about 4:30 pm, and a small group came to see Srila Prabhupada who were members of a family organizing the program we were attending. One of the ladies brought an offering of prasadam—a fried potato snack called aloo chidwa, made with fried cashews, raisins and spices. Srila Prabhupada took some and then distributed it to the other devotees there. Then he said to me, “Do you like these?” And I replied, “Oh, yes, they’re very, very tasty.” He said, “You should learn how to prepare this. I like it very much. My Guru Maharaja was also very fond of this chidwa—potato chidwa. Sometimes he would request it late in the afternoon. He was very fond of it.” Srila Prabhupada then spontaneously began speaking about Srimati Radharani. He began:*

*Srimati Radharani’s excellence is Her cooking. She can also sing and dance, but Her greatest service is Her cooking for Krishna. Mother Yasoda would ask Her personally to come and cook for Krishna and the cowherd boys. So, all in a line, She would feed them prasadam. Srimati Radharani keeps Krishna under Her control by Her cooking. It is so powerful—radhikara pakka anna vividha byanjana. In every art, Radharani is so expert, but Her cooking is Her superexcellence.*

*Then he began discussing his quarters in Vrindavan:*

*“I had lived in Vrindavan since 1956 until I went to the United States \[in 1965\]—in Vrindavan and in Delhi. In 1959, I retired from vanaprastha and took sannyasa. You have seen my rooms there in Vrindavan by the bhajan kutir of Rupa Goswami. Why have I taken all this risk? Simply because my Guru Maharaja requested me to do so.”*

*Then he said, “We have so many Mirabais. You have heard of Mirabai? Not just one Mirabai—Yamuna is number one Mirabai; Himavati is number two Mirabai; Madri is number three Mirabai—so many Mirabais.”*

*Late that same afternoon a gentleman brought Srila Prabhupada an article from one of the Indian weekly magazines about the London temple. It also included a picture of the beautiful Sri Sri Radha-Londonisvara Deities. Srila Prabhupada proudly displayed the article and picture to us, and his happiness at seeing Them highlighted in such a way was wonderful to witness. He had such deep affection for those Radha and Krishna Deities that he had personally brought to the temple and installed. We can’t possibly imagine the depth of how much this pastime meant to him, because he repeatedly stated how much his Guru Maharaja wanted a temple established in London. And so Srila Prabhupada had taken the service very seriously. As Srila Prabhupada held the article and picture, he smiled and said to me, “Oh, your Radha and Krishna have Their picture on the front page of the paper today.” And then he laughed very loudly. He said, “Yamuna, you will become as famous as the Yamuna River.” And he laughed and laughed. Of all the many expressions of Srila Prabhupada, his laughter was particularly unique. It was not loud or boisterous, but rose from within, almost like a chuckle in a base tone. You could not hear Srila Prabhupada laugh without laughing yourself. Even if the laughter was at my expense as a result of teasing me, I could not help but be charmed by it.*

*Prabhupada was always concerned that London remain a strong center under strong management, but unfortunately, he had been receiving reports at this time that the management was lacking. Several times we sat in front of him and he said, “What are you going to do? Decide amongst yourselves; something must be done. Someone must go to London and manage. This is disturbing me very much.” Still, somehow or other, no one among our party was able to decide what to do or who would go.*

**December 10, 1970**

*We had a great nagar sankirtan today from 6:oo am until 8:30 am on the city streets. Much to our ecstatic surprise, Srila Prabhupada arrived half way into it to lead the kirtan through the streets of Indore. He sang a melody himself three times to show how to chant responsively, and the remainder of the way I felt as though I was just gliding through the streets—immersed, ecstatic and fortunate. We traveled on the main roads and dirt roads. The morning sun caressed his golden frame, the trees bowed in humility, and his pure harinam sankirtan purified hearts on that smoke-filled morning in Indore.*

*I asked Srila Prabhupada, “Guru Maharaja, sometimes I am overwhelmed that you have accepted the service of such a wretched devotee as me.” Srila Prabhupada simply replied, “I have no choice. I have to accept your service. My Guru Maharaja wanted me to recruit Westerners into Krishna Consciousness, and I am simply following his instructions.”*

*One gentleman started to criticize my pronunciation of “Namah от vishnu padaya." I repeated twice “padaya” and Srila Prabhupada said, “paddya.” I said again “padaya,” and the gentleman said, “No, it is padaya.” Srila Prabhupada then said to me, “Never mind.” I apologized for being so fallen that I could not hear properly, and Srila Prabhupada then said, “No, your heart is pure; it does not matter this pronunciation. It matters how your heart is situated. Do not bother to study Hindi; it is an unnecessary waste of time. We can preach in English. You cannot convince by your scholarship, but if your heart is pure, you can convince them.”*

**December 11, 1970**

*Srila Prabhupada spoke about Krishna’s protection:*

*In 1933, there was an earthquake which caused havoc in Bihar, and one of my Godbrothers, Mr. Chatterji, whose home town was there, heard that everything had become demolished. So then he went to see his house, and only his house was saved. So a Krishna bhakta is never vanquished. One who is a devotee of the Lord should always be very sincere and execute his duty, and then he will never be in need. He will always trust that the Lord will protect him in any condition.*

*That afternoon Srila Prabhupada continued preaching in his rooms:*

*Reading and hearing from the Spiritual Master are both sravanam. Chanting and preaching is kirtanam. What I have heard from my Guru Maharaja, I am speaking, and similarly you must do the same thing. That is the way of spiritual knowledge. Spiritual knowledge is received from higher authorities, not by some electrical shock.... Knowledge is such a nice thing. The more you impart and distribute, the more you receive. Otherwise you will become envious. When you do not instruct others with what you have learned from your Guru Maharaja, you become envious.*

*This same instruction was repeated to me in Srila Prabhupada’s quarters in May of 197I in Calcutta.*

## He Teaches by Example—Srila Prabhupada with Maharaja and Maharani Holkar

Also on December n, 1970, Srila Prabhupada and some of the party visited Maharaja Tukoji Rao Holkar and Maharani Sarmistha Bhai Holkar at the Lal Bhag Palace. Yamuna used to comment that Srila Prabhupada was fearless in approaching prominent people for help in establishing temples or in making Life Members. During the visit, they held a nice kirtan before the royals, and then Srila Prabhupada preached vigorously to them, ultimately concluding with a plea for assistance. He was the consummate preacher, in that he could find the smallest thread of similitude between the Hare Krishna mission and whoever he spoke to, and then he would use that thread to try to encourage them to help spread Krishna Consciousness. In this case, Srila Prabhupada pointed out our relationship with the great ksatriya kings of the Bhagavad-gita:

**So this movement, from very old days, is beginning from the sun-god, and again five thousand years ago between Lord Krishna and the Pandavas, the pious kings. So this movement has got a very intimate relationship with the ksatriya kings. So I would request Your Highnesses ... If you could kindly give us a little place here in Indore, we can immediately start a nice center.**

**— CONVERSATION WITH MAHARAJA AND MAHARANI HOLKAR, DEC. 11, 1970**

Srila Prabhupada then cordially invited them to visit ISKCON temples, especially the one in London, and again requested their help:

**When Your Highnesses may visit London or New York or Los Angeles ... I invite you to our temple at 7 Bury Place near the British Museum. It is a very prominent place. And this girl in front of you, Srimati Yamuna devi, she and her husband Guru das are in charge of the temple. But because I have come to India, they are assisting me. She has seen the Prime Minister also, Indira Gandhi, and she \[Mrs. Gandhi\] is very much impressed with the Sankirtan Movement. So this Krishna Consciousness and patronization by the royal family is a very old relationship. So I came especially in Indore to see Your Highnesses—that if you give us some shelter we can immediately open a branch of the Krishna Consciousness movement.**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

During his informal talks with the Maharaja and Maharani, Srila Prabhupada used ingenious yet simple analogies to illustrate that God is a person. He said that to get water, a pump is needed, but in the coconut tree, each coconut encased a kilo of water—so who is pumping that water? He also pointed to a beautiful flower and asked who could paint it more perfectly. Yamuna noted that Srila Prabhupada was fully invested in his service of defeating the impersonalists—yet he did it with such style, it was stunning to simply observe and marvel.

A unique and fascinating addendum to this visit was Srila Prabhupada’s realization that not only was Maharani Sarmistha Holkar an American, born in Seattle, Washington, but she was considerably younger than her husband, who was an octogenarian at the time. Again taking the thread of similitude, Srila Prabhupada wanted Hansadutta das to ask the royals for ten lakhs of rupees to build a temple, and then he remarkably asserted that after the death of her older husband, the Maharani could become the president of the temple! Yamuna was astonished to see how expert and determined Srila Prabhupada was in the service of Krishna and his Guru Maharaja.

**And as soon as the king dies, the queen’s position is very precarious, almost finished. So if she becomes our president, she’ll continue to keep her honor and prestige. That’s a fact. She’s a good lady. We have no objection to make her the president of the local center. And she is American. She will be able to tackle these American boys and girls with motherly affection. And we shall keep her always in good respect so that throughout her life she shall be honored all over as she was with her husband. This is a fact.**

**— CONVERSATION, SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

**Yamuna’s Journal: December 12, 1970** — *Rascals want to join if you flatter them. But our process is to surrender. Become a blank slate and give up puffed-up ideas of knowledge. There is one music school in Germany where a student who knows music is charged more because there is so much to unlearn first. Like here, I have to spend hours removing these polluted ideas.... The slate must be clean from polluted ideas. In India the difficulty is we have to make them forget. Here they come to test me and waste my time. They only want my confirmation of their nonsense.... It is so difficult to speak the truth when they are so polluted, for they reject. To them it is so unpalatable.*Yamuna was uncertain of some of the distinctions between the understanding of the impersonalists and the Vaishnavas, especially in relationship to how to understand the eternal associates of Krishna in Vrindavan. Consequently, she questioned Srila Prabhupada on the distinction between seeing Krishna as one’s child and following in the footsteps of the residents of Vrindavan. It was important for her to understand because Srila Prabhupada had previously said that one view was Mayavadi and one was the proper Vaishnava concept:

**Yamuna: There is a mention in the Teachings of Lord Caitanya that a devotee in attachment selects one of the inhabitants of Vrindavan and follows in his footsteps in order to be successful in his own devotional service. Does that mean that one of our Spiritual Masters is an eternal representative of Vrindavan?**  
**Srila Prabhupada: What is that? Let me see.**  
**Yamuna: It says, “All inhabitants of Vrajabhumi, Vrindavan, are very dear to Krishna. A devotee in attachment selects one of the inhabitants and follows in his footsteps in order to be successful.”**  
**Srila Prabhupada: A devotee is devoted to the Vrindavan inhabitants. You don’t directly think of yourself that “I shall see Krishna as my son.”**  
**Yamuna: No.**  
**Srila Prabhupada: That is Mayavada.**  
**Yamuna: Yes.**  
**Srila Prabhupada: You have to follow in the footsteps of Yasoda Ma.**  
**Yamuna: Yes. You’ve told me that before.**  
**Srila Prabhupada: Then it will be successful.**

**— SRILA PRАВHAPADA - LILAMRTA**

**Yamuna’s Journal**:

**December 14, 1970**

*Duringtheafternoonvisiting hours, Srila Prabhupada was stressing that it is essential to accept a Spiritual Master. He said that one must approach the expert to know the science of Krishna Consciousness. That is the injunction of all Vedic literatures. In the Katha Upanisad, in the Bhagavad-gita, in the Srimad-Bhagavatam, the summation is that one must surrender to the Guru.*

*A very famous palmist and astrologer came to take darshan of Srila Prabhupada and asked if he wanted to have his palm read. Srila Prabhupada said, “No, I am finished with that. But you may read my disciples’.” Then in front of Srila Prabhupada, he read the palms of several of our members. Srila Prabhupada just sat and observed. So it soon became very clear that His Divine Grace was fully conversant in the science of palmistry, as well as the astrological science, and that he could understand the meaning of everything this palmist was saying. He would sometimes respond with very big eyes, and say, “Yes, yes, that is so.” I felt quite amazed. He seemed to know the future of many devotees, and as the astrologer would speak, sometimes the things would not be so pleasant to the ears of the disciple, and Srila Prabhupada would simply say, “Yes.” Looking into the palm of one of the sannyasis, the palmist told him he would not remain a sannyasi, which disturbed him immensely. When he took my palm, he said that I would become famous. Srila Prabhupada smiled, and his eyes grew very big, and he said, “Yes, then she can lead our World Sankirtan Party.”*

**December 15, 1970**

*This morning I was assisting Srila Prabhupada’s cook by preparing his breakfast, and I brought him some puffed rice, fresh yogurt and cut fruits. One devotee who was present said, “Does Krishna like that, Srila Prabhupada?” And Srila Prabhupada replied, “Krishna only wants your love and devotion. He likes anything, provided it is offered with love and devotion. Krishna is not in need of any breakfast. He is not hungry like us. He is self-sufficient. But He will accept our devotion. This knowledge is revealed in the scriptures and must be delivered by a bona fide Spiritual Master. Our Vaishnava Acharyas are the only hope.”*

*One day Giriraja das asked, “Srila Prabhupada, may we publish pictures of you without a tilak?” Srila Prabhupada replied, “Yes, my Guru Maharaja has been recorded without tilak. You have seen that picture where he is looking up from his books at his working table?” And I said, “Srila Prabhupada, I have also seen you look in that very same way, with the very same expression as in the picture of your Guru Maharaja.” And Srila Prabhupada replied, “All that glitters is not gold. You have only seen the glitter. He is the gold. I am only iron. Iron can never be gold.”*

**Prabhupada had come to Indore for the Gita Jayanti Mahotsava, but actually the Mahotsava was but a small part of his preaching in Indore. He met hundreds of people, made Life Members and friends. He had touched their lives. His presence in Indore would leave a lasting impression.**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

*I am but a small spark in the great conflagration of harinam sankirtan under the direction of Srila Prabhupada, yet I feel fulfilled, encouraged and nourished. Wherever Srila Prabhupada takes me on the next leg of the tour, or wherever he drops me off into unknown destinations, I have full faith in his protection, though I lack full surrender, as I lament when I am away from his association. My dear Lord, I feel the only cure for my disease is if You give me the ability to feel the presence of Srila Prabhupada at all times and in all places. It is asking a lot, and I am unworthy, yet I brazenly pray for such a gift. Please forgive me.*One of the sadhus who attended the Gita Jayanti, Baba Balmukund, eloquently summarized Srila Prabhupada’s contribution in Indore, especially in relation to his making Westerners take to Krishna bhakti:

**Baba Balmukund: I’ve seen many sadhus and great saints in this Gita Bhavan. I saw Srila Prabhupada also in the same place. I was very much impressed by Srila Prabhupada and his preaching. It was because Prabhupada had revealed the reality about bhakti because he was a pure bhakta that he could change the people of the West and give them another dress, he could give them another diet, and he could entirely change their culture and give them true bhakti. And this was the greatest thing Prabhupada has done. Let the world say as it likes, but he has done a marvelous thing regarding Lord Krishna’s bhakti. What Swami Vivekananda, Swami Ramtirtha and others could not do, Srila Prabhupada has done. It is a marvelous thing.**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

The next stop on the tour for Srila Prabhupada and the World Sankirtan Party was the Gujarati town of Surat. Srila Prabhupada had expressed to the devotees that the Gujarati people were in general very pious, and that they would be received very cordially there. He wrote to Guru das to come from Delhi and other devotees to come from Bombay, and they would inundate the streets of Surat with glorious harinam sankirtan. Yamuna was thrilled for this next adventure with Srila Prabhupada.

## Surat — “One God, Krishna; One Mantra, Hare Krishna”

Surat, located in the state of Gujarat, is the ninth largest city in India. The Mahabharata mentions Surat when telling the history of Krishna moving His cows from Mathura to Dwaraka. On the way, they stopped in Surat, and the cows’ footprints are said to be still visible at a pilgrimage site known as “Gai Pagli.” To this day the entire state of Gujarat is well known for its many worshipers of Krishna, especially in His form as a young cowherd boy, Bala Krishna.

Commercially, Surat is famous worldwide for its textiles and diamonds. It is said that 92% of the world’s diamonds are cut and polished in Surat, and the silks manufactured there are considered among the best in the world. The Gujarati culture is one of refinement—in everything from the innate piety of its people to its subtle and delicious cuisine.

Srila Prabhupada had previously met their Surat host, Mr. Bhagubhai Jariwalla, in San Francisco in 1968. At that time, Mr. Jariwalla invited Srila Prabhupada to come to Surat with his Western disciples, and Srila Prabhupada readily accepted the invitation.

**All over \[Gujarat\] there are so many Vaishnavas. So they should come forward to cooperate with me, then it will be a very nice organization. We want to establish one God, Krishna; one scripture, Bhagavad-gita; one mantra, Hare Krishna; and one work, service to the Supreme Lord. And people are responding.... I thank you very much once more for your nice letter and appreciation of my activities, and if you kindly cooperate with me, I shall be still more encouraged.**

**— LETTER TO MR. B. JARIWALLA, OCT. l6, 1968**

**Giriraja Swami**: Srila Prabhupada said that the people of Gujarat are naturally Krishna Conscious and gave the example that Krishna Consciousness will catch on according to the situation of the people. Just like if a spark falls on dry grass, it will immediately burst into flame, so the people of Surat were like dry grass, and as soon as Srila Prabhupada arrived, they burst into flames of appreciation. So we were staying in Mr. Jariwalla’s house, and somehow or other Srila Prabhupada had been in correspondence with him from before. And when we arrived at his house we found that he had a beautiful letter from Srila Prabhupada placed under the glass of his desk.

Yamuna was blissfully experiencing the glorious effects of harinam sankirtan with Srila Prabhupada, and her journal from this time is filled with superlatives. Her long-cherished desire to come to India and traverse its roads and byways with Srila Prabhupada on nagar sankirtan was being realized. She had been given a promise by Srila Prabhupada, and now that promise was being fulfilled:

**Yamuna**: *In San Francisco in 1967, Acyutananda das sent pictures from India of Srila Prabhupada on nagar sankirtan in Calcutta. And when we saw a picture of Prabhupada chanting in the streets, we all wanted to join him— to be there with him. In my case, it had been my desire from the beginning of my devotional life, and I prayed for the day that I would be in India with Srila Prabhupada. So when he returned to San Francisco, he asked me if I still wanted to go to India. Tears immediately came to my eyes, and I said, “Yes, Swamiji, very much.” He then told me not to worry, and that he would personally show me India on foot. I had some small inkling of what that meant when we saw the pictures in San Francisco, but it wasn’t until we actually came to India and walked and danced in the streets with Srila Prabhupada on nagar sankirtan that I realized something of what it meant. To walk in the footsteps of great Vaishnavas who chanted and danced in the streets before us, and to be able to touch the hearts of people along the way with harinam sankirtan, were simply the most wonderful and nectarean things. Srila Prabhupada assured me that he would take me to the highest place, and for me, nagar sankirtan with Srila Prabhupada was that place.*

For Yamuna, as well as for many of the others, Surat was the zenith of their nagar sankirtan experience in India. She revealed in later discourses and interviews that they had been treated with such respect and honor that she would simply be left in awe at the people’s piety and sincere service mood.

**Yamuna**: *I arrived in Surat on December 17, and the layers of my appreciation and devotional awareness in India were just continuing to grow. As we traveled and chanted together, our sankirtan party was becoming tighter and tighter, and our relationships sweeter and sweeter. This is another benefit of devotee sadhu sanga: the more you chant together, the more you want to exchange the six symptoms of love—giving and taking prasadam with each other, revealing and hearing each other’s minds, and giving gifts and receiving gifts. This is how Vaishnavas exchange love. And the more we did that, the tighter our party became, because through the heartbeat of it, if you chant Hare Krishna for seven hours a day, you’re not in the material world anymore, practically speaking.*

*So after Srila Prabhupada’s glorious preaching program in Indore, he brought us to Mr. Jariwalla’s house in Surat, Gujarat. This stay in Surat was one of the highlights of our entire sankirtan program in India. Mr. Jariwalla was an elderly gentleman who engaged his entire family in the pursuit of Krishna Conscious activities. We quickly realized that the whole of Surat was devotional, with many of the Vaishnavas worshiping Bala Krishna in the line of Vallabhacharya. They were genuine in their simple sincerity and enthusiastically participated in glorification of the Sankirtan Movement.*

*Mr. Jariwalla had a son and daughter in their fifties, and he was somewhere in his seventies, yet they were tireless in their desire to care for what turned out to be many young devotee guests. They were just wonderful, selfless people. The women ran the household with great efficiency. Their main floor was opened up for the devotees to preach to guests who came to the house during our stay there. Also on the main floor the devotees assembled to take prasadam. The husband and wife both took care of a great deal of the personal needs of the devotees, which included treating the near continual illnesses caused by the unfamiliar food, water and our unregulated schedule in India. They kindly gave Srila Prabhupada the entire second floor, which consisted of a front room, sleeping room, servant’s quarters, and his own balcony. The balcony turned out to be extremely important, because masses of Surat’s citizens would clamor outside to get a glimpse of him and, like the Pope, he would sometimes come out onto the balcony to acknowledge them.*

*On the third floor, the Jariwallas had given over the bedrooms for the ladies to reside in, and the fourth floor had been given to the men. The Jariwallas themselves moved onto the roof, so virtually the entire building, known as Motorcycle House, was offered to accommodate Srila Prabhupada and his World Sankirtan Party.*

*Although there were no pandal or other formal programs, Mr. Jariwalla brilliantly arranged for the sankirtan party to reach virtually all of the people of Surat, principally through advertisement of our nagar sankirtan schedule each day. Every time we went onto the streets for sankirtan, each route would be published ahead of time, both in the papers and by handbills placed throughout the city. Some of them said, “Welcome to the American and European devotees of Krishna.” So block after block they would know ahead of time when we were coming. It was the most welcome of all welcomes. The Mayor of Surat even declared a holiday on one of the days of our visit and closed the schools so the workers and children could come.*

*Each street along our route would hang decorations and receive us in a glorious manner. The streets were decorated with large plantain stocks every few feet. Strings of leaves and flowers were hanging across the roadways, which were also decorated with rice flour designs in various flower shapes. Scented flower garlands and sandalwood paste were offered to the devotees as we walked past. There were lamps and incense burning at various intervals.*

*All along the advertised route, from the second or third floor of a building on one side of the street to the second or third floor of the other side, the ladies would stretch across their colored saris. By their extending and tying a rope to each end and stringing them across the route, as you went down the streets there were clouds of cloth suspended above you in all of these different colored saris. It was their way of festooning the streets. Also, the people on the higher floors would throw flowers down upon us along the way. It was such a wonderful expression of respect and gratitude.*

**Kaushalya devi**: Surat was very special. The whole town was surcharged with Krishna Consciousness, and for some inexplicable reason they welcomed us—I mean everybody welcomed us wherever we went, but they welcomed us more in Surat than any place we ever went.... People would line the streets and garland us with so many garlands that we would have to start taking them off because they would be piling up, and in the middle of kirtan people would say, “Please come in my house.” And they would bring us in, feed us bananas or sweets or milk, and then we would go on. And it was so ecstatic; sometimes whole streets would be closed off, and we would set up a vyasasana for Prabhupada on a platform or stage. He would speak for hours, and ... the whole town shut down. It was like the town was ours while we were there—it was absolutely amazing. For me it was one of the most ecstatic moments of my entire life.

**Yamuna**: *In the evening they would arrange a program at a large square in the city, and the entire city square would be roped off so no cars could travel on it. And they would erect a large dais for Srila Prabhupada to sit on, and a sound system for him to speak with and for the devotees to have sankirtan.*

*So there were these two-fold activities to reach the people of Surat, all brilliantly arranged by the Jariwallas. And it appeared from Mr. Jariwallas lofty position as a respected and wealthy businessman that he was able to engage so many people to assist him in making our presence felt in Surat.*

*In addition to our city programs, Srila Prabhupada lectured in his room every morning from the Srimad-Bhagavatam on the Ajamila chapter in continuation of the discourses he had begun in Indore. And all the devotees and members of the Jariwalla household would attend that discourse. The household was a joint family system, so perhaps there were ten or twelve members who took advantage of hearing His Divine Grace. It was surely the perfection of their lives to be able to hear this series of lifechanging lectures in the mornings.*

*The arrangements for the care of Srila Prabhupada and the devotee were like nothing I had experienced before. I felt like I was on a higher planet. The prasadam was very healthful, very nicely prepared, and Srila Prabhupada seemed to enjoy it very much. On several occasions he instructed the women to find out how a particular preparation was made. For me this was especially enthusing because it was the first ti me I had direct experience of the delicate subtleties of superb Gujarati cuisine. I tried to make excuses to find my way into the kitchen as much as possible and watched with full attention and appreciation. Srila Prabhupada told me later that Mr. Jariwalla had brought this up to him—how Yamuna devi loves to learn this cooking.*

*All the devotees would line up on the floor so that we respected prasadam with Srila Prabhupada during the noon and evening meals. We took the morning meal by ourselves, and Srila Prabhupada ate later, in his room.*

## Sankirtan in Surat — “Prabhupada Appeared As if He Were the Rising Sunlight”

**Yamuna**: *So there was one nagar sankirtan in Surat that struck me in the heart just like lightning. It was the culmination and fulfillment of Srila Prabhupada’s words. Our group of sankirtan members had been informed that the next morning our nagar sankirtan would begin at 4:00 am and proceed through some of the main streets of the town as it was awakening. In India, of course, almost everyone rises early, unlike in the Western world. They take advantage of the coolness of the morning to bathe, clean and perform their spiritual practices. And so it was a very good time for nagar sankirtan. We had gathered and were all walking through the streets chanting very ecstatically. Hansadutta das led kirtan for an hour or so, and then I led. Also, Revatinandana das led for a while. It was very wonderful, and after about two hours we were all decorated externally with many garlands of flowers and internally with the glorious chanting of the Holy Names.*

*Sometime between 6:30 and 7:00 am, all of the people were out building their morning fires, and a haze of smoke stretched lazily across the early morning sky. The sun was just beginning to peek above the horizon on the long dirt road we were traveling on. By now a good-sized crowd of people were following behind us. And as we continued down this dirt road, it took a slightly upward slope that then crossed a river. As the road became a bridge, we began moving toward the center, and just as we reached the crest of the bridge, the sun rose across the trees, and Srila Prabhupada was standing in the dead center of the road with this light illuminating from all sides of him, just as if he were the rising sunlight itself. That picture is burned in my memory. It is still very emotional to think about this—there he was, with his hands raised and his robes draping on the ground, and he looked just like descriptions of Lord Chaitanya, he was so powerful and so beautiful. I remember all of the devotees simply went mad with ecstasy—first having this wonderful nagar sankirtan, and then seeing Srila Prabhupada in this surreal way. It was unbelievable.*

*And then His Divine Grace personally walked through the streets with us and chanted on nagar sankirtan until about 8:30 am. We had this little bullhorn microphone system, and I was leading kirtan at the time. Then Srila Prabhupada motioned for someone to get the bullhorn, and he began leading us in a new melody of the Hare Krishna mahamantra. We were simply transported—there is no other way to put it. Walking behind Srila Prabhupada, actually following in his footsteps as the party wound its way through the streets of Surat, was the promise, the fulfillment, the highlight and the perfection.*

*We had the added catalyst of being told each morning in Srila Prabhupada’s Ajamila lectures that no small amount of service rendered is ever lost, and here we were experiencing the fulfillment of that promise—we were being given a taste of the transcendental realm.*

**Giriraja Swami**: As we would pass down the street in procession, chanting Hare Krishna, the people would come out to offer us respects, so practically every half a block or every one block we would be stopped by some householder who would come up with an arati tray and offer arati to us with a flame, and put kumkum on our foreheads and place garlands around our necks. One day in particular it seemed that every few steps we were stopped and worshiped and garlanded, and pretty soon we started getting ten, fifteen, twenty garlands around our necks. And we didn’t know what to do with them because we had never had this experience. But it became so much that we started to have to take them off and throw them back to the people in the crowd, who would very eagerly grab for the souvenir or the prasadam from the devotees. So it was like another world altogether.

## The Palm Tree and the Madras

There is a wonderful few minutes of film of the devotees on nagar sankirtan in Surat. If the adage is true that a picture is worth a thousand words, then the film must be worth many millions. There is Yamuna alongside Kaushalya, each wearing identical, donated yellow saris. The faces of the devotees are elated and beatific, and one can see the many garlands adorning their necks and the masses of people following them.

A young man named John Greisser arrived in Surat late one evening. Hired by Asia Magazine to write photo-essays on the Hare Krishnas, he had already spent time in New York with the devotees and wanted to interview Srila Prabhupada and observe the devotees in the environment of India.

**Inside I found an old friend from the New York temple whose beaming face told me what I wanted to know—“Welcome to India!” That night I entered another world. First, my host, Mr. Jariwalla, gave me a garland of flowers and a silver tray filled with Indian cooked foods and fruits. When I had finished, my devotee friend took me in to meet his Spiritual Master, His Divine Grace A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada. Srila Prabhupada sat on a pillow, and he looked very stately. A devotee handed him a copy of Asia Magazine and told him I had done an article on the devotees. After looking through the article, he smiled and said, “Yes, that is very nice.”**

**— YADUBARA DAS, BACK TO GODHEAD, 1976**

**Yadubara das**: The summer before, I’d done a couple of magazine articles on the movement... I brought those magazine articles with me and showed Srila Prabhupada, and he liked them. He went through each of them page by page, much to my embarrassment, because one of them had some nudity in it. Srila Prabhupada didn’t bat an eye; he just kept going through until he reached the article on Krishna Consciousness. And then his comment was, “Even if we find gold in a dirty place, we take it.” The second day I was there Srila Prabhupada asked me, “So you’re going to become a devotee?” I couldn’t imagine myself wearing the robes and the shaved head, so I said no, although inwardly I felt I was. So Srila Prabhupada’s reply was, “Then you cannot stay.” I was naturally shocked. And I didn’t leave; I stayed with the party for two months. Every day I’d sit in Srila Prabhupada’s room, and invariably when a visitor came in he’d introduce me. He would say, “This is Mr. John; he is from America. He is an expert photographer.” In this way Srila Prabhupada encouraged me, and he could understand I was becoming a devotee gradually.

Although he had no intention of either becoming a devotee of Krishna or a disciple of Srila Prabhupada, John did indeed become “captured by Krishna.” Srila Prabhupada’s presentation of the philosophy of Bhagavad-gita and Srimad-Bhagavatam, as well as his reception and the wonderful kirtans and programs they attended, convinced him that he had found his path to the Supreme Godhead. Prior to his arrival, most of the pictures in India had been taken by Guru das, a keen photographer. He can be seen in the film running ahead of the sankirtan party and then turning and quickly taking pictures. Now, with the addition of John in their party, many more photos would be taken, among them a much-loved series Yamuna referred to as the “palm tree mudra” pictures. In an interview in 1994, Yamuna brought up the photographs with Yadubara das.

**Yamuna: It was outside of the city \[Surat\]. Tell me what you noticed about that palm tree.**  
**Yadubara das: I just remember Prabhupada’s gestures. They were so animated.**  
**Yamuna: I went back to the archives and looked at them, and I counted that there were over twenty separate mudra shots that you got of Prabhupada during that lecture. And afterwards, I remember asking Srila Prabhupada about them. I said, “Srila Prabhupada, you did so many things with your hands today in the lecture. Did that have some significance?” And he said, “Yes, those are called mudras. My Guru Maharaja was very expert in expressing himself through mudras. He said that each one has a different significance according to shastra. And they are used to make a point.”**

**— YADUBARA INTERVIEW, 1994**

**Yamuna**: *Earlier I had asked Srila Prabhupada what the hand positions on the Deities meant, so I knew something about mudras. And so, when we were having different Deities made, I would ask him what mudra he wanted for the particular Deity. I remember once asking about the significance of the mudra of the Srimati Radharani of Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati in Mayapur.*

Although Yamuna did not speak in the interview of that particular mudra, Sri Gandarvika in Mayapur beautifully poses in a flower-holding mudra, with both hands held forward in open fists as though carrying bunches of flowers.

## Yamuna Expresses the First “Stirrings of Dissatisfaction”

Through the experience of traveling and living in India with Srila Prabhupada, Yamuna began to understand the high degree of etiquette ingrained in the Indian culture. Contrasting that with the occasional lack of good manners shown by some of the party from the West, she felt that they sometimes embarrassed Srila Prabhupada by not understanding the proper etiquette expected of a guest in India. Of course, this was not the responsibility of any one individual, but rather the result of contrasting value systems. In India, a guest was to be honored and treated as god-like; in the West, the standard is more informal.

**Giriraja Swami**: Although Mr. Jariwalla and his family were perfect Indian hosts, we were not really experienced in how to deal with respectable Hindu families. So just like one of the main functions which brought us in contact with our hosts was taking prasadam. They would always set up very nice plates for us, and we would sit in lines on the floor to take prasadam. It is the Indian custom or Vedic conception that the guest should be received or treated like God, and therefore they would personally come and serve us prasadam—kneeling down and offering us whatever we wanted.... After preparing the whole meal for us they would ask, “Is there anything else you would like?” And of course, in Vedic culture one is not aggressive or demanding, but in our Western culture we are very aggressive and demanding. So someone would say, “I want this,” or “I want that,” and then they would go and have to cook another preparation and serve that to us. But it’s also the Vedic culture for the guest not to impose or make demands upon the host. But since we didn’t know that part of it, we were demanding more and more, and then we started getting reports—perhaps originally from Srila Prabhupada and passed down through Hansadutta—that we shouldn’t be so demanding of our hosts, that we should be better guests, and that whatever they offered us, we should accept very respectfully and very cheerfully.

Srila Prabhupada wrote in the Caitanya-caritamrta of his father’s standard for receiving guests in his childhood.

**According to the Vedic principles, there must always be a guest in a householder’s house. In my childhood I have actually seen my father receive not less than four guests every day, and in those days my father’s income was not very great. Nonetheless, there was no difficulty in offering prasadam to at least four guests every day. According to Vedic principles, a householder, before taking lunch, should go outside and shout very loudly to see if there is anyone without food. In this way he invites people to take prasadam. If someone comes, the householder offers him prasadam, and if there is not much left, he should offer his own portion to the guest. If no one responds to his call, the householder can accept his own lunch. Thus the householder’s life is also a kind of austerity.**

**-CAITANYA-CARITAMRTA, MADHYA 3.41**

Whenever the devotees were chanting on nagar sankirtan or with Srila Prabhupada in any capacity, Yamuna felt ecstatic and in harmony with the group; but perhaps due to the persistent illnesses within the party, or the jostling for leadership among some of the men, she began feeling stirrings of dissatisfaction. Also, on the morning of December 24, Srila Prabhupada had mildly chastised her in the temple. Because of her sensitive nature, these chastisements, however mild, weighed heavily on her. Never one to be able to camouflage or hide her feelings, Yamuna’s disaffection was noticed by Srila Prabhupada immediately.

**Yamuna’s Journal**: **DEC. 25 1970** — *I had been feeling some unhappiness from difficulties with the devotees in charge here. Srila Prabhupada saw me after I had been emotional, and rather sternly asked if everything was all right. “Yes, Srila Prabhupada,” I replied, not wanting to have to explain myself. “What is the matter?” he said. I answered: “I am feeling very sorry to have displeased Your Divine Grace yesterday morning for my commenting about touching japa beads in front of the Deities. And your chastising me so harshly makes me very uncomfortable and saddened.”*

*Srila Prabhupada replied, “I have not chastised you. Why do you manufacture these things? I do not even know what you are talking about? Oh, the beads. You should be equipoised—that is answered in Bhagavad-gita—in honor and dishonor. You should always be joyful and happy in Krishna Consciousness.”*

*The next morning, Srila Prabhupada asked me, “How are you feeling?” I replied, “I have been serving maya for twenty-four hours.” Srila Prabhupada twisted his whole face and said, “Why do you waste your time? Kick her. Kick maya away. How are you enjoying the lectures of Ajamila? A person who can explain Srimad-Bhagavatam has reached the highest perfection of transcendental knowledge—there is nothing beyond Srimad-Bhagavatam. But you go to kirtan, and we will discuss later.”*

## Notes from. Yamuna’s Journal in Surat

**Yamuna’s Journal:**

**December 22, 1970**

Weare struck with the physical beauty of Srila Prabhupada. He always advertises himself as a Vaishnava, a devotee of Krishna. His dressing is meticulous. He is always very well groomed, with beautiful, clear tilak on. And his hand is always in his bead bag. As he sits to greet people, one is struck with his inconceivable beauty, and how he carries himself.

Srila Prabhupada said that persons who give themselves to anyone are called magnanimous. And no one can be more magnanimous than Krishna because He is always prepared to give Himself completely to His devotee. Even to one who is not a devotee, Krishna in His form of Lord Chaitanya is prepared to give Himself and grant deliverance. So this perfectly describes Srila Prabhupada during his stay in Surat. He is always delivering Krishna to everyone he speaks to. He can affect people’s minds simply by his great potency.

**December 23, 1970**

Prasadam at the Jariwalla’s usually involves misri \[sugar candy\] and peanuts served as snacks. The main meals are variegated—breakfasts can be sevya khir and hot bundis, iddli, rice and urad dal dhokra, apple jam, mango jam, puris, rice flakes, curd, milk and fruits. Gujarati cooking is excellent, usually spiced with mustard seeds and coriander. A typical meal for eating out at lunch is mung dal with curry leaves, coriander and mustard, shrikhand, puris, roti, poppers, rice served two-thirds through the meal, potatoes, cauliflower or a dry vegetable, plain curd, pickle, kadhi and a wet aubergine vegetable. Not many sweets were served at lunch—perhaps a Gujarati laddu made with gur.

**December 24, 1970**

I have been observing that Srila Prabhupada is chanting japa all the time. Whether during visiting hours, walking, riding in the car, standing or sitting, his fingers are always moving within his saffron bead bag.

This is Ekadasi, and Srila Prabhupada gave an amazing Bhagavatam class about how Krishna makes us remember and forget, and that is His mercy. He told the story of how Indra became a hog and did not want to leave when he was called back to the heavenly planets.

Krishna is so merciful to remind us about our spiritual identity, He gives knowledge of His relationship, He comes and personally delivers Bhagavad-gita and requests us to give up the life of the hog, and “Please come back to Me.” He is not happy that the living entities are rotting like the hogs. He sends His representatives, His favorite sons, to bring the living entities back home, back to Godhead. Only Vedic literature is complete.... In Kali Yuga people deviate from Vedic rules, but the information is there. The Vedas state that God is a witness, and there are many other witnesses. The first witness is the sun—you cannot conceal yourself from the sun—then fire, then sky, then air, the moon, the junction between day and night (there are three junctions, three Gayatri mantras: morning, noon, evening); the ten directions are witnesses. According to Manu Samhita, these personalities can understand the psychological activities of the mind—what you are thinking, feeling and willing.

**December 25, 1970**

We have been in Surat since December 17. There is tremendous fanfare here for Lord Chaitanya’s Sankirtan Movement, and the inhabitants are primarily devotees.

During conversations Srila Prabhupada said, “Do not cut down desire; just purify desire. One must be free from designation and take the eternal position of Krishna’s servant.”

**December 27, 1970**

Srila Prabhupada said: If you read Bhagavad-gita with some commentary, you become even more of a rascal. Their business is how to avoid God. That is their whole scheme. Kamsa’s policy: how to kill Krishna. And even though he was very cautious, he was killed by Krishna. Krishna’s policy is always victorious; therefore take the shelter of Krishna.

Srila Prabhupada’s garlands are nicely made of roses and white jasmine with silver threads of tinsel. He is always given one-foot-round pillows to lean on and mattresses covered daily with clean cloths. Srila Prabhupada said, “This is the real way to take rest if you want to stretch out your legs.”

Wherever we are invited, such care is taken by our hosts for serving guests. There are special serving containers which keep the prasadam always hot. People sit on grass place mats and eat on wooden tables. There are rice flour designs on the floors, whether cement, marble or cow dung.

In the Srimad-Bhagavatam lecture that morning, Srila Prabhupada said:

There are many varieties of these three modes of nature. And each living entity is under the control of these modes. From goodness we can change our position to a high quality. This can be done—like a diseased man is cured if he follows the direction of a physician. Shastra is there, treatment is there, and Krishna Consciousness is the panacea for all diseases. Simply by chanting Krishna’s name one is freed from the stringent laws of material nature. So this is not a story. It is seen practically in the Western countries. As there are these varieties now, similarly in the next life you can understand one must have such and such body ... So just as you can suggest that in certain seasons there are certain effects, similarly, one who follows dharma or adharma, they will have such and such body. That takes a little intelligence to understand. As we know, there are many witnesses; similarly Paramatma in your heart is witnessing, so according to your desire, you will have a certain type of body. You are working, but you are working for your next body.

Simply to understand “I am Brahman” is for a devotee as good as hell; and the karmi’s aim is to go to heaven. That is for us like a flower in the sky—a phantasmagoria that has no existence. The yogis try to control the mind and senses up to samadhi. Senses are like snakes; when they touch something it becomes poisonous. But for devotees they are poisonous, but the teeth are broken. If the venom is gone, there is no more danger. You must not control senses, but control the poisonous teeth of the senses. That is bhakti—to transfer the work for Krishna. Krishna’s servants work so hard they sometimes fall sick. Bhakti is to apply the senses to the master of the senses, Hrishikesha. Dovetail your senses to the Supreme Master....

When one is no longer on the material platform, how does he become on the spiritual platform? Because by rendering service always, one can gradually become a devotee. But we must accept the process. Srila Rupa Goswami says we must be:

- 1\. Patient;
- 2\. Enthusiastic—we must go on with our prescribed duties;
- 3\. Confident to serve the Spiritual Master who represents Krishna and follow his orders;
- 4\. Determined to follow the rules and regulations of devotional practice;
- 5\. Honest—not superficially, that I am surrendered to you, but at heart something else;
- 6\. Desirous to always keep the association of devotees.

**January 1, 1971**

Conversations with Srila Prabhupada: If one falls from Krishna Consciousness, there is no loss, and one who does not take to Krishna Consciousness, what does he gain? One who takes to Krishna Consciousness to accept the shelter of Krishna or to execute devotional service, but is not mature and could not follow strictly the rules and regulations, can be attracted to maya to fall down. What mistake is there? There is no mistake. But one who strictly follows their occupational duty without Krishna Consciousness does not make any profit. What is his gain? Nothing—he is simply laboring hard. Becoming anything without Krishna Consciousness, you are the loser. Others may manufacture some bogus dharma, but Bhagavad-gita confirms this.

**January 2, 1971**

Conversations with Srila Prabhupada: In a Hindu family, the system is that some foodstuffs are always kept in reserve for any guest who comes. In my childhood my father kept fifteen maunds of rice in stock. Rice, ghee, potato— that is the system. And for all these services he was not proud. These are only qualifications: friend to all living entities, not that you offer respects only to father and then cut the throat of an animal... By meeting a Vaishnava one becomes successful, full of sense, engaged in the supreme quality of occupation. People are coming and bringing so many fruits and sweets; you do not work, and you get fruits. We must be confident that Krishna will send food. Like Mrigari the hunter, He will take care of us. If you chant the Hare Krishna mantra and distribute prasadam, you will get everything.

**January 3, 1971**

On the morning of January 3, after sankirtan at about 11:30 am, I was in the women’s quarters, and Srila Prabhupada’s servant, Nanda Kumara, called me and said that Srila Prabhupada wanted to speak with me.

So I immediately went down to Srila Prabhupada’s quarters and paid my obeisances. No one else was in the room, and Srila Prabhupada said, “Come here.” So I came rather close to his desk—perhaps four or five feet. And he said, “No, come here—closer.” So I moved very close to Srila Prabhupada’s desk, and he had his head resting within his hand, and his hand was holding the bridge of his nose; his head was down, and he was leaning on his knee. And he said to me, “Now, tell me what has happened in England.” This issue was still very much concerning His Divine Grace. Now he had brought the subject matter up several times to the men, and there was no solution, and so for some reason His Divine Grace asked me this question.

Though I was always reluctant to be placed in this position, I tried to explain to Srila Prabhupada the progression of some of the difficulties that had come by having too many authorities in one place. And how each devotee, to the best of his ability, tried to listen to the Spiritual Master, follow his instructions and distribute his teachings. But sometimes there were bound to be differences. In the fall of 1970, before we had come to India, Srila Prabhupada had created the Governing Board, and the two GBC members in Europe and England had different ways of managing, and this was creating havoc.

So Srila Prabhupada said, “I am making an experiment with this Governing Board. I do not know if it will succeed, but I am making the experiment. My Guru Maharaja had the idea for a Governing Board. And although he tried to implement it, it was a failure within the Gaudiya Math. And I am also trying to implement. But if there is no success, then once again I will have to take all managerial responsibilities. You know, I was planning that you and Govinda dasi would be as one Governing Board member. Half.” I was very surprised and said to Srila Prabhupada, “I don’t think this would be very successful, because I have a female body, and it simply wouldn’t work.” And he said, “Yes. Tamai Krishna has also agreed. It will not work. But I am always thinking that if you had not left London, there would not have been these problems. So do you think that you and Guru das should return to London?” I replied, “Whatever you think is best, Srila Prabhupada; we can serve in any capacity that you require.” And he said, “No, you will stay where you are. We will have Mukunda take over the management of the temple.”

Srila Prabhupada remained in Surat from December 17 until January 4, and at this time there was a massive program in Allahabad, the Ardha Kumbha Mela. We left by train with a two-day stopover in Bombay, and then Srila Prabhupada went on to Calcutta. We then next met him in Allahabad.

**The entire Surat experience gave Yamuna and the other devotees perhaps their clearest insight into what living in a Krishna Conscious culture would be like. Many years later she would remember that time and place with great feeling, in interviews and among close friends. I found a draft of a letter to the Jariwallas in one of Yamuna’s collections, and it expresses her mood and appreciation beautifully:**

**January 3, 1971**

Dear Vaishnava Sadhu Jariwallas, I do not know how to say how much I learned from your hosting of our party in Surat. I only know that it changed me. I learned so much from you that I hope to use in my service to my Guru Maharaja—how to serve selflessly, how to show the utmost humility at all times, how to tolerate our sufferings and roughness, how to show concern and care for us at all times. I do not know if I can ever be such Vaishnavas as yourselves, but you are like a living university of how to serve, and I pray that a million blessings are returned to you for your selfless service. Everything was simply the best—the cooking (I am sorry if I made a nuisance of myself in your kitchen), the prasadam, the cleanliness, but most of all you and your pure example of serving Krishna and the Vaishnavas. At your lotus feet, Yamuna devi dasi.

In summation, Nanda Kumara das, who was serving Srila Prabhupada in Surat, wrote an insightful remembrance of the Surat experience:

**Nanda Kumara das**: We were guests, all 20 or 25 of us, in the home of a retired banker, Sri Bhagubhai Jariwalla, who took care of us in a most wonderful way. We were all young Westerners, still filled with Western habits, even though we were learning the Vedic culture and doing our best to apply it in our daily lives.

Every day, we would be served wonderful prasadam by Mr. Jariwalla and his extended family. None of them ever took any prasadam until every one of us had been fully satisfied. Sometimes there was nothing left after our voracious appetites had been satiated, and still they would serve every last bit of it to us if we would accept. Often they would have to cook again for their family, sometimes many hours after their normal meal time.

For a good part of the time we were there, many of us had campylobacte-rial dysentery from ingesting contaminated water or food, and were completely out of commission. Many of us were so sick that we could not even take care of our own personal cleanliness very well. It was quite intense. Not only did Mr. Jariwalla and his family serve us with unlimited prasadam, they also cleaned up after us and did all our wash daily, which was often gross.

There were a few young and passionate brahmacharis present who for some reason had not yet developed proper Vaishnava etiquette.... Never once did the Jariwalla family take offense. All they did was humbly serve the devotees with a smile on their face and Krishna in their heart. On the last day of our stay, Mr. Jariwalla asked if we could all gather in Srila Prabhupada’s room. I can still remember it clearly, and the powerful effect it had on me then, as well as many other times over the years.

Here is what he said to us, after giving each of us an envelope with a thank-you card and 5I rupees: “My family and I are so honored and blessed to have had the chance to serve all of you, especially Your Divine Grace Srila Prabhupada. Please forgive us for the many offenses we have committed against you.” At this point he began to cry, bowed down and paid his humble obeisances to every devotee present. Srila Prabhupada looked at each of us, looking deep into our eyes and soul, and said very powerfully, “This is a real Vaishnava. He sees no faults, even though there may be many. You should all take his pure example and follow it as much as possible.”

## A Short Bombay Stopover

**Giriraja Swami**: On the train we met a Surat factory owner named Mr. Kotack, who actually had his house in Bombay. We explained to him that we had no place to stay in Bombay, so he invited us to stay at his house at Chowpatty. We were all thinking how wonderful India is, that wherever you go you meet some nice devotee, and he offers to take care of you.

**Yamuna**: We all left Surat by train for Bombay on January 4,1971, and after a two- or three-day layover, we went on to Allahabad. Before we left Bombay, Srila Prabhupada flew to Calcutta before coming to Allahabad himself. In Bombay, we connected with a Life Member we had known in London, Mr. Ramachand Chabria, who owned the Sea Palace Hotel near India Gate, v

**Giriraja Swami**: Mr. Chabria had known the devotees in England because Guru das had started our center there. Now Guru das and the rest of us went to visit Mr. Chabria, and we explained our difficulty—that we had no place—and he offered that we could stay with him at his Sea Palace Hotel, which was vegetarian and which didn’t serve drinks or anything like that. So at that time there were Shyamasundara, Guru das, Rsi Kumara, Tusta Krishna and myself in one suite, and in the other room were Yamuna and Malati. So during this period Yadubara, who at that time was John Greisser, also came to Bombay from Surat.

In preparation for writing her memoir, in 2006 Yamuna and I visited many of the places of Srila Prabhupada’s pastimes in Bombay, one of which was the Sea Palace Hotel. We walked on the same sidewalks where he had walked, gazed at the harbor he gazed at, and felt that connection that comes from time standing still even amidst the general hubbub of Mumbai. The following are some of Yamuna’s notes from the 2006 visit.

**Yamuna**: *The Sea Palace Hotel is nestled in between Victorian buildings on Appolo Bunder Marg overlooking the Bombay Harbor. Srila Prabhupada had a nice suite on the top floor, with a sea breeze coming off the ocean. Today it still looks much the same as in 1971. The name is also the same as when Prabhupada was there. It fronts a wide boulevard, and boats float in the harbor. Srila Prabhupada would take his walk along that broad sidewalk across from the hotel. It gave him just a short time to rest before going on to the massive and austere Ardha Kumbha Mela in Allahabad.*

*The steps are still black granite; there are flower boxes on the sides, and mosaics on the floor. The small hallway with inlaid marble that Srila Prabhupada walked on appears as it was. The foyer is white and red marble with a small desk. In those days, I was not so focused on the scenery, but of course, Prabhupada would have walked by the Gateway to India and the nearby Taj Mahal Hotel. What I do remember is where the vendors were located, readily available to enable me cook or shop for Srila Prabhupada. When you walk out of the Sea Palace Hotel, forty or fifty yards to the right is the Radio Club, and just next to that are many little stalls which sold vegetables and fruits. So early in the morning, Srila Prabhupada would send me down to get his fruits for breakfast; then I’d go into the kitchen and cut them. Now this was a busy vegetarian restaurant kitchen. There was constant activity there. Still, I would boldly go into the kitchen and say that my Guru Maharaja required this preparation made in such and such a way. Sometimes I would cook myself. They were typically generous and kind in allowing me to interrupt their schedule in the kitchen. But my focus was on Srila Prabhupada, and I was prepared to make a nuisance of myself if needed for his service*

On the morning of January 5,1971, at 6:30 am, Srila Prabhupada spoke to a small gathering about the ongoing managerial problems in the London temple, this time in relation to book distribution. Their strategy was to use advertisements to try to sell Srila Prabhupada’s books, and he was not in accord with this. He again expressed a desire for an experienced manager to return there, but the devotees had just recently arrived in India on the much-anticipated World Sankirtan Party tour and were not enthusiastic to leave Srila Prabhupada’s association:

**They are trying to sell by advertising, but you cannot distribute by advertising. That is the wrong policy. These books are managed and sold by propaganda work. Unless one is interested in Krishna, he will not buy. You have to create propaganda interest. Simply advertisement will get no result. Will someone go back to London? You do not sound very much hopeful.**

**— Yamuna’s journal**

Then Srila Prabhupada began speaking about sincerity and how it relates to our success in being able to give Krishna bhakti to others. He especially spoke about the importance of following the process of devotional service to gain spiritual potency:

**Our success is only possible when we are very much sincere and spiritually strong. Of course, in any dealing, both parties must be sincere. The hearing party must be sincere in understanding transcendental subject matter, and we must also be qualified that we can present it. Then everything is all right. Because people do not know about Krishna. They know kirtan, so they speak as authority. What the people do not know is that this Krishna Consciousness is a process. Without the process, the kirtan is simply a sound vibration. It has no real effect. Bhaktivinoda Thakur has said that it is simply like the vibration of the alphabet: ABCDEFG. If you vibrate AB or KR, it is the same. It is the process that is important, \[emphasis Yamuna’s\]**

**— Yamuna’s journal**

Later, Srila Prabhupada sat with the devotees and the family of Ramachand Chabria and spoke about the position of the Spiritual Master:

**Caitanya-caritamrta also says, “The Vaishnava Acharya—his activities are never to be understood, even by the wisest of men.” (Then Srila Prabhupada spoke that in Bengali.) The Acharya is completely surrendered to Krishna. He has taken the shelter of Krishna, being freed from all material entanglements. Everyone has got some material desire to fulfill, but the Acharya, the Guru, he has no such desire. That is the symptom of the Acharya. He has no more desires to fulfill in this material world. He is finished with all the business of material satisfaction, and he has taken a full bath in the ocean of transcendental sound vibration.**

**One should surrender to such a Spiritual Master, and when one is actually serious about inquiring into transcendental subject matter, he will fall at the lotus feet of such an Acharya. Otherwise there is no use inquiring from the Acharya. The point is that one must be interested in transcendental subject matter. So many people come and talk and waste valuable time. If you find an Acharya to whom you can surrender, you do not need to canvas any longer. In spiritual science, there is no bluffing. Everything must be very clear cut, or everything will not come out satisfactorily.**

**— Yamuna’s journal**

## The Pomegranate Juice Pastime

Yamuna often told the pomegranate juice story as an example of how one had to expect the unexpected with Srila Prabhupada. In one form or another, a similar scenario played out between Srila Prabhupada and Yamuna several times in India. Yamuna would think her service requirements were concluded; she would then leave or take rest, and somehow Srila Prabhupada would reappear and request her service. When she would finally arrive, he would sometimes say, “Where did you go? Why were you not here?” Sometimes it would be in the nature of teasing; sometimes not.

**Yamuna**: *We stayed a short two or three days in Bombay, and then Srila Prabhupada left for his flight to Calcutta (or so I thought). So I had been engaging extensively in services and was both tired and sick with dysentery. Some pomegranates had been offered that day to Srila Prabhupada, and for some reason I remembered them after he left. So I went to the kitchen, made myself pomegranate juice, offered and drank it, and then just sat on the sofa and kicked up my heels. I remember just sitting back on the sofa with feet up, and then the telephone rang. The voice on the other end simply said, “Srila Prabhupada is coming back and will be there in ten minutes.” And for some strange reason, I thought of the pomegranates. And wouldn’t you know, as soon as he walked in the door, he asked for pomegranate juice. It was mystical—somehow he knew I had taken the pomegranates. So, of course, there were no pomegranates left. I had to race out and try to find some, and when I finally did, someone came down to the kitchen and said, “Prabhupada wants to know why you are taking so long to make his pomegranate juice.” And when I finally walked into his room with the juice, he said, “Why have you taken so long for my juice?” and then he laughed. He knew what was going on and was just trying to tease me. He was sometimes playful like that, and seemed to enjoy keeping his servants in a state of uncertainty—“Oh, how will I get this service done for Srila Prabhupada?” So it was part of the intimacy—the incomparable personality of Srila Prabhupada.*

## Ardha Kumbha Mela in Allahabad

In the short time they had been in India, Sril a Prabhupada’s World Sankirtan Party had made an immediate and pronounced impact. No other swami, guru or guide from India had ever succeeded in not only inducing masses of young people from the materialistic West to dedicate themselves to an orthodox Vedic practice—bhakti-yoga—but also in bringing them back to India, chanting and dancing enthusiastically. Knowing that a rare and auspicious event, the Ardha Kumbha Mela, was occurring in Allahabad in mid-January, Srila Prabhupada felt it would be a perfect venue at which to introduce his Western students to the masses of people who would attend.

**Kumbha Mela is the greatest congregation of human beings on earth. Every twelve years in Allahabad, sadhus and pilgrims from all over India gather at the Triveni, the confluence of the three holy rivers Ganges, Yamuna and Sarasvati. And at an auspicious time that assures the worshiper liberation from the cycle of birth and death, as many as fifteen million people enter the sacred waters. A smaller version, the Magh Mela, takes place annually, during the month of Magh (December-January). January of 1971, however, happened to fall halfway through the twelve-year cycle from one Kumbha Mela to the next, and the Mela was known as Ardha Kumbha Mela. Millions would attend, and Srila Prabhupada decided to take advantage of the opportunity and attend the Mela with his disciples to preach....**

**The Mela committee had given ISKCON a good location near one of the entrance gates, and a few of the experienced devotees engaged workers in setting up the tents. ISKCON’s pandal was large and brightly colored, with three smaller tents close by—one for the men, one for the women and one for Srila Prabhupada. A flimsy shack of corrugated tin served as a kitchen. Prabhupada was to arrive the next day, and the devotees worked quickly putting down hay and rolling out durries (large carpets of coarse cotton fabric). The devotees would have to build their own fires, gather their own vegetables, wash their own clothes and do everything for themselves—all in the middle of a cold, barren sand flat. It was a far cry from being served like princes at a Life Member’s home.**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

## Yamuna’s Description of the Mela — “An Ocean of Tents"

For most of the devotees, the Mela was their first experience of seeing the divergent varieties of spiritual practices displayed in India. Whether it was the naked Shivaites covered in crematorium ashes, the mystics who pierced their bodies with various sharp objects, or the varieties of sadhus with their distinctive tilak and other bodily markings, the whole experience was eye-opening and often outrageous. In addition, if you tried to imagine the entire population of New York City crammed into Central Park, it would give some idea of the logistical and other problems faced there. Electricity was nonexistent much of the time; the sanitation was unmentionable; and the act of trying to bathe in the holy waters was an immense challenge. Yamuna addressed some of her first perceptions.

**Yamuna**: *An ocean of tents had been erected to house the millions of attendees, and our camp was perhaps the only camp out of the entire festival with Radha and Krishna Deities. We had a prestigious location near one of the entrance gates to the temporary city of pilgrims, so we were perfectly situated for facilitating great numbers at our programs.*

*I believe that we had five or six tents—one for Srila Prabhupada, one for the temple, one for the sannyasis, one for the other men and one for the women. There was also one rather shabby metal structure where we cooked. During the Mela, Srila Prabhupada had a twenty-four-hour guard around his tent because he said that it was possible we could have intruders into our camp. We were a great novelty. And there were people coming from all classes of society within this multifarious arena. Srila Prabhupada’s tent was in the very center of the living quarters. There was an outer tent, and then a corridor of cloth, and then the inner tent that Srila Prabhupada stayed in, and it had one small kerosene heater. As I recall, Srila Prabhupada’s tent had occasional electricity—it would go on and off. So we kept these kerosene heaters because at night it would become very cold, while the days were clear and warm.*

*I shared a tent with Himavati, Malati, Kaushalya and Madri. The floor of the tent was covered with kusa grass, and we were off the floor with our little trunks underneath us—the metal being the only thing that kept us warm. But as the morning sun peeked through the clouds hanging in the soft blue sky, the chill was warmed by the many fires that burned. Thick smoke then filled the air. Everyone tended to congregate around whatever small fires there were, whether made in little metal containers or an old wok. Our only water was the holy Ganga. We bathed in it, cleaned with it and drank it.*

*Most of the sadhus or saintly persons were worshiping Lord Shiva. Every camp had its own unique assortment of sadhus—some in loincloths, some naked, many covered in ashes, and most with matted hair. In addition, every camp had its own sound system, so there was a cacophony of sounds filling the air, each competing for prominence through its amplification.*

**Sitting in his tent with his disciples, Prabhupada explained the significance ofArdha Kumbha Mela. For millions of years, he said, this had been among the most sacred places in India. During the appearance of the tortoise avatar, when the demons and demigods had been churning immortal nectar, a drop of that nectar had fallen here. Since then, every six and twelve years certain auspicious planets form a jug, and this jug, filled with immortal nectar, is said to pour that nectar upon the Triveni. Lord Rama-candra and Hanuman appeared here in Allahabad, and here Lord Chaitanya taught Rupa Goswami the science of devotional service. Prabhupada said he had also lived in Allahabad with his wife and family, and Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati had initiated him at Allahabad’s Rupa Goswami Gaudiya Math in 1932.**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

## Bathing in the Triveni and Mangal Arati with Srila Prabhupada

**Yamuna**: Srila Prabhupada instituted a program whereby each morning the devotees were to rise between 1:30 and 2:30 am. He said that in order for the devotees to navigate the masses of people, go to the river, take bath and then return for mangal arati at 4:45, we must rise at that time, as did the majority of others in that great camp. It took over half an hour just to walk each way to and from the river. Then one got onto a boat for another fifteen-minute ride down to the confluence of the rivers—an amazing and wondrous site. The Ganga flows from one direction, the Yamuna flows from the other direction, and the Saraswati comes from underground. I used to go with Kaushalya, and those memories of chanting our Gayatri mantra and Sri Isopanisad in the middle of the night at this most holy site are very treasured memories for me.

So it is at this confluence where bathing was to be done. There were literally hundreds of boats, each carrying a load of pilgrims, and they lodged on a sandbank out in the middle of this massive river; then everyone bathed in the sacred waters. If you can picture the scene—it was virtually the middle of the night, and you could see very little, but there was an explosion of everyone vibrating different transcendental sounds, kirtans, japa and various mantras. And there were just so many bodies, but you couldn’t really see anything because of the blackness—the only light being the moon reflecting off the water.

So almost every morning some of us would go on this long walk, then the boat ride, then the bath, then the boat back in the same way. After we returned, we would walk around our pandal site chanting, and at 4:45 we would have our mangal arati program. Unfortunately, this austerity was too much for some of our party, so Srila Prabhupada encouraged them by not only rising early himself, but then very publicly bathing with a bucket of cold water. He very much appreciated those who rose early and took advantage of this sacred place and time, and he would openly acknowledge them. I remember once when Kaushalya and I returned from our morning ablutions, he was standing outside and said with deep feeling, “Thank you. Thank you very much.”

Another special memory I have occurred during the mangal arati in the dark of night. There were one or two low-watt light bulbs hanging, and a few candles on the altar.
