We began chanting the Gurvastakam prayers to the Spiritual Master and then, not far into the chanting, Srila Prabhupada spontaneously began chanting the prayers to the Six Goswamis. We did not have song books at that time, but Srila Prabhupada had recorded some of those prayers. So somehow I had learned the words to this prayer, and I began chanting with Srila Prabhupada—just the two of us singing, with the devotees playing their instruments. I remember feeling like I was in this sound bubble with Srila Prabhupada, and surrounding that sound bubble were all these other transcendental vibrations coming up. For me it was this wonderful reciprocation of kirtan with Srila Prabhupada. He kept his eyes closed throughout most of the kirtan. I remember closely watching him and feeling almost out of body. Then at the end of the prayer, he resumed again with the shlokas of the morning prayers glorifying the Spiritual Master. The whole occurrence was extremely powerful and unusual, but not unprecedented. He did this on a few occasions, and of course, the Conway Hall chant to Narada Muni comes to mind. Srila Prabhupada saw Narada Muni come to our kirtan then, and for some reason, here at the Ardha Kumbha Mela, he became immersed in the presence of the Six Goswamis, and we were fortunate enough to witness it. To this day, that beautiful memory remains fixed in my heart.

## Mela Kirtans and Nagar Sankirtan

**Yamuna**: I cannot say enough how much the thread of the Holy Names pervaded our activities and lives throughout the entire Mela. We woke up with the Holy Names, and we went to bed with the Holy Names. And in between that is all there was: Srila Prabhupada and the Holy Names. Whether we were alone, in our own group of devotees or in the midst of masses of people, the Holy Names tied everything together.

There is some wonderful film footage of Srila Prabhupada on nagar sankirtan with the devotees during the cold mornings—walking surely and swiftly with all of us chanting around him, and with sadhus bowing at his lotus feet as he walked. It was magical. I think each devotee would say the same about the experience. Even though it was cold and damp, somehow we felt encased in the warmth of being on nagarsankirtan with Srila Prabhupada. We became as if one heartbeat, and no longer these cold bodies marching along with red toes from our open sandals. Not only were our own hearts melted by the power of the nagar sankirtan, but it melted the hearts of the people around us. We felt connected to Lord Chaitanya’s Movement and to Srila Prabhupada’s branch of the tree of Lord Chaitanya. We felt transported to the spiritual world— the sound of the kartals, the beat of the mridanga, and all of us dancing and chanting in time with the Holy Names. We became immersed in the Holy Names, saturated in the Holy Names, and felt extremely fortunate despite the challenges of our environment.

I can remember one morning where there was a dual megaphone system. Hansadutta das had one microphone, and I had a microphone. And I would chant a verse, and then the party would chant, and then he would chant a verse, and the party would chant. One megaphone was pointing in one direction and the other pointed in the opposite direction. And the kirtan was so enlivening and exciting that Srila Prabhupada joined in, and then we put both of our microphones on him. So Srila Prabhupada would chant a verse, and then we would all chant, and then Hansadutta would chant a verse, and we would chant, and then I would chant a verse. And in that way all three of us led the kirtan that morning—it was very special. It really can’t be described what impact all of this had. It was surreal and unforgettable.

So after the morning program and breakfast prasadam, the devotees would go on nagar sankirtan throughout the entire city of pilgrims—a different route every day. There were maps showing where each tent would be, and our processions were always extremely colorful and enthusiastic. It was very exciting, as we created a great stir wherever we went, for our “uniqueness.” And the kirtans were wonderful—the street kirtans were almost always led by Madhudvisa das, Acyutananda Swami, Dinanatha das or Hansadutta das. I remember them as being very exuberant and ecstatic kirtans. One of our members, Shyamasundara and Malati’s daughter, Saraswati, was a young child only two years of age. And everything we did, she did. It wasn’t as if her mother kept the child somewhere else. Whatever program was going on, Saraswati attended that program, and this child was so enthusiastic for kirtan that sometimes she would lead or dance in such a way that large groups of people would be inspired to chant—simply by seeing this little girl with her arms raised in the air.

## Yamuna Learns About Vani and Vapu — “I am Speaking Because You Want to Hear”

Prior to the pivotal event described below, since the time she had become a disciple of Srila Prabhupada in 1967, Yamuna remembered very little distinction made between the positions of men and women in Krishna Consciousness. Of course, there was the understanding of restraint and the importance of following the regulative principles, but who would sit where or who would have access to Srila Prabhupada, these issues had not been formally addressed. Most of the Western devotees in India still maintained the perspective of ISKCON as a family of like-minded souls—sometimes dysfunctional, certainly, but a family nonetheless. That all changed for Yamuna at Allahabad.

In going through literally hundreds of pictures and many films from those early days, Yamuna can be seen almost always sitting next to Srila Prabhupada, either recording him or writing in her journal as he spoke. Her dedication was unquestionable and unique. When the devotees arrived at the Ardha Kumbha Mela, Yamuna took her usual position of sitting near Srila Prabhupada with journal in hand. She often said that the Ajamila lectures given by Srila Prabhupada over the course of their India travels changed her heart and increased her faith immeasurably. She said that they allowed her to see the tie-in between the kirtan of chanting and the kirtan of the shastra, and this was illuminating and thrilling to her. And to her eternal credit, she learned from the great challenges that would come before her in the ensuing years. They would all become faith-enhancing, and they would all cement her relationship with Srila Prabhupada—even in his physical absence.

**Yamuna**: *Srila Prabhupada’s focus during the Srimad-Bhagavatam classes on Ajamila was on the concept of how, if one engages in Krishna Conscious activities, there is never any loss, but if someone falls down, one again becomes attached to the material nature. And with a sense of proprietorship and belonging in the material nature, a tremendous degradation can take place. So he was saying over and over to please become immersed in the Holy Names; chant as life’s main activity. So there was a whole month of that preaching, and I think it was the first time in my life with Srila Prabhupada where there was this one concentrated focus. It was also the first time in India where I had Srila Prabhupada’s association on an extended daily basis, and it was so powerful, with his constant preaching on taking up the Holy Names. He was practically imploring us to do this—to Take It.*

*One of the changes during the Ardha Kumbha Mela was the increase in the numbers of ISKCON sannyasis who attended. I did not know some of them who had come from the Calcutta side. One of them had been living for a long time in India, some of that time with members of the Gaudiya Math. He had adopted some of their kirtan techniques as well as their understanding and application of the position of women in Vedic culture, and he had no qualms about trying to enforce what he had learned among our party of Westerners. If someone led kirtan or played an instrument in a manner disapproved of by him, he would simply stop the kirtan, make a critical remark or two, and then ask someone else to lead or play the instrument. I remember several kirtans stopped with a boisterous, “Isn’t there anyone here who can play kartals?” In hindsight, I saw it with some humor, but at the time, I did not. Where women were concerned, that same forcefulness was prominent.*

*Srila Prabhupada was again speaking from the Sixth Canto history of the life of Ajamila, and all of us lived just to hear him speak. To be with Prabhupada was one thing, but to hear his Bhagavatam class every morning was something we would just run for. It is difficult to describe, but for me it was clarification that Krishna Consciousness is an ocean of mercy. Whether it be chanting, hearing or the smallest service, it was all-merciful. I would sit right next to Srila Prabhupada’s vyasasana at his lotus feet, writing in my journal as he spoke. Throughout my early years of Krishna Consciousness, Srila Prabhupada was so open and merciful to the ladies that we never felt the stricture of separation or division between us.*

*So one morning this sannyasi brusquely approached me and said, “Yamuna, have you noticed where the other women are sitting?” I replied, “Yes, I have.” They were seated in the back. He then said, “You should be sitting back there with them, not in the front by Srila Prabhupada.”*

*So the next morning I sat way in the back. I believe another day went by when I also sat in the back. The following morning I was hanging my wash outside, and Srila Prabhupada called me. As I paid my obeisances, even before I rose up, he looked at me with an almost plaintive look in his eyes and said, “You don’t like to hear from me anymore?” I immediately burst into tears because I had no words to express how much I was appreciating his discourses on the life of Ajamila. So I said, “I love to hear from you more than ever, Srila Prabhupada. More than anything in the world, all I want is to hear from you.” Prabhupada inquired, “So why aren’t you sitting where you usually sit?” I said, “A sannyasi told me that it was the etiquette that I sit far in the back with the ladies.”*

*Prabhupada was quiet. Then he said, “Yes, that is the etiquette.” I paused, already lamenting and feeling his separation—somehow knowing that the physical intimacy I had freely shared would now have to be curtailed in India. So I spontaneously said, “Srila Prabhupada, how many times were you with your Guru Maharaja?” Without a pause, he said, “Since I met him, I have never been away from him—not for one second.” But I was not satisfied and wanted more, so I said with some force, “But how many times were you actually with him physically?” Prabhupada said, “Very few—maybe five or six times—but they were intimate to me. He used to walk and talk with me so many intimate things.”*

*Then he said, “Many of my Godbrothers were big sannyasis and thought that associating with the Spiritual Master personally was most important. But in some cases, they were no better than mosquitoes on the lap of a king. And what is the business of a mosquito? It is simply to suck blooood \[drawn out\]. So don’t think that the only way to associate with the Spiritual Master is by his physical association. You try to hear.” For me this was a monumental, life-changing moment. Up until then, I couldn’t conceive of being separated from Prabhupada. Neither could I bear the thought that he would ever leave us. But I realized from this exchange—from this experience—that there would be a point in the future when I would be physically separated from him, and I would have to learn to feel his presence through his vani, his instructions and his example.*

*And then, looking at me with great feeling and love, he said, “I am giving these lectures because you want to hear them so much. That person who is most favored by the Spiritual Master is one who follows his instructions. So do not think that you are being separated from me.” And again, the flood of tears came.*

*So I could tell, as early as January 1971, that from then on there was to be a seeming distance from the prior intimacy I had in Srila Prabhupada’s personal association. And I was prepared for it; I knew that it was destined to come. And Srila Prabhupada had explained many times that in the early stages of association, the Spiritual Master is like a father. But he said that when the son matures, it is then the duty of the son to take care of the father. The father no longer has to spoon-feed the son. So this was the maturing process in understanding my responsibility to my Spiritual Master, and it began in this very small way on this very special day.*

*Another manifestation of the change in mood and etiquette was that I was naturally feeling less inclined to lead kirtan, even though Srila Prabhupada would often ask me to lead. Because there were now many male members who wanted to lead, and some of them were sannyasis, sometimes when I did lead, I perceived a noticeable slackening in the kirtan among our group. And I felt that this was due to the fact that I was a woman. Somehow this reticence to lead actually had a physical effect on my voice. Srila Prabhupada would ask me to lead, and I would freeze inside. It was affecting me physically. Even though my Spiritual Master had asked me to do this, I was backing off and feeling I shouldn’t lead kirtans. So this was another manifestation of the beginnings of what were to be ongoing challenges of being female in our society.*

In reading Yamuna’s description of this time and also hearing talks she gave to myself and others about it, it is astounding to see how she took what became to many women devotees insurmountable obstacles in their progress in devotional service, and turned them into learning and even growing experiences. She used to say that there was a clear distinction between the process of bhakti and the misapplication of that process by some of Srila Prabhupada’s students, and she had no intention of allowing that to interfere with either her relationship with Srila Prabhupada or her dedication to the path of Krishna Consciousness.

## Sri Sri Radha-Madhava and Worship at the Meta

There is a film of the altar and the beautiful Sri Sri Radha-Madhava Deities at the Ardha Kumbha Mela. Looking at the film, it is hard to conceive of Their being in a tent. It all looks very gorgeous, like any ISKCON temple anywhere. Below the larger Radha-Madhava Deities stand Srila Prabhupada’s smaller Radha-Krishna, who had traveled with him from the beginning.

**Yamuna**: *The beautiful Deities of Sri Sri Radha-Madhava are about 17 or 18 inches in height, and They were the center of our pandal. What to speak of our kirtans and the uniqueness of Westerners performing nagar sankirtan, we also became very famous that year for the gorgeous worship of Radha-Krishna archa vigraha in difficult circumstances. Srila Prabhupada’s Deities were the same Deities he had trained me with. They were small six-inch Radha-Krishna Deities, and They had been traveling with Srila Prabhupada all this time. At the Mela, They were served most of the time by Nanda Kumara das. They had stayed in Bombay while we were in Amritsar and Indore, and Srila Prabhupada then had Nanda Kumara bring Them to Surat, where They were kept in his room. We worshiped Them with aratis during that time. Now They were here at the Ardha Kumbha Mela and joined with Sri Sri Radha-Madhava in a large tent on a little makeshift altar—simply made, but beautiful.*

## Prasadam and Other Challenges in the Tent City

**Yamuna**: During the Mela, Srila Prabhupada determined what our activities would be from morning until night, both for purification and to show by example what Vaishnavas do. While a program of Deity worship went on with aratis and offerings throughout the day, one of the main challenges was cooking and serving prasadam—not only to the devotees in our party, but for the prasadam distribution that Srila Prabhupada wanted carried on. Revatinandana das almost single-handedly cooked much of our devotee prasadam in impossible circumstances. It was an amazing accomplishment. Most of the others contributed in some way to the distribution programs. So people were cooking and distributing prasadam throughout the whole day, and different devotees volunteered for that cooking service. Sagar Maharaja was instrumental in showing us how to shop in this environment, and Revatinandana das was instrumental in the making and distribution of both halava and kitchari. Various other devotees made puris and chutneys. Those were the four main types of prasadam distributed by us at the Mela.

The devotees basically lived on kitchari, yogurt and roasted peanuts during the entire festival. The prasadam was purposely kept very simple. The kitchari had some vegetables in it, and a few chapatis were served. Srila Prabhupada wanted us to distribute prasadam practically twenty-four hours a day.

There was virtually no facility to speak of—everything was makeshift, everything was outdoors. And from morning to night there was always the smell of wood hres—a massive number of wood hres. Because many people stayed up throughout the night and kept the fires lit, there was always choking smoke in the air. So although it was a very flat environment because it was a river bed, if you were on any platform or raised building, you could look out and see hundreds of twinkling fires in the encampment, covered by a blanket of smoke.

Of course, the fires were there because of the cold nights. In addition, there were many days of cloudy skies and even some rain. It was impossible to dry your clothes in one day there. If you got a really warm afternoon sun and draped your saris over the makeshift walls of our encampment, there was a possibility they would dry; and if they were old enough and dirty-looking enough, there was even a possibility that no one would bother to steal them. Any new cloth tended to immediately disappear. But one positive note is that at least within our encampment there was not a great deal of strife. Everyone just went about their business to chant, hear from Srila Prabhupada and survive throughout the day.

## Outside Darshans and Programs with Srila Prabhupada

**Yamuna**: During the days, we would sometimes be invited to various programs. Whether we traveled by foot, by rickshaw or boat, wherever we went, our program remained the same—kirtan, katha, kirtan, katha, and then prasadam. Mostly, we traveled to each engagement by rickshaw. Srila Prabhupada would be in his own rickshaw, and his disciples would go in a convoy of several other rickshaws. I remember only one or two engagements where we took a boat across the river.

These programs in Allahabad were very grand. Again, Srila Prabhupada spoke a great deal about what real atonement, or prayaschitta activities, meant because many of those present were there to relieve themselves of sins by bathing at the auspicious times. So Srila Prabhupada hammered home the principle that the only atonement, or the only way to kill the seed of sinful activities, was through the process of Krishna Consciousness. It was the only way. By taking a bath you could erase so many sinful activities, but you couldn’t kill the seed of sinful activities which had not yet fructified. Somehow Srila Prabhupada fit this theme into every single one of his discourses during the Allahabad Mela.

## Visit with Srila Prabhupada to the Rupa Gaudiya Math

**Srila Prabhupada: Today we will go to this temple \[Rupa Gaudiya Math\] in full strength and give nice sankirtan. The Acharya was Rupa Vilasa Brahmachari, and he is now Bhagavat Maharaja. This is the only Math that came to visit me in Calcutta.**

**— Yamuna’s journal**

**Yamuna**: *One day we went with Srila Prabhupada to the Rupa Gaudiya Math in Allahabad. For the devotees this was a most exciting visit, but for me it was very special because those Deities, Sri Sri Radha-Govinda, were the first ones of this size I had ever seen from India. Pictures of Them had been sent to San Francisco in 1967 by Acyutananda das and Ramanuja das, and I was hoping that we would be able to go and see Them because somehow They always remained within my heart. Also, this was the temple where Srila Prabhupada worshiped during his householder life in Allahabad. He was not only instrumental in helping secure the temple; he also donated money for the Deities and performed many other services there. When some of the disciples of Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati wanted to open a temple in Allahabad, Saraswati Thakur told them to go see Abhay Charan, and he would certainly help them. So this was an important place in Srila Prabhupada’s life, and therefore important for us. It was here that Srila Prabhupada received first and second initiation, and when he was initiated, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta said, “Yes, he likes to hear. He does not go away. I have marked him.”*

*We had a very long and ecstatic sankirtan in front of those wonderful Deities. Krishna appeared in black marble and Srimati Radharani in white marble. And Srila Prabhupada personally bore the responsibility for the transcendental service of installing Their Lordships in this temple. It was his service to his Spiritual Master. We had a luncheon program there as well, and Srila Prabhupada was in a very happy mood.*

*One day, His Divine Grace brought all of his disciples to the Dasasva-medha Ghat. That particular holy place of pilgrimage is the place where the Supreme Lord, Gauranga Mahaprabhu, instructed Rupa Goswami about the truth of Krishna, the principles of devotional service, and the transcendental mellows of divine love. His Divine Grace spoke and glorified the pastimes between Rupa Goswami and Lord Chaitanya at this holy place. He spoke about the potency of Srila Rupa Goswami’s Bhakti Rasamrta Sindhu, and asserted that if devotees would simply read four books: Teachings of Lord Caitanya, The Nectar of Devotion, Bhagavad-gita and Srimad-Bhagavatam, which are full of transcendental histories, we would obtain full and perfect instructions for attaining pure love of Krishna. Srila Prabhupada’s discourses and discussions always left us surcharged, and we released that through chanting with great enthusiasm at that holy place.*

The following excerpts are from Yamuna’s dated journal. They are her personal reflections on the given day and reveal the depth of her dedication to Srila Prabhupada’s teachings and personal example.

**Yamuna’s Journal:**

**January 14, 1971**

Oh, my little red sleeping bag is a great discomfort to have on me, as it stays perpetually damp. In the cold of night it is alarming without the comforts of electricity, and flashlight batteries only for emergencies. I don’t even know what time it is, but I seem to wake up automatically in the morning. Night sounds are still audible, and there is something about the association that ignites me—in this case, almost seven million people. The fact that there is almost always something happening, and everything is so close, since there are no walls, makes you more keenly aware of the activities around you, and in some way they are all centered on purification, even though on another level.

Since I am not attending Srila Prabhupada in any personal capacity here, I fill my days with association through kirtan and katha—that is my deep connection right now in terms of personal service to Prabhupada. Oddly, it is almost as profound, because I know that it is another means of pleasing Srila Prabhupada. He wants to encourage us in every way to learn and deeply experience Krishna Consciousness, and I perceive just a small glimpse of this through being present at his lectures on the importance of purification in this place. He reiterates that it is not meant for anything else other than Krishna Conscious activity and purification. Our devotional process is the means of purification, which I am trying wholeheartedly to delve into through the glories of the Holy Name. So this austerity of getting up and chanting during the pre-mangal hours is perhaps the most memorable time of the entire day in terms of its purifying effect.

Day sky is different from night sky. How could I possibly describe it? Tonight it is totally overcast—like a gray blanket hanging low in the sky. As soon as you get to remote areas, the Holy Name is the only solace that you have. But fortunately there are always people here, even in the darkness of night, and all of them are speaking in their own voices—even the monkeys and other animals that are constantly hanging on the electric wires. I think that is part of the reason why the electricity is always going out all of the time. Now the flame of my candle is starting to dance and sway to one side, so that means the wind is starting to pick up, and perhaps I have only a little time before it goes out. I hear Nanda Kumara filling a bucket with icy cold water for his bath and not going down to the river, so he can remain available for Prabhupada’s service. I am not thus engaged.

I so much look forward to going and taking bath in the morning, even in this biting cold. It is difficult as you fumble through the night, however. The electricity is almost an enemy instead of a friend because you tend to become dependent on the few bulbs that hang. Chances are, they may go out, which they do regularly. Sometimes the thought comes that someone is playing a joke on us to truly make us work for this all-auspicious bath.

**January 15, 1971**

We have had a good lot of rain in the last two days. It caused a lot of mucus. I often wonder how this cold climate is affecting Srila Prabhupada, because even 1, with a body only in my late twenties, am affected, so I can’t imagine how he is. Thank goodness we have cots to keep us off the ground, or it would be intolerable. There is no wind this morning; that could mean colder temperatures. I wonder how my little box of matches will carry me through the day. I have three matches, since the electricity has gone off again.

My thoughts go to what Srila Prabhupada is doing right now, and I hope he is in the center of his tent with his heater on. I know Prabhupada is affected by this biting cold, because you can tell that he has a lot of mucus. Of course we all have mucus, but when I even think to imagine how Prabhupada is feeling, it causes pain to me. He always bundles up with almost twice as many clothes as I do. He always has his spittoon pot. I never understood what a spittoon pot was until I met Prabhupada.

I would like to bring up the subject of hygiene or lack thereof. Bathing is done in the river and once in the morning. Personal scents have long dissipated. I now bathe in river mud, rinse in river water, and must certainly smell like river mud/water. Immediately a clean but damp petticoat is put on. There are no oils or creams here, so my feet now have deep crevices in them. They went from pinkish white to small cracks from the toes to the center of the heel. Now they are permanently dark. Whether I scrub with rocks or use brushes, the black never comes off, and the cracks continue to get deeper. I think Westerners age more quickly than Indians do. Indians are more used to the climate and probably have systems that don’t require the unguents, creams and lotions we do to try to keep the skin young and healthy. If they do have such systems, we have yet to find them out.

Warmth. When you wake up in the morning, you immediately begin walking. The cold is so biting. In the black of night I get up from the red sleeping bag, put on as many clothes as possible and start a brisk walk to the river. Below me a sea of bodies is moving in all directions. Rivers of people are moving to and from the river to take bath, the dim glow of the light above accentuating the movement of their heads as they take each step along the ground, the earth moist and wet beneath our feet. The cacophony of sound rising from all of the mouths yields an intense sound vibration unlike anywhere else on the planet. The chirp of the birds at sunrise filters through this loud, moving sound vibration of the morning.

**January 16, 1971**

The Triveni is the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and Saraswati rivers. The water of the Yamuna is green, clear and cold, the Ganga is brown and warmer, and the Saraswati is flowing from a spring underground. The Ganga is flowing from the head of Shivaji. During this Mela there are so many bathers. There is a sand bank at the point considered most auspicious for bathing by astrological calculation. While bathing, I recited the full Isopanisad and Gurvastakam.

Srila Prabhupada is displeased this morning with the pujari. “Why is arati not ready?” he says. “If you cannot get up and bathe, you will have to stop pujari work. The way of Krishna Consciousness is to rise and chant. Someone must organize this party.”

From the Srimad-Bhagavatam lecture that morning:

**Yamuna**: I surrender to your lotus feet, Srila Prabhupada.  
**Srila Prabhupada**: All right. So anyone, if you have got doubt, you can clear it. Now you can try to understand how powerful is this pure chanting of the Hare Krishna mantra. Offenseless chanting of the Hare Krishna mantra means you remain liberated always. With offenseless chanting, chanting once is sufficient. But because we are not offenseless, therefore we have to make a regulated program that we must chant Hare Krishna so many times. Otherwise one chanting of Krishna is sufficient to make you liberated, one chant, “Krishna,” “Rama,” once, that’s all-sufficient. Just like this Ajamila. Once he chanted “Narayana.” He became immediately liberated because he was offenseless. But because we cannot do that, therefore we have to make a prescription.... So we should not neglect. Chanting, chanting, chanting... this is one side. Another side is when you become liberated, the chanting will give you transcendental pleasure, so that you cannot cease chanting. That is the liberated stage, just like Rupa Goswami and Haridas Thakur.... When you are liberated, then there is no need of giving you direction. You’ll feel transcendental pleasure by chanting. You cannot cease. Yes?

**January 17, 1971 - Conversation:**

**Yamuna**: I was just thinking, Prabhupada.  
**Srila Prabhupada**: Immediately there is “dung, dung, dung, dung,” all temples—immediately. And people are running. Oh, and they will all gather at the temple in front of the Deity. Hundreds of people will go automatically. The same man who was living at home in a very degraded condition, as soon as he goes to Vrindavan he becomes habituated to all these things automatically. Yes. The society—the association—is very important.  
**Yamuna:** Those beautiful birds, the peacock birds also at this time, they are flying in trees and waking up now and make that sound. Oh, Vrindavan.  
**Srila Prabhupada**: So the Society is a very important thing.... Therefore the standard of this International Society should be kept very carefully. Then whoever will come in touch with this Society will be improved automatically by association. All right. Even in the bird society there are swans and there are crows. By nature the crows will never go to the swans, and the swans will never come to the crows. “Birds of the same feather flock together.” Yes. Therefore society is required. Unless you come to the Krishna Consciousness Society, how can you develop Krishna Consciousness?

**January 18, 1971**

We are sleeping in our tents with kusa grass on the entire floor; we bathe in and drink Ganga water. Ardha Kumbha Mela happens every six years, and many auspicious planets come together to form a jug filled with nectar, and on this sacred spot of the Triveni, the conflux of Ganga, Yamuna and Saraswati, the demigods pour nectar on this sacred spot. At four different places on this planet Kumbha Mela occurs, but the Triveni is foremost. It is a most auspicious yajna.

\*\*\*

It was at this Mela that Yamuna came across a poem often attributed to Bhaktivinoda Thakur, but initially written in a book called “Establishing God’s Eternal Form” by Pandit Mohan Gosvami Nyaya-ratna. In 1883, Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur wrote a review of the book which was intended for the English-speaking reader. In this review, prior to including this poem, Bhaktivinoda Thakur said: “Not only reasoning of a healthy kind, there is enough of that superior sentiment which is called affection for things beyond the regions of the senses. The shlokas of which the following are translations have created a sort of thrilling sensation in our heart, which we feel unable to express in writing:

Let crowded sins repeat my trial scenes,  
and lead me on from woe to woe!  
Care I for that? If love of God alone,  
would bless my heart where’er I go.  
The Holy seat of Love is Vrindavan,  
where matter’s laws have no domain  
Ah! When my panting soul shall find  
its rest in that Eternal Realm again!”

Yamuna’s prayer books and journals are full of pasted and copied prayers of Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur. She found an enduring affirmation of her own faith through his connection to Godhead, his honest and urgent appeals for mercy, his sincere humility and compassion for all fallen souls, and his consistent and piercing pleas for ever-increasing bhakti. She often said that he taught her both how to pray and what to pray for through his songs. Throughout her devotional life, whether she chanted and prayed before the Deities or ecstatically shared the songs of Bhaktivinoda Thakur among many young and enthusiastic devotees, her connection with Bhaktivinoda Thakur was an integral and profound aspect of her spiritual life.

**Yamuna's Journal**

**January 19, 1971**—Notes from Srila Prabhupada’s lecture:

Bhagavad-gita says that it is Krishna’s special mercy that devotees are always in light. This is Krishna’s special mercy. For those who are constantly engaged in devotional service with love and affection, Krishna is within us, and knows our sincerity of purpose ... Krishna’s mercy is equal to everyone, and each person can take mercy, and one only gets mercy depending on his capacity to take it. The process is to be very enthusiastic and very much attentive how to please the Lord.

**January 19, 197I** — Yamuna wrote the bhajans Jiva Jago, Sri Yugal Arati, Gaura Arati, and Tumi Sarvesvaresvara in her journal.

**January 24, 1971**—Notes from Srila Prabhupada’s conversation:

I was initiated in Allahabad in 1932. My business failed, or I gave it up in 1930. Dr. Bose was like my father. I became disgusted and gave it to them. When I left it \[the business\] collapsed, and after I left, there was a great thunderbolt that struck that building.

**January 26, 1971**—Notes from Srila Prabhupada’s lecture:

Although we apprehend this Name as something material, it is not. You must have ears to understand. But if you continue chanting you will taste the sweetness. It requires simply time. In our gross state we cannot understand what is God, and relish His form, His Name. The Mayavadis do not understand that if we put on a dress, coat, etc., it takes form because it is over form. Dress has existence from form. Without spirit soul having form, how has this body taken form? The body is the dress of the soul, \[emphasis Yamuna’s\]

**January 27, 1971**—Notes from Srila Prabhupada’s lecture:

Sukadeva concludes: How much powerful is the Holy Name of God? He \[Ajamila\] was with a prostitute and going to hell, but a revolution took place. People follow so many rituals by different religious scriptures, but simply by uttering the shelter of Krishna’s Name there was a revolution in his heart. Take shelter of the Holy Name of Krishna. Bhaktivinoda says, “Simply by taking shelter of the Holy Name and going on with your work, there will be a revolution in your heart.” Whether grihastha, rich, poor, brahmana—remain in your place—just take shelter of this Holy Name of Krishna. This life is temporary—this dress will be finished today or in 100 years—but the soul is eternal. The material world is full of danger. For those who are Krishna Conscious, this material world is empty. Those who take to the shelter of the transcendental lotus feet of Krishna have no fear.... We must chant constantly to avoid maya; she is always trying to grab us. Take shelter of the Holy Name and chant offenselessly.

**January 28, 1971**—NotesfromSrilaPrabhupada’s lecture:

Kirtan means to speak or glorify the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Lecturing is kirtanam, chanting and dancing are kirtanam. Preaching, logic and argument are kirtanam. Kirtanam is the speaking vibration, but it must always be in the service of the Lord. Anukirtan means following the Spiritual Master in kirtan. And bhakti means: I am only in the service of the Lord, like Arjuna was fighting simply to execute the order of Krishna. So you preach, but don’t think you are very good. You must just follow in the footsteps of the Spiritual Master.

Grantha-Bhagavat must be heard from the person Bhagavat, not from a hired reciter. Sanatana Goswami says do not hear kirtan from a non-devotee. An unscrupulous man cannot deliver the message of Bhagavat. Milk touched by the lips of a serpent causes poisonous effects.

I remember at the Ardha Kumbha Mela in Allahabad, when some of your disciples felt it was too difficult to rise early, take bath and attend the morning program with you. Seeing this, you encouraged us by personally going outside in the dark of night, at 3 am, to bathe in unheated water and in near freezing weather, despite your age and dwindling health. Then, wrapped head to toe in wool, you sat with us outside in the wet predawn cold for a full three-hour morning program—without fail. In this connection, I pray that this vision of you always remain framed in my heart to give me strength against austerities. This is one of the greatest gifts you gave us—to gather together and relish your company for mangal arati and Srimad-Bhagavatam study. Its benefit cannot be calculated.

We remained with Srila Prabhupada in Allahabad at least through the 28 of January. Slightly before the end of the Mela, Srila Prabhupada dispatched a group of us to Bombay to open a temple there.

**Radhanath Swami**: Srila Prabhupada knew how to transform people’s hearts. Srila Prabhupada saw that little spark—that little spark of the propensity to serve Krishna, even if that spark was surrounded by volumes and volumes of pollution and smoke. He just concentrated on that spark and fed it in whatever way would make it grow—anything to fan that little tiny spark with encouragement. That is love. When you understand truth, you must know how to apply the truth: whatever brings a person closer to Krishna. Prabhupada conquered people’s hearts because he loved them. Love is reciprocal.

## ISKCON's First Temple in Bombay — February Through April 1971

Just prior to the end of the Ardha Kumbha Mela in Allahabad, Yamuna and some of the other devotees were sent by Srila Prabhupada to Bombay to finalize arrangements for the new temple on the seventh floor of the Akash Ganga Building. Her husband, Guru das, and others had stayed behind to secure the two flats covering the entire seventh floor of the new and prestigious building. This period in ISKCON’s history has been very thoroughly and eloquently covered by others, yet in relation to Yamuna devi herself, there is more nectar to churn from the ocean of her remembrances, experiences and devotional qualities.

## Akash Ganga Temple—“Ganga in the Sky”

**Yamuna**: *It was considered quite a coup to have our first official temple in the new Akash Ganga Building on Bhulabhai Desai Road in Bombay. We had two flats which comprised the entire seventh floor. The layout was in the shape of a long rectangle, with the front left corner of the rectangle as Srila Prabhupada’s room, which had its own veranda overlooking the sea, and the front right corner of the rectangle as the temple room, which ensured wonderful cross-ventilation from the sea breezes. The other flat housed the devotees. There were rooms for men, women and office space. Every room contained many windows, except the kitchen, which had small windows higher up. Although large, our temple soon became crowded with the constant comings and goings of guests and temple programs.*

*So at the end of January of 1971, we returned from Allahabad and set up and furnished the apartment in preparation for Srila Prabhupada’s arrival. As we had little money, the furnishings were sparse. Some devotees had followed Srila Prabhupada to Gorakhpur, Benares and Calcutta, so when Srila Prabhupada came to Bombay near the end of February, several other devotees joined us as well—Madhudvisa das, Tamai Krishna das, Hansadutta das, Tusta Krishna das, Malati devi and Kaushalya devi, to name a few. We were eventually a party of near twenty-strong. Our young photo-journalist friend, John (later Yadubara das), who had been traveling with the party, came, and his girlfriend Jean (later Visakha devi), also a young photographer, arrived in March from the United States.*

**Giriraja Swami**: And although large by anyone’s standard, the flat wasn’t really set up to be a temple. Entering through the front door one came upon a small vestibule. On the left was a store room and a small Indian-type kitchen—an empty room with a couple of burners on the floor. Straight across the vestibule was the temple room, where Their Lordships Sri Sri Radha-Rasabihari stood on an ornately carved wooden altar; and behind the altar, a porch overlooked the ocean. Next to the temple room was Srila

Prabhupada’s room. Light, breezy and comfortable, it also had a porch overlooking the ocean and served as Prabhupada’s office and bedroom. Three more bedrooms at the back of the flat, a few bathrooms and the Life Membership office—a partitioned section of the temple room—made our first Bombay temple. It was a tight squeeze, and Yamuna, who didn’t like crowds, usually ended up sleeping on one of the tiny balconies outside the rooms.

**Visakha devi**: I first met Yamuna prabhu when I came to Bombay in March of 1971. And at that time I was not a devotee; in fact I was not interested in becoming a devotee. And one of my first impressions was of seeing Yamuna prabhu, when she heard Srila Prabhupada give class.... The knowledge and the emotion that he had for Krishna were conveyed through his words. And Yamuna would sit erect, and she would focus on Srila Prabhupada. And his words entered her ears like rivers entering an ocean. But we know that ordinarily the ocean that we are familiar with, when rivers enter it, it does not overflow.

But Yamuna prabhu, when those rivers entered her ears and came to the ocean of her heart, unlike the material ocean, her heart overflowed. And tears would come down from her eyes while she was hearing Srila Prabhupada. And I had never seen anything like that before. I had never even imagined anything like that before. And just seeing her hearing Srila Prabhupada, aroused in me also a desire to hear Srila Prabhupada, to try to hear what she was hearing, because the effect was so extraordinary. So from the very beginning, she was a siksha guru for me, even from that time—just observing her. And over the years that continued. I learned from her about how to serve the Spiritual Master, how to apply your mind, your intelligence, whatever assets you have in his service selflessly, without material motivation. And also in observing her hearing, one would wonder, well, what is the result of hearing with rapt attention, because she was in fact a personification of rapt attention.

**Yamuna:** *It has always been my nature to seek some little space for privacy—just to center myself and chant, write or pray. In Akash Ganga, I lived on the porch of the women’s quarters, reveling in the breezes and views over Bombay. One day I was dressing in the women’s room and someone walked in wearing pants while I was not fully dressed. I think I shrieked because I thought a man had invaded the women’s quarters, as no women wore pants there. The “man” quickly left, and much to my embarrassment and many light-hearted reminders over the years, it turned out to be Visakha devi, who had just arrived. What a reception!*

**Visakha devi**: The women’s ashram there had an attached balcony, and Yamuna had her mat and other sleeping gear on that balcony; the balcony was small, so her things took up almost all of it. She relished that space and would sometimes chant japa there while looking over the Bombay skyline. At the time, the devotees were preparing for the first-ever pandal program, and the temple was a hub of nonstop activity, with Shyamasundara and Madhudvisa heading the publicity, and the ladies, including Malati, Yamuna and Madri, organizing the Deity seva.

\*\*\*

At the Akash Ganga temple the water would run for a short time each morning, and the devotees would collect it in large barrels and use the water from those barrels for cooking, bathing and everything else throughout the day. One such barrel was in the women’s bathroom, and once Saraswati, who was about three at the time, dipped her toothbrush into that large, full barrel of freshly collected water. In this way she wet her toothbrush before she put toothpaste on it.

Even though the landlord at Akash Ganga had originally been enthusiastic to have Srila Prabhupada and the Western devotees as tenants, relations with him very quickly deteriorated. It so happened that the Pakistani Consulate was also located in the same building, and propaganda was being circulated that the ISKCON members were actually CIA agents disguised as sadhus, and their business was spying or worse. Another significant problem was the exuberant and loud kirtans, which disturbed some of the other residents. Yamuna commented on some of the ensuing difficulties.

**Yamuna**: *We had increasingly bad relations with the landlord. One of the main reasons was because we hung our laundry on the porches. It was a prestige building, and to have saffron dhotis hanging out of the building angered some of the residents, and they didn’t like us. We learned that they were organizing committees to evict us, and even though we now had some influential friends, they still wanted us out of the building and conspired to do so.*

*When Srila Prabhupada was in residence, I often cooked for him, and I remember how excited the devotees would be to receive his remnants. He would also often have guests or go out to meetings with prominent persons and prospective Life Members. So I stayed heavily involved in my two services—overseeing the cooking and the Deity worship, especially in preparation for the upcoming pandal program.*

**Giriraja Swami**: While Prabhupada rested, Yamuna would distribute his remnants. She knew that Gurukripa liked chapatis', Mahamsa, bhaji; Saraswati, laddus; and she gave according to the devotees’ preference. We would then go and take our prasadam, which would be served in thalis in the temple room. Madri, Malati and Saraswati would go shopping for the Deities’ outfits, and respectable Indian ladies were struck by how demure they looked, dressed up in saris, with their hair covered.

Another thing about Yamuna devi struck me as amazing. About the time of the first Bombay pandal, when we were staying in Akash Ganga, a high-rise apartment building in an affluent part of central Bombay, she would stay back and clean. She would clean the whole place for hours. And while cleaning, she would sing in a very ecstatic mood. The rest of us were going here and therefor service, of course, but there were incidental benefits: seeing exotic India, meeting all sorts of cultured and interesting people, tasting varieties of delicious prasadam—and she was staying back and cleaning. She put her heart into it and would be singing in an ecstatic mood. \>

\*\*\*

In the preparation and writing of this tribute to Yamuna devi, I envisioned it as a tapestry of sorts, made up of woven threads. One thread throughout the tapestry of her life was her dedication to Srila Prabhupada’s service, one was her immersion in Deity worship, and one was her love of and devotion to kirtan in all its myriad forms. These threads wove the tapestry of how Yamuna practiced Krishna Consciousness throughout her adult life. Srila Prabhupada taught her to maintain a degree of cleanliness virtually unheard of in the West, and it was in her nature to take what he taught her to heart and practice it throughout her remaining years.

## Yamuna’s Deity Preparations for the Cross Maidan Pandal

As the devotees tirelessly made arrangements for the upcoming pandal, or “Bhagavat Dharma Discourses,” as termed by Srila Prabhupada, Yamuna concerned herself with having a throne \[simhasana\] made for the Deities. Four pairs of Radha-Krishna Deities were to be donated by the Birla Trust, and one set of those beautiful marble Radha-Krishna Deities would be installed at the pandal. They would later be named Sri Sri Radha-Rasabihari, and today They stand majestically and are gorgeously worshiped at the ISKCON Juhu Beach temple.

**Yamuna**: *I remember a conversation with Srila Prabhupada on March 19,1971.I had been becoming increasingly concerned that I never found women engaging in direct seva of the archa vigraha \[Deities\] in India. Srila Prabhupada was having me prepare all of the Deity preparations for the pandal program. One set of Deities was to be installed in Bombay, one pair went to the Calcutta temple, and one pair of Deities was to be sent to our Los Angeles temple. So although very engaged, I was a little worried, and I asked, “Srila Prabhupada, I have never seen any female pujaris in India. Is it bona fide for women to be serving the Deities directly?” Srila Prabhupada answered, “We make no distinction between male and female.” I said, “Yes, Srila Prabhupada, but why is this so in India?” “That is the etiquette,” he replied. I pressed on, “Srila Prabhupada, what is our policy?” After some time Srila Prabhupada said, “We can follow the etiquette. Otherwise they will not accept our Deity worship. Therefore I have called for Nanda Kumara.” So from then on, in all of the pandals and programs, Nanda Kumara or Devananda Swami performed the outward Deity worship.*

A revealing aspect of Yamuna’s focus and character is expressed in the story below by Giriraja Swami. When Yamuna and I were visiting Vrindavan on pilgrimage in 1994, she interviewed Giriraja Swami, and he reminded her of the story of Mr. Baruch and the throne in Bombay. In

Yamuna’s own notes, she simply mentioned that she had “something to do with getting the simhasana." She never told the actual story to me, and as usual, in her notes she relegated her role to that of a supporting or negligible position. It was only through the later memories of devotees like Giriraja Swami that the whole wonderful story unfolded.

Even though the large marble Deities were there at Akash Ganga, the smaller brass Deities were going to be used in the pandal, because there was not enough money to have a large throne made for Them. This caused great sadness to Yamuna, as she wanted the beautiful, large Deities to be the center point of the pandal.

**Giriraja Swami**: Then came the Bombay pandal. Shyamasundara Prabhu, who was the temple president, divided the work into different departments, with one devotee in charge of each.... And Yamuna devi was in charge of the Deities. We had very little money then. Although we were raising funds for the pandal program, we needed it all for the event. And the treasurer, Rsi Kumara, was very tight with the money, which Srila Prabhupada considered a good quality for a treasurer. Sometimes Rsi Kumara would put a sign on his office door: “Closed for three days.” So Yamuna devi was charged with raising the funds for the Deities. That was the year we got big marble ones. Those at the pandal were small and made of brass, and on the last day of the program there was to be a procession from the pandal, at Cross Maidan, to Chowpatty, where there was to be a program at the beach, at which Sri Sri Radha-Rasabihari would be revealed for the first time to the people of Bombay. And she just couldn’t raise the money.... So we had little brass Deities.... So one day \[Yamuna\] was standing on the street, and one nice man asked her if she needed a ride anywhere. She was probably trying to get a taxi. She said, “Yes.” So this man took Yamuna in the car and he said, “You look very disturbed.” She said, “Yes, I have to make a simhasana for the Deities, but I don’t have any money.” She started to explain the whole situation, and then, as she was talking, she started to cry. So the man was very, very impressed with Yamuna’s devotion to Krishna, and he said, “Well, don’t worry. My father is the chairman of a big trust. So I am sure if you explain your situation to him, he will give you a donation.” So the man’s father, Mr. J. M. Baruch, was a retired judge and the manager of the Mamadevi Temple Trust and the Maha Laksmi Temple Trust, which are two of the biggest old temples in Bombay. I think the cost of the simhasana was about 8,ooo rupees, which was a lot in those days, but Mr. Baruch arranged whatever money Yamuna needed

\*\*\*

Below is Yamuna’s recorded remembrance of that event from the 1994 interview with Giriraja Swami in Vrindavan. Again, it reveals her heartfelt and enthusiastic approach to Krishna Consciousness and is also indicative of the sweetness of her nature.

**Yamuna**: *I remember now. These two men came to Akash Ganga. It was Krishna’s arrangement. And then I actually went with them and designed a simhasana. I had forgotten that wonderful story. \[It is\] so strange how the memory works. Wouldn’t it be incredible to become Krishna Conscious where you can remember everything that happened around Srila Prabhupada’s service? I really want that day to come when I’ve cleared so many inebrieties that I can remember everything. But now I remember bringing them \[the throne-makers\] into the front room in the temple and also the joy of the boys when we told them. And they came into the temple room to make arrangements for the altar, and then Srila Prabhupada knew. Later, this one man \[Ranchodlal\] made simhasanas for many temples in our society (including that of Sri Sri Radha-Banabehari). It was all actually unbelievable; it was a miracle that that happened.*

## The Cross Maidan Festival — “Bhagavat Dharma Discourses: A Hare Krishna Festival”

**Shyamasundara das:** Giriraja almost single-handedly went out on the street... and got the money for this whole festival. Tamai Krishna arranged the pandal and the physical aspects. I did the advertising. And somehow or other, in March ’71, it all came together, and it was the biggest festival in ISKCON history up to that point, and maybe ever since. Suddenly, every day there were ten thousand people at a time hearing the mahamantra and realizing what Prabhupada had done in the world. And Prabhupada loved that festival. Afterwards that was all he could talk about. He said, “Yes, this is the way. This is the way.” So it began a whole series of pandal programs—in Delhi, in Calcutta and in other places

**Yamuna:** *Our Bombay Cross Maidan program lasted for eleven days. Srila Prabhupada was exceptionally pleased with the turnout of the pandal. Every day we had upwards of twenty thousand persons. Prasadam was being served constantly; there were question-and-answer booths; and there was intense interest in us as a Krishna Consciousness Movement. Shyamasundara’s approach of bringing American-style advertising techniques such as balloons and billboards was a huge success, so it was all very wonderful and pleased His Divine Grace very much.*

*Srila Prabhupada spoke both mornings and evenings during the pandal. In the mornings he usually lectured from the Srimad-Bhagavatam, and in the evenings from the Teachings of Lord Caitanya. During the pandal programs, he changed the subject matter of his discourses from the Sixth Canto history of the life of Ajamila to the Seventh Canto history of Prahlada Maharaja.*

*During this time Srila Prabhupada was stressing that if one could attain love of God, it did not matter whether one was a sannyasi, brahmachari, vanaprastha or grihastha. He also spoke to many, many influential people—government officials, ministers and prestigious men within the business community. It was a very grand success.*

**Radhanath Swami**: It was on that first day of the pandal program, and tens of thousands of people attended. I was way, way back in the crowds, just watching, and Prabhupada came on stage. Madhudvisa prabhu was leading kirtan, and devotees were dancing and Guru das prabhu was taking photos. I saw Guru das called over by Prabhupada, and they were talking for some time. Then Guru das was looking, looking, looking through the crowds for quite a while, and he came all the way to the back of the crowds and took me by the hand and said, “Prabhupada wants you to sit with him on stage.” I asked, “How does Prabhupada know who I am?” And he didn’t say anything, he just pulled me up. When we came to the stage, Prabhupada smiled at me, and with his hand he gestured that I should sit not far from his vyasasana, and I sat. I saw Srila Prabhupada when he was speaking. He just had such a sincere longing to reach people’s hearts—such deep compassion, such deep concern. \>

**Yamuna**: *On March 29, 1971, at the Bombay festival, Srila Prabhupada performed a marriage ceremony on stage which pleased the audience immensely. It was the first time they had seen serious Western devotees marry in a traditional Vedic ceremony. During the ceremony Srila Prabhupada said something very powerful about his young followers that profoundly struck me:*

*“My Guru Maharaja ... Srimad Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Maharaja Prabhupada was creating more brahmacharis and sannyasis for preaching work, but I am creating more grihasthas, because in Europe and America the boys and girls intermingle so... it is very difficult to keep one brahmachari. So there is no need of artificial brahmacharis. It is sanctioned. My Guru Maharaja wanted to establish daivi-varnashrama ... It doesn’t matter whether one is sannyasi or one is grihastha or a brahmachari. The main principle is bhagavad-bhajan. But practically also, I may inform you that these married couples, they are helping me very much because ... For practical example, I may say that one of my Godbrothers, a sannyasi, was deputed to go to London for starting a temple, but three or four years he remained there, \[and\] he could not execute the will; therefore he was called back. Now, I sent three married couples—all of them are present here—and they worked so nicely that within one year we started our London temple, and that is going on very nicely.*

On the final day of the festival, the Deities were taken on procession and placed on Their beautiful new throne. The Indian Express newspaper gave a glowing report of the festival and procession:

**FITTING FINALE TO HARE KRISHNA FESTIVAL**

**It was a grand, fitting finale to the n-day Hare Krishna festival, which attracted thousands of devotees at Cross Maidan in South Bombay. The decorated murtis of Radha and Krishna were taken in procession on a regal ratha from the venue through Dirgaum Road to Chowpatty in the evening.**

**Dozens of nama-sankirtan mandalas from all over the city spearheaded the procession with loud and ecstatic chanting of the Hare Krishna mahamantra, followed by His Divine Grace A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada in an elegant horse-drawn coach, chanting. Crowds chanted Hare Krishna on the road sides as the ratha was pulled by devotees along the route.**

**At Chowpatty, the four-foot-tall Deities, splendidly dressed and decorated with jewels and garlands, were displayed on Their magnificent simhasana (throne) donated to the Hare Krishna movement by Madhav Bhag and Mumba devi temples.**

**During the celebrations, Prabhupada spoke from the Gita and Srimad-Bhagavatam daily, morning and evening. More than thirty of his foreign disciples conducted kirtan, arati, and film shows in the specially erected pandals.**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

**Wanting to take immediate advantage of the momentum created by the festival, Srila Prabhupada wrote a letter to supporters and Life Members requesting that they meet to discuss how to further the Hare Krishna Movement. Srila Prabhupada was a brilliant strategist, and many followers have told compelling stories of his open-hearted and fearless plans to spread the mission of his Guru Maharaja. This letter not only expresses Srila Prabhupada’s desires and plans, but as it turns out, it was also a prophecy, because everything he wanted for Bombay happened just as he planned.**

**By the Grace of Their Lordships Sri Sri Radha and Krishna, our recent festival in \[the\] Cross Maidan Exhibition Ground has been counted a grand success, and quite noticeably the spirit of bhakti has been actively revived in Bombay. My blessings go especially to all of you who have joined with us in service.**

**As you may know, my plan is to establish in this most auspicious city a unique International Krishna Conscious Training Center, where hundreds of persons from abroad may be educated in the Vedic way of life, while at the same time Indian boys and girls may be trained up for prachar (preaching) work in foreign countries. We will construct classrooms, workrooms, dormitories, kitchens for large-scale public prasadam distribution, a lecture hall, library, and a beautiful temple for the glorification of Radha and Krishna. We are on the threshold of bringing this important project to fruition, and we are very excited to inform you of the progress made in this respect.**

**You will agree with me that your active participation and your direct involvement in this is most essential, and hence I appeal to you to spare your valuable time for Krishna and make it a point, in spite of your extremely busy life, to extend your unstinted cooperation. It is proposed to hold a meeting on Monday, the 26 of April, 1971, at 6:30 p.m., “Akash Ganga,” 7th floor, 89 Bhulabhai Desai Road, Bombay-26, to discuss and to finalize plans to channel our united energies to achieve the goal. It will also be a great opportunity for like-minded Krishna devotees to meet, to have darshan of the Deities and to exchange views and suggestions to make rapid progress in spiritual life.**

**I very much want to meet you again, so kindly make it a “must” to attend our meeting; there is a lot of ground to be covered to spread Krishna Consciousness to millions and millions of our slumbering brothers and sisters!**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

## “Hari Hari Biphale” with Srila Prabhupada

There is a beautiful series of photographs taken of Srila Prabhupada chanting Hari Hari Biphale at Akash Ganga, with Yamuna holding a microphone as he played the harmonium and sang. Some of the young devotees who visited us at the Saranagati community will remember Yamuna speaking very feelingly about this prayer and revealing how she saw Srila Prabhupada exhibit ecstatic symptoms while chanting it. Narottama das Thakur laments in this prayer that although the Lord sent this Hare Krishna mahamantra from the spiritual world to deliver the fallen souls, why did he not develop any taste for it? Of course, for exalted devotees like Srila Prabhupada, this humility is real, but it comes from a platform of separation and has no tinge of any material feeling. This was one of the prayers Yamuna liked to chant alone, and it would invariably bring about remembrance of those moments with Srila Prabhupada, and then the tears would freely flow as she sang.

**Yamuna**: *Beginning in 1968, when Srila Prabhupada first taught us the prayer Hari Hari Biphale in San Francisco, until his departure, I had the good fortune of witnessing Srila Prabhupada chant this exceedingly humble song of Narottama das Thakur four times. The last time was at Akash Ganga in 1971. I was holding the microphone up, and watched as he went so deeply into the ecstasy of chanting that he exhibited bodily transformations. His meditation that day was so deep and profound that the skin on his face became slack. His face would just transform into something very different—all from diving deeply into the ocean of that prayerful appeal.*

During a Japa Retreat held at the Saranagati community in 2008, Yamuna spoke about her relationship with the prayer Hari Hari Biphale and Srila Prabhupada:

**Yamuna**: *I was saying earlier how this one time in London when Prabhupada prayed—and it wasn’t very often that we had the opportunity to see Srila Prabhupada in this mood of prayer. One morning I asked Srila Prabhupada, “What is your favorite prayer?” He said, “Hari Hari Biphale.” Then he asked what mine was, and since we had no song books, and since I didn’t have any idea what prayer (by singing) was yet, I said, “Well, Siksastakam,” because the Siksastakam prayers were in the Bhagavatam. And then he said, “That’s very nice.” Then I proceeded to ask Prabhupada, “Would you chant that prayer, Hari Hari Biphale?” And then he chanted the first line, Hari hari biphale janama gonainu, maybe twenty times. Prabhupada sang it over and over and over, and every time he sang it again, \[he went\] deeper and deeper and deeper. I felt like I was going from the surface of the ocean to the very deep ocean—the ocean of the Holy Name. As Srila Prabhupada would go into this prayer, he would go deeper and deeper, and this was one of those crux points of being with your Spiritual Master and getting to witness the Spiritual Master’s depth, whatever that depth may be, and however it manifested differently.*

*So again, thank you so much for bringing up this prayer aspect of getting access to the Holy Names and the potency of just trying—each one of us knowing that our previous Acharyas and all great saintly persons before us have done this, and that we have a chance to do this too. We have a chance to do this by their potency and by all of you bringing us together to chant these prayers.*

*Similarly, last summer one of the things we tried to offer as the theme of our Rathayatra was this prayer. So all of us in Saranagati and those in our Friday night japa sessions would practice this*

In a prayer reflecting on her unforgettable and life-changing experiences of hearing Srila Prabhupada deeply dive into the ocean of prayer, Yamuna wrote:

**Dear Srila Prabhupada: I remember how kirtan was so intense and joyous in your presence. How time and place dissolved in those kirtans. How your thumbs lifted off the surface of your kartals as they sizzled in sound, and how your vocal cords and mouth vibrated and extended as you filled a space with hauntingly beautiful transcendental sound vibrations. I remember losing myself in that sound and wishing never to leave this space or your presence. In this connection, I pray, even if only one more time, to hold the microphone for you as you chant your favorite Vaishnava prayer, Hari Hari Biphale, as experienced that final time at Akash Ganga in Mumbai.**

## Lessons from Srila Prabhupada on Chanting Japa

**Yamuna**: *It was the habit \[in Akash Ganga\] that sometimes the men would chant japa in a circle, kind of walking quickly. They would get really immersed, and they would walk, maybe because they were tired, or for whatever reason; they would go around in a circle chanting “Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna, Hare Hare, Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare.” And some people were just sitting and chanting japa; I was one of those disciples. We were chanting in front of the beautiful archa vigraha form of Sri Sri Radha-Rasabihari, now in Juhu.*

*Then Srila Prabhupada walked in from his bedroom and got on his vyasasana. He didn’t say a word; he was just looking at us chanting our japa. I immediately became aware of his presence. We all paid our respectful obeisances to him, and rather than immersing himself, he became intently focused on each and every one of us in the room. Other than on this occasion, I have never experienced that anywhere to such a degree. It became very profound. You’ve heard some devotees say that when Srila Prabhupada looked at you, he saw you and he saw through you, and he saw the past, present and future—he just saw so much. So during that japa period he was looking very intensely at each disciple, and something very, very transcendental happened. All of a sudden, the men who were walking around in a circle sat down. And all of a sudden, devotees started to sit up very straight.... I felt as if we were a big lotus flower, and Srila Prabhupada was in the whorl of the lotus flower, the center, and we were all these petals opening up around him in transcendental sound, and from Srila Prabhupada’s presence the quality of the japa changed dramatically, without one word said.*

*And then straight away, of course, in my foolishness (I had finished fourteen rounds), I took out a little notepad. So immediately, the first thing Prabhupada said was, “Yamuna, what are you doing?” I was so embarrassed. I said, “I am just writing something down, Srila Prabhupada.” He said, “Have you finished all your rounds?” I said, “No, I have two more to go.” He said, “No writing until you finish your rounds. Chant attentively and then write.” So that’s one big instruction ... I have taken a little seriously in my life. If I focus on my rounds first in the brahma muhurta hour without doing anything else—if I don’t write lists—then my day is different than if I do otherwise, (pune yatra talk, 2001)*

**Giriraja Swami**: Early one morning in Bombay, Srila Prabhupada came into the temple room when the devotees were chanting their japa, and from the vyasasana he observed them—and corrected them. Seeing Yamuna devi reciting her Gayatri mantra, he asked her if she had completed her rounds. When she said no, he told her, “You should complete your rounds before you do Gayatri.” Because Gayatri is supposed to be recited at dawn, Yamuna devi took it that Srila Prabhupada was instructing her to finish her rounds before sunrise, and so she began her lifelong practice of rising early, at 2:00 am, to chant her rounds.

## Notes from Yamuna’s Journal

**Yamuna’s Journal: march 16, 197I** —Notes from Srimad-Bhagavatam class:

One can know Krishna by symptoms and characteristics. In this world there are so many things that require a nice brain. How are things going on so nicely? The gold expert finds particles and knows there is a mine. Similarly, as you see wonderful things, you must think there is a big brain behind it.... What is the relationship of consciousness and soul? It is like the sun and sunlight. Where there is light there is illumination.

**March 20, 1971**—Notes from Srimad-Bhagavatam class:

Surrender is voluntary. Only by the mercy of the Spiritual Master can you surrender. But you ask to please be merciful so I can get out. Like if you are in the well and someone drops down a rope, and you cry, “Be merciful so I can take the rope!” This is a false plea. Surrender is in your hands. Mercy is already there. Krishna comes; He sends His representative; He speaks the Bhagavad-gita. So what is there else to want? It is hopeless if you do not want to surrender. “I cannot accept your instructions, but I am very obedient to you.” Then nobody can help you. You must be willing to cooperate. Responsive cooperation, not duplicity or negligence, \[emphasis Yamuna’s\]

**March 21, 1971**—Notes from Srimad-Bhagavatam dass:

You cannot understand God by any process except devotional service. That is the only way. Prahlada Maharaja says that this is the perfect method of self-realization. How does it begin? Somehow or other become attached to Krishna. Never mind how it is done; just try to become attached. Other rules and regulations come after attachment. There is no forcing good qualifications. Only when one is serious to chant Hare Krishna do the rules and regulations come. Then the rules and regulations will make us automatically attached to Krishna.

**March 24, 1971**—Notes from Srimad-Bhagavatam class:

Krishna Consciousness to the atheist is nonsense. Therefore preaching work is not so easy. Still we must tell them to chant. “You will say, ‘Chant, chant, chant,’ and they will say, ‘Can’t, can’t, can’t.’” But we must expect the atheists to say no, but we will follow Lord Nityananda and even undergo broken pots and disadvantages, but that is progress in spiritual life. Even if you preach, taking risk, without regulative principles, immediately you will be successful. Anyone in preaching is immediately recognized by Krishna.

## On to Other Services — Delhi and Calcutta, 1971

Yamuna and Guru das stayed in Bombay until April 21, 1971, just over two weeks after the Cross Maidan festival, and then were sent by Srila Prabhupada back to New Delhi. Srila Prabhupada had left Ksirodakasayi das in charge there, and as Guru das and Yamuna had actuated the preaching in Delhi, they were the obvious choice for Srila Prabhupada to send in answer to Ksirodakasayi’s request for married couples.

**Today Guru das and his wife Yamuna are going there. You wanted some married couple. They are the best pair, and if required they can remain in Delhi to organize things nicely.**

**— LETTER TO КSIRODAКASAYI VISHNU DAS, APR. 21, 1971**

**Ksirodakasayi hasn’t got to go to Russia. Let him concentrate his business in Delhi as leader. And if your presence in Delhi is no longer required, then you are required in Calcutta. So after finishing your important business in Delhi, you should go to Calcutta for at least one month.**

**— LETTER TO GURU DAS, APR. 27, I971**

## “Make Me Dance As You Like”— The Austerity of Constant Uncertainty, 1971

**Delhi Stopover—End of April, 1971**

Yamuna did not record much about her and Guru das’s brief stopover in Delhi on the way to Calcutta. It is evident from Srila Prabhupada’s letter of April 21, 1971, to Ksirodakasayi Vishnu das that they were to leave that day from Bombay to Delhi. Ksirodakasayi Vishnu das was an older Indian gentleman who had been initiated by Srila Prabhupada in London and left in charge of the Delhi program as Yamuna and Guru das served elsewhere. In a letter to Guru das on April 27, barely a week later, Srila Prabhupada requested him and Yamuna to proceed to Calcutta to assist in organizing a pandal program mirroring the successful Cross Maidan pandal in Bombay. The Calcutta pandal was set for May 14 through 23 at the Chowringhee Maidan, across from the Victoria Memorial. One of the large marble pairs of Radha-Krishna Deities donated by the Birla Foundation was to be showcased at the pandal, and Srila Prabhupada wanted Yamuna to make all the arrangements for Them as she had in Bombay. Giriraja das and Tamai Krishna das were also sent from Bombay to assist in the pandal organization and collection of funds.

The change in direction of Srila Prabhupada’s instructions, whether in person or by letter, was not a new or unusual occurrence to any of the devotees in his personal service. Yamuna often imagined herself in the same manner Srila Prabhupada expressed in his \]aladuta prayer to the Lord: “I am just like a puppet in Your hands, so if You have brought me here to dance, then make me dance, make me dance, О Lord, make me dance as You like.” So as seen here, Yamuna would understand that they were going somewhere to serve in one capacity, and then on a moment’s notice, they would often be sent somewhere else. That is surrender, and that is what Srila Prabhupada expected of his dedicated followers.

## Calcutta and the Chowringhee Maidan Pandal

When Yamuna arrived in Calcutta near the beginning of May 1971, the Hare Krishna temple on 3 Albert Road was already established, and there was a flurry of activities going on. Some of the devotees were chiefly concerned with fulfilling Srila Prabhupada’s desire to purchase land in Mayapur, while others worked on the upcoming pandal festival. Yamuna immediately took up the service of making arrangements for the Deities, Sri Sri Radha-Govinda. Srila Prabhupada arrived from Sydney, Australia, on May 16, and he seemed to be very pleased with the pandal itself and very hopeful for the acquisition of land in Mayapur.

**We have just now concluded our “Hare Krishna Festival” here in Calcutta, and it was very successful, even more so than in Bombay; daily 35,000 people were attending. Now we are wanting to make twelve such programs in the greater Calcutta area, one each month. In that way we will win over the city. From here I shall be going to London via Bombay or else to Russia. Then I shall return to U.S.**

**— LETTER TO BHAGAVAN DAS, MAY 26, 1971**

**Yamuna**: *So now we had established two camps in India of our own— Bombay and Calcutta—and within a short period it was changing the face of the preaching activities in the country. From the fall of 1970 through the late spring of 1971, we had done a tremendous amount of nagar sankirtan in the north of India. We hadn’t yet preached in the south. That was to take place later, in early 1972, with another nagar sankirtan program. But for now Srila Prabhupada was concentrating on Delhi, Bombay and Calcutta.*

**Giriraja Swami**: From Bombay, Srila Prabhupada sent Tamal Krishna Goswami and me to Calcutta to arrange a similar pandal program there, and eventually Yamuna devi also came, and soon she was engaged in the service of the temple Deities, Sri Sri Radha-Govinda. Every morning we would look forward to the darshan \[viewing\] of the Deities. The worship was so beautiful—so devotional. One day when the curtains opened, a devotee noticed that Krishna’s flute was put in backward, such that the holes where His fingers would play the tune were at His lips, and the hole where He would blow into the flute was by His fingers. The devotee pointed out the mistake to Yamuna, but she replied, “Krishna can perform the functions of any part of His body with any other part of His body.” The devotee thought that she was making light of it all and went to Prabhupada and told him what she had done, and Prabhupada replied, “Angani yasya sakalendriya-vrtti-mantv. Krishna can perform any bodily function with any part of His body”—the exact same thing.

## “You Must Teach Others What I Have Taught You”

If the totality of Srila Prabhupada’s personal instructions to Yamuna devi over the years could be condensed into a few key directives, one would be that it was paramount that she must pass on to others what he had taught her throughout her life. Anything she later accomplished in the fields of chanting, cooking, authoring and preaching can be traced back to this instruction—one he reminded her of and even chastised her over for several times during his remaining years.

**Yamuna**: *“You must teach others what I have taught you.” This instruction was again repeated to me in Srila Prabhupada’s quarters in May of 197I in Calcutta. At the time I was only visiting the temple in Calcutta, having been sent by Srila Prabhupada to assist with the pandal program at Chowringhee Maidan. Srila Prabhupada had just sent Bhavananda das and his wife Palika devi to help manage the center. One day I was bringing Srila Prabhupada’s luncheon plate into him, and because I was just visiting, I was careful not to try to supersede any authority within the temple. But as I placed his plate before him, Srila Prabhupada said, “So are you teaching all the girls how to cook?” And I said, “Well, no, Srila Prabhupada, I am just assisting here.
