Palika is in charge of the women.” Srila Prabhupada then repeated, “No, are you teaching them to cook?” So as I was hesitating in trying to answer him, I remember Kaushalya was just outside the door, and she loudly hollered, “No, Srila Prabhupada, she is not teaching us to cook.” So Srila Prabhupada looked at me and very seriously said, “You must teach others what I have taught you. If you don’t distribute what you know, then you will become envious.”*

*And of course, I came to understand that this is the life and soul of the devotee. That whatever we have been given by the Spiritual Master, we have to hrst try to truly understand. And then we have the duty to distribute that knowledge to other persons. We can distribute what Srila Prabhupada has given us on so many levels. Anyone can distribute his books and give the medicine of Krishna prasadam. So even though this instruction was given to me, it is actually for all followers of Krishna Consciousness.*

## Yamuna's Vyasa Puja Homage from Calcutta, 1971

During the summer of 1971, a young devotee, Jananivasa das, came to the Calcutta temple. He remembers the creation and publication of the Vyasa Puja book for Srila Prabhupada that year.

**Jananivasa das**: The Vyasa Puja celebration was held in the temple with about 30 people. Special guests included T. K. Ghosh and the Birlas. Each devotee read their offerings out. When Yamuna was reading hers, she became extremely emotional. It was the first time I ever saw someone become that emotional due to devotion, and I was very moved.

Yamuna’s revealing and heartfelt Vyasa Puja offering in 197I was inspired by one of her constant sources of devotional inspiration at the time, Teachings of Lord Caitanya.

*Thousands and millions of souls are wandering in this material world, and some fortunate ones by the grace of Lord Krishna and the Spiritual Master can get the seed of devotion.*

*О my eternal Spiritual Master, I beg to be in constant remembrance of Dawning of Love at Their Lordships’ Lotus Feet, of Their Names, Fames, Pastimes, and Their Devotees pure, the mundane plane may I forget and come in truth to You.*

*One has to be like a gardener and water the seed with chanting and hearing or by taking part in devotional discussions.*

*О my eternal Spiritual Master, I beg to hear and beg to chant in the groves of Braja, with expressions of love, the mahamantra with your blessings, and sow the seeds of Love in the hearts of all.*

*The plant of devotional service sprouts up and penetrates the length and breadth of the universe and the Brahmajyoti beyond the Viraja, or causal waters, and reaches the spiritual sky.*

*О my eternal Spiritual Master, I beg to leave all of maya’s weeds of hypocrisy, envy, anger, lust and greed by Sri Nama Sankirtan and pierce the vain glory of calling myself your devotee.*

*There it gradually enters the Goloka Vrindavan planet and attains the Feet of the Supreme Lord Sri Krishna.*

*О my eternal Spiritual Master, devotional service kills the seeds of material desire, and the duration of diseased life withers. The wistful glance at the most beloved Radha-Damodara in Vrindavan, in exquisite glow of beauty, consumes my heart in all Satisfaction.*

*After attaining such a position the plant produces fruit which is known as the fruit of devotion of Love of Godhead. The devotee, however, must pour water on the seed daily by the process of chanting and hearing in devotional service.*

*О my eternal Spiritual Master, You are pure and true, and mercifully conferring on us all the secrets of the loving principles of Radha’s loving service for her Sri Krishna. May I always drink of the flood of devotional practices in the Lotus of Sridham Navadvipa, above the region of the mind, and sing of Your place in my heart forever*

## Yamuna and Guru das Return to New Delhi and Vrindavan—Summer of 197I

By the summer of 1971, the land in Mayapur had been obtained, the first Calcutta and Bombay pandals had been major successes, and Srila Prabhupada sent Guru das and Yamuna back to Delhi to help establish a temple and preaching foothold there, as had been successfully done in Bombay and Calcutta. Giriraja das also came during that time. After the land had been secured in Mayapur, Srila Prabhupada wanted to invite Indira Gandhi to come for the cornerstone-laying ceremony, so he requested Yamuna, Guru das and Giriraja to invite her to come to Mayapur.

**Yamuna**: *At the end of May, we were dispatched by His Divine Grace back to Delhi and eventually to Sri Vrindavan dhama for different engagements. We traveled mostly between Delhi and Vrindavan until October, living in different quarters in Old Delhi when we were there. This part of the city is where Srila Prabhupada stayed when he came to Delhi for publication work during his Vrindavan years. One of the families he stayed with and cultivated was the Joshi family, the same family we spent some time with that summer. I learned so much from Mrs. Joshi, a friendly and pious woman. She said that to save money, Srila Prabhupada would travel around Delhi on foot. He would come to their house to respect prasadam and deliver Krishna Consciousness to the family. Srila Prabhupada even initiated their eldest son as his disciple. Srila Prabhupada instructed me that whenever I was in Delhi I should study cooking from Mrs. Joshi, as he very much enjoyed her preparations. So whenever I could, especially when Srila Prabhupada went to the West for preaching, I would study cooking techniques from her. She was very expert in both North Indian and Bengali cooking, and she freely taught me some of Srila Prabhupada’s favorite preparations. They ranged from beverages to vegetables to dais. Srila Prabhupada was very pleased when he would hear reports from us of how we were encouraging the Joshis in Krishna Consciousness, and they would invite us almost daily for prasadam when we were in Delhi that summer. We would also try in our small way to give Krishna Consciousness to them as Srila Prabhupada had given it to us.*

*Unlike Calcutta and Bombay, in Delhi we did not yet have an established center. We were not able to collect enough money to rent a place of our own yet; still we canvassed among the business and politician communities for assistance in setting up a large pandal program to introduce our Society to the public as we had done in Bombay and Calcutta. Srila Prabhupada encouraged us by letter during this time, helping us to organize our programs both in Delhi and Vrindavan.*

**Better try to open a center in Delhi, because the dharmshala is already open to us and can be permanently gotten if we open a center there. Sadaji Witlal saw me the other day and he said that on some nominal condition of say Rs 1/- per year, they will give the dharmshala for a Radha-Krishna temple. Hans Raj Gupta, the mayor of Delhi, is friendly and he can help also, so take this dharmshala and open a center there. Also I heard that Dalmia is willing to give us his place in Vrindavan. Take it. Recently I have asked Karandhara to send another 50 to 60 men here under the leadership of Dayananda. So we want to keep at least too men here in India for preaching. The people are appreciating our movement, so there is great potential.... So far as Indira Gandhi attending the function, we shall accept a day according to her convenience, and we shall hold the function on her arrival. That is my desire. I think your wife and Giriraja have already gone to Delhi to help you in this connection.**

**— LETTER TO GURU DAS, JUNE 11, 1971**

## An Unforgettable Visit in Vrindavan with Giriraja dass Parents

As seen in the letter of June n, 1971, Srila Prabhupada wanted a permanent temple in Vrindavan and had heard that J. Dalmia was willing to give his family’s dharmshala. Yamuna mentioned making a few trips to Vrindavan over that summer. One of the most memorable visits for her occurred when the wealthy parents of Giriraja brahmachari came to visit their son.

**Giriraja Swami**: What I recall now is that Yamuna and I \[went\] to Delhi to try to meet with Indira Gandhi, and we had some friends trying to arrange the meeting, but they said it would take some time—and it was taking time—and so we decided to go to Vrindavan and wait for further news there. Later, I left Vrindavan to meet my parents in Delhi and accompany them back to Vrindavan, where I introduced them to Yamuna devi. By the time we all went to the town to look for a restaurant and a place for them to stay, it was already evening, and when they were “horrified” by what they saw, we rushed to Mathura, because restaurants and guesthouses closed early then, and we were afraid everything would be closed. When we finally reached the Dalmia Guest House, it was closed, though we did try to speak to someone anyway.

Almost anyone who knew Yamuna devi or came in contact with her was usually charmed at her ability to put each person immediately at ease. She had an open-hearted and generous nature that was at once both accommodating and warm. It did not matter if she was meeting the Prime Minister or the person who swept her room; she was of the same nature. This was wonderfully displayed when Giriraja das’s parents were first introduced to Yamuna in Vrindavan. Upon meeting each other, Yamuna and Giriraja das both fell flat on the road offering full obeisances. Naturally Giriraja’s parents, especially his mother, were horrified, but Yamuna immediately placated them by saying that actually in their hearts they were embracing, but according to our Vaishnava etiquette, it was expressed by bowing down. This diffused a potentially difficult moment for Giriraja’s parents, who were charmed by Yamuna’s open warmth and loving nature, qualities which characterized her throughout her life.

It is almost impossible to imagine how the very dignified and patrician parents of Giriraja Swami must have felt in a so-called Vrindavan “restaurant” all those years ago. Now there are air-conditioned restaurants and guesthouses throughout Vrindavan. Then, there were dirt-floored, soot-filled, open-air rooms with the foods openly displayed and covered with flies. Rodents ran freely under one’s feet. Yamuna felt so much empathy for them when soon they left, unable to bear the filth of the place. As there was nowhere else to go, they all realized that for something even remotely civilized, they would have to go to Agra. So Yamuna, acting as hostess, went with them to Agra and saw them situated as best she could. She often told this story as an indicator of how in devotional service it is our duty to try to give everyone some taste of the real thing. For Yamuna, this came naturally and unpretentiously.

**Giriraja Swami**: My parents always remembered Yamuna, and even in his last weeks of life, my father asked how Yamuna devi was.

Also that summer, Yamuna met John and Jean Greisser again in Vrindavan.

**Visakha devi**: Vrindavan, July 1971—My friend John and I are living and photographing in Vrindavan when Yamuna and Guru das come on pilgrimage. One especially hot day, Yamuna, who strikes me as exceptionally straightforward, friendly and insightful, and I sit up to our necks in the Yamuna River (the water buffalo do likewise) and talk. She is absorbed in and excited by her service to Srila Prabhupada and has full faith in his wisdom, teachings and guidance. She tells me how fortunate we are to be in Krishna’s land and to have the opportunity to hear about His pastimes there. Still unsure about the devotees’ enthusiasm for Prabhupada, I listen without comment.

One morning John, Yamuna and I are in Loi Bazaar, in downtown Vrindavan, when Yamuna asks John if he would donate money to purchase brass Deities of Radha and Krishna. John readily agrees, and Yamuna, who has already chosen the Deities she wants, immediately has John buy Them. '

## More Travels in the Fall of 197I — Delhi, Vrindavan and Calcutta

In August, Yamuna was back in Calcutta in the service of Sri Sri Radha-Govinda. Srila Prabhupada was in London at this time and observed that the Deity worship there was not up to the standard of Yamuna’s worship. He even suggested that if Yamuna wanted to come back to care for Sri Sri Radha-Londonisvara, he had no objection to that. However, he did not approve of the plan of Yamuna and her husband to go to Africa at the time. Reading the letter below, the undercurrent of the difficulties Yamuna was experiencing in Calcutta can clearly be seen in Srila Prabhupada’s reply.

**Please accept my blessings. I beg to acknowledge receipt of your letter dated 3 August, 197I and have noted the contents. So far going to Africa is concerned, I have answered that point in the enclosed letter to Guru das. It is not advisable at this time. Frankly speaking, the Deities are not as opulent as when They were being taken care of by you. So if you want to come back here and take care of Them, I have no objection. But you are taking care of the Calcutta Deities, so what is the difficulty there? Does the “democratic management” not allow you to go to the Deity room? What is the difficulty? Let me know frankly. Very soon we will have Deities installed in Mayapur also.**

**— LETTER TO YAMUNA, AUG. 11, I971**

In the meantime, Yamuna engaged in her services and made deep and lasting impressions on many devotees during those challenging times, especially on the women. One of her endearing qualities was the seriousness with which she entered into personal relationships. They were important and meaningful to her. Years later, upon reflecting on an interaction with her Godsisters and -brothers from these early days, she seemed to always find the positive essence of their characters. As Visakha notes below, she was expecting cynicism but found sincerity instead. That was Yamuna’s defining essence.

**Visakha devi**: Calcutta iskcon temple, 3 albert road, august 197I —Immediately after John and I arrive at the temple, sooty and enervated, I am quickly directed to the women’s quarters, which I access, lugging my backpack along, by walking through the temple room, the office, the bathroom, down a short servant’s hallway and up a narrow spiral staircase. My roommates are Yamuna; Kaushalya, a forceful young American in a white sari (indicating that she has separated from her husband); and motherly, soft-spoken Chitralekha, also a young American. I try to appreciate the welcome that the women extend, but feel thoroughly out of place. The four of us sleep on straw mats in a good-sized room that is adequately ventilated but always gloomy.

The next morning, Yamuna wakes me up at 2 am so I can bathe and join her and the other women in the temple room for japa—the soft chanting of the mahamantra. I have never gotten up at 2 before; it never occurred to me that a person would want to get up at that hour or could physically do it. I certainly don’t feel able to: I feel as if I haven’t yet slept. Somehow I go downstairs and bathe, go upstairs and dress, struggling with a sari that had innumerable wrinkles from having dried in a clump because someone (me?) had forgotten to hang it up the day before. I creep downstairs and through the bathroom. Some devotee men sleep in the office that is between the bathroom and the temple, so by the light of one candle, groggy, disheveled and grouchy, I gingerly pick my way past these sleeping male bodies, faintly recalling that I’d forgotten to brush my hair. Suddenly, just before I enter the temple, Yamuna, whom I hadn’t noticed, stops me. She looks straight into my eyes and with a Colgate smile says, “You’ll look even more beautiful if you put some tilak on.” “And I’m considered cynical?” I think, as I peer back at her in the dimness. More surprising than what she said, however, is her expression. She is sincere. I take the tilak and a small mirror from her and try to apply it. Finally, with relief, I finally settle, cross-legged, in the dark temple room.

Japa quickly becomes tedious, but I am piqued by the fervor of my companions. Kaushalya is especially impassioned, sitting cross-legged on a slight mat, swaying rhythmically as she enunciates each word of the mantra, eyes shut, back straight. Chitralekha’s japa is as focused as Kaushalya’s, but sweeter and slower. Yamuna has yet another style of concentration, which makes the words of the mantra into an intense song with alternating pitches. Observing these women helps pass the time, but I couldn’t possibly do the same thing the next morning—or ever again. Hours later, when John appears, Yamuna tells him of my morning activities as if I had been a willing participant. I don’t interject.

Yamuna maintained that style of sing-song chanting throughout her life. Her japa sometimes reminded me of the song of a mockingbird, with its alternating pitches, rhythms and intonation. It was captivating and sometimes made it very difficult to focus on your own chanting. Often I would find myself listening to her chanting instead of my own.

**Chitralekha devi**: Yamuna was asked to train me in Deity worship, so I worked with her on Radha-Govinda’s altar for about a week or two. Then one morning Yamuna asked me to dress Radha-Govinda by myself. I was very nervous about dressing Them, knowing that the devotees would be having darshan. My fears were quickly confirmed when after greeting the Deities, Tamai Krishna called Yamuna over and questioned who had dressed the Deities—They didn’t look so nice. Yamuna quickly came to my defense saying, “I think Chitralekha dressed Them with as much love as she could muster.” That was the end of the conversation. She had summed it up exactly as it was. I’m still working on mustering the love.

On August 27, Srila Prabhupada wrote to Guru das to no longer try to get Indira Gandhi for the cornerstone-laying ceremony in Mayapur. Understanding the political volatility of the times makes it a simple matter to understand any reticence she may have had. By March of 1971, she was dealing with another Indo-Pakistani conflict, this time centered in what was then East Pakistan and now Bangladesh. East Pakistan launched a bid for autonomy from Pakistan, and fierce fighting started in March, sending millions of refugees pouring into neighboring West Bengal that year. Many thousands were killed in the uprising. During the summer of 1971, Indira Gandhi had hammered out a strategy for what soon became the independent country of Bangladesh. Still, behind the scenes, Mrs. Gandhi would continue to assist the devotees in important ways.

## Calcutta Temple Difficulties — “Our Real Business is to Hear and Chant About Krishna”

That fall in Calcutta, Yamuna’s frustration with the temple management was mirrored by many of the other devotees. The harmony in the temple had deteriorated to such an extent that Yamuna realized that only Srila Prabhupada himself could affect a solution, and so she anxiously awaited his arrival there. Although he was due to arrive on October 25, Srila Prabhupada was quarantined in Bombay for nine days after visiting Nairobi. He finally arrived in Calcutta on October 29 to be welcomed by a barrage of disheartened devotees.

**Visakha devi**: Although Calcutta is home to a large number of excellent cooks, the hired temple cook isn’t one of them; both the ingredients he uses and the way he prepares them are substandard. The devoted and thoughtful Giriraja is the first to get weak from poor nutrition and then sick with indigestion. Others follow. Someone is hired to clean the temple but, although there are many excellent cleaners in Calcutta, ISKCON’s hired cleaner isn’t one of them. The temple is never clean. The devotees are disheartened. On top of all this, and partially due to it, the devotees in Calcutta ISKCON argue. There are arguments about money and books and Life Members and position and behavior.... Dividing issues are everywhere; no topic is exempt. Watching this, I wonder what makes these people, especially the women, carry on.

The morning after Srila Prabhupada arrived, he called the devotees together for an istagosthi.

**Visakha devi**: After breakfast the day after Srila Prabhupada arrives, he asks all of us to come to his room. About thirty of us duly file in and sit on the thin, sheet-covered mattresses, facing him. I sit in the corner farthest from the door with no idea of what to expect.

Srila Prabhupada first notes that two devotees are absent and sends Revatinandana Swami to ask them to come. When everyone is finally present, Srila Prabhupada begins to speak. His voice full of concern, his words drawn from a deep well of knowledge; he talks not of the particular difficulties we face but of the attitudes that created them. He appeals to our higher nature, a nature that he knows beyond a doubt we have. His mood permeates the room and slowly the hard collective knot choking our hearts relaxes. The atmosphere settles; we enter a place beyond calmness.

We hear about camaraderie and cooperation, about tolerance and humility, about steadiness and fortitude while engaging in the sublime service of the Supreme Lord. Srila Prabhupada says that by evoking spiritual consciousness—by self-realization—godly qualities will manifest in us, and we will transcend the troubles of this world. He speaks about the Vaishnava spiritual legacy and tells us of trials from his own life. When he was seventy years old and had recently arrived in the U.S., before he had founded the Hare Krishna Movement, he was living in Lower Manhattan with someone who kept meat in the refrigerator. He says the word “meat” with such disgust that for the first time I realize what an austerity it was for a person of Srila Prabhupada’s caliber to be in such a situation. From his words we understand that we could also rise above disturbances; it would require clear thinking, enthusiasm, confidence and patience.

Giriraja Swami specifically remembered Srila Prabhupada’s mood changing-encouraging, cajoling and, more importantly, trying to keep the devotees focused on the real “business” of hearing and chanting in Krishna Consciousness.

**Giriraja Swami**: After hearing so many complaints from so many devotees, Srila Prabhupada called a meeting of all the devotees. Practically all the devotees in the temple came into Srila Prabhupada’s room, and he listened very sympathetically to what every devotee had to say, and he was really concerned and wanted to improve things. At one stage the GBC for India protested: “Srila Prabhupada, my only intention was to execute Your Divine Grace’s will.” And Prabhupada replied a little sarcastically, “Is it My Divine Grace’s will that the devotees should be disturbed?”

And he made a system. He named certain leaders—Tamai Krishna, Yamuna, me—and said that they should get together every week and discuss the problems, and whatever they decided they should write down in a minute book, and they should all sign and then do what they agreed.

But after all was said and done, Srila Prabhupada’s mood seemed to change. He said, “Actually, we shouldn’t become too involved in such concerns, because our real business is to hear and chant about Krishna, and if we become too absorbed in making material arrangements, we will forget our real business of Krishna Consciousness.” He said that as it is our tendency to discuss mundane topics, so we should be careful and try to minimize the mundane talks and concentrate on hearing and chanting about Krishna.

Then Srila Prabhupada said that in his life he never complained, because his policy was always, “Everything for Krishna and nothing for me.” He mentioned how he struggled to get the passage to America, and then on the way he suffered two heart attacks at sea. And even when he got to America, he suffered in so many ways; he had some buzzing sound in his ears and his head. “I cannot even describe how much I suffered—nor do I want to.” He said he had suffered in so many ways to establish the Krishna Consciousness Movement, but he never complained because his policy was always everything for Krishna and nothing for himself. So that is why, as a service to Krishna, Srila Prabhupada was serving the devotees, because his ultimate goal was to bring them back to their eternal relationship with Krishna. He was practically bathing them, feeding them and dressing them—teaching them how to live as human beings—so that ultimately he could bring them to the position where he could offer them for the service of Sri Krishna. And he never asked anything in return, never expected anything in return, so he was never disappointed.

In 2002, Yamuna used her experiences in Calcutta in speaking to a gathering of youth in Alachua that was arranged by Kartamasa das. I include her talk below because it illustrates the meaningful and very heartfelt way she connected with those young devotees.

**Kartamasa das**: I was having programs for the youth (my peers) at my apartment in Alachua on Sunday mornings, at which I invited a different senior devotee each week to give their advice to us. The speakers were basically asked to tell us what they considered the most important things they could pass on, and that evolved into why they joined and why/how they stay. Yamuna’s talk that day is still my guiding principle that I forever have to work on: patience, enthusiasm and commitment. Many devotees attended that day—about forty in my tiny apartment, including several older devotees who crashed it uninvited—but Yamuna made sure everyone got prasadam.

**Yamuna**: *Once when we were in Calcutta near the end of 1971, the temple was in low consciousness. So you will be able to study when you are in low consciousness and influenced by the lower modes of nature, and also when devotees around you are in low consciousness. And our temple was in a state where respect, honor, generosity, affection, consideration, etc. were at a low point. The real and tangible nature of what Krishna Consciousness is was not very evident in our Calcutta temple at the time.*

*And so Srila Prabhupada called the devotees together to his room. And one woman devotee was really upset; she was in bad consciousness, so she didn’t come to the room. Prabhupada immediately noticed her absence and said, “Where is such-and-such devotee?” And one brahmachari said something to the effect that she went off somewhere in a stew, or something like that. And Prabhupada looked at that brahmachari and said, “Go find her.” Shocked, the brahmachari said, “But I’m a brahmachari; a woman should go find her.” And Srila Prabhupada again said, “You go find her.” The brahmachari said, “But I have no idea where she is in the whole of Calcutta.” Of course, she wasn’t far away; she happened to be across the street chanting her rounds by a lake that’s in front of the Calcutta temple. So anyway, he found her and brought her to the room. The mood was very sober, but Srila Prabhupada wanted to hear from everyone. He went around the room and asked each devotee what they thought was wrong in the temple. And each person gave their realization, and everyone else listened to that realization.*

*And then Srila Prabhupada spoke. He said that we were all here because he had followed the instructions of his Guru Maharaja and come to the West. And he then added with great emphasis: “Do you think it was easy for me to leave India all alone and come to America?” And none of us had ever really thought like that—whether it was easy or hard. We had just assumed that he had done that by Krishna’s mercy. Then he continued, “Do you think it was easy for me when I was in Butler, Pennsylvania, and I opened the refrigerator, and there was cat food next to my vegetables? Do you think that was easy?” And all the devotees almost began to cry, because they began to understand what Prabhupada did for us, and it wasn’t easy. He came from a place where his mother was carried in a palanquin from one house to the other. He was from another culture, almost like another planet; and he yet came to the West with a trunk full of books and seven rupees. And we know the prayers he wrote on the Jaladuta—some of the most beautiful things that Prabhupada ever wrote were those prayers on the Jaladuta^where he talks to Krishna, he prays to Krishna.*

*So he told us to try to just understand that Krishna Consciousness will not always be easy, and then he said, “Three things are required for success in Krishna Consciousness, and you must always rely on them: enthusiasm, will (or determination) and patience.” So now you can take just that one little instruction from Srila Prabhupada and start to apply it in your life, and to the degree that you want to become conscious—to the degree that you want to become committed—start examining these things. For almost thirty years, I’ve been going around and asking devotees, “What does will or determination mean to you?” Because I felt it was one of the weak things for me; if I had more determination I might be a devotee. So I wanted that then, and I want that now. So you’ll decide how much you want these things, but you can go very quickly to Krishna if you want them enough. And the wonderful thing is you never get filled up—there is never an end to it. Just like Krishna is unlimited, so are these things. So, once we get an inclination of what it means to be a disciple, what it means to surrender, what it means to be committed, what it means to be these three things, they become more and more of your focus, and more and more attractive. And you ask questions about how other people have them, and you study how you can get them. Because that place that you can go to, even while being in this Kali Yuga place, is so wonderful, so glorious. It’s what human life is meant for. (ALACHUA 2002)*

## Yamuna Remembers Srila Prabhupada's Childhood Home and Deities

**Yamuna’s Journal: October 1971***—Srila Prabhupada appeared in Calcutta at 14/2 Mahatma Gandhi Road. Down the street is the sitting room he spent much of his childhood days in at the home of a well-known Calcutta aristocratic family named Mullik, and they accepted Prabhupada as a regular family member. The Victorian room is decorated with marble tables on which stand porcelain dukes in swaggering capes and marble boys with floppy hats. There are grandfather clocks, tiled walls of ceramic, marble floors, Chinese rugs and lace curtains, with crystal chandeliers.*

*In the Mullik residence, the brass family Deities are over 300 years old and are called Sri Sri Radha-Govinda. They were tended in Srila Prabhupada’s childhood by his elder sister, and in 1967 those Deities called Prabhupada back to India. He said that one day as a child he entered the door of the Deity room with his father, stopped short and looked at the Deities, and as he saw Krishna, he said to his father, “How can they say God is dead? God is not dead. He is standing just here.” And so from his very early childhood he was Krishna Conscious.*

Srila Prabhupada worshiped those Deities of Radha-Govinda throughout his childhood. In the spring of 1976, when we sent a picture of our worshipable Deities Sri Sri Radha-Banabehari to Srila Prabhupada, he told us that They very much reminded him of those Radha-Govinda Deities from his childhood.

## The Second Calcutta Pandal at Deshapriya Park

Unlike the first pandal in Calcutta when the temple was just becoming established, by the time of the second pandal at Deshapriya Park in November, the Hare Krishna Movement was becoming widely known throughout India, assisted in no small part by an unflattering portrait presented in a popular movie. Movies were cheap entertainment, and the poorest of the poor were able to find a few hours’ shelter from their burdens there. Srila Prabhupada openly accused the government of subsidizing the movie to diminish the popularity of the Hare Krishna Movement. Even many years later, devotees in India would still be regaled in the streets by the movie’s kitschy song Dum Maro Dum.

Also, the radical Naxalite communists were openly threatening violence at the pandal. A note was sent to Srila Prabhupada which said, “Quit India or die.” So instead of being intimidated or threatened, Srila Prabhupada actually invited the radicals into the pandal and then began singing the Govindam prayers from the Brahma Samhita. Somehow this diffused the tense situation, and the pandal went forward.

**Chitralekha devi**: Toward the end of the Calcutta pandal program, the ladies who were preparing Prabhupada’s evening prasadam would ride back in the car with Prabhupada. It was very a simple meal of puffed rice and hot milk to prepare, but sometimes there were four or five of us crammed in the back seat, sitting on each other’s laps. Even though all of us weren’t cooking, it was the opportunity to ride back with Srila Prabhupada. Yamuna engaged me in helping her cook and serve prasadam to Prabhupada. I remember cooking fried bitter melon, but we didn’t just slice it and fry it; we soaked it in salt water for a couple of hours to help tone down the bitterness, dried it off and then fried it. During the Calcutta pandal program, preparing evening prasadam for Prabhupada at the temple was the sweetest, because the men were still at the program, so only the ladies were there to serve him. Often, Yamuna would ask me to bring Prabhupada’s plate to him in his room. She was always nurturing the love in simple ways

## The First Delhi Pandal — November 14 through November 24,1971

Between November 22 and December 17, 1971, India had entered the conflict between east and west Pakistan on the side of the separatists. Therefore India, and especially its capital, New Delhi, were under constant threat of bombings. Undeterred, Srila Prabhupada wanted the Delhi pandal program to go on, and the devotees worked tirelessly in its preparation.

**Yamuna**: *We had now had successful pandals in both Bombay and Calcutta, and we were preparing for the first pandal to be held in Delhi. We canvassed throughout the industrialist and business communities for donations for the pandal and appealed to favorable politicians, most notably the Mayor of New Delhi, Hans Raj Gupta, who had a prior friendly relationship with Srila Prabhupada, for their assistance in introducing our Society to the public in New Delhi. Srila Prabhupada was preaching to us by letter, both encouraging us and helping us organize. Because we did not have a facility of our own, there was also no permanent place for His Divine Grace or the nearly fifty devotees who were attending to reside. Ultimately, through the grace of J. Dalmia, we stayed at the Dalmia Guest House. Srila Prabhupada arrived just shortly before our program was to begin. The organization towards the very end of our preparation for this pandal was furious and rather frenzied. It was only by Krishna’s mercy that the pandal opened on time.*

*When Srila Prabhupada arrived for the first Delhi pandal, he was received at the Delhi Palam Airport as a VIP guest. Several members of Parliament and other important government officials greeted Srila Prabhupada, garlanded him and offered their respects to him. Whenever I witnessed Srila Prabhupada receive acknowledgement or praise, he always appeared untouched by it. He humbly accepted on behalf of his Guru Maharaja, yet he was unaffected by the praise and distinction. I often wondered how this must have appeared to him after all the difficulties he had faced in Delhi getting his books and Back to Godhead magazines published prior to coming to the West.*

*Now Srila Prabhupada was big news. The pandals were very widely covered in the press, and the leaders in government and society were inquisitive and in many cases appreciative of his efforts in bringing India’s spiritual heritage to the West. Even Prime Minister Indira Gandhi herself was appreciative of our Krishna Consciousness Movement. And through some of the honorary Members of Parliament who spoke on our behalf to her, she was helpful in those early years.*

**Srila Prabhupada went from the airport to a Life Member’s home, where he was interviewed by a reporter:**

**“I understand,” said the reporter, “that by ‘Krishna’, you mean some eternal principle.”**

**“I do not mean a principle,” Prabhupada replied. “I mean a person like you and me.” Prabhupada was explaining Lord Krishna as the Supreme Person when suddenly sirens began sounding.**

**“Blackout! Blackout!” cried the reporter and others in the house. War between Pakistan and India had been imminent for weeks, and air raid drills and warnings were now commonplace in Delhi.**

**“Sir”—the reporter spoke tensely in the darkened room—“this is the presence of reality. We are being threatened by this fight with Pakistan. The siren is the ugly reality coming for us.”**

**“We are always in the ugly reality,” Prabhupada said, “twenty-four hours a day. Suppose there is no blackout? Still, if you go in the street, there is no guarantee that you will get home. In this way, you are always in the ugly reality. Why do you say only this blackout? This is just one of the features of this ugly reality. That’s all.”**

**Reporter: “Yes, but at the moment...”**

**Srila Prabhupada: “You do not realize that you are in ugly reality twenty-four hours a day? Padam padamyad vipadam. There is danger at every step.”**

**— SRILA PRАВHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

The first Delhi pandal began on the L.l.C. grounds near Connaught Place and lasted for ten days. After being introduced by the Mayor of Delhi, Sri Hans Raj Gupta, Srila Prabhupada spoke against the path of materialism and exalted the process of surrender through the chanting of the Holy Names:

**At Prabhupada’s arrival hundreds of people surged forward to touch his feet and receive his blessings, as a ring of disciples escorted him through the crowd. Prabhupada, wearing a gray wool chaddar, his “swami hat” pushed back casually on his head, moved calmly forward toward the stage with natural, aristocratic poise. He sat on the vyasasana, and the audience quieted.**

**New Delhi’s mayor, Sri Hans Raj Gupta, spoke first. He had met Srila Prabhupada in the early 60 s when Prabhupada had approached him for a donation to publish the first volume of Srimad-Bhagavatam. Mayor Gupta, recognizing Prabhupada as “someone sincere and near to God,” had helped, and Prabhupada had later presented him with complimentary copies of the first two volumes of his Srimad-Bhagavatam. Mr. Gupta was impressed by Prabhupada’s success in spreading Vaishnavism in the West, and as he introduced Srila Prabhupada, he expounded on the Krishna Consciousness philosophy he had read in Prabhupada’s Bhagavatams.**

**He said, speaking in Hindi, that as mayor of Delhi for five years he had many times welcomed important visitors and delivered addresses, but such functions were usually only formalities. This was not, however, the case with Srila Prabhupada, he said, since no one he had ever known could compare with him. He praised Prabhupada for doing “an immense amount of good work in India and the whole world.” Said Mayor Gupta, “He has also given me love and affection, and I am more affected by that than anything else....”**

**“This is religion,” Prabhupada said. “Simply surrender to Krishna. Become a Krishnite. It doesn’t require a church. It doesn’t require a mosque. It doesn’t require anything. But wherever you sit down, you can chant Hare Krishna. This is the easiest method.”**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

**Yamuna**: *There was a stage within the pandal on which the large marble Radha-Krishna Deities stood in all white, and for the duration of the program, every morning and evening, Srila Prabhupada and his disciples would have a full temple program there. In the mornings attendance was sparse, but each evening after work, tens of thousands of local people would attend.*

**Visakha devi**: First there would be a full arati ceremony for the Deities, led by Dinanatha, Acyutananda Swami, Hansadutta, or one of the other men. After that, Srila Prabhupada would sing \]aya Radha Madhava and give a 45-minute discourse. And then, before the devotees distributed halava and puris to everyone, there would be a final uproarious kirtan. Prabhupada liked Yamuna to lead that kirtan as, with her encouragement, many members of the audience enthusiastically joined in chanting of the holy names of Krishna. Yamuna excelled in leading kirtan yet was not attached to it. She did it because Srila Prabhupada asked her to. The men were eager to lead this final kirtan, and one day Yamuna, responding to their eagerness, decided to bow out.

So, the next evening after his lecture, when Srila Prabhupada picked up his kartals and gave a nod to Yamuna to begin chanting, Yamuna, who was sitting a little distance from Prabhupada, held her throat and shook her head to indicate that she wasn’t well and couldn’t lead. Although her indication was clear, Srila Prabhupada acted as though he hadn’t understood it and gave another nod for her to begin singing. Again Yamuna signaled that her throat was painful and she couldn’t possibly sing, and again Srila Prabhupada ignored her mime and signaled for her to begin. Yamuna surrendered to Prabhupada’s desire and led a captivating kirtan, drawing many of the men and women in the audience to their feet to dance in joy.

## Beautiful Sri Sri Radha-Gokulananda at the Delhi Pandal

Yamuna made all arrangements for the Deity worship for the first Delhi pandal, even traveling to Jaipur and Vrindavan to see to the sringar, throne, and the Deities Themselves. The Deity dress at this pandal captured the hearts of devotees all over the world. To see Their Lordships, who would become Sri Sri Radha-Gokulananda, in Their all-white setting was simply captivating.

**Yamuna**: *So one of the skills of expert makers of Deity sringar \[clothes and jewelry\] is how to make the clothes draw the eyes immediately to the Deities from far away, regardless of Their size or the size of the altar. At the Delhi pandal, Sri Sri Radha-Gokulananda wore beautiful white satin outfits with very large white and silver sequins, which were soon imitated by seamstresses around the Movement. So from every angle the Deities could be seen and appreciated. They were so beautiful. Later, Srila Prabhupada commented on this particular sringar, saying that it was ideal for a pandal.*

*The smaller Deities had been purchased that summer in Vrindavan by Yadubara das, then John Greisser. I had seen these gorgeous little Deities in a shop, and I shamelessly asked John to buy Them. It was these Deities who were showcased in many of the later bathing ceremonies beginning at the Delhi pandal. They were installed with me performing the bathing and one of the brahmana men performing a fire yajna, in what became the standard installation procedure. Ultimately, after many travels, They became the resident Deities in ISKCON’s Hyderabad temple.*

One of the services Yamuna engaged in as soon as she arrived in Vrindavan was the continuing study of the specific styles of Deity dressing in each of the major temples. She not only carefully studied each temple, she also met repeatedly with the pujaris and then meticulously illustrated the unique designs of the Deity sringar of the temple. She later included all of her research, illustrations and pictures in what became famously known as Yamuna’s Deity Book. Some pages of the book are reproduced here, but it is hoped that the entire Deity Book—an amazing accomplishment in itself—will be published as a stand-alone study of Deity worship as it was in the early years. Yamuna learned that even with a smaller Deity, such as Sri Radha-Raman, the dressing style pulled the senses to Him in a wonderful and magical way, even though He stands only twelve inches tall.

**Yamuna**: *As you study the art of dressing in the Six Goswami temples, you’ll see that each tradition has its way of pulling the senses, the mind and the heart of the aspiring servant right into the core of the garbha grha where the Deity is standing. This art has been carried down through centuries such that where and how it all began is often lost to time. What is known is that each of the principal Deities in Vrindavan can be immediately identified by Their unique dress, each differing from the rest in substantial ways.*

**Yamuna’s Bout with Jaundice Brings Unexpected Blessings from Srila Prabhupada**

**Visakha devi:** By the time the pandal began, Yamuna was exhausted and became ill. To recuperate, she moved from the room where the devotee women were staying into a six-foot by four-foot walk-in closet that adjoined that room. One morning I went to visit her in that closet. She was lying on her back on a thin mat on the floor of one side of the closet, and on the walls near her head she had put photographs of Srila Prabhupada. I sat next to her cross-legged, and as we discussed what I could buy that might help her, suddenly she rolled over to offer her prostrated obeisances. I looked up and saw Srila Prabhupada, barefooted, walking through the unoccupied women’s room toward the closet where we were. He peered in the closet and asked, “Yamuna Prabhu, you are not feeling well?” “I’m always thinking of you, Srila Prabhupada,” Yamuna replied. “And I am also thinking of you,” Srila Prabhupada said. “You need to have a place with air and light so you can get better.” Later that day, Srila Prabhupada arranged a small room with a window, where Yamuna could rest

In 1978 Yamuna recalled the mercy and kindness of Srila Prabhupada toward her during her illness at that time.

**Yamuna**: *At that point, due to the intense preparations for the pandal and the extremely long hours of service over many days, I was taken down with a severe case of jaundice. It was the only time I was extremely ill during my time in India. So after the Deities were installed, and just as I came back to the tent side of the pandal, I became unconscious, and for maybe two weeks or more I had a burning fever. So I ultimately attended very little of the pandal itself. We were staying at Dalmia Bhavan at the time, and it was a very crowded situation—perhaps ten to fifteen of us in one room—and the only place free was the bottom shelf in one of the walk-in closets. We had all of our paraphernalia piled up, and I was in a sleeping bag down on the bottom shelf. So somehow, Srila Prabhupada noticed I was missing, and I was later told he had inquired many times where I was.*

*One day I became aware of the door being opened, and turned to see Prabhupada’s lotus feet walking into that closet room. I offered my obeisances as best I could, and by then he is leaning down, all the while chanting the mahamantra. Then he placed his hand on my head and inquired, “Yamuna? How you are doing?” Firstly I said, “I am always thinking of you, Srila Prabhupada.” Then I gave him my symptoms, and he said, “I think this is jaundice; I think you have got hepatitis-jaundice. Now I will take charge of your recovery. You will never get well in these conditions on the floor.”*

*Srila Prabhupada had a hospital bed brought in for me and moved me into a room right next to his, with floor-to-ceiling windows, neem trees outside, and a fan. And I remember being propped up in this bed, and he came in every day to check on my progress.*

*He also called in an Ayurvedic doctor and gave me a diet for jaundice. He said I had to take something called petha, a wax gourd or a white kind of pumpkin that is taken raw. It’s covered in a thick layer of caramelized sugar, so to me it looked like a ghastly thing to eat. Srila Prabhupada said, “This is your medicine, and you have to eat it every day; and you also have to drink sugarcane juice.” So I remember the first time I took a bite of petha; it tasted like the most bitter, horrible thing because of the jaundice. Srila Prabhupada would personally stand and watch me eat the petha, feeling miserable because of the taste, and he would actually smile and chuckle about that.*

*So unfortunately, I was not able to engage in my services through the rest of the program, as I was fully bedridden for over two weeks. Yet I was feeling great bliss and happiness by the personal care and unfathomable kindness of Srila Prabhupada. He was so engaged, so busy, preaching to tens of thousands of people and taking care of our entire Society, yet he personally took charge of my recovery. To this day I become emotional just remembering this. For me it only increased my dedication to see that this small insignificant soul Yamuna was so cared for and nurtured by Srila Prabhupada. In my later challenges, I drew strength and determination from this episode in my devotional life.*

*Another thing I remember about the illness was the loving care of my Godsisters, among them Visakha devi and Chitralekha devi. I felt so grateful to have had not only the care and loving attention of my Spiritual Master, but also my Godsisters.*

## Yamuna’s First Pilgrimage to Vraja Mandala with Srila Prabhupada

**Yamuna**: *So just at the close of this grand pandal program, again through Mr. Dalmia’s family, it was arranged that Srila Prabhupada and his entire party would go to Vrindavan, take pilgrimage, and stay at the Saraf Bhavan. He arranged for cars for Srila Prabhupada and his party, as well as one big bus for all of the devotees. By now, more devotees were coming from the West to join our party, so we were near fifty. When it came time for the entire group to board the bus, I remember I wanted to try to see Srila Prabhupada as he was getting into his car. I was still extremely weak, and literally just back on my feet again after my extended illness. So as I was coming around from the back side of the bus, Srila Prabhupada saw me. I paid my obeisances, and when I got up he inquired how I was doing. I said, “Thank you, Srila Prabhupada, for making so many wonderful arrangements for me; I am always thinking about you and how your programs are going on.” So his car, of course, was hlled with people, and still he said, “You are too weak to ride on the bus. You will ride in my car.”*

*So he had one or two men leave the car, and we were all still scrunched in—so many of us—and I, of course, was the only woman in the car. Srila Prabhupada was so kind in every circumstance. He made allowances for me to try to be comfortable by riding in the car with him instead of the bus. So that ride was very wonderful. It was the first time that I physically accompanied Srila Prabhupada into the holy dhama of Vrindavan, the center of the spiritual world.*

**Giriraja Swami**: After the Delhi pandal I went to Madras, while the rest of the party went to Vrindavan with Srila Prabhupada for the first time. There was one car—an Ambassador—with Srila Prabhupada and some men, and a bus with the rest of the devotees. Prabhupada was in the car, and he noticed Yamuna climbing into the bus.

He said, “Wait! Wait!” He called her, knowing that she was very sick, and told the men to get out. Then he had her get in the back seat with Guru das and one other man—Prabhupada was in the front with the driver—and the other men went on the bus.

**Yamuna**: *So now as we were riding in the small Ambassador car towards Vrindavan for the first time with Srila Prabhupada, all of the devotees were individually understanding that we were entering into the realm of Vrindavan only by Srila Prabhupada’s mercy. As one reaches the outskirts of the 84 square miles of Vrindavan dhama, there is one small village called Ajhai, and Srila Prabhupada showed us there was a well that contained sweet and drinkable fresh water. So he instructed the driver how to reach that well, and we stopped there, and Srila Prabhupada took the small breakfast that was packed for him—fresh fruits and some fried items; then we stopped for refreshments. After this there were only fifteen or so miles until we reached the cut-off road then known as Chattikara Road, now Bhaktivedanta Swami Marg, one of the two roads that enter into Sri Vrindavan village. As we proceeded down that road, we actually passed the site that would later be our Krishna-Balarama Temple.*

*I was still very ill, so I wasn’t present for many of the things that happened on that first day. But there were some very historical things, because this was really the first time that so many white-skinned Vaishnavas were in Vrindavan. So it was a very big event for Vrindavan, and Srila Prabhupada was given an amazing reception. Everyone in Vrindavan was talking about this, and so many people came to visit Prabhupada during that time.*

*We were staying at Saraf Bhavan, and many important things happened there. It was at Saraf Bhavan that Srila Prabhupada had a very historic meeting with three of his Godbrothers present, Dr. О. B. L. Kapoor, Sri Krishna das Babaji, and one devotee from Brahma Kunda, whose name I don’t recall. So in the presence of those three Godbrothers, Srila Prabhupada called for Madan Mohan Goswami and Gaurachand Goswami, the sevaites of Sri Sri Radha-Damodara, to come to Saraf Bhavan, and there was a very magical, mystical kind of arrangement where somehow or other Srila Prabhupada got permission for some disciples to come to Vrindavan and stay in the rooms upstairs above his rooms on Madan Mohan Goswami’s side of the temple. This was rather monumental to be able to get either Goswami to agree to let Srila Prabhupada’s mleccha disciples live upstairs. It is interesting to note that later I talked with the son of Gaurachand Goswami, Nirmal Chandra Goswami (who was called Panchu at the time), and he remembered the incident clearly and also remembered me as being the first white-skinned lady to live in Vraja.*

**Radhanath Swami**: It was really a very spectacular event for the Brijbasis. Because I was living amongst the Brijbasis, and they were really proud of Srila Prabhupada—that one of their local residents who was living for so many years at Vamsi Gopal Temple and Radha-Damodara Temple had gone to the West and started temples and transformed Americans and Europeans into devotees of Sri Sri Radha-Shyamasundara. This was just astounding, amazing for the Brijbasis. Thus, they really had very, very high esteem for Srila Prabhupada. They considered him to be like the ambassador of Vrindavan for the world. They were looking forward to seeing the American and European sadhus coming. Prabhupada would have the devotees doing harinam sankirtan in the streets, and it had a very heartwarming effect on the residents of Vrindavan. They were joyful to see people from all over the world—young people full of life and opportunities—who had accepted their culture, their faith. And especially they accepted the mercy of Srimati Radharani, and this was very meaningful to the Brijbasis. At that time, I was with Prabhupada from the mangal arati through the evening. But then after the evening darshans, I would go back to the bank of Yamuna, and I would be with my friends, the local inhabitants of Vrindavan, and they were very much talking about the glories of Srila Prabhupada. It was the first time Vrindavan had ever seen anything like this in history.

**Shyamasundara das**: \[Srila Prabhupada\] was constantly concerned with everyone’s health and well-being, and everyone had a task. Prabhupada would assign the different duties and jobs and tasks for each of us, and we would all report to him every day what we had accomplished. He would give us guidance for the next day’s tasks. We had to become Vaishnavas finally in manner and in dress. So Prabhupada taught us all the ropes, all the different ways a Vaishnava should act in India, by example. We got to follow him around and watch him every moment, and we just began to emulate what Prabhupada did.

**Chitralekha devi**: On the way to Vrindavan, Palika started feeling sick. So when it was time for all the devotees to leave Vrindavan with Srila Prabhupada, Tamai Krishna asked me to stay there with Yamuna, for her to have more recovery time, and to help take care of Palika. We moved into Srila Prabhupada’s rooms at Saraf Bhavan and stayed there on our own for about a month.

That was the most incredible month of my entire life! I couldn’t even grasp how much mercy Krishna was giving me to have such intimate association with the holy dhama and Yamuna’s depth of devotion to guide me. Yamuna and I would take turns staying with Palika while the other would walk to Madana Mohana Temple for darshan and to drink water from the well, or Radha-Damodara Mandir for arati and darshan of Srila Prabhupada’s rooms and Srila Rupa Goswami’s samadhi.

Yamuna was always conscientious about cleanliness, and would teas-ingly instruct me about my kitchen habits, which weren’t up to par. All these years have passed and I can still hear her in her kind but firm way telling me to clean the kitchen. She had such a gentle way of saying things that no one would ever take offense.

Every day we would have our simple morning program—chanting and reading. It was the time of the Pakistan war with India, so there was a blackout every evening. We couldn’t even burn candles for light, though we tried. One evening we wanted to read, so we hung blankets over the windows and lit a candle to read Bhagavad-gita. It wasn’t long before we had a knock at the door, scolding us for having a light.

**Yamuna**: *While we were in Vrindavan, the Pakistanis had tried to bomb a large Indian military installation situated in Agra, only 34 miles away. The bombs missed and hit some farmland instead. So there was a tense feeling among the community members in Vrindavan, that if the Pakistanis were so blind that they missed the military installation they were trying to hit and instead hit some farmland, they might miss again and hit something in Vrindavan. So every evening the village of Vrindavan went through a complete blackout period. All of the windows were to be covered with blankets, and the electricity was cut off by the city so there could be no lights shining. There was only candlelight, so it was complete darkness. In Delhi also the blackout was in place, and when Srila Prabhupada went back there, he had to speak by candlelight. Taking advantage of the tense times, he spoke very strongly about the warring propensity in this age of Kali Yuga.*

**Visakha devi**: At first, Vrindavan was for me a simple Indian village, with birds chirping while elderly ladies bent over short brooms to sweep the dustladen streets, sending up clouds of dust in the process, with men balancing milk jugs on both ends of a long stick that straddled their shoulders, with school-aged children in uniforms gleefully running to their classes along the sunlit roads, with the smells of vegetables cooking on outdoor cow dung fires. But after a short time, another aspect of Vrindavan manifested: everyone was chanting the names of Radha, and sometimes of Krishna. And there were temples and worship and sacredness everywhere, on every street and lane and in every corner. We stayed at Saraf Bhavan in November 1971, after the Delhi pandal program. At that time, Palika was seriously ill, and Yamuna and Chitralekha were caring for her. Prabhupada instructed them to give Palika charanamrita, and after they did that, Palika slowly recovered. Prabhupada took the devotees on parikrama at that time to Govardhan, Radha Kunda, Brahma Ghat and other places, but Yamuna didn’t come, as she was caring for Palika.

Srila Prabhupada had come to realize the need for sannyasis to push on the movement of Krishna Consciousness, and he began asking some of the men if they would like to enter the sannyasa order. Yamuna remembers the first time Srila Prabhupada asked her husband, Guru das, to take sannyasa.

**Yamuna**: *Srila Prabhupada first requested that my husband, Guru das, take sannyasa while we were staying at Saraf Bhavan. One morning after taking breakfast prasadam, there was an informal meeting with a few disciples. Srila Prabhupada said something to the effect that now we are in this holy place of pilgrimage, Guru das can take sannyasa. Then he immediately turned to me and said, “Do you mind?” And I said, “No, Srila Prabhupada, of course I do not mind.” Srila Prabhupada said, “See, you have no excuse. Your wife knows you will be protected by Krishna.” However, this was somewhat disturbing to Guru das, and he did not take this opportunity. The matter came up again when Tamai Krishna Goswami was taking sannyasa; Srila Prabhupada then asked Guru das again. Over the years, perhaps there were five or six times that the question of sannyasa came up either from Srila Prabhupada directly or during informal discussions with Srila Prabhupada and his disciples about taking sannyasa.*

It is important to mention here that 1971-1972 began what appeared to be an intensive initiative within ISKCON to make sannyasis. Some of this was certainly motivated by sincere devotees wanting to please Srila Prabhupada, but there was also peer pressure among the men, which included openly denouncing the position of householders as being not as committed, devotional, or worse.

## An Early-Morning Japa Walk to Radha-Damodara Mandir

**Yamuna**: *One miraculous pastime that took place during this time with Srila Prabhupada occurred in relation to his rooms at Radha-Damodara Mandir. Srila Prabhupada very frequently gave instructions to us on how he wanted his rooms at Radha-Damodara to be maintained nicely. He was extremely fond of his quarters there. One night during the stay in Saraf Bhavan, he decided that he would stay for one twenty-four-hour period in his rooms at the Radha-Damodara Temple. It was a very exciting event for all of us to look forward to. He selected three or four men to accompany him to spend the night. So it was a glorious occasion.*

*I was also very much looking forward to Srila Prabhupada being in his rooms. Saraf Bhavan was some distance from the Seva Kunj area, where the Radha-Damodara Temple is located. So during the very early hours, between 1:30 and 2:00 am, I rose, bathed, and walked through the streets of Vrindavan chanting my morning rounds until I arrived at the Radha-Damodara Temple. When I got there, the front gate was closed, and I remember pushing it open centimeter by centimeter so it wouldn’t make any noise, and Prabhupada wouldn’t hear me. When I got into the courtyard, I noticed that the light was on in Srila Prabhupada’s room, so I was quiet, no japa—I mean my lips were moving, but no sound was coming out. I chanted like that for what couldn’t have been more than three minutes, and all of a sudden both of Srila Prabhupada’s two doors (he had two doors to his room) were pulled open and he said, “Yamuna, come here.” I thought, “Oh, my God! How does he know I am here?” I was stunned. So I came up into the little pool of light from the one light bulb in his room and paid my obeisances. “How did you get here?” he asked. “I walked.” “You should never have done this,” he told me. “Vrindavan is a very dangerous place at night. There are many dacoits here. And if they see just a little sliver of a copper lota, they could cut you just for the lota.” I said, “I didn’t know.” “Never mind,” he said. “You have come; you can chant.” So I sat just outside of Srila Prabhupada’s room, and he was walking back and forth in his room, both of us chanting japa. So there was some chastisement from Srila Prabhupada on one hand, and on the other hand, he was very pleased. Then at about 4 AM, other pilgrims began to filter in, some for the morning arati program. Srila Prabhupada came out to where I was chanting japa, and he said that this corner at Radha-Damodara Mandir was just like the hub of the wheel of the spiritual world—it was the center. He again requested that these rooms be maintained very nicely, and that they should be cleansed daily. He actually wanted that, if need be, we go to the courts to preserve the rooms at Radha-Damodara for him as his eternal residence. I also used to sit in the courtyard and watch Srila Prabhupada—how he chanted in this very sacred place.*

**Radhanath Swami**: This visit in 197I of Srila Prabhupada was very, very historical in our Gaudiya Vaishnava sampradaya. It was the inauguration of the fulfillment of Lord Chaitanya and Lord Nityananda’s desire that the Holy Names of Krishna be spread to every town and village throughout the world. Lord Chaitanya went to Vrindavan, and He sent the Six Goswamis there. When Rupa and Sanatana went to Vrindavan on Lord Chaitanya’s order, they were there to establish it as a place of pilgrimage for people from all over the world, obviously for people who would become Vaishnavas from every town and village in the world. That was Lord Chaitanya’s vision. And this visit was the beginning of that fulfillment, the first time Vaishnavas from the West who were committed to Krishna Consciousness came in a relatively large group on pilgrimage to the holy dhama of Sri Vraja.

## Yamuna’s Prayer for Srila Prabhupadas Mercy in Vrindavan

**Yamuna**: *In the introduction to the Teachings of Lord Caitanya, Srila Prabhupada begins to give some indication of what he has found in this place called Sri Vrindavan dhama. He explains that Vrindavan is the place where there are desire trees, the land is made of touchstone, and the Lord is herding spiritual cows known as surabhi cows. He is worshiped by hundreds and thousands of gopis, who are all goddesses of fortune. And when Krishna descends, that same Vrindavan descends. Therefore, Vrindavan is not in this material world, and therefore devotees take shelter ofVrindavan. He then says that no one can appreciate Vrindavan without being highly elevated in spiritual knowledge in Krishna Consciousness. Vrindavan in ordinary experience appears to be just like ordinary land, but in the eyes of a highly elevated devotee, it is as good as the original Vrindavan. Srila Prabhupada told us that you cannot purchase a ticket to go to the land of Vrindavan. You must go there by serving a bona fide Spiritual Master and following his instructions.*

*Srila Prabhupada, I am still hoping to learn what service means, what purity means, and I am still hoping to get that ticket.*

## The Jaipur Pandal and the Beautiful Face of Govinda, 1972

In January of 1972, Srila Prabhupada sent two of his disciples, Kaushalya devi and Srimati devi, to Jaipur in Rajasthan to make arrangements for marble Deities for some of the temples in the West, especially for New York. The Srila Prabhupada-lilamrta biography of Srila Prabhupada describes in detail the difficulties faced by the women due to Srimati’s missing passport, but as with so many experiences of devotees, what at first appears as a great challenge becomes an even greater blessing by the mercy of the Lord, the Spiritual Master and the Vaishnavas.

**Yamuna**: *Although most of the devotees were dispersed to their various posts throughout India in December of 1971, I stayed on in Vrindavan for most of that month. Then a party initially consisting of two women, Kaushalya devi and Srimati devi, were sent to Jaipur to prepare for some Deities to be carved who were to become Sri Sri Radha-Govinda in ISKCON’s New York temple. While in Jaipur, the two devotees would go every day to the glorious Sri Sri Radha-Govinda Temple and have kirtan there. This was during the time of the Pakistani conflict, so there was suspicion among some of the authorities that they were in fact spying. However, the principal authority of the temple, P. K. Maharaja, as well as other prominent people in Jaipur, had closely observed their behavior and reassured the doubters that they were sincere devotees. To whomever they met, Kaushalya and Srimati spoke about Srila Prabhupada and the importance of bringing him to Jaipur, and somehow it was arranged that our party would come with Srila Prabhupada for a large pandal program there. Even more impressive was that the pandal was to be within the temple compound, so the tens of thousands of people who came each day to offer respects to Sri Sri Radha-Govinda would then be able to attend the pandal. So although nothing very concretely had been organized for the program, the two ladies invited Srila Prabhupada to come with his World Sankirtan Party to Jaipur. Even though Srila Prabhupada later chastised Kaushalya and Srimati for some organizational deficiencies, what they did in such a short time was impressive, especially the fact that they had endeared themselves to prominent citizens of Jaipur who ultimately helped in funding the entire pandal.*

*So all of us were to assemble in the compound for this big pandal program, but it was clear that there were some serious problems. When our party from Delhi arrived in Jaipur one cold January morning, very little had been organized for the pandal program or Srila Prabhupada’s quarters. A great deal of work remained to be done, even though according to the advertisements there was only a one or two day period before the pandal was due to start. So we had to work fast and furiously under difficult conditions to try to get the large canvas tents set up just behind the main temple. As it turned out, when His Divine Grace arrived he initially chastised the two women, but then encouraged them for their sincerity and determination and on how they had made a positive impact on some of the prominent leaders in Jaipur city. So although there were some mutterings among the men that women should never be allowed to arrange programs because they simply did not have the skill, Srila Prabhupada decided to go on with the program.*

*To give a physical picture of this glorious place, there was one gigantic temple wall and what was essentially a city within a city—the royal city was within the outside temple wall. Then there were many buildings. Another temple wall held the royal compound and quarters of the Jaipur state, as well as the large Sri Sri Radha-Govinda Temple, the temple gardens and lake, and two large palaces. And that was inside the inner temple wall. So Srila Prabhupada was given one small kutir very close to the temple of Radha-Govinda. It was a small hexagonal structure with one room and bathing facilities, and it overlooked the large empty area where we were to set up our pandal.*

*The women resided several blocks from the temple, and the men were given a separate residence some distance away. We would meet in the day for our pandal program, and all of the devotees ate a large noon meal at the temple—it was all nicely arranged. The maha prasadam from the temple kitchens was wonderful. I believe that a small fruit breakfast was provided in the morning, and then in the evening some maha prasadam from the Deity kitchens. It was a very exciting time for all of the devotees because we were not only gathering in this sacred place but, more importantly, we were once again reunited with Srila Prabhupada for preaching. As with all our other pandal programs, His Divine Grace would attend morning and evening.*

**Each evening Prabhupada spoke at the pandal, and often a respectable Jaipur citizen would introduce him. When the queen of Jaipur introduced him one evening, she expressed her devotional sentiments for Prabhupada and his movement.**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

**Yamuna**: *The idyllic pandal setting within the compound of the famed Sri Sri Radha-Govinda Mandir worked out wonderfully for Srila Prabhupada and the devotees. Each day a prominent person inaugurated the festival, and this began with the Rajmata (Queen Mother) of Jaipur herself, Srimati Gayatri devi. When she agreed to host the program and be a guest speaker, that day there was an especially large gathering—and Srila Prabhupada spoke, and then the Rajmata spoke*

**Kaushalya devi**: During the five-day program, the Maharani of Jaipur invited us to her palace. I went there with Srila Prabhupada, Devananda Swami and Shyamasundara. The Maharani was so impressed with Srila Prabhupada that she offered to donate an elegant old residence on the grounds of the City Palace. The next day we toured the building and although it needed some renovations, Prabhupada loved it. He asked me to stay in Jaipur to finalize the transaction along with Devananda Swami and a new Indian devotee. Unfortunately, the Maharani's family would not allow it, and we never received the building

Srila Prabhupada mentioned in a letter to Hayagriva on January 18, 1972, that he had met with the Queen Mother, Rajmata Gayatri devi, and that she had offered a building near the palace as a prospective center. However, as her husband, the Maharaja, had died a year and a half earlier, the succession had passed on to her stepson, so it is not surprising that the offer did not actually transpire. Although she maintained cordial relations with Srila Prabhupada and his disciples, as a leader of the opposition party to Indira Gandhi and a Member of Parliament, she was then embroiled in one of the most turbulent eras of India’s modern history. Yamuna met her on two or three occasions and remembered her as gracious and regal, always charming, yet definitive in her views. I saw her only once, in 1994, while walking with Yamuna in Khan Market in New Delhi. Although accompanied by only one other person, she was still deferred to and offered great respect by all who recognized her. We did not approach her, but noted that at the then age of seventy-five she still appeared gracious and regal, and cordially greeted all who approached her.

## A Short History of Sri Govindaji

Anyone who has been to the unforgettable darshans at Sri Sri Radha-Govinda Mandir in Jaipur knows that as soon as the gates open, massive floods of people literally run to the temple to have the darshan of Their Lordships. Long before I ever had the experience of witnessing this myself, Yamuna used to speak about the enthusiasm of the people of Jaipur and how Sri Sri Radha-Govinda were truly the cynosure of everyone’s eyes and hearts. Each of the three times we went together, she used to say that she wanted to see the beautiful face of Govindaji at mangal arati before His face was decorated in chan-dan so she could fully appreciate how stunningly gorgeous He was. Here stands the same Govinda whose beautiful face Uttara, the mother of Maharaja Parikshit, said looked the most like Krishna when He was present 5,000 years before. So the pandal placement was perfect in that it would be natural for those coming for darshan to then come to the pandal, both morning and evening.

**Yamuna**: *So at the very onset of the program, I remember Srila Prabhupada had a nice vyasasana, and we were advertising that our program would take place just after the morning darshan at the main temple, so the same crowd who came running in to see Radha-Govindaji in the morning could then proceed on to our large pandal program afterwards. The agenda was fixed. Srila Prabhupada would chant the Govindam prayers from the Brahma Samhita. This was Radha-Govinda, after all. He would often ask me to chant these prayers before the program began. He also requested the same installation and abhisheka ceremony we had performed in New Delhi’s pandal. So on the first day of the Jaipur pandal, Srila Prabhupada watched as one of his men performed the fire sacrifice and I bathed the small Deities. Then Srila Prabhupada would lecture, we would have very long sankirtan, and then conclude with distribution of prasadam. The main programs took place in the mornings and evenings rather than all day long, because in the afternoon the Deities of Radha-Govindaji take rest, and so there was little activity within the compound.*

Shyamasundara das: This was one of the most intimate and relaxing highlights—Prabhupada’s stay in Jaipur in the palace grounds as a guest of the Queen, Gayatri devi. She was so thankful to have Prabhupada there. The devotees coming in and out of Govindaji’s temple would parade by Prabhupada’s bungalow throughout the day, and there were so many wonderful devotees in Jaipur. Every one of Prabhupada’s lectures, morning and night, was packed with thousands of people, devotees of the Govindaji Temple there. He was appreciated in Jaipur in a way that he had not been appreciated in other cities in India. Almost every citizen came to these speaking engagements. They were already full-fledged Vaishnava devotees. He was very happy in Jaipur.

**Yamuna**: *One day Srila Prabhupada went on nagar sankirtan in Jaipur with us. He rode in front of the party on a bullock cart. Two gigantic white bulls with regal horns pulled the cart. The cart itself was a plain platform draped in gold lame, with a fleur de lis pattern around the base. Armed police in red turbans and khaki uniforms and turbaned footmen walked alongside the cart. A red and gold umbrella was held over Srila Prabhupada as he entered the gates to the interior part of the Pink City. Our sankirtan party followed behind the cart on foot, and we ended at the pandal site.*

## The Looting Langurs

**Yamuna**: The area was just filled with monkeys, and they were the very large gray monkeys with black faces and long curly tails known as Hanuman langurs. These langurs, although considered sacred in India, were a continual disturbance to us, stealing this or that—either cloth or food—and it was a constant battle to actually protect Srila Prabhupada and his quarters from them. When it was not in use, these langurs inhabited the veranda of Srila Prabhupada’s kutir, so naturally they considered it as their territory, and we were the interlopers. Nevertheless, we had to arrange a permanent monkey guard surrounding Srila Prabhupada. Srila Prabhupada gave us very strict instructions on dealing with monkeys, both here and in Vrindavan. He said that we should always remain neutral to them and neither make them our friend nor enemy. This was difficult to accomplish when they very easily opened doors and stealthily swooped down from rooftops or trees to steal whatever they could. 3\*\*

## Srila Prabhupadas Instructions to Yamuna in Jaipur on Deity Worship

**Yamuna**: As with our Delhi pandal, the Jaipur pandal featured a large pair of Radha and Krishna Deities. This time They were the large black and white marble Deities of Radha and Krishna with conch shell eyes acquired by Kaushalya and Srimati, who were to become the Radha-Govinda Deities of ISKCON New York. Again the small set of Deities used in our abhisheka at the first Delhi pandal, now named “Yamuna’s Deities” by Srila Prabhupada, were worshiped in the bathing ceremony. These Deities traveled with us and were worshiped in the abhishekas at our pandal programs in Delhi, Jaipur, Madras and Visakhapatnam.

I was always anxious to rise early in the morning in India, especially when I was allowed to associate personally with Srila Prabhupada. After he finished his chanting and translating work in the mornings, there were sometimes short periods in and around mangal arati when he would have a meeting with some of his devotees. Often it involved giving instructions for the day and receiving reports, and at other times it was for Krishna Conscious instruction. Once, in the dark hours of one morning in Jaipur in that January of 1972,I saw the light shining from inside Srila Prabhupada’s little round kutir. And it was bright enough to illuminate the pathway going toward his door. His servant greeted me on the outer veranda and opened the wooden doors into the warm room where Srila Prabhupada sat behind a small wooden desk. His Divine Grace was speaking with three or four disciples regarding the upcoming program. Just as I crossed the stone and wooden doorstep, he observed: “The clay pot of sweetmeats you are carrying has touched the floor. Now you cannot offer the contents to the Deity.
