Lord Chaitanya was very strict about bhoga offered to the Deity. The items must be kept very nicely, and they must never touch the areas where many feet pass. We can never be careful enough in serving the Supreme Lord.”

Srila Prabhupada continued by relating a story from the Caitanya-caritamrta describing the pure devotional service of Raghava Pandit. One servant was engaged in bringing very sweet coconuts from a distant place for offering to the Deity. One day when the green coconuts were brought, it was right before the offering. The servant was standing near the door and accidentally touched the ceiling above the doorway, then again touched the prepared green coconuts with the same hand. In this way Raghava Pandit explained that the coconuts had become contaminated, and he rejected the offering and sent for more, even though they were some distance away. Srila Prabhupada said that it was not that Raghava Pandit was a crazy person suffering from some cleaning phobia, but rather in his exalted spiritual position, he was eager to maintain the highest standard of cleanliness in the service of the Lord. He added that bhoga must be secured and prepared while meditating upon the lotus feet of the Lord.

## Srila Prabhupadas Instructions to Yamuna in Jaipur on Cooking

The following is taken from a cooking article Yamuna wrote for Back to Godhead magazine. It illustrates how Srila Prabhupada always instructed her to learn from the expert cooks wherever she went. Just as he said he educated himself in cooking in his youth by watching the street vendors cook, so under Srila Prabhupada’s direction, Yamuna learned from the simple Rajasthani women making a lunch in an open field. These often spontaneous instructions to study the culinary arts of India, whether from rudimentary one-stove meals made in fields or the elaborate kitchens of Maharajas, ultimately contributed to the writing of Yamuna’s first awardwinning cookbook, Lord Krishna’s Cuisine.

**Yamuna**: *It was about 10:30 in the morning when I arrived at Sadhu Kutir, Srila Prabhupada’s quarters. The two stone rooms, connected by a veranda, were perched on a knoll overlooking a panorama of craggy hills, a pomegranate orchard, a small lake and a field.... This idyllic setting lay within the compound of the famed Sri Sri Radha-Govinda Temple in Jaipur, in the Indian state of Rajasthan. A clear January sky had made my shopping pleasant that morning, the fog of dawn dissipated by a warm winter sun. Laden with bags of kitchen supplies and mentally planning the lunch menu, I was less aware of the scenery than of the brazen long-tailed monkeys eager to snatch my goods.*

*Srila Prabhupada came into view only moments after I’d laid down my bags. Draped in a wool shawl, he was strolling to and fro on the veranda, quietly chanting on his beads. He called me over to observe a group of Rajasthani women preparing lunch in the open field. Pungent smoke from their cooking fire of margosa wood and cow dung wafted our way as a narrow-necked brass pot of dal (legume) soup simmered on a makeshift stove.*

*As the women worked on the noon meal, Srila Prabhupada commented on their ingenuity and expertise: They’d gathered wood, collected stones and built a small stove, set up a workable cooking area, and arranged an eating place. But more than anything, he extolled the virtues of the dal soup cooking on the fire. Dal—nutritious, versatile and easy to prepare—is India’s main source of protein, he told me. The innocent cow needn’t be slaughtered to satisfy the demands of the tongue. Srila Prabhupada encouraged me to experiment with the goodness of this simple noon meal of dal, flame-toasted chapatis, and perhaps a little yogurt and pickle (Back to Godhead, 1992)*

## Yamuna’s Ref lections on How Srila Prabhupada Interacted with Others

**Yamuna**: During this time in India, Srila Prabhupada would often glorify Giriraja das, speaking about how he had given up so much in the way of family ties and money in order to engage in menial service at the lotus feet of his Spiritual Master, and how this was exemplary behavior. So when preaching to the goswami class, whether they were his Godbrothers or caste goswamis, he would strongly affirm that one’s spiritual identity does not depend on one’s birth in a particular family or in a particular caste or creed, but rather with one’s resolution that he will engage in this Krishna Consciousness process. Just like when Lord Chaitanya formed His Sankirtan Movement in so many cities and towns, He showed so many miracles, He taught the principles of bhakti, He engaged in harinam sankirtan, and still there was great criticism among the brahmana class toward His activities—they became jealous of Lord Chaitanya’s success. Similarly, there was an underlying current of jealousy among many of the caste-conscious brahmanas or goswamis, and although they frequently came to Srila Prabhupada to challenge him, he marched on with the banner of harinam sankirtan and not only astonished all of his devotees with his blazing and relentless Krishna Consciousness presentation, but very often encouraged nonbelievers to follow him, gaining the respect of many caste goswamis along the way. I recall in this connection one instruction that Srila Prabhupada gave to me, Guru das and Ksirodakasayi das, for we were three members who were being dispatched to Vrindavan dhama to help develop programs there. He said that in Vrindavan we would show our potency by worshiping the Deity nicely, by having nice sankirtan and through prasadam distribution. He added that there were then nearly 25,000 inhabitants of Vrindavan. Some 5,000 were Bengali widows, another 5,000 were caste goswamis, and of the balance, many were merchants.

He said, “You should not intimately deal with any of them. Do not reveal your mind to them. For etiquette purposes, you should be very congenial. You can associate with them enough to get your work done, but never become intimate with them.” He explained it as a science, and of course Srila Prabhupada was so masterful in training us how to deal with different mentalities within the human community. As he traveled all over India, so many people were attracted by his message in different ways—either to listen or actually to become spiritualized by his touchstone association. The goswami class was generally hesitant to even pay respects. But there were a few great personalities who did offer respect, and during the Jaipur pandal, P. K. Goswami, the temple administrator, was one who stepped forward and offered his enthusiastic support at Srila Prabhupada’s lotus feet.

After the pandal program in Jaipur, our party dispersed. Srila Prabhupada sent us all to different posts around India, and I was not to meet Srila Prabhupada again until mid-February, when we assembled with him in Madras as the guests of a Madrasi businessman, Mr. Balu.

## Learning Vaishnava Etiquette with Srila Prabhupada in Madras and Visakhapatnam

**Giriraja Swami:** In December of 1971, I arranged a speaking program for Srila Prabhupada in Madras, India. Thousands of people came to hear him, and the leading newspaper carried a summary of his lecture every day. Then the Chief Justice of Madras invited him to speak before a large gathering of High Court judges, advocates and other leading citizens. Srila Prabhupada appealed to the audience to follow the examples of Sri Sanatana Goswami and Rupa Goswami, who in the sixteenth century had given up their exalted posts as Prime Minister and Finance Minister in the Bengal government to help Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu spread the Krishna Consciousness Movement. So his talk was very well received, and then after that the Chief Justice invited him to his house for dinner....

\[Srila Prabhupada\] was there for five days. The first day they had a procession in the town down the main street. And then the next three days there were programs every night in a big hall. And then the last night there was this program, and after that Prabhupada went to Visakhapatnam for Puri Maharaja’s program. So every night of those three nights, the place was completely packed. There were about 3,000-5,000 people—and very nice people. And there Prabhupada’s line of preaching was mainly Bhagavad-gita As It Is....

So we also had a press conference, and Srila Prabhupada spoke to the reporters very personally. This was one thing that struck me. He wasn’t speaking to them as if they were newspaper reporters, but... as spirit souls, as individual personalities who are meant to be devotees of Krishna. So even though they were addressing him as newspaper reporters, he was answering them in a completely different way. And he was encouraging them and saying that “This reporting that you have done is very nice. Krishna will bless you. Please help spread this movement. This is the real benefit for human society.”

## Mr. Balu Hosts Srila Prabhupada and the Sankirtan Party in Madras

The short visit of Srila Prabhupada and the devotees in Madras, and especially to the home of their host, Mr. Balu, would have a profound and enduring effect on Yamuna’s Krishna Consciousness. She often expressed that this was a turning point for her in that here she fully understood the level of sacrifice Srila Prabhupada had made and the criticisms he continued to receive because of his open-hearted acceptance of women and so-called mlecchas from the West as Vaishnavas. She was also consistently awed by his skill in dealing with all classes of people, determined to encourage them in their spiritual lives regardless of any misconceptions they held, as evidenced in his interactions with our hosts, the Balus, themselves.

**Prabhupada’s host, Mr. Balu, although a prominent businessman, was also well known as a religious man. He received Prabhupada warmly and respectfully, according to proper Vedic etiquette. Prabhupada noted that Mr. Balu had his own temple, with beautiful Radha-Krishna Deities and a large tulasi plant. When the devotees accompanying Srila Prabhupada asked Mr. Balu why the Deities were often dressed in black, he replied that They were so effulgent that if he didn’t dress Them in black he wouldn’t be able to look on Them. He did not make prostrated obeisances to his Deities because he and his wife were Krishna’s father and mother, he said, and how can the father pay obeisances to his son?**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

**Yamuna**: *By traveling with and observing Srila Prabhupada’s interactions with all varieties of people, we saw that in every circumstance he exemplified Vaishnava etiquette and behavior. Every activity of his personal sadhana and how he represented our previous Acharyas in the preaching field according to time and place were impressed upon us. He was a living university of Krishna Consciousness and the epitome of what it meant to teach by example. In the Balu household, Srila Prabhupada was very gentle with Mr. Balu because he recognized his sincerity and felt that he had been influenced by various kinds of bad association. Mr. Balu was a gentleman, and he offered all kinds of facilities for the comfort of Srila Prabhupada and his party. But in another sense, he knew very little about the science of Krishna Consciousness. So Srila Prabhupada was very tolerant with this family, always complimenting them on how nicely they did everything.*

*At that time I was still taking care of one set of Radha-Krishna Deities which Srila Prabhupada affectionately named “Yamuna’s Deities.” As the Deities who were bathed in the abhisheka ceremonies at both the first Delhi pandal and the Jaipur pandal, They had become our traveling sankirtan Deities during this time. Formerly, at the programs in Allahabad, Surat and Gorakhpur, Srila Prabhupada’s small Deities were used. Those were the same Deities he had traveled in the United States with, and later, while residing at John Lennon’s estate in England, taught me how to perform Deity worship with.*

**Prabhupada and his host related to each other graciously. But one night Mr. Balu and his wife came to Srila Prabhupada and asked him to please speak about the rasa lila of Radha and Krishna. Prabhupada replied that the rasa lila, being the most exalted spiritual topic, was meant only for liberated souls. Only one completely free of material desires, Prabhupada explained, was fit to hear the rasa lila. “No, Swamiji,” Mr. Balu insisted. “My wife and I are very keen. You must recite rasa lila.” Again Prabhupada described the exalted position of the rasa dance, repeating that only when one is completely free of all material attachments to wife, family, home and money could he become fit to hear of Krishna’s rasa dance. Mr. Balu then folded his hands and politely repeated, “Swamiji, my wife and I plead with you. Please recite rasa lila." Then Prabhupada replied, “Well, you may be fit to hear rasa lila, but I do not feel that I am qualified to speak it. So kindly ask someone else.”**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

**Yamuna**: *So Mr. Balu had a small temple in his home compound, as do all respectable Hindu gentlemen, and they had a pair of beautiful marble Deities of black Krishna and white Radharani the same size as “Yamuna’s Deities.” So the first day that I arrived there with our Deities, They were placed on the altar in Mr. Balu’s small temple. In Vrindavan, we had been using a tailor named Lalit Prasad, who made the outstanding white outfit for the large Delhi pandal Deities. I had also had him make four sets of dresses for our traveling Deities. And immediately Mr. Balu was stunned by the beauty of the dresses. Srila Prabhupada was also very pleased, because they were flashy and made with some of his favorite colors. One was a deep pink with vivid green and another white—like that. So immediately Srila Prabhupada asked me to allow Mr. Balu to take any of the dresses he liked for his Deities. So although I heard this instruction, I was not eager to give up the dresses, all the while wondering when I would get some more. So as embarrassing as it is to reveal such a flaw in my character, even though Srila Prabhupada had given the instruction, I was reluctant to offer the dresses to Mr. Balu.*

*So we stayed for about five days at the Balu residence, and then Srila Prabhupada sensed that we were becoming a burden with our large party. The pandal program was also not very long. So one day Srila Prabhupada called me into his room and said, “Have you donated the dresses to Mr. Balu?” and I simply said “No.” He then explained that I should understand that whatever I do will be a reflection on him. And this man, Mr. Balu, had hosted us so nicely, so we should be very generous in return and offer him whatever we can for his advancement in Krishna Consciousness. So immediately I was struck with remorse for my diseased mentality and requested Mr. Balu to come look at the clothes. So he and his wife came, chose one dress, and we then decorated his Deities very nicely. It was inspiring for his Krishna Consciousness, and I was, of course, again reminded that when one gives in devotional service, he or she is never the loser. Preaching means to give Krishna Consciousness through whatever you have learned and heard from the Spiritual Master, so one’s rapid advancement in Krishna Consciousness is certain according to the ability to cent-percent follow the orders of the Spiritual Master. It was an important lesson for me to learn.*

## A Glorious Afterward to the Balu Deity Story—Srimati Radharani's Youthful Face

Prior to the visit to Madras, Yamuna had begun gathering information and pictures for what would become “Yamuna’s Deity Book.” During their stay at the Balu residence in Madras, Yamuna had become so charmed by the sweet face of the Balu’s Srimati Radharani that she determined that if ever she had Deities made, she would use Her beautiful face as the inspiration. So she had a close-up picture taken, and later, when the Deities were being conceived for the Krishna-Balarama Temple in Vrindavan, she gave that picture to the Deity sculptors in Jaipur. The picture is reproduced here along with a picture of Srimati Radharani’s face near the time of Her installation in Vrindavan’s ISKCON temple.

## Yamuna’s Appreciation for South Indian Cuisine

**Yamuna**: *Madras was my first real exposure to the vegetarian cuisine of the South, and the prasadam served to Srila Prabhupada and the devotees by the ladies of the Balu household was simply exceptional. We could see the importance not only of having very tasty and properly prepared prasadam, but of the atmosphere in which prasadam was served and respected as well. Once again Srila Prabhupada took pleasure in seeing the assembled devotees honoring this nice prasadam, and on several occasions he requested the lady members of our party to go and study how these preparations were made. The repertoire was classically South Indian—fiery-hot liquid preparations offset with mild and bland steamed rice preparations. Most of the cooking in the South of India centers on variegated rice dishes, and there are popular steamed, feather-light sponge dumplings known as iddli, usually served with liquid coconut chutney. Two large prasadam meals were served each day to the devotees, and Srila Prabhupada frequently came to see all the preparations we were eating. Although we would help a little to prepare some dishes, most of the cooking was done exclusively by the Indian ladies of the household. Srila Prabhupada seemed to enjoy it very much, and South Indian cuisine became one of my life-long favorites.*

Anyone who had the fortune to honor prasadam made by Yamuna devi, whether a light snack or opulent feast, would have noted that the presentation of the meal was as important to her as the taste. If a group came for a festival or special prasadam meal, she would often sit quietly, beads in hand, seemingly staring at some far distant point. Sometimes this would go on for two or three hours. Then she would jump up and begin preparation, having all the designs, textures, colors, place settings and tastes completely worked out during that time. I don’t ever remember seeing her put less than 1,000% into these meals, programs or festivals, whether for two or two hundred. To her they were an extension of her Deity worship—service to the Vaishnavas, to Srila Prabhupada and to Sri Radha-Banabehari. Guests invariably wanted to take pictures of her table before partaking of the indescribably delicious meal itself.

## A Godbrother Controversy and a Life-Changing Revelation for Yamuna

**Srila Prabhupada’s most acute controversy in Madras was not with smarta-brahmanas, Mayavadis or Shivaites, but with some of his own Godbrothers. Although some of them acknowledged his incomparable preaching in the West on behalf of their Spiritual Master, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati, others were envious.**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

The vitriolic letters to the Madras newspapers and to Srila Prabhupada himself from a person or persons connected with the Madras Gaudiya Math have been detailed in the Srila Prabhupada-lilamrta and in Giriraja Swami’s remembrances, yet on a personal level, Yamuna took from the incident a profound life lesson which helped to strengthen her faith, commitment and devotional perspective in the challenges to come in her devotional journey.

Initially this Godbrother had written an extremely virulent letter to Srila Prabhupada complaining about many perceived wrongs, but specifically mentioning the dancing devotees and the mixing of men and women. He also brought up petty things, like Srila Prabhupada’s wearing a gold watch, which was ironic, as it was identical to the criticisms their own Spiritual Master, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur, had to endure during his manifest presence. Each devotee processed the experience in their own way, but to Yamuna, it was the first time she fully realized how much Srila Prabhupada had personally sacrificed in coming to the West, especially in allowing women such free and open-hearted access to both the process of Krishna Consciousness and to himself. It was a life-changing revelation. Whenever women came to her throughout her later life, she would try to encourage them to put into context how much Srila Prabhupada had actually diverged from the strict patriarchal culture he came from—not just within his own family dynamic, but within his Krishna Conscious Society, the Gaudiya Math—to give women the same opportunities to become Krishna Conscious. Throughout his remaining years with us, Srila Prabhupada was roundly criticized by the caste goswamis and many of his own Godbrothers for this very thing. Yamuna felt it was unfair for women to feel that he had not gone far enough. Taking into account the rigidly circumscribed position of women in Indian society in both the social and religious context of the times, she saw that he had given so much, sacrificed so much, to include women. She always said that she never felt excluded by Srila Prabhupada himself in devotional service, but sometimes felt marginalized by the attempts of the Western male devotees in those early years to enforce Indian stereotypes on women. She understood Srila Prabhupada’s mood with regard to this perhaps more than anyone, as he had discussed it with her several times. Further, she realized the importance to the acceptance and success of his mission in India that his women disciples follow its strict etiquette. Yet she worried that if it was misconstrued or corrupted, there were ample opportunities to use “etiquette” as a means of demeaning women who had given their lives to serve Guru and Krishna. Later in Los Angeles in 1975 and 1976, Yamuna and I would have open and honest conversations with Srila Prabhupada about this. I will enter more thoroughly into those conversations later, but he essentially encouraged us that each of us has to endure the challenge of criticism in our devotional lives, and we should try to use it as a means to grow in humility. Yamuna never forgot this instruction, and remained eternally grateful that he endured so much criticism to bring the great gift of Krishna Consciousness to us in the West. “Had you not come...”

## ‘You are Not a Woman, You are a Vaishnava”

One of the loving exchanges Yamuna had on several occasions with Srila Prabhupada related to his teasing her, or as she used to say, “trying to get a rise out of her,” by quoting the Chanakya Pandit verse, “Never trust a politician or a woman.” Another variation was when he would purposely make a statement about women being less intelligent. This may have started in San Francisco, but specifically she mentioned that it occurred in London, then in Madras and Bombay. Once, she was riding in a car with him, and he quoted the Chanakya verse and then turned around to look directly at her with an almost impish smile on his face. When she didn’t react, he repeated it and looked around again in the same way. Yamuna simply smiled and said, “Yes, Srila Prabhupada, you are certainly correct.” Then some time passed, and Srila Prabhupada praised her to show that he in fact saw no distinction on the basis of body, but saw her as an eternal spirit soul sincerely engaged in practicing and promulgating Krishna Consciousness.

**Yamuna**: *I had numerous exchanges which illustrated Srila Prabhupada’s demeanor and mood with regard to my position as a woman. However, one such series of exchanges is what I call the Chanakya Pandit episodes. I was present on four occasions when Srila Prabhupada repeated the Chanakya adage: “Never trust a politician or a woman.” On each occasion, Srila Prabhupada looked me in the eye to see my response. On the last occasion, in Bombay in 1973, he quoted the Chanakya shloka again, heartily laughing in front of a small group of men. Then he said, “What do you think, Yamuna?” Immediately I retorted: “Of course, it is true, Srila Prabhupada,” whereupon he became grave, looked at me with great feeling, and said, “But you are not a woman; you are a Vaishnava.”*

Another episode is remembered by Giriraja Swami in Madras:

**Giriraja Swami**: One time Yamuna came out of Srila Prabhupada’s room, flushed with excitement because Srila Prabhupada had told her something very confidential. She told me that Srila Prabhupada had told her that women are less intelligent, or that it is harder for them to make spiritual advancement. But how I perceived it was that she wasn’t upset or flustered.

Yamuna was always reluctant to reveal anything Srila Prabhupada said or did which exalted her in any way. She once reluctantly revealed to me the rest of this Madras pastime with Srila Prabhupada. After speaking to her about it being more difficult for a woman to make spiritual advancement, he reiterated his comment to her that “But you are not a woman, you are a Vaishnava.” However, he then added to this, “If you continue worshiping and serving the Spiritual Master as you are, you will go back to Godhead in this very life.”

## “Where is Krishna?”—A Loving Exchange and a Lesson on Separation

**Yamuna**: *Malati had been training her young daughter, Saraswati, to perform little aratis to a small picture of Radha and Krishna. And in the Calcutta temple or wherever she was, she would set up her arati set. Srila Prabhupada would sometimes come and watch her perform her arati, and Saraswati would bring him the remnants when it was completed. In Madras, one of the Indian gentlemen who was charmed by her had given Saraswati a silver Deity about six inches high of Govinda playing a flute. It was similar in detail to the carved sandalwood Deity seen all over India.*

*So Srila Prabhupada saw that she now had this silver Krishna, and he expressed to her mother and father, Shyamasundara and Malati, that Saraswati was too young to be in possession of a silver Deity. She didn’t know the value. So he took this Deity from the place where she was worshiping it and kept it aside. Later that evening, we were all in his room, and Srila Prabhupada was preaching informally. Then little Saraswati, although generally quite shy with Srila Prabhupada, burst into the room, rushing to her mother and loudly lamenting, “Oh, Krishna is gone!” So Srila Prabhupada immediately picked up on her sorrow and, in a very deep and profound exchange, intensified her feelings of separation from the Deity. Srila Prabhupada called her forward, immediately capturing her attention, and said, “Saraswati, where is Krishna?” So at first she was saying, “I don’t know where Krishna is. Someone has taken Him.” And although she was very young, Srila Prabhupada almost made it known to her that he had taken her Krishna, and Saraswati knew that. So Prabhupada again repeated, “Where is Krishna, Saraswati?” She replied, “I don’t know.” He said, “Is He under the cushion?” and so she ran over as he pointed to the cushion, picked up the cushion, and said, “No, He’s not under this cushion.” “Is He on the shelf?” Then Saraswati went over to the shelf. “No, He’s not on the shelf.” And all the devotees were feeling the depth of the exchange between this little girl and Srila Prabhupada. “Oh, is He on the window ledge?” She went to the window ledge, and Krishna wasn’t there. So the full intensity of feelings of separation from her Krishna Deity was becoming manifest in this little girl. Then in the middle of the exchange, Srila Prabhupada began reciting the seventh verse of the Sad-goswamy-astaka, composed by Srinivasa Acharya:*

*radha-kunda-tate kalinda-tanaya-tire ca vamsivate*  
*premonmada-vasad asesa-dasaya grastau pramattau sada*  
*gayantau ca kada harer guna-varam bhava-bhibhutau muda*  
*vande rupa-sanatanau raghu-yugau sri-jiva-gopalakau*

**I offer my respectful obeisances unto the Six Goswamis, namely Sri Rupa Goswami, Sri Sanatana Goswami, Sri Ragunatha das Goswami, Sri Ragunatha Bhatta Goswami, Sri Jiva Goswami and Sri Gopala Bhatta Goswami, who are sometimes on the bank of the Radha Kunda lake, on the shores of the Yamuna, and sometimes in Vamsivata. They were appearing just like madmen in the full ecstasy of love for Krishna, exhibiting different transcendental symptoms in their bodies, and they were merged in the ecstasy of Krishna Consciousness.**

*So as this pastime with Saraswati was becoming heightened and intensified, she was in tears, searching, “Where is Krishna? Where is Krishna?” Finally, Srila Prabhupada reached behind his seat, and he pulled out a little Krishna just the same size as the Krishna he had taken from her. And with his eyes very large and a big smile, he said, “Saraswati, here is Krishna.” And she ran over to Srila Prabhupada’s chair and all the tears stopped, replaced by big smiles. And in her ecstasy of finding that Srila Prabhupada held Krishna, she wasn’t even noting that it was not the same Krishna that had been given to her, but rather another Krishna. So in this way, this one beautiful pastime captivated the assembled devotees’ hearts, and several of us were even crying ourselves at the intensity of the beautiful exchange between a devotee in a child’s body and Srila Prabhupada, who so freely gave love of God to anyone who was just a little receptive for it.*

**Notes from. Yamuna’s Journal**

Y**amuna’s Journal: February 18, 1972**—We were having another small private audience with Srila Prabhupada in the home of Mr. Balu, where several devotees were situated in a nice, comfortable room provided by our host. Srila Prabhupada was sitting in an armchair, his bead bag in his hand, and he said:

Krishna Consciousness is a training process. You cannot be elevated by following nonsense activities. When one takes diksha, one must stop nonsense activities. Anyone can come and do it. The purification comes from chanting Hare Krishna. Then the condition of stopping all nonsense activities must also be accepted. One must simply come and hear submissively. Even a passive person, if he just comes and hears, he will advance. Feed them prasadam in a feast atmosphere. Let them hear, and then by association only, they will come forward to become devotees and preach the message of the Lord.

In this regard, one point is that Srila Prabhupada often said that teaching by precept is good, but teaching by example is superior.

## Visakhapatnam—A Meeting with. Srila Prabhupadas Godbrother

**Yamuna**: *From our stay in Madras we traveled by train—all of us together this time, to the Gaudiya Math temple in Visakhapatnam, north of Madras, on the Bay of Bengal between Madras and Jagannatha Puri. Now again we were going to the next preaching venue with Srila Prabhupada, this time as guests of his dear Godbrother, His Holiness В. V. Puri Maharaja. It was the first time we had been hosted by a member of the Gaudiya Math, and Srila Prabhupada appeared very much appreciative of the mood and atmosphere. As the temple was managed by Puri Maharaja, he had made very nice arrangements for Srila Prabhupada to stay within the temple compound. The brahmacharis and grihastha men were given a house close by. A separate apartment for the women was provided close to the temple.*

*In addition to Puri Maharaja, another of Srila Prabhupada’s dear Godbrothers who resided there, Anand Prabhu, would later come to Vrindavan with us and teach me so much about cooking and what it means to act as a Vaishnava, even though he spoke little English. The atmosphere at this temple was warm, friendly and permeated with an open-hearted disposition of Krishna Consciousness. It was very refreshing for all of Srila Prabhupada’s disciples to see such loving exchanges between Srila Prabhupada and his Godbrothers. Earlier in Bombay, when we were staying at the Akash Ganga temple, one or two of Srila Prabhupada’s Godbrothers would sometimes come from the Bombay Gaudiya Math and pay dandavats in Srila Prabhupada’s quarters, and Srila Prabhupada would get off of his simple vyasasana and pay his dandavat obeisances, also on the floor. But this was the first time I had seen actual loving exchanges in service and mood between Srila Prabhupada and his Godbrothers, and I think it was unique in practically all our time in India. In Mayapur there was always some separation, and certainly in Vrindavan. Perhaps at the end, when Srila Prabhupada was in Vrindavan in 1977, some of his Godbrothers came with much more respect within their hearts for Srila Prabhupada’s activities and pastimes. But until this time in Visakhapatnam in 1972, there was formality, but not intimacy, with his Godbrothers.*

*So during our time there in the latter part of February, there was a constant stream of guests coming to the temple. It was a very neatly kept, nice temple, with very sweet kirtans and preaching programs arranged by our hosts throughout the town—usually in halls. Srila Prabhupada requested the devotees to engage in nagar sankirtan in the town. So we all went on nagar sankirtan throughout the streets on a regular basis in the mornings, and frequently in the evenings as well.*

*And again one of the outstanding exchanges was that Srila Prabhupada arranged to personally donate all of the money for the prasadam distribution, not only for his devotees, but also for the guests coming to the temple. It came to thousands of rupees. He gave it to Puri Maharaja in exchange for our staying there, as part of a transcendental exchange. And Anand Prabhu was supervising all the cooking at this time for the assembled devotees, and also he was cooking for Srila Prabhupada. So there are some wonderful photographs of his Divine Grace during this period. His health was strong, his bodily luster brilliant and illuminating, and he would often appear with just his outer covering tied at his shoulder, and no shirt. And he would walk about frequently looking at the different activities in the temple and listening to the devotees’ kirtans.*

*When we assembled in the mornings at about 11:30 for prasadam, all the devotees would line up on the veranda outside Srila Prabhupada’s quarters in the temple compound—the men on one side and ladies on the other side. And as Anand Prabhu would distribute the prasadam down the center, Srila Prabhupada would sit in a wooden chair with his japa beads, simply observing the devotees take prasadam. This pastime went on for many days. So of course, the combination of the loving exchanges between Anand Prabhu and Srila Prabhupada, partly in Bengali and partly in English, was not understood by the devotees, yet we could perceive the ecstatic mood. It felt like a pastime out of the pages of the Caitanya-caritamrta—two devotees serving and sharing in great ec-*

*Srila Prabhupada and Anand Prabhu stasy. The prasadam was superlative, and all of the devotees were respecting rather than eating prasadam. There was a mood of great respect and honor.*

*I noted down one menu which Anand Prabhu cooked at that time. There were deep fried chunks of potatoes covered in powdered spices; a moist cabbage preparation; rice pilau; homemade yogurt; small raj keli, a particular type of sweet banana, for dessert; sandesh; and of course, there was a dal soup. So these transcendental prasadam preparations would be served round after round, and devotees would respect, and Srila Prabhupada made it the policy, of course, that there was never to be even one grain of anything left on the devotees’ plates. So as mentioned before, we had a small girl in our party, Saraswati, and she would invariably leave some prasadam, so all of the ladies would have to take a little bit of extra prasadam. And when we were all finished and filled beyond our capacities, Srila Prabhupada would say the Jaya от vishnupada paramahamsa prayers, and all the devotees would roar out, “Ki jaya!!’’ like that. And then he collected our plates. It was all very sweet.*

*Srila Prabhupada was training us. Actually, it is inconceivable to put an estimate on how much energy he put into training us in every aspect of Krishna Conscious activity, in every aspect of social behavior and, of course, every aspect of developing love of Godhead. But throughout these days of traveling, on many occasions Srila Prabhupada said that he had tried to train us to perform this service or that service in each place we went—that he personally had given us so much direction—because he expected us to learn from the direction and then train others. Then he would encourage us with so many kind words, pat us on the heads and compliment us for doing some insignificant, menial service. He always showed by example how to behave. So these pastimes were so relishable.*

*Aside from the wonderful prasadam pastimes at Srila Prabhupada’s lotus feet, there was a daily morning walk along the Bay of Bengal, and the atmosphere was surcharged with the presence of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. En masse—I don’t think he ever excluded any of us from those morning walks on the beach—all of the devotees knew what time Srila Prabhupada would be taking his walk, and they would come from their different quarters and all follow him down to the seashore. The walks were brisk and refreshing and full of transcendental Krishna katha. Somehow or other we were all able to hear Srila Prabhupada speak.*

**Visakha devi**: In Visakhapatnam, where we stayed in В. V. Puri Maharaja’s Gaudiya Math ashram, a small group of us, including Yamuna, would walk on the clean, wide beach every morning. The atmosphere was intimate, relaxed and ecstatic. We all relished this time with Prabhupada, knowing that it was a rare chance to be with him in such a setting, and Yamuna was especially grateful and most attentive to Srila Prabhupada’s words and mood.

## A Pilgrimage to Sri Simhachalam

**Yamuna**: During our short stay in Visakhapatnam, our party was escorted to a very great temple located seven miles from the modern city of Visakhapatnam, the beautiful temple of Sri Simhachalam. Srila Prabhupada spoke about this temple in a play pwcis on Lord Chaitanya with Hayagriva das, recorded in San Francisco in 1968. In those recordings, Srila Prabhupada called this temple Vijayanagara, and he mentions that the temple is situated five miles from the railway station of the modern city of Visakhapatnam.

So on our visit there, I wrote the following short history given by our hosts: Simhachalam rises about 800 feet above sea level and is about seven miles north of the town of Visakhapatnam. Near the top of the north side of the hill, in a wooden hollow surrounded by higher ground resembling an amphitheater, is the temple of Varaha Lakshminarasimha, which gives the hill its name. The way leading up to the temple runs along a glen of terraced fields of pineapples dotted with mangoes, jackfruits and cashew trees. It leads up a broad flight of stone steps numbering in the thousands. There is a perennial spring, locally called Gangadhara, on the hill. It is purported to have great medicinal properties for bathing, healing and fertilizing all of the flowers and fruit trees with abundant natural minerals. Champa flower trees grow profusely throughout the entire temple grounds. Architecturally, the temple deserves high praise. It comprises a square shrine surmounted by a high tower, or gopuram, a portico with a small circular tower over it, a square sixteen-pillared mandap called a mukhamandapam facing this, and a stone car drawn by two horses and closed by a veranda. The entire temple is made of black granite carved with the conventional formal ornaments and scenes from the Vishnu Purana. Outside of this enclosure to the north sits the Kalyana Mandap, with 96 carved pillars of different ornamentations, motifs and capitals arranged in 16 rows of six each, where a special marriage festival is performed on the eleventh day of the bright half of the month of Ksetra. There are many murtis carved there of the forms of Lord Varaha, and numerous forms of the Nrsimha murti and scenes of Lord Nrsimhadeva’s pastimes. Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu came to this temple in 1512.

This information was passed on to us as we traveled with Srila Prabhupada throughout the temple compound. It took nearly half a day to complete. Many pilgrims, just as in Vrindavan dhama or around the parikrama of Govardhan, walk up to the temple on bare feet. So as that takes some hours to do, we climbed up the windy road leading to the temple in a procession of autos. We were shown the temple as a group, and Srila Prabhupada was, of course, the leader of our group. During parts of the tour when it was a bit too steep or there were too many stairs, Srila Prabhupada was carried in a palanquin by four men, two in the front and two in the back, much like we have photos of Srila Prabhupada when he was in Varsana being carried from one temple to another in the early 70 s. We were also brought into the center of the temple.

Regarding the Deity who is seated in this temple, we were told that the murti dated to the time of Prahlada Maharaja, and from that time long ago the temple fell into disuse and decay. One king, Purusrava, and his consort Urvasi are said to have visited this hill, and at the insistence of Urvasi, the Deity was dug up from under the ground when He appeared to her in a dream. The Lord ordained that He should be exposed to view for darshan only on the third day of the bright half of the month of Visakha, and the rest of the year should be entirely covered with ground sandalwood pulp mixed with camphor and nice scents. So when one goes into the Deity area to see the Lord, one doesn’t see the conventional form of a carved murti, but rather only a shape like a linga, which is rounded on the edges and completely covered in a thick layer of sandalwood. And Srila Prabhupada commented that the sandalwood covering was to keep the Deity “coolheaded.” The sandalwood covering is removed only on that one day a year, and then the beautiful form of Lord Nrsimha is revealed.

So these were some of the pastimes during our stay at Visakhapatnam. Srila Prabhupada’s preaching during this time was mostly to the devotees in his party. We also had some ecstatic kirtans in halls, where several thousand people came, and our programs generally consisted of a Hare Krishna chant, followed by Srila Prabhupada speaking in either Hindi or English, sometimes with a translator, and then a final Govinda Jaya Jaya chant and sankirtan chant.

## Srila Prabhupada and the Champa Story

**Yamuna**: *At one time during the tour, at about 11:30 am, Srila Prabhupada was standing under an immense banyan tree at the lower end of the entire temple grounds where the temple appeared in an amphitheater surrounded by these high mountains on three sides. And Srila Prabhupada carefully looked at this banyan tree from all directions—the back, and from both sides—and he commented that this tree was so immense that is must be over 5,000 years old. The tree had actually grown big, thick pillars to support its limbs in an expansive area of ground.*

*As I noted earlier, champa \[plumeria\] trees were growing nicely throughout the entire compound. There was a beautiful scent filling the air, and one devotee, I believe Nanda Kumara das, picked one of these lovely golden yellow flowers and handed it to Srila Prabhupada as he was standing under the banyan tree. The photograph taken of that moment in history has been lovingly captured by our Godsister Visakha devi, and is printed on the back of the Krsna book, where Srila Prabhupada is seen holding the flower to his beautiful face. After Srila Prabhupada smelled the flower, he commented, “This flower is the color of Lord Chaitanya, and is most loved all over India. The flower is beautiful to look at and beautiful to smell.” And he carried the small saffron-gold flower between his forefinger and thumb throughout the rest of the entire morning at the temple*

*Dear Srila Prabhupada: What I treasured most during our visit to Visakhapatnam was your sweet and intimate exchanges with your Godbrothers, your open-hearted acceptance of each of us wanting your association twenty-four hours a day, and your firm yet gentle training by your instructions and personal example. I will treasure always the champa flower you gave me which you had immediately seen through eyes tinged with love for Lord Chaitanya, and I pray for the gift of seeing Krishna everywhere and in all things, as you do, by your mercy alone.*

Although Yamuna did not mention it here, Srila Prabhupada later gave that flower to her, and she lovingly dried and preserved it. She eventually made a shadow box which featured both the flower and the picture of Srila Prabhupada smelling the flower—a treasured memento of that pilgrimage that has since been hung in every temple of Sri Sri Radha-Banabehari. It is also not surprising that Srila Prabhupada associated so much of this dhama with Lord Chaitanya, because it is close to Ramananda Raya’s meeting place with the Lord, and Ramananda Raya had onceruled the kingdom on behalf of King Prataparudra before moving to Puri to reside with the Lord.

**Yamuna**: *From Visakhapatnam, our party moved on to Mayapur for the cornerstone-laying ceremony for the Sri Mayapur dhama Radha-Madhava Temple*

## Mayapur and the Cornerstone-Laying Ceremony: February—March, 1972

**A Short History of Srila Prabhupadas Mayapur Vision**

We cannot measure the magnitude of what the establishment of temples in Mayapur and Vrindavan must have meant to Srila Prabhupada. The following short history will attempt to give perspective to his sense of urgency for the projects. In 1895, Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur wrote in his Sajjana-toshani publication, “Sriman Mahaprabhu did not descend with His associates to deliver a certain number of human beings in the land of India, but rather to deliver and uplift all living beings in all countries of the world, by practicing the eternal religion of all souls.... When will that day come when all greatly fortunate souls take up banners, drums and hand cymbals and cause the ecstatic waves of harinam sankirtan and the singing of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu’s Holy Name to rise in the streets of their towns and cities?” It was clear that Srila Prabhupada was the personified fulfillment of the Thakur’s prayer, yet ironically many of his own Godbrothers refused to recognize his humble and selfless efforts.

From the beginning of his preaching mission in the West, Srila Prabhupada reached out to his Godbrothers for their support and assistance in fulfilling the desire of their Spiritual Master, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur, to spread Krishna Consciousness all over the world. His heartfelt early letters from New York bear witness to his humility and desire to work in full cooperation with his Godbrothers. Unfortunately, this was not to be.

Srila Prabhupada’s principal aspiration in both Vrindavan and Mayapur was to establish comfortable facilities for his Western students to come and experience the shelter and unsurpassed blessings of the holy dhamas. Srila Prabhupada constantly stressed to Yamuna the importance of taking special care of the devotees who came on pilgrimage to Mayapur and Vrindavan so their experience would strengthen and reinvigorate them spiritually.

**Yamuna**: *Srila Prabhupada instructed us from the beginning that we were establishing the Mayapur and Vrindavan facilities for devotees to come and do two things: To taste the mercy of Krishna Consciousness in the holy dhama, and to become more enlivened in their Krishna Conscious practice so they could enthusiastically go back, distribute his books and perform other services. He remarked that the devotees can’t continually go onto the streets without having a taste of sadhana in the holy dhama. And he said that because they are not used to austerity, we must make our residences very comfortable for the Western devotees. He was trying to train the devotees in India to take care of the Western devotees so that they would be very comfortable and become surcharged in their Krishna Consciousness*

The letters below give an indication of some of the difficulties Srila Prabhupada faced in attempting to bring his desire into fruition. What is astonishing in these letters is the resistance proffered by his own Godbrothers—the same Godbrothers who well knew of Srila Saraswati Thakur and Bhaktivinoda Thakur’s similar desires to establish such facilities.

**Please accept my humble dandavats. I beg to acknowledge receipt of your rubber-stamped circular letter of January 29,1969, regarding the Golden Jubilee Festival of Sri Chaitanya Math. Previous to this I heard about it from Sripada Sraman Maharaja and Sripada Y. Jagannatham, and expecting your invitation, I expressed my desire that during the ceremony a special home for the European and American brahmacharis may be established at Mayapur. Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur and Srila Prabhupada \[Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati\] desired that such American and European devotees may live at Mayapur for studies of Sri Chaitanya philosophy, and now the time is ripe when many American, European and Japanese students working as my disciples are ready to go there for this purpose.... I have therefore requested Sripada Sraman Maharaja (because you have stopped correspondence with me and I don’t know why) to give some place for my disciples at Mayapur.... But on my proposing this scheme, Sraman Maharaja, in his letter of 24 January, 1969, writes as follows: “I do not think we will be able to give accommodations to your American and European students. Even after the ceremony I do not think it will be advisable to call for the American and European students here in Mayapur. Even though we make special arrangements for them, that will not be for many days. Even though you make payment for your students, the other students will feel inferiority complex. You know very well our standard of living, and therefore it will not be possible for us to accommodate your European and American students here in Mayapur. The best suggestion which I can give you is that you better rent one house in Vrindavan and accommodate them there for their education in Sanskrit and Bengali.” \[emphasis Srila Prabhupada’s\]**

**— LETTER TO В. V. TIRTHA MAHARAJA, FEB. 7, 1969**

Srila Prabhupada was obviously disturbed by these slights, yet he remained undeterred and continued to try to work in cooperation with his Godbrothers as his Spiritual Master wished. He requested that he be given a plot of land near the Chaitanya Math to finance and construct a facility for his Western students in proximity to the samadhis of both Srila Gaura Kishore das Babaji and Srila Saraswati Thakur, as well as the gupta, or hidden, Vrindavan conceived of and built by his Guru Maharaja. He continued:

**This is most discouraging and against the will of Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur and Srila Prabhupada Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur. I therefore request you to give me a plot of land within the precincts of Sri Chaitanya Math to construct a suitable building for my European and American students ... who may go in numbers to visit the site of the Birthplace of Lord Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. I can take the responsibility of constructing such building at Sri Chaitanya Math and bear all expenses for the boarding and lodging of such students who will go there. Sraman Maharaja says that Sri Chaitanya Math is not in a position to meet their standard of living. But that does not matter. If you simply give me a plot of land, I shall arrange everything at my responsibility.**

**— LETTER TO В. V. TIRTHA SWAMI, FEB. 7, 1969**

Srila Prabhupada also expressed his displeasure that the pamphlet for the Golden Jubilee Festival broadcast the glories of the preaching in the West of Bon Maharaja some 40 years previously, but did not even mention his own present contributions in this regard or the phenomenal results he was achieving. Srila Prabhupada was surprised and humbly pointed out that although he did not personally want such advertisement, it was improper to not have mentioned it in the pamphlet.

It appears that Srila Tirtha Maharaja sent a short reply on February 14 promising to address Srila Prabhupada’s request in due course, but by December 7 no answer had been forthcoming. Srila Prabhupada again wrote to Tirtha Maharaja:

**In this connection I beg to draw your attention to your letter to me dated February 14,1969, in which you assured me that I could expect some reply sometime afterwards. I am enclosing a copy of this letter for your reference. I am especially interested in the land which I asked from you within the vicinity of Chaitanya Math. This is in pursuance of the desire of Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur and Srila Prabhupada. It is not for my personal use or satisfaction of personal whims. So if you would have given me a small piece of land within the vicinity of Chaitanya Math, then I would not have tried to make these students home anywhere else. I hope this will find you in good health, and I am awaiting your reply with great interest.**

**— LETTER TO В. V. T1RTHA SWAMI, DEC. 7, 1969**

In 1971, Srila Prabhupada again approached Srila Tirtha Maharaja to allow his Western students to occupy the Birla Guest House in Mayapur for Gaura Purnima. Again he was rebuffed.

**Your letter dated 6 March, 1971, in hand. I understand that the Birla Guest House along with other guest houses has been already booked and occupied by pilgrims and guests. I informed you to go there more than one week before they were supposed to be occupied and still it was physically impossible to arrange any accommodation for my party although they have come from Europe and America, some thousands of miles away. Anyway, I shall be pleased to know when they shall be vacant. I wish to go there with my party and stay there for a few days. Kindly let me know when I can occupy the Birla Guest House.**

**— LETTER TO В. V. TIRTHA SWAMI, MAR. 10, 1971**

**Prabhupada was certainly empowered, yet he conducted himself very humbly, with no assistance from others. He had repeatedly invited his Godbrothers to join him in the West and take their places beside him as preachers in the Krishna Consciousness Movement. Why had they not come forward to assist him in their Spiritual Master’s mission, instead of complaining about him, the one Godbrother who was carrying out Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati’s mission?**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

Realizing that no help would be forthcoming, Srila Prabhupada made arrangements to purchase a small plot of land on Bhaktisiddhanta Road closer to the Jalangi River and Hular Ghat. Jayapataka das was already living in a thatched hut on the land to keep it secured while negotiations continued.

**The land they were trying for was a nine-bigha plot on Bhaktisiddhanta Road, less than a mile from the birth site of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. The Sek brothers, Muslim farmers who owned the plot, had been asking a high price. Only recently had a Calcutta lawyer familiar with Navadvipa been able to seriously negotiate a fair price. The Sek brothers had settled for 14,500 rupees, and Prabhupada had authorized withdrawal of the funds from his bank in Krishnanagar. Thus Tamai Krishna and Bali Mardan had left for Mayapur, while Prabhupada had remained in Calcutta, carrying on with his affairs but thinking often of the activities of his disciples in Mayapur. Their mission was very important to him, and he kept them in his mind, personally blessing them with his concern.**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

**Negotiations had been going on to purchase the first piece of land there; this was governed at every step by Prabhupada’s personal direction. In Mayapur, Jayapataka Prabhu (my Godbrother) was living in a hut on the land we were attempting to purchase. We were getting legal advice from a lawyer, one Mr. Das, and Tamai Krishna Prabhu was trying to get this deal finalized. Somehow I became involved, and Prabhupada asked me to accompany Tamai Krishna to Mayapur to finalize the purchase and see that the land was formally registered with the government in the name of 1SKCON. Negotiations were soon completed, papers signed, and the final activity involved registering the deed at the district capital at Krishnanagar. Due to the dacoit danger, we were transported in an army truck surrounded by armed soldiers. We paid the money and saw that all our papers received all the proper stamps, seals and signatures. Deed in hand, we became eager to return to Calcutta to bring Srila Prabhupada the good news.**

**Very late at night we arrived at the Calcutta temple. We were filthy from our journey and exhausted, and it appeared everyone was asleep. Then we noticed a light emanating from Srila Prabhupada’s room, and we could understand that he was awaiting our return. Entering his room, we fell down at his feet to offer our obeisances. Under Prabhupada’s questioning gaze, we explained the successful outcome of our journey and produced the legal papers. ISKCON’s Mayapur plans had now become a reality. Prabhupada’s anxious demeanor gave way first to relief and then to a broad smile of unabashed joy. It was an ecstatic moment that will never be forgotten. The whole room was spiritually energized. Glowing with the pleasure of seeing his dreams become reality, Prabhupada ushered us off to take rest. Our mission completed, my Guru Maharaja pleased, I lay down on the floor to take rest, still basking in the golden glow of Srila Prabhupada’s merciful glance.**

**— BALI MARDAN DAS, JOURNEY TO THE PACIFIC RIM**

## Srila Prabhupada Brings His Western Devotees to Mayapur

Yamuna devi was overwhelmed with excitement at the opportunity to visit Mayapur with Srila Prabhupada for the first time. She had read the Teachings of Lord Caitanya several times since it had been published and already felt an instinctual connection to the dhama, especially the all-forgiving mercy aspect of it.

**Yamuna**: *From Visakhapatnam, our party moved on to Mayapur for the cornerstone-laying ceremony for the Sri Mayapur dhama Radha-Madhava Temple. On the new property, Srila Prabhupada lived in a grass Bengali-style thatched roof hut, which he appeared to relish very much. It was built in a village style, with two rooms, a little entranceway and a kitchen, with a narrow terrace along the front side. There was very nice ventilation from the cross breezes that would come, and at the back was a small, private outhouse for his use. The devotees were sleeping in shyamiyana tents on the grounds surrounding him.*

The grounds were moist and undeveloped at that time, which made getting around something of a challenge. As soon as evening came, armies of mosquitoes appeared and vigorously attacked the devotees. Those who had traveled with Srila Prabhupada on his World Sankirtan Party to Allahabad and other places were somewhat used to the austerities, but the newer arrivals were not. This merely fortified Srila Prabhupada’s desire to establish comfortable facilities for his Western disciples, so they could then truly appreciate Lord Chaitanya and the all-merciful dhama of Mayapur.

Yamuna was pleasantly surprised that with little facility or money, the devotees were able to arrange nice large tents (shyamiyanas) for the festival. The women’s white shyamiyana tent stood so close to Srila Prabhupada’s thatched hut they could actually hear him speak. It even had electricity.

**Visakha devi**: It \[the women’s tent\] was spacious, with fluorescent nights— neon lights. \[This was\] quite unusual for India, especially in Mayapur, such a remote place. As soon as the sun would go down, the mosquitoes would come—these gigantic mosquitoes. You would have to either stay moving or cover yourself with some kind of lotion to keep them away, or stay under a mosquito net. It was rather austere from the mosquitoes. Yet Prabhupada was very transcendental to all these inconveniences and felt very much at home. "

**Yamuna**: *In the center of the small piece of land which started our Mayapur project were a shyamiyana and a podium where Sri Sri Radha-Madhava and our smaller traveling Deities (“Yamuna’s Deities”) were installed during the festival. Srila Prabhupada’s personal secretary at that time was Shyamasundara. His personal servant was Nanda Kumara, and his principal cook was Malati. Throughout much of the time that Shyamasundara was Srila Prabhupada’s secretary, Malati was his cook if the Indian ladies or our hosts did not arrange it. She was a very ingenious and clever servant, and always seemed to figure out a way to make an arrangement for Srila Prabhupada to have nice prasadam. She was very expert in her service, and certainly gained the respect of many of us for her sincere dedication to serve Srila Prabhupada.*

Jananivasa das went with the other devotees from Calcutta to the cornerstone-laying ceremony, where the beautiful Deities of Radha-Madhava presided over the festivities. He had not seen Yamuna for several months, as she was traveling extensively during this time. During the Mayapur festival, he had been assigned to cook the quantity prasadam, which was a simple kitchari. One day, while he was cooking, Yamuna walked in and told him that she had heard so much from Tamai Krishna das about his excellent kitchari that she had to come and taste it. Jananivasa was embarrassed, because he felt there was nothing special about the kitchari, but Yamuna tasted it and then raved about how superexcellent it was. She added that it was the best kitchari she had ever tasted. Jananivasa was struck by how encouraging she was about such a humble service. It is not difficult to draw parallels here to how Srila Prabhupada would often visit a temple and then comment that the Deities there were the most beautiful Deities in 1SKCON. Certainly Srila Prabhupada felt so when he said this, and over the years, Yamuna would often taste the cooking efforts of someone, and in much the same way comment that it was the best she had ever tasted. She was also sincere in saying this, and I soon realized that what she tasted was the devotion of the person preparing the prasadam, and this enhanced the quality of its taste, thus making it “the best.”

**Jayapataka Swami**: At that time, Prabhupada lived in the grass hut. There was no other place to live in. I remember one time we were sitting in the grass hut and he \[Srila Prabhupada\] just said, “This grass hut is in the mode of goodness, and this is all you need for spiritual life—live in a grass hut and live by the side of the holy river and chant Hare Krishna. But if we do this, people won’t come here. So we have to build the big buildings with concrete and steel and bricks. Those buildings are in the mode of passion. But for preaching, we can build those buildings. But for our own selves, this would be enough.”

Whenever Yamuna and I visited Sri Mayapur dhama, a pilgrimage to the simple thatched hut of Srila Prabhupada was a highlight for us. Even this past January 2013, for me to see the magnificent structure being built for the glory of our Vaishnava heritage next to the humble quarters of Srila Prabhupada was astounding. Even though he was very content staying in his simple grass hut, Srila Prabhupada was adamant that the facilities for the visiting devotees must be comfortable and not too austere. He was well aware that Western devotees were not used to the extreme renunciation and austerities pilgrims routinely underwent in holy places, and wanted their experience of Mayapur to be memorable for its sweetness rather than its austerity. His desire has become a reality a thousand times over in both Mayapur and Vrindavan.

**Visakha devi**: Prabhupada said that the Westerners are not used to the austerities that the Indian people are accustomed to. Like at the Kumbha Mela, so many people throng to the Ganges to take their bath, and they will live in the most uncomfortable situations from the climatic point of view, housing point of view and prasadam point of view. And everyone in the West is completely unfamiliar with that sort of austerity. So he wanted to give them a facility where they weren’t inconvenienced, because if they were inconvenienced, naturally their attention towards spiritual life may be interrupted, or their experience of the holy dhama affected, so he planned this building where they would have electricity and conveniences.

**Giriraja Swami:** Before the festival, I had approached Srila Prabhupada on the balcony in Calcutta and said, “Srila Prabhupada, I’ve been trying to understand what you want of us, what your desire is.” I could see that Srila Prabhupada was really listening and taking every word into his heart. And then I said, “Two things seem to please you the most—distributing your books and building the big temple in Mayapur.” And Srila Prabhupada’s eyes opened wide, his face lit up, he smiled and glanced at me and he said, “Yes, you have understood.” And then he said, “If you build this temple in Mayapur, Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur will personally come and take you all back to Godhead.”

## ISKCONs First Mayapur Gaura Purnima Festival

**The five-day Gaura Purnima festival featured twenty-four-hour kirtan with groups of devotees chanting in two-hour shifts. Each morning the main body of devotees would form a kirtan procession and go out visiting Navadvipa’s holy sights: the neem tree under which Lord Chaitanya was born, the house of Srivas Thakur where Lord Chaitanya and His associates had performed nocturnal kirtan, the spot where the Kazi had tried to stop Lord Chaitanya’s sankirtan, the residence of Bhaktivinoda Thakur. (Often Bhaktivinoda Thakur had stood in front of this house, Prabhupada told the devotees, and looked out across the Jalangi toward where Srila Prabhupada now had his land.)...**

**On Gaura Purnima day, ten of Prabhupada’s sannyasi Godbrothers visited to participate along with Prabhupada’s disciples and hundreds of visitors in the dedication and cornerstonelaying ceremony. Prabhupada was gracious and friendly toward his Godbrothers, and he was gratified that they could all sit together to dedicate the World Headquarters of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness.**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

## The Cornerstone-Laying Ceremony

**Yamuna**: *Srila Prabhupada had dispatched his secretary to procure the paraphernalia required for our cornerstone-laying ceremony. He instructed that a pit was to be dug at least 15 feet deep and at least five feet wide on each side. The following articles according to scripture were to be collected for placing within the pit. Five kinds of each of the following: flowers—jasmine, lotus, tulasi, parijata and mogra; grains—rice, wheat, barley, mung and urad; leaves—mango leaves, peepal, neem, bael and banyan; metal—gold, silver, copper, lead and nickel; nectar—sugar, honey, ghee, yogurt and cream; colors—yellow, blue, green, red and white; fruits—mango, apple, grape, banana and chiku-, jewels—coral, diamond, sapphire, ruby and emerald. And there was a beautiful little golden Ananta Sesa Deity with ruby eyes, which Srila Prabhupada placed as part of the metal category.*

*During the actual cornerstone-laying ceremony, several of Srila Prabhupada’s Godbrothers came with their dandas and tilaks, and all of them spoke some appreciation of Srila Prabhupada’s powerful preaching work in the West. So in this way, with a gigantic sankirtan and fire yajna, the Mayapur cornerstone was laid during an enlivening Gaura Purnima celebration with enthusiastic kirtans, fasting and feasting, and glorious katha in the shelter of Srila Prabhupada s transcendental presence. Devotees were taking bath in the Ganga and Jalangi, and Srila Prabhupada foretold that just as the Bengalis were coming here by the thousands for parikrama around Mayapur dhama, one day thousands of devotees from the West would come for parikrama in the same way.*

*In his lecture during the festival of Gaura Purnima, to the surprise of myself and others, Srila Prabhupada spoke at length about cleanliness and basic hygiene. Some of the comments I noted down were that you may drink from the same lota used for the toilet if you wash it three times in Mayapur dirt. He said you may pass stool wearing silk without washing it, but all cotton cloth must be washed. He also said, “Keep yourself clean on the outside by regular bathing and on the inside by regular chanting of the Hare Krishna mahamantra. And in this way your rapid advancement in Krishna Consciousness will be certain.”*

**Visakha devi**: Prabhupada was speaking, and I was so struck that he spoke about bathing properly, keeping clean and personal bodily cleanliness. Amongst all his Godbrothers and the initiation ceremony and so much hullabaloo, he spoke on such a basic principle. Again, \[he was\] trying to train the devotees in a very practical, down-to-earth manner how to keep themselves pure.

**Throughout the day and especially in the evenings, the devotees would gather on the stage of the orange-striped pandal, while Radha-Madhava stood at center stage within a traditional Bengali simhasana of carved banana stalks covered with colored foil and flower garlands. Prabhupada would have his disciples do most of the public speaking, with Acyutananda Swami, lecturing in Bengali, as the main speaker.**

**Hundreds of people came and went in a steady stream, and the devotees distributed Bengali, English and Hindi Back to Godhead magazines. In the evenings, they would present a slide show or a film. Prabhupada was especially pleased to watch the prasadam distribution from his window, hundreds of villagers squatting in long rows, eating kitchari from round leaf plates. “Continue this forever,” Prabhupada told his disciples. “Always distribute prasadam”**

**— SRILA PRABHUPADA-LILAMRTA**

**Yamuna**: *Once on a walk in San Francisco around Stow Lake, Srila Prabhupada actually foretold the creation of this temple. He told me that we would establish something in Mayapur and Vrindavan to glorify our Vaishnava Acharya Bhaktivinoda Thakur. He remarked that actually there are already so many places of worship in these holy dhamas, but for the pleasure of Bhaktivinoda Thakur, in appreciation for his Krishna Conscious preaching spirit in the West, we would create something very glorious for him.*

*It was a very wonderful time for us because Srila Prabhupada was again preaching a great deal to his devotees. Every once in a while some influential gentlemen might come from Calcutta, and sometimes some of the local pilgrims would come to his quarters. But we were new in Mayapur, just becoming established, and most of the thousands of Bengalis who passed our camp going on parikrama of Mayapur dhama were not actually coming to see Srila Prabhupada in his quarters. He did lecture during our pandal programs on his vyasasana, but the lectures were not very long. I recall that a great deal of preaching was done personally with the devotees in his quarters, and although the public lectures were very nice, they were mostly in Bengali—or maybe Bengali one part of the day and English the other, so that the pilgrims would hear Krishna Consciousness. But most of us relished the visiting hours in his humble quarters the most.*

## Srila Prabhupada's Exalted Sister Pishima

On first sight, one would usually be taken aback when meeting Pishima, because her facial features were almost identical to Srila Prabhupada’s, only in a female body. She had a simple nature, devout personality, and was a sincere and dedicated Vaishnavi. She was also ardently devoted to her brother, Srila Prabhupada, and shared many poignant and humorous pastimes with him. Her favorite service was cooking for him, and whenever possible she would take on that role. Whenever a devotee met her, they could expect to find themselves covered with smatterings of holy water from an achmana cup she routinely carried to purify them. She spoke no English, and so Srila Prabhupada sometimes teased her in English, and she would simply smile her beatific smile—filled with love for Prabhupada and the devotees.

**Yamuna**: *Srila Prabhupada’s sister Pishima came to Mayapur and was a central figure of love on the women’s side. One’s first impression was, of course, the facial resemblance to Srila Prabhupada. Otherwise, she looked like many other Bengali widows in their simple white saris wrapped in the distinctive Bengali style. Many of the elderly women do not wear cholis or blouses, so the wrapping is done in a manner which covers the body in one cloth. The style must be age-old, because there is a famous picture of Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur’s wife wearing her widow’s sari in the same manner. It would be wrong to judge Srila Prabhupada’s sister by her simple appearance. Srila Prabhupada often praised his loving sister Bhavatarini \[Pishima\] for her dedication, Vaishnava qualities and steadfast determination in the midst of many challenges in her life. To me she was sweetness personified— the living embodiment of the commitment I was always seeking. Even though she spoke little English and I spoke little Bengali, we bonded in our mutual love of cooking and Srila Prabhupada. Even after her passing, she has remained one of the important mentors in my life.*

*On the men’s side there was a great love for performing kirtan, which was to go on twenty-four hours a day on a revolving basis—sometimes even the women would chant over the loudspeaker for two hours at a time. And this went on all day and all night.*

## Perfect Questions, Perfect Answers — A Mayapur Epiphany

Yamuna often spoke of the powerful exchange of questions and answers between a young visitor to Mayapur named Bob Cohen and Srila Prabhupada, later immortalized in a book entitled Perfect Questions, Perfect Answers. The exchange took place from February 27 through February 29,1972, and the devotees soon realized the important and profound nature of both the questions and answers and crowded around Srila Prabhupada as he eloquently answered the probing and poignant queries.

**Giriraja Swami**: *While we were at Mayapur, one young man named Bob Cohen came to our camp. And we were really surprised, because we didn’t get visitors just coming like that. Bob Cohen was very intelligent and sober. He was a Peace Corps worker in India. So he came to meet Srila Prabhupada.*

*He had attended our pandal program at Deshapriya Park in south Calcutta, and he began to ask Srila Prabhupada very intelligent questions, and Srila Prabhupada gave very elaborate answers. It became a regular routine that Bob would come and ask questions to Srila Prabhupada and, knowing that there was going to be an important discussion, I would ask Srila Prabhupada, “Should I call the others?” and he would say, “Yes.”*

**Brahmatirtha das**: One of the most dramatic moments for me personally was when I realized it was time for me to leave Mayapur. Because the night before on Gaura Purnima night, Yamuna had come to me with tears in her eyes. And I remember the moon reflecting in her eyes, and she had tears and she said, “You are so fortunate. Prabhupada is spending so much time with you.” She said it with such conviction that I was completely overwhelmed, and I realized that I might have to surrender. So I went behind the temple, behind the pandal, and just collapsed in the rice paddies and started crying. I said, “I can’t give everything up.” So the next morning Prabhupada called for me again, asked if I had more questions. I said, “Thank you very much for what you’ve done, but I have to leave now. I have to get back to my teaching.” The Peace Corps had no idea where I was or what I did, so I could go back or not go back. And Prabhupada said, “Don’t talk L-E-A-V-E,” he spelled it out, “talk L-l-V-E. Don’t talk leave, talk live.” So I said to Prabhupada, “So you want me to stay longer?” He said, “Yes.” I said, “Well, if you tell me to, I will.” And then he said to me, “Good boy,” the same way you would say it to your pet. So at that time, in my heart I felt I had become Prabhupada’s pet, not realizing that 1, in essence, had accepted him as my guru.

Bob Cohen did indeed stay and later was initiated as Brahmatirtha das. In an interview in 2013, he was asked what it was about Yamuna devi which had so impressed him at the time. He answered:

**Brahmatirtha das**: \[It was\] her sincerity, her conviction. She was so sincere, so convinced of Prabhupada. Absolutely to the core convinced of Prabhupada’s position that she could convey it in ways that no one else there could convey it to me. It wasn’t so much what she said, because what she said was very simple to me; it was how she said it with tears in her eyes, and her face was glowing. It was absolutely convincing, not at the intellectual level, because she didn’t give me an intellectual argument. But she gave a heart argument. It got right to my heart—it was pure heart. I had so many intellectual arguments going on; I had intellectual discussions of course with Prabhupada, other devotees, “What about this; what about this; what about that?” Yamuna wasn't going to waste her time with that. She just went right for the heart; she was an expert cardiologist, a real heart person.

## Sri Sri Radha-Madhava

Sri Sri Radha-Madhava toured with Srila Prabhupada and the World Sankirtan Party. Although Yamuna speaks about Them as standing on the altar in Allahabad with Srila Prabhupada’s own small Deities, she considered Their formal installation as having taken place in Gorakhpur in 1971, where Srila Prabhupada sang his heartfelt prayer of \]aya Radha Madhava in front of Them before going into a trance-like state. Afterward, he said that this song is “a picture of Vrindavan. Everything is there—Srimati Radharani, Vrindavan Govardhan, Yasoda, and all the cowherd boys.” When the Deities came to Mayapur for the cornerstone ceremony, Srila Prabhupada formally named Them Radha-Madhava and insisted They stay in Mayapur. Somehow, after the Mayapur festival, the devotees brought Them to Hyderabad for a program. When Srila Prabhupada inquired which Deities They were, he was informed that They were Sri Sri Radha-Madhava from Mayapur. Srila Prabhupada then became very angry and ordered Them to be taken back to Mayapur and never to leave again.

**Yamuna**: *A pandal for the festival was arranged for Sri Sri Radha-Madhava and the smaller traveling Deities Srila Prabhupada referred to as “Yamuna’s Deities.” And in the Bengali tradition they had carved an altar for the Deities’ simhasana out of banana stalks beautifully decorated with different colored foils. It is a dying craft. They use it a lot for Durga puja in Bengal. And that was the altar—a beautiful structure.*

For some of the festival, most of the Calcutta male devotees, along with the Deities, were staying with Srila Prabhupada in his bhajan kutir. Jananivasa Prabhu remembers the beautiful Deities of Radha-Madhava standing on a simple table with a curtain in front and having only two changes of dress. He would carefully watch the pujari, a French devotee, all the time, learning how he served Their Lordships by bathing, cooking, offering arati and otherworship. He thought to himself, “This must be the fastest way to become Krishna Conscious!” In his heart he longed for the opportunity to perform that service of being a pujari. Sri Sri Radha-Madhava must have heard his sincere prayer because the French devotee left, and Jananivasa was appointed pujari in his stead. Then Yamuna devi trained him in the simple standard of Deity worship Srila Prabhupada had taught her. Jananivasa said that to this day he considers Yamuna devi as his Deity worship guru. Yamuna also taught him how to repaint the Deities just as Srila Prabhupada had taught her at John Lennon’s estate in England. Since that time, Jananivasa Prabhu never has left the service of the Deities.
